docs.title: macro-symbiosis
docs.text:
This site holds a research framework under open development. It has three parts:

  • The spine: a mathematical specification (companion r10; the equations themselves in r7), with a verification script that checks its internal consistency.
  • The corpus: guidance and five tiers of apertures. Each aperture maps the working concepts of one discipline or tradition onto the spine. Every such mapping is a hypothesis, not a finding.
  • The protocol: how the main hypothesis, \(H_1\), is to be tested. In brief: do independent AI models, conditioned on the spine and corpus, agree when they analyse data they have not seen?

docs.title: What is claimed, and what is not
docs.text:
The protocol (§0) separates three kinds of claim:

  • Verified: the internal consistency of the spine, and only to the extent of the checks recorded in the companion (§5). The verification script runs on every change.
  • Testable hypotheses: \(H_1\) and the predictions of Stages II–IV. None of them has been tested yet.
  • Not claimed: anything about consciousness, its evolution or trajectory, or what the framework brings about.

The framework may be used as a working language for design and practice before it is tested. That use is legitimate in its own terms, but it is not evidence. Exploratory work, which is open and local, is kept separate from confirmatory studies, which are blinded and pre-registered. Exploratory results are never presented as confirmation.

docs.title: How it is developed
docs.text:
The spine and corpus are written with AI models and audited by fresh model sessions that have seen no earlier discussion, following Stage I of the protocol. What appears here is a snapshot of a private working repository; the status page says what each part has passed. Material that must stay hidden from the models that will evaluate the framework is not published.

docs.title: Guidance for Generating, Adapting, and Iterating Orthogonal Aperture Specifications
docs.text: Document ID: aperture_generation_guidance.md Companion Reference: foundational-manifold-2026-10-20-r7.json and foundational-manifold-companion-2026-10-20-r10.md

docs.title: 1. Architectural Separation: The Invariant Spine (\(\mathcal{T}\)) vs. Evolvable Aperture Basis Sets (\(\{\mathcal{E}\}\))
docs.text: To prevent category confusion and allow the framework to scale across diverse geographical, cultural, and scientific contexts, this methodology enforces a strict separation between two architectural layers:

docs.title: 1.1 The Immutable Mathematical Spine (\(\mathcal{T}\))
docs.text: The differential-geometric and non-equilibrium thermodynamic specification locked in foundational-manifold-2026-10-20-r7.json and foundational-manifold-companion-2026-10-20-r10.md (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\)) is not one aperture among many. It is the candidate substrate-independent mediating structure (\(\mathcal{T}\)) onto which epistemological, physical, biological, somatic, and expressive apertures are mapped. Whether these mappings constitute a structure-preserving functor latent in the source disciplines, rather than one imposed by the act of mapping, is the hypothesis \(H_1\) tested in empirical_validation_protocol.md §1.2. Its 39 equation blocks across coordinates \(O_0 \to O_\Omega\), index valences, regularity classes, and standing hypotheses remain invariant across all domains.

docs.title: 1.2 Evolvable Orthogonal Aperture Basis Sets (\(\{\mathcal{E}_{k,m}\}\))
docs.text:
An Orthogonal Aperture \(\mathcal{E}_{k,m}\) (where \(k\) indexes the organizational tier and \(m\) indexes the slot within that tier) is a formal specification of a distinct scientific discipline, philosophical lineage, linguistic calculus, or embodied modality mapped homomorphically onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\).

Unlike Spine \(\mathcal{T}\), no specific list or grid of apertures is permanently frozen. An aperture array is a working topological basis chosen to span the degrees of freedom of a given inquiry: * Portability: Any slot may be re-instantiated with another discipline, tradition, or language family that addresses the same structural problem, under the protocol of §2.2 and the level-of-description rule of §3.1, while preserving the exact operator mappings to Spine \(\mathcal{T}\). * Evolutionary Refinement Across Research Stages: Even within a single research program, the selection and grouping of apertures is expected to evolve as empirical findings accumulate. Validating the mathematical skeleton \(\mathcal{T}\) requires locking a coherent working basis set for each experimental milestone while maintaining a transparent protocol for modifying, splitting, merging, or substituting apertures in future iterations.

docs.title: 2. Reference Organizational Heuristic & Modification Protocol
2.1 The Multi-Tier Scale Cascade and Four-Part Functional Homology
docs.text:
While domain-specific adaptations are encouraged, a high-coherence reference architecture organizes apertures into a five-tier scale-and-coupling cascade, where each tier internally reflects a four-part functional homology:

  1. Five-Tier Scale Cascade (Vertical Axis):
  2. Tier 1 — Foundational Epistemological & Linguistic Ontologies (tier_1_ontological_grammars.md): Macro-grammars of open, non-Cartesian reality.
  3. Tier 2 — Abiotic, Continuum & Tectonic Physics (tier_2_abiotic_continuum_physics.md): Condensed-matter and phase-transition physics, continuum fluid and wave mechanics, atmospheric radiative and thermal boundary physics, and geomorphic and structural mechanics.
  4. Tier 3 — Ecological, Metabolic & Phenological Networks (tier_3_ecological_living_networks.md): Vascular plant physiology and rhizosphere coupling, movement ecology and ecotone foraging, benthic and edaphic biogeochemical metabolism, and chronobiology and phenological synchrony.
  5. Tier 4 — Somatic, Neuro-Attentional & Affective Interiority (tier_4_somatic_contemplative_interiority.md): Myofascial biotensegrity and postural mechanics, vestibular equilibrium and sensorimotor contact, neuro-attentional and autonomic regulation, and affective regulation and psychophysiological resilience.

  6. Tier 5 — Acoustic, Poetic & Cross-Substrate Symbiosis (tier_5_expressive_collective_symbiosis.md): Environmental acoustics and rhythmic entrainment, poetic prosody and psycholinguistic condensation, spatial choreography and relational kinesiology, and inter-subjective and cross-substrate symbiosis.

  7. Four-Part Intra-Tier Homology (Horizontal Slot Logic): Within any tier \(k\), ordering the apertures across four functional slots creates vertical resonance across the entire matrix:

  8. Slot \(k.1\) (Structural & Relational Substrate): Establishes the foundational lattice, ontology, vascular/fascial architecture, or resonant medium (\(O_0, O_2, O_5\)).
  9. Slot \(k.2\) (Dynamic Flow, Wave & Trajectory Kinetics): Governs cyclic excitation/damping, wave dispersion, movement ecology, contact balance, or prosodic flow (\(O_1, O_2, O_6\)).
  10. Slot \(k.3\) (Boundary Gating, Directional Exchange & Metabolic Filtering): Governs selective permeability, direct/inverse phase-lead indexing, radiative/biogeochemical boundary flux, attentional scope modulation, and threshold navigation (\(O_1, O_4, O_6\)).
  11. Slot \(k.4\) (Coalescence, Hysteresis & Macroscopic Closure): Governs network percolation, condensed memory archives, multi-scale phase-locking, boundary convexity, and homothetic co-evolution (\(O_3, O_5, O_7, O_\Omega\)).

docs.title: 2.2 Protocol for Modifying the Aperture Basis Set
docs.text: When substituting apertures or extending the tier system to a new disciplinary focus or evolutionary iteration, synthetic active states should follow three rules: 1. Preserve Span Across Scales: Any modified basis set must retain coverage across abiotic physics, living ecology, embodied interiority, and relational/symbolic expression so that Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) is exercised across both material and informational substrates. 2. Document Basis Substitutions Explicitly: When substituting or adding an aperture, explicitly state which functional slot(s) and tensor coordinates (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\)) the new aperture spans. 3. Follow the Native Topology Inside Each Aperture: Within any individual aperture, never force the exposition into a mechanical checklist if the domain's native logic is organized around dual feedback cycles, a grammatical paradigm, or a specific boundary layer. Let the discipline's authentic structure lead the prose while mapping its operators rigorously onto \(\mathcal{T}\).

docs.title: 2.3 Per-Aperture Declarations and Coordinate Coverage
docs.text:
Coverage. Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) (r7) has two asymptotic branches.

  • Branch I (\(H_0 > 0\)) is the unbounded homothetic horizon, verified by the r10 §5.1–§5.12 witnesses.
  • Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)) is a bounded non-equilibrium steady state, verified by the r10 §5.13 witness.

The apertures fall into three groups:

  • Tier 1 apertures are ontological and grammatical homologies. They map onto all nine coordinates \(O_0 o O_\Omega\), in either branch, as conceptual correspondences. They declare no empirical domain and make no empirical claim.
  • Twelve empirical apertures in Tiers 2–5 (all except 4.3, 5.2, 5.3, and 5.4) instantiate all nine coordinates on their declared domains and declare Branch II. Bounded physical, ecological, and somatic systems settle toward a non-equilibrium steady state under sustained throughput; they do not expand without bound. Finite windows test that state only through the tests of §5.5. Statements that hold in Branch I only (r10 Decision 6) are never applied to these apertures.
  • Four apertures (4.3, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4) are provisionally homological in this epoch. Their systems are quasi-static (bioelectric potentials in conducting media), inertial (airflow in phonation), or advective (goal-directed movement). r7's storage–diffusion balance law cannot represent these systems literally. These apertures map all nine coordinates as conceptual correspondences, like Tier 1, and make no empirical claim until a future spine epoch provides the needed forms. A homological aperture may read its correspondences against one branch form, with a stated reason; it then declares no branch in the sense of closure (v), because nothing is evaluated.

Declarations. Every empirical aperture declares the following in its §1 Scope block and in the master table below. Each declaration must satisfy every requirement r7 places on it.

  1. Domain \(\mathcal{M}\) and boundary \(\partial\mathcal{M}\): the system's own region, compact and connected, of dimension \(n = 3\), with smooth boundary. It is \( au\)-independent within a declared observation window, so growing systems declare a window in which the domain can be treated as fixed. Supply must cross \(\partial\mathcal{M}\): r7 admits interior sinks but no interior sources. The cover \(\{\mathcal{U}_i\}\) of \(O_5\), the Neumann Laplacian of \(O_4\), the overlaps of \(O_6\), and the boundary flux of \(O_1\) are all defined on \(\mathcal{M}\).
  2. Metric \(g_{\mu u}\):
  3. Flat by default. The physical metric of a region of Euclidean space is flat, so by default \(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\). Then \(T^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\), \( abla\cdot\xi = 0\) (with \(n = 3\)), \(\xi\) is a Killing field, and the \( au\)-compatibility equation reduces to \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma]_{\mu u} = rac{n-2}{n}( abla_\mu abla_ u heta - g_{\mu u} abla^2 heta)\) (so \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma] = 0\) wherever \( heta\) is spatially uniform), which is the Saint-Venant compatibility that real strain rates satisfy. The stress sector is then trivial or Killing.
  4. Curvature requires a declared material metric. \(G_{\mu u} eq 0\) is admitted only where the aperture declares and justifies a non-Euclidean material metric. An incompatible-growth metric in morphoelasticity is the standard example.
  5. Cone speed. Speeds carry units, so each aperture declares a cone speed \(c_*\), with \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2 < 1\). All tracer speeds must satisfy \(\ll c_*\), so that \(f_{\mathrm{drive}} \approx a_{\mathrm{d}}\).
  6. Free energy \(\mathcal{F}\):
  7. \(\mathcal{F}\) is a named energy per unit volume, with \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) on \(\mathcal{M}\), and it has a non-negligible storage term: its relaxation time to a change in boundary data (\(\ell^2/D\) for domain size \(\ell\) and diffusivity \(D\)) is finite and resolvable. \(\mathcal{F}\) may be steady within a window, as a Branch II state approaches steady state.
  8. It obeys the r7 \(O_4\) balance law \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), with \(J_W^\alpha = -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\).
  9. Quasi-static fields, which follow their boundary data instantly, are not admissible.
  10. \(\mathcal{F}\) is declared in a form linear in the diffusing quantity (for example concentration times a declared constant yield, or a linearized energy density above a datum).
  11. \(\mathcal{F}\) carries a declared absolute datum \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}}\), with \(\mathcal{F} \ge \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}}\) throughout \(\mathcal{M}\). Every first-order sink is \(k(\mathcal{F} - \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}}) \ge 0\).
  12. Transport tensor \(\mathfrak{K}\): the default \(D_{\mathcal{F}}g^{\alpha eta}\), or a declared parametric anisotropic tensor. Any conversion factor needed to express a measured flux as a free-energy flux (for example \( ho g\), a specific storage, or a reaction free-energy yield) is a declared parameter.
  13. Interior sink \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\): the default \(0\), or a declared consumption law (for example first-order relative to the datum, or Michaelis–Menten). It must be continuous: a sharp reaction front is represented as a smooth sink zone.
  14. Drive acceleration \(a_{\mathrm{d}}\): the default \(0\) (force-free tracers), or a declared law for forced or purposeful trajectories, entering through the cone-preserving drive of r7 \(O_2\) Eq. [3].
  15. Branch II evidence (closure (v)): a pre-declared estimator and acceptance criterion for three quantities:
  16. the trend of \(\langle heta angle\);
  17. a bound on \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\);
  18. an estimate of \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\), from measured dissipation and not from \(\mathfrak{K} abla\mathcal{F}\).

This evidence is obtained independently of the \(O_1\) test.

Binding constitutive closure (r7 \(O_4\)). Every non-default \(\mathfrak{K}\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), or \(a_{\mathrm{d}}\) must satisfy four conditions:

  • (i) it is a named law with its functional form fixed before the test;
  • (ii) it has a finite number of pre-declared parameters, estimated from data independent of the test, meaning a different measurement modality on the test specimen or a declared perturbation regime, not a sister sample and not merely another time window; tabulated or fitted fields are not admissible;
  • (iii) every acceptance tolerance and criterion is fixed in advance;
  • (iv) the default model is fitted for comparison only, and if it fits at least as well, the departure is rejected.

Every evaluation also satisfies (v): the branch is declared in advance and never switched on the same data. In Branch II, \(J_E = J_W/p_0\) is fixed. A term fitted to the data it closes does not satisfy any coordinate in which it appears.

docs.title: 2.4 Future Basis Shells (Roadmap)
docs.text:
\(\mathcal{B}_0\) is a mesoscale terrestrial and embodied core. Later basis sets may add concentric shells of apertures in further regimes, each mapped onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) under the same declarations and closure:

  • horizon-scale and relativistic physics;
  • limit-situation phenomenology;
  • non-ordinary neuro-phenomenological states;
  • reflexive metascience.

Proposals for specific shell apertures and their mappings are kept in a separate planning document outside the conditioning corpus.

docs.title: 3. The Zero-Leakage Holdout Standard
docs.text: To preserve the empirical validity of downstream out-of-distribution testing, all Stage I and Stage II theoretical specifications must enforce strict independence from held-out empirical test contexts across two levels:

docs.title: 3.1 Direct Lexical Independence
docs.text: Specifications must contain zero proper nouns, geographic coordinates, institutional identifiers, regional landmarks, internal application variable names, or biographical narratives associated with any downstream empirical test site or practitioner. Tier 1 traditions and language families are described only at the level of the family and its comparative reconstruction or of the classical tradition, never through subgroups below the family level, local communities, or localized geography.

docs.title: 3.2 Indirect Semantic & Structural-Proxy Independence
docs.text: Removing proper nouns is necessary but not sufficient. If a theoretical specification illustrates its principles using hyper-specific scenarios that mirror a held-out test set, it introduces structural-proxy leakage. * The Universal Formulation Rule: All mechanisms, boundary conditions, and illustrative dynamics must be formulated in universal, textbook-general terms derived strictly from the first principles of the discipline under consideration. * Prohibition of Cross-Tier Motif Clusters: Specifications must never repeat a signature cluster of site-specific motifs across multiple tiers, and conditioning documents must never enumerate held-out site features, concretely or by category, where they could function as a positive descriptor of \(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{test}}\). The categories auditors use for this check are maintained in a withheld auditor-only annex (annex_a_auditor_motif_hygiene.md) and are not reproduced in the conditioning corpus. * Population-Level Formulation: Somatic, contemplative, and expressive dynamics are described at the level of populations or cohorts, with example modalities rotated across apertures, never through a single recurring practitioner profile. * During Iteration: Auditing instances must actively scan for and generalize any phrasing that over-constrains a universal law to a narrow, idiosyncratic scenario that would bias blind empirical evaluation.

docs.title: 4. Core Principles of Epistemological Orthogonality (\(\perp\))
4.1 Orthogonality vs. Reductive Syncretism
docs.text: In an inner-product or Hilbert space, two non-zero subspaces \(\mathcal{E}_A\) and \(\mathcal{E}_B\) are orthogonal (\(\mathcal{E}_A \perp \mathcal{E}_B\)) when their inner product vanishes (\(\langle u, v \rangle = 0\) for all \(u \in \mathcal{E}_A, \; v \in \mathcal{E}_B\)), so that the orthogonal projection of one subspace directly onto the other is identically zero. * Non-Reduction of Ontologies: Never assert a reductive identity between a domain's native concepts and a differential-geometric object (avoiding reductive identity claims between domain concepts and geometric operators). Scientific, linguistic, and contemplative traditions carry irreducible historical, contextual, and phenomenological hysteresis that cannot be collapsed into differential equations; conversely, differential geometry carries strict requirements of dimensional homogeneity, index valence, and falsifiability that cannot be replaced by metaphor. * Functorial Correspondence Across Relational Operators: Correspondence between orthogonal domains \(\mathcal{E}_A\) and \(\mathcal{E}_B\) is established through a structure-preserving homomorphism (functor) mediated by Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) (\(\mathcal{E}_A \leftrightarrow \mathcal{T} \leftrightarrow \mathcal{E}_B\)). Each orthogonal aperture is a candidate formalization of a distinct discipline or tradition, hypothesized under \(H_1\) (empirical_validation_protocol.md §1.2) to have independently developed operational calculi that map via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to six structural problems of open, non-equilibrium systems: 1. Throughput & Emergent Time (\(O_0, O_1\)): Absorbing continuous exogenous flux and sustaining positive entropy production without collapsing into static equilibrium. 2. Constraint Stiffness, Volume Insulation & Hysteresis (\(O_2, O_3\)): Navigating extrinsic curvature while algebraically isolating the volume element from anisotropic shear and consolidating transduced variance into structural memory. 3. Selective Boundary Gating & Stress Conservation (\(O_4\)): Filtering high-spatial-wavenumber ambient noise into low-eigenvalue spatial modes while conserving load-bearing boundary stress. 4. Non-Annexing Coalescence (\(O_5\)): Fusing distinct subsystems across shared overlap zones via the Riemannian geometric mean into a contiguous macroscopic medium without erasing local metrics, supporting lossless circulation around closed spatial cycles. 5. Asymmetric Coupling & Mutual Information (\(O_6\)): Pairing directional phase-lead asymmetry and trace-free stretching/folding under explicit non-degeneracy and flux-positivity hypotheses across a geodesically convex interface. 6. Impedance Relaxation & Homothetic Stationarity (\(O_7, O_\Omega\)): Relaxing spatial impedance gradients via a gauge connection and settling of form (\(\partial_\tau\tilde{g}_{\mu\nu} \to 0\)). In the \(\tau \to \infty\) limit (\(O_\Omega\)), empirical apertures approach the Branch II steady state (bounded volume, sustained throughput), and Tier 1 homologies may map either branch (§2.3).

docs.title: 4.2 Strict Lexicon Isolation
docs.text: Each aperture specification must preserve the integrity of its native technical or traditional vocabulary. Do not blend terminology from unrelated cultural traditions or adjacent tiers within a single aperture (for example, never import terminology from a Tier 1 metaphysical ontology into a Tier 5 poetics or systems aperture, and never import civil-engineering terminology into pure continuum fluid dynamics), and do not re-introduce retired or unverified metaphors (such as calling agents or organisms "solitons") that lack an explicit operator definition in r7 or r10.

docs.title: 5. Mathematical & Notational Alignment Checklist (r7 & r10 Standard)
docs.text:
Both during initial generation and during iterative technical audits, every mathematical expression referencing Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) must be verified against the locked conventions of foundational-manifold-2026-10-20-r7.json and foundational-manifold-companion-2026-10-20-r10.md:

  1. Spacetime Foliation & Normal Expansion (\(O_0, O_1\)):
  2. Use the \((n+1)\)-dimensional Lorentzian foliation \(ds^2 = -N^2 d au^2 + g_{\mu u}(dx^\mu + eta^\mu d au)(dx^ u + eta^ u d au)\) on a compact, connected manifold \(\mathcal{M}\) (\(\dim\mathcal{M} = n \ge 3\)) with smooth boundary \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) in synchronous normal gauge (\(N = 1, \; eta^\mu = 0\)).
  3. Write the normal extrinsic expansion scalar as \( heta \equiv -N K \overset{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0}{=} rac{1}{2}g^{\mu u}\partial_ au g_{\mu u} = rac{1}{\sqrt{\vert g\vert}}\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g\vert} = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\) (\(> 0\) in Branch I), and the throughput rate as \(\Theta_E \equiv \dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}/s_0\), with \(s_0\) the \(O_\Omega\) Eq. [0] constant; \(\Theta_E > 0\) follows from the \(O_1\) sign condition. Never write \( heta = abla_\mu J_E^\mu\): in Branch II, \( abla_\mu J_E^\mu eq heta\).
  4. Use \(d\Sigma_\mu \equiv \hat{n}_\mu dA\) (outward unit normal \(\hat{n}_\mu\)) for directed boundary area elements so they never collide with the gauge connection \(A_\mu\), and avoid overloading reserved spine symbols (\(G_\infty\), \(\Psi\), \(\lambda\)).
  5. Write scalar free-energy density as \(\mathcal{F} \in C^2(\mathcal{M})\) (an energy per unit volume, never a potential in other units such as a voltage), inverse temperature as \( eta_{\mathrm{th}} > 0\), reference pressure as \(p_0 \equiv ( eta_{\mathrm{th}}v_0)^{-1}\), expansion work as \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} = p_0\oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\) (\(> 0\) in Branch I), dissipative power as \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} = \int_{\mathcal{M}}(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F})\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx > 0\), total power \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} + \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\), and entropy production in full constitutive form as \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}} J_E^\mu abla_\mu \mathcal{F} > 0\).
  6. \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = \int_{\mathcal{M}}\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\) is the physical volume of the declared domain under its physical metric. In Branch II it converges to a finite \(V_\infty\) (\(\int\langle heta angle\,d au < \infty\)), and openness is carried by \(\Theta_E > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\), not by expansion.

  7. Currents. In Branch I, \(J_E^\mu \equiv J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \equiv J_{\mathrm{ambient}}^\mu\vert_{\mathcal{M}}\), as in r6. In Branch II, \(J_E^\mu \equiv J_W^\mu/p_0 = -p_0^{-1}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\) is fixed and admits no alternative, so \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\) holds identically wherever \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\). The empirical content of \(O_1\) in Branch II is therefore the flux-prediction test of the binding closure (§2.3): the declared parametric \(\mathfrak{K}\), with parameters estimated per closure (ii), predicts an independently measured flux \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}}\), with \( abla\mathcal{F}\) also obtained independently, within a pre-declared tolerance. Never map an inward supply current to \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\), and never let a cyclically varying volume stand for \( heta\).

  8. Extrinsic Geometry, Weyl Factorization, Geodesics & Shear Damping (\(O_2, O_3\)):

  9. Credit the unimodular Weyl factorization \(g_{\mu u}( au, \mathbf{x}) = \Omega^2( au, \mathbf{x})\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\Omega > 0\), \(\det\hat{g} = 1\) in the fixed reference chart, \(\mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) = 0 \implies \det g = \Omega^{2n}\)) with algebraically isolating the volume element from anisotropic shear (\(\hat{h}\)). Never claim that this change of variables dynamically decouples \( heta\) from environmental precision stiffness: in every \(O_2\) block, explicitly state and display the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation (r10 Decision 2): $\( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\)$ which couples \( heta\) to the precision-weighted control 1-form \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) (via \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\)) and to the shear tensor \(\sigma_{\alpha eta}\).
  10. Whenever citing the \(O_2\) Eq. [3] trajectory equation for coordinate velocity \(v^\mu = dx^\mu/d au\), write it in its complete r7 form, with the cone-preserving drive: $\(\left.\left( rac{d v^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}, \quad f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2)\left(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu ight), \quad u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2 < 1\)$ With the default \(a_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\) this is the r6 geodesic equation, which governs force-free timelike tracers. Forced or purposeful trajectories (drag and gravity on grains, taxis in foraging, controlled balance or articulation, movement toward goals) use a non-zero drive acceleration \(a_{\mathrm{d}}\) declared under the binding closure: a named law with a finite number of pre-declared parameters estimated independently of the trajectories it predicts. The equation never describes static curves (principal-stress lines, grain or fibre lines, catenaries and other equilibrium shapes), and null rays are not timelike.
  11. Write the shear evolution law in mixed \((1,1)\) form: \( abla_ au \sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv \partial_ au \sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma \sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) (\(\gamma_\sigma = \mathrm{const} > 0\), \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\mu} = 0\)), driving \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\) (where in the r10 §5.8/§5.11 witness, the shear rate \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) decays exponentially while the integrated deformation amplitude \(a( au) = (2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma)(1 - e^{-\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)})\) increases monotonically from \(0\) to \(a_\infty\)) and anchoring the explicitly indexed asymptotic unit-determinant reference metric \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)).

  12. When discussing systems with non-zero boundary stress (\(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} ot\equiv 0\)) and a strongly convex hysteresis basin (\( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H} \succ 0\)), never universalize the specific r10 §5.11 witness profile \(w(z) = z^{1/\sqrt{2}}\) or \(\mathcal{H}_0(z)\) as a physical law. State only that, where an aperture declares a justified non-Euclidean material metric (§2.3), its stratified profiles are candidate realizations of a configuration with \(G_{\mu u} ot\equiv 0\) and \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H} \succ 0\), and that the r10 §5.11 warped-product witness demonstrates that such configurations exist (r10 §5.7: "The model establishes consistency of the hypothesis set, not genericity").

  13. Spectral Gating & Boundary Stress Conservation (\(O_4\)):

  14. Use the spatial spectral low-pass projector \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\) onto Neumann eigenmodes of the spatial Laplace–Beltrami operator \(- abla^2\) on \(L^2(\mathcal{M}, d\mathrm{vol}_g)\) acting on the positive trace-class state \( ho_{\mathrm{total}}( au)\) to define \( ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\) and the global spectrally gated density \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au) = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0\), with dimensionless surprisal \(q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv -\ln(v_0 Q(\mathbf{x}, au))\) and variational power \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\). Do not conflate the spatial cutoff \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}\) directly with temporal frequency (Hz) or electromagnetic wavelength, do not apply the r10 §5.4/§5.10 witness mode labels \(\phi_0\) and \(\phi_1\) generically outside witness discussions, and do not conflate the global \(O_4\) density \(Q\) with the \(O_6\) subsystem marginals \(Q_i\).
  15. Physical wavenumbers and gate drift: the gate acts on Neumann eigenmodes of \(- abla^2_g\) on the declared domain with its physical metric \(g\). Its eigenvalues change only as \(g\) changes; in Branch II, \(g o G_\infty\), so the spectrum converges and drift vanishes asymptotically. Within a finite window the drift is bounded by the change in \(g\) and must be stated as negligible when \(g\) changes by a small fraction. In Branch I's homothetic regime the comoving reference is \( ar{g}_{\mu u} \equiv e^{-2H_0 au}g_{\mu u}\) (r10 Decision 3).
  16. Note that \( abla_\mu q = - abla_\mu\ln Q o 0\) requires \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au)\) to be spatially uniform across \(\mathcal{M}\) (\( abla_\mu Q o 0\)), not merely \(Q = P\).

  17. Pair the Einstein-type (trace-adjusted) stress tensor \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = abla_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)} - rac{1}{2}g_{\mu u} abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\) with the elliptic conservation equivalence \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\).

  18. Topological Coalescence, Relational Edge & Geodesic Convexity (\(O_5, O_6\)):

  19. Distinguish the candidate geometric overlap graph \(\mathcal{K}_0 \equiv \{\langle i,j angle : i eq j, \; \mathcal{U}_{ij} \equiv \mathcal{U}_i \cap \mathcal{U}_j eq \emptyset\}\) (over which the \( au\)-independent partition of unity \(\sum_i \psi_i + \sum_{\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}_0}\psi_{ij} = 1\) glues \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)}\) and the Riemannian geometric mean \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} = (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\) into \(g_{\mu u} \equiv g_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{macro}}\)) from the actively coupled subgraph \(\mathcal{K} \equiv \{\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}_0 : \eta_{[i o j]}^\lambda ot\equiv 0\}\), which defines the percolation fraction \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) \equiv \vert\mathcal{K}\vert / \vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c \in (0,1)\). \(\mathcal{K}_0\) is fixed by the geometric overlaps of the \( au\)-independent cover: coupling never adds edges to \(\mathcal{K}_0\), it only determines which edges of \(\mathcal{K}_0\) belong to \(\mathcal{K}\). The asymptotic hypothesis of r7 \(O_5\) Eq. [4] (\(e^{-2H_0 au}g^{(i)}_{\mu u} o G^{(i)}_{\infty,\mu u} \succ 0\)) holds for common \(H_0 \ge 0\); empirical (Branch II) apertures state it with \(H_0 = 0\) (\(g^{(i)} o G^{(i)}_\infty\)), and the \(O_6\) Eq. [4] limit \(c_{ij}\) follows (§2.3).
  20. Note that the precision-symmetrized phase-lead 1-form \((J_{[i o j]})_ u \equiv rac{1}{2}(\hat{\Pi}_{ u\lambda}^{(i)} + \hat{\Pi}_{ u\lambda}^{(j)})\eta_{[i o j]}^\lambda = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\) is odd under \(i \leftrightarrow j\) (encoding directional phase-lead sign), while it enters \(M_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\) and \(S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\) via its even outer product. State explicitly that \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) is an independent standing hypothesis under which \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = \sum_{a=1}^n m_a = 0\) implies opposite-sign extreme eigenvalues \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\) (with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general for \(n \ge 3\)), and that positive mutual-information growth \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u dA > 0\) for \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\) is likewise an explicit standing hypothesis in r7 \(O_6\) (which, in the spatially constant coupling witness of r10 §5.5 and §5.7, requires suitable non-spherical overlap geometry and orientation).
  21. The quadratic bracket \(F_{\mu\alpha}^{(i o j)}F_ u^{(j o i)\alpha}\) in \(S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\) is non-zero only where both curvatures \(F^{(i o j)} = dJ_{i o j}\) and \(F^{(j o i)} = dJ_{j o i}\) are non-zero. Non-zero partner fields \(\eta_{i o j}^\lambda\) and \(\eta_{j o i}^\lambda\) do not guarantee this: in the r10 §5.5 and §5.11 witnesses the fields are non-zero and \(F = 0\). Fully symmetric reciprocity (\(\eta_{i o j}^\lambda = \eta_{j o i}^\lambda\)) gives \(\eta_{[i o j]}^\lambda \equiv 0\) and removes the pair from \(\mathcal{K}\).
  22. All r10 numerical results hold only for the tested configurations and parameter ranges. For example, positivity and growth of the normalized flux \(C(a)\) in §5.12 were found for the tested ellipsoids over \(a \in [0, 8]\); never extend such results to all \(a\) or to general overlaps.

  23. In the r10 §5.11–§5.12 witness, convexity of the chosen coordinate ellipsoid \(E\) for all \( au\) requires \(a_\infty = 2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma < a_c(E)\), with \(a_c\) estimated numerically. This is a design constraint on \(E\) in that construction, not a universal law. When a domain threshold is discussed in an aperture, label it explicitly as an aperture-level empirical conjecture mapped to the witness criterion.

  24. Macroscopic Coherence & Homothetic Closure (\(O_7, O_\Omega\)):

  25. Use the \(C^2\), kink-free anisotropy index \(\chi( au, \mathbf{x}) \equiv rac{n\,\mathrm{Tr}(\mathcal{D}^2)}{(\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathcal{D})^2} = 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2} \ge 1\) (\(\chi o 1\)), the non-Abelian adjoint covariant derivative \(D_\mu \hat{\chi} = \hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\) (\(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\)), and the type-\((1,1)\) density endomorphisms \((\hat{ ho}_g)^\mu_{\; u}\) and \((\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}})^\mu_{\; u}\) constructed with the inverse asymptotic reference metric \(\hat{g}_\infty^{\mu\alpha}\). In Branch II, where \( heta o 0\) and \(\chi\) is undefined, use \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}/( heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2)\) (r7 \(O_7\) Eq. [5]), which is not \(n\,\mathrm{Tr}(\mathcal{D}^2)/(\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathcal{D})^2\), and \(\hat{\chi} = \chi_E\hat{u}\).
  26. \(\chi\) measures the anisotropy of the global deformation \(\mathcal{D}\) (r10 Decision 5): \(\chi o 1\) means the deformation becomes isotropic as shear decays. It carries no phase, synchronization, or coherence content; attribute any synchronization claim to gauge transport (\(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1} o 0\)), not to \(\chi\).
  27. \(O_\Omega\) has two branches (r7 \(O_\Omega\) Eq. [0]–[2]). Branch I (\(H_0 > 0\)) is the unbounded homothetic horizon: \( heta o nH_0 > 0\), \(V_{\mathcal{M}} \sim e^{nH_0 au}\), \(\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}\Psi = 0\). Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)) is a bounded non-equilibrium steady state: \( heta o 0\) with \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au < \infty\), \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\), \(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\), \(\sigma o 0\), \(\partial_ au g o 0\), \(\mathcal{I} o s_0V_\infty\), and, with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly, \(\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}\Psi o 0 \iff J_E\cdot abla q o 0\). In Branch II each coupling pair's \(O_6\) boundary flux must be integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\), so sustained, non-decaying coupling is never asserted for a Branch II aperture. Neither branch is static equilibrium or a periodic return: open throughput (\(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} > 0\)) persists in both. Statements that hold in Branch I only (listed in r10 Decision 6) are never applied to a Branch II aperture.
  28. Finite observation windows: no finite window \( au \in [ au_0, au_{\mathrm{obs}}]\) exhibits a \( au o \infty\) limit. Empirical claims at \(O_3\)–\(O_\Omega\) are within-window rate, residual, and sign tests: (1) exponential decay of \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) at constant \(\gamma_\sigma > 0\); (2) decay of \(\chi_E - 1\) at rate \(2\gamma_\sigma\) wherever \( heta \approx 0\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle\) is approximately constant across the window; (3) \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u}\) and \(\partial_ au ilde{g}_{\mu u}\) residuals decaying at the predicted rate; (4) non-degeneracy \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), with \(\sum_a m_a = 0\) as an estimator check computed with the same metric (never \(m_+ + m_- = 0\)); (5) the signs of \(\Theta_E > 0\), \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} > 0\), and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} > 0\) (the magnitude of \(\Theta_E\) depends on \(s_0\), which no finite window fixes, so only signs and \(s_0\)-independent rates are tested); (6) the \(O_1\)/\(O_4\) flux-prediction test of the closure; and (7) the pre-declared Branch II evidence of closure (v): the trend of \(\langle heta angle\), a bound on \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\), and an estimate of \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\).

docs.title: 6. Protocol for Iterative Auditing and Shear Elimination
docs.text:
When a synthetic active state is tasked with reviewing or iterating upon an existing set of aperture specifications, it must execute a structured four-axis diagnostic audit before approving or modifying the text:

  1. Axis I — Mathematical & Indexical Audit:
  2. Verify that every equation, tensor index, contraction, sign convention, standing hypothesis, and regularity class matches r7 and r10 exactly (including the traced elliptic \(\theta\)-equation and complete r7 trajectory equation with its cone-preserving drive in \(O_2\), explicit tensor indices on \((\hat{g}_\infty)_{\mu\nu}\) in \(O_3\), spatial low-pass projector \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}}\) and global \(Q\) vs. marginal \(Q_i\) distinction in \(O_4\) vs. \(O_6\), explicit hypothesis labels on \(M^{(ij)} \neq 0\) and \(\frac{d\mathcal{I}}{d\tau} > 0\) in \(O_6\), strict non-universalization of r10 §5.10–§5.12 witness constructions and numerical ranges, \(O_1\) sign checks against the domain's physical transport direction, and consistency of each aperture's §2.3 declarations at every coordinate).
  3. Axis II — Thermodynamic & Dynamical Audit:
  4. Verify that openness is preserved at every coordinate (\(\Theta_E > 0\), \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} > 0\), \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} > 0\); \(\theta > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} > 0\) in Branch I only), that each aperture declares its branch before any test (closure (v)) and never relies on a statement of the other branch, that every non-default drive, transport tensor, or sink is declared under the binding closure (named law, finite pre-declared parameters, independent estimation, pre-declared tolerances, default comparison), that no quantity mapped to \(\theta\) oscillates in sign, that monotone relaxation is never conflated with periodic oscillation, and that finite-window claims are rate, residual, sign, or flux-prediction tests (§5.5).
  5. Axis III — Epistemological & Lexical Audit:
  6. Verify that the domain's native conceptual architecture is represented accurately according to primary scholarship in that discipline, using functorial correspondence language ("mapped via Spine \mathcal{T} to") without reductive identities or cross-aperture lexical mixing, and that no conditioning document asserts as fact a hypothesis that empirical_validation_protocol.md is designed to test.
  7. Axis IV — Holdout & Leakage Audit:
  8. Scan the text for any direct proper-noun leakage, regional linguistic signaling, or indirect structural-proxy motifs that could telegraph a held-out test site (using the categories in the withheld annex_a_auditor_motif_hygiene.md), replacing any suspect passages with universally portable formulations.

docs.title: Experimental Architecture: Multi-Model Consensus, Basis Portability & Out-of-Distribution Empirical Validation
docs.text: Document ID: empirical_validation_protocol.md Companion Reference: foundational-manifold-2026-10-20-r7.json, foundational-manifold-companion-2026-10-20-r10.md, and aperture_generation_guidance.md

docs.title: 0. Scope, Framing, and Expectations
docs.text:
What this protocol is. A framework for testing one hypothesis, \(H_1\) (§1.2): that diverse disciplines and traditions independently formalized operational calculi that map through Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the same structural problems of open systems. It also gives initial descriptions of empirical methods that later studies may adopt, refine, or replace.

Three kinds of claim. * (A) Verified: the internal consistency of Spine \(\mathcal{T}\), established only to the extent of the witnesses and checks in foundational-manifold-companion-2026-10-20-r10.md §5. * (B) Testable hypotheses: \(H_1\), the Stage II–III convergence predictions, and the Stage IV sensor predictions. Each remains a hypothesis until tested as described here, and the mappings in the aperture tiers are hypotheses under \(H_1\). * (C) Not claimed: anything about consciousness, its evolution or trajectory, or what the framework brings about. Nothing in this protocol or the corpus asserts such claims, and no result described here would establish them.

Site independence. The framework does not depend on any particular site or research program. Any site that meets the requirements of the relevant stage may serve as a test site, and sites may be chosen or replaced over time. Studies at a site are of two kinds: * Confirmatory studies use the pre-registered, blinded procedures of Stages III–IV, including holdout protection. * Exploratory studies are descriptive and hypothesis-generating. They may be open, local, and practice-centred, but their results are not cited as confirmation of \(H_1\) or of any spine prediction. An exploratory study that uses the framework at a site makes that site permanently ineligible for confirmatory use (Part 2 below).

Eligibility for confirmatory testing: two-part site assessment. Blindness to a site is a matter of degree, not a yes-or-no property. Every site considered for confirmatory use as the Stage III held-out site \(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{test}}\) is assessed in two parts, evaluator exposure (Part 1) and framework exposure (Part 2), and is eligible only if it passes both.

Sequence. (0) The full audit package (§4) has passed Stage II at the pinned versions and is frozen; its hash is recorded in the sealed assessment. (i) Before any data are collected: Part 2 and Part 1 item 1. (ii) A candidate package is compiled. (iii) Part 1 items 2 and 3 are run on the candidate package. (iv) If the site passes, the package is frozen as \(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\), and Part 2 is repeated. (v) Part 2 is repeated immediately before evaluation, and Stage III evaluation follows.

Lock. From step (0) until evaluation is complete, the audit package is not revised. A repeated Stage II (Stage III item 2) consists of the two consecutive zero-context audits of Stage II item 1, for the replacement family only, on the frozen package, and may only confirm that package. If the repeated audits do not pass, the replacement version is not used, unless the package is revised. Any revision of the package voids the assessment, and the sequence restarts at step (0). Benchmarks A–C are not a gate: after a replacement, their agreement is recomputed from the replacement family's new results together with the existing results of the other two families, and reported.

Sealing. From the moment a site is first considered for confirmatory use, its identity is sealed from everyone who authors or revises the audit package. Site selection, the probes of Part 1, and custody of the sealed record are carried out by people who are not authors of the audit package. Everyone who knows a candidate site's identity is recorded in the sealed assessment.

Record. The full assessment, its threshold and scoring scale, and its log are pre-registered sealed (for example as a timestamped hash, or in an embargoed registry) and kept outside the conditioning corpus. Before evaluation is complete, only a summary that does not identify the site is published (see Data ethics below).

  • Part 1, evaluator exposure: what each evaluating model, at the exact version pinned for Stage III (Stage III item 2), could know or infer about the site.
  • Training cutoff. Each model's stated cutoff is compared with the date of the first public record that links the site to the framework. Stated cutoffs are treated as approximate, because later material can enter a model through further training. A model is classed as exposed if that record is dated before its stated cutoff, or within a margin after it declared in the sealed assessment. An exposed model must meet a stricter identification threshold in item 2, also declared in the sealed assessment. Records that link the site to the study are not made public before evaluation is complete (Data ethics).
  • Identification probes. The candidate package is tested in separate probe sessions at the same pinned versions, both unconditioned and conditioned on the conditioning corpus, which are asked to identify the site. Responses are scored on a scale declared in the sealed assessment, which counts identification coarser than exact identification as well as exact identification. Provider settings that do not retain submitted data are used where available. Probe sessions are discarded and never become evaluating sessions.
  • De-identification. Measures that reduce identifiability (for example cropping, resampling, removal of metadata) are declared in the sealed assessment, are identical for every model and every arm of §3.1, and are stated with their residual risk and their effect on the information the Stage III coordinates require. Measures chosen for a particular site appear only in the sealed assessment, never in this protocol.

The site passes Part 1 only if, for every evaluating model, identification is below the pre-declared threshold that applies to it (item 1). Otherwise the site is ineligible. No model is replaced or dropped after the probes, except the replacement of a retired version under Stage III item 2; if the replacement does not pass Part 1, the site is ineligible. Residual evaluator exposure is reported with the results. * Part 2, framework exposure: whether the site has shaped, or been shaped by, the framework. A site is exposed, and ineligible, if its design, operation, or exploratory record has used the framework's vocabulary or methods, or if it informed the selection or specification of the spine, of any aperture, or of any other document of the audit package (§4), in this or any earlier revision. Stage III convergence on such a site would be circular, and no property of the evaluating models (Part 1) removes this exposure. To make this checkable, everyone who authors or selects material for the audit package, including model sessions whose inputs are logged, makes a dated declaration of the sites that informed it. For revisions made before this rule, the known human authors make retrospective declarations, checked against the program's records. The rule covers every revision of every document of the audit package. Where provenance cannot be established, the site is treated as exposed, except that for model sessions whose inputs were not logged, a site counts as exposed only if it was named or described in the program's records, communications, or logged sessions dated before the document concerned; the custodian determines this from those records. The provenance declarations are kept in the sealed record, outside the audit package; they are never shown to any model session, and a named human custodian checks them.

Scope. The assessment applies to the Stage III held-out site. Where Stage IV tests Stage III predictions against sensor streams from that site, those streams are withheld until Stage III evaluation is complete. Stage IV tests on other systems follow the designs of the withheld procedures annex. Exposure under both parts is declared and logged, in the sealed record, for every site considered for confirmatory use.

Use before verification. The framework may be used as a working language for design, practice, and coordination before or without empirical confirmation. Such use is legitimate in its own terms but is not evidence for \(H_1\), and it is described without claims beyond kind (B) above.

Data ethics. Data involving people are collected only with informed consent and appropriate ethical review. Data are de-identified before any publication. Nothing that could identify a blinded test site is published before its evaluation is complete.

docs.title: 1. Architectural Premise & Formal Hypotheses
1.1 Separation of the Invariant Spine (\(\mathcal{T}\)) from Evolvable Aperture Basis Sets (\(\{\mathcal{E}_{k,m}\}\))
docs.text:
To prevent category conflation between universal mathematical laws and domain-specific interpretive lenses, the experimental architecture distinguishes two formal layers: 1. The Immutable Mathematical Spine (\(\mathcal{T}\)): The 39 equation blocks across coordinates \(O_0 \to O_\Omega\) locked in foundational-manifold-2026-10-20-r7.json and established as jointly satisfiable in foundational-manifold-companion-2026-10-20-r10.md (with exact symbolic verification of all closed-form PDE/algebraic sectors and numerical verification of overlap flux and second-fundamental-form convexity in e2e_5_11.py, flux.py, and convex.py, subject to the explicit non-closed-form caveats for the curved-domain Neumann mode \(\phi_1\), the Rosenblatt copula maps, rim rounding, and the scale argument for geodesic uniqueness recorded in r10 §5.11–§5.12). Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) is the invariant candidate mediating structure under empirical test. 2. Evolvable Orthogonal Aperture Basis Sets (\(\mathcal{B} = \{\mathcal{E}_{k,m}\}\)): A structured collection of epistemological, physical, biological, somatic, and expressive specifications (instantiated in the current reference corpus as a symmetric \(5 \times 4 = 20\) basis \(\mathcal{B}_0\) across five scale tiers \(k \in \{1,\dots,5\}\) and four functional homology slots \(m \in \{1,\dots,4\}\)). The design assumes, and Benchmark A measures rather than presupposes, that the native surface lexicons \(\mathcal{L}_{k,m}\) and \(\mathcal{L}_{k',m'}\) of distinct apertures have low unmediated pairwise overlap, quantified by a lexical-overlap score \(\ell_{\mathrm{lex}}(\mathcal{L}_{k,m}, \mathcal{L}_{k',m'}) \in [0,1]\) computed on spine-free primary-source text (the symbol \(\mathcal{I}\) is reserved for the r7 mutual information).

While Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) remains fixed within an epoch, the aperture basis \(\mathcal{B}\) is substitutable: any slot may be re-instantiated with another discipline or tradition that addresses the same structural problem (\(\mathcal{B}_0 \to \mathcal{B}'\)), changing the surface projection coordinates while, under \(H_1\), preserving the operator homomorphisms into \(\mathcal{T}\).

docs.title: 1.2 Primary Hypothesis (\(H_1\): The Orthogonal Functor & Cross-Substrate Invariance Hypothesis)
docs.text:
\(H_1\) (Latent Dynamical Isomorphism): Diverse scientific disciplines, non-Cartesian philosophical ontologies, process-primacy grammars, and embodied somatic practices independently formalized operational calculi mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the same six structural problems of open, non-equilibrium, boundary-maintaining dynamical systems: across all nine coordinates \(O_0 \to O_\Omega\), with empirical domains declared in Branch II of Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) (a bounded non-equilibrium steady state) and observed on finite windows, and with the Tier 1 ontological grammars and the provisionally homological apertures 4.3, 5.2, 5.3, and 5.4 mapping homologically (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3).

If \(H_1\) holds, conditioning independent foundational model architectures on Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) and a site-blind orthogonal aperture basis \(\mathcal{B}\) makes explicit a structure-preserving functor (\(\mathcal{L}_{k,m} \leftrightarrow \mathcal{T} \leftrightarrow \mathcal{L}_{k',m'}\)). Routing cross-domain translation and multimodal empirical observation through \(\mathcal{T}\) yields: 1. Statistically significant inter-architectural convergence when decomposing held-out multimodal field data \(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\); 2. Invariance of operator assignments under basis substitutions (\(\mathcal{B}_0 \to \mathcal{B}'\)); and 3. Quantitative alignment with external physical, ecological, physiological, and kinematic sensor telemetry from the empirically declared apertures.

docs.title: 1.3 Null Hypothesis (\(H_0\): Post-Hoc Associative Compliance)
docs.text: \(H_0\) (Unconstrained Linguistic Projection): Cross-domain mappings between Spine \(\mathcal{T}\), the aperture basis \(\mathcal{B}\), and empirical observations are artifacts of surface linguistic fluency and post-hoc metaphorical compliance. Under \(H_0\): 1. Independent model architectures audited in zero-context sessions will fail to converge above chance on operator assignments, eigenvalue sign pairings, or stability bounds when presented with held-out multimodal data \(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\); 2. Ablating or scrambling the mathematical constraints in \(\mathcal{T}\) (e.g., replacing r7 with an inconsistent specification that violates conservation laws, unimodular volume-shear isolation, or the branch-appropriate asymptotics at \(O_\Omega\), homothetic stationarity in Branch I or the bounded steady state in Branch II) will produce no measurable degradation in cross-domain coherence or inter-rater convergence; and 3. Quantitative parameter trajectories extracted via \(\mathcal{T}\) will fail to match external physical and biometric sensor measurements.

docs.title: 1.4 Conditioning Corpus and Withheld Annexes
docs.text:
The Stage III conditioning corpus consists of exactly nine documents: foundational-manifold-2026-10-20-r7.json, foundational-manifold-companion-2026-10-20-r10.md, aperture_generation_guidance.md, empirical_validation_protocol.md, and tier_1_ontological_grammars.md through tier_5_expressive_collective_symbiosis.md. Within this corpus, the mappings between apertures and Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) are asserted only as hypotheses under \(H_1\). The spine's verification script, r10_branch2_witness_check.py, accompanies the spine in the audit package and is not part of the conditioning corpus.

Two further documents are withheld from Stage III conditioning and are audited in Stages I and II under the same four axes: * annex_a_auditor_motif_hygiene.md — auditor-only reference for holdout-leakage review; * annex_b_stage_iv_sensor_procedures.md — concrete Stage IV test procedures.

No conditioning document reproduces or paraphrases annex content beyond a pointer to its existence.

docs.title: 2. The Four-Stage Validation Architecture
docs.text: To test \(H_1\) against \(H_0\) without circularity, context decay, or data contamination, the research program is organized into four sequential stages:

docs.title: Stage I — Rotating Peer Audit & Iterative Shear Elimination
docs.text:
1. Locked Mathematical Spine: Maintain strict invariance, within an epoch, of foundational-manifold-2026-10-20-r7.json and foundational-manifold-companion-2026-10-20-r10.md. The Branch I witnesses of r10 §5.1–§5.12 carry the r9 verification (36 checks in e2e_5_11.py, with the caveats of §5.12); the Branch II witness of r10 §5.13 is verified by r10_branch2_witness_check.py (40 exact symbolic checks), which accompanies the spine. 1a. Epochs and pre-registration: the spine may be revised between epochs (\(\mathcal{T}^{(r)} \to \mathcal{T}^{(r+1)}\)) only on the basis of internal mathematical consistency and Stage I/II structural review, never on Stage III or Stage IV holdout or sensor data. Each epoch's spine is frozen and pre-registered before any blind evaluation, and \(H_1\) is tested against that frozen spine. A revised spine is audited on its own (two consecutive clean fresh passes on the spine package) before any aperture is mapped onto it.
  2. Rotating Author–Auditor Audit: An authoring instance (Instance A) revises the twelve-file audit package (the nine-document conditioning corpus of §1.4, both withheld annexes, and the spine's verification script). A fresh, zero-context auditing instance (Instance B) audits the package and returns findings graded High, Medium, or Low. Instance A revises until that Instance B reports zero High and zero Medium findings. Instance B then becomes the authoring instance, and a newly instantiated, zero-context Instance B audits the package. Prior audit reports, revision logs, and deliberations are never supplied to a fresh Instance B.
  3. Four-Axis Diagnostic Iteration: Audits apply the four axes defined in aperture_generation_guidance.md §6:
  4. Axis I (Mathematical & Indexical Fidelity): Exact alignment of every equation, tensor index, contraction, standing hypothesis, and asymptotic limit with r7 and r10, without universalizing witness-specific profiles or numerical ranges (r10 §5.10–§5.12) into general axioms, and with each aperture's declarations (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3) used consistently at every coordinate.
  5. Axis II (Thermodynamic & Dynamical Completeness): Preservation of openness at every coordinate including \(O_\Omega\) (\(\Theta_E > 0\), \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = -\beta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu\nabla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\), \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} > 0\) in both branches; \(\theta > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} > 0\) in Branch I only, with \(\theta \ge 0\), \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} \to 0\) in Branch II), branch declared before every test, pairing of feed-forward stretching (\(m_+ > 0\)) with regulatory damping/folding (\(\gamma_\sigma > 0, \; m_- < 0\) under \(M^{(ij)} \neq 0\)), strict separation of the \(\tau \to \infty\) asymptotics of either branch from periodic cycles, and formulation of finite-window claims as rate, residual, or sign tests.
  6. Axis III (Epistemological Orthogonality & Lexicon Isolation): Absence of reductive syncretism, cross-aperture vocabulary contamination, and circularity between the conditioning corpus and the hypotheses under test.
  7. Axis IV (Zero Direct or Indirect Holdout Leakage): Complete removal of any geographic proper nouns, regional linguistic signaling, biographical context, or cross-tier structural-proxy motifs that could telegraph a held-out empirical test site \(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{test}}\).
  8. Stage I Gate: Stage I is complete when two consecutive, independent, zero-context Instance B audits each report zero High and zero Medium findings on the same package.

docs.title: Stage II — Cross-Architecture Theoretical Consensus & Ablation Benchmarks
docs.text:
1. Multi-Family Adversarial Review: Submit the Stage I consensus corpus to newly instantiated, zero-context sessions across three independent foundational model families: Gemini Argon 4, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Astra, each at an exact version, recorded. Apply the Stage I rotation and gate with each architecture in turn: the package advances when two consecutive, independent, zero-context audits from each architecture report zero High and zero Medium findings.
  2. Controlled Theoretical Benchmarks (Pre-Empirical): Execute three quantitative benchmarks across fresh instances of all three architectures, at the versions recorded under item 1:
  3. Benchmark A (Blind Operator Assignment): Present anonymized phenomenon descriptions alongside anonymized equations from r7, measuring inter-architectural assignment agreement via Fleiss's Kappa (\(\kappa\)). Stimuli are drawn from independent primary-source disciplinary texts (or written by writers blinded to Spine \(\mathcal{T}\)), never from the aperture specifications, and are stripped of all spine-derived vocabulary before presentation. A quantitative lexical-overlap score between each stimulus and each candidate equation's surrounding text is recorded as a control covariate, so that agreement driven by lexical matching can be separated from structural assignment.
  4. Benchmark B (Multi-Hop Functorial Round-Trip): Measure structural and mathematical preservation across multi-hop translations routed through Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) (\(\mathcal{E}_{k,m} \to \mathcal{T} \to \mathcal{E}_{k',m'} \to \mathcal{T} \to \mathcal{E}_{k,m}\)) across both horizontal coordinate progressions (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\)) and vertical slot homologies (\(1.m \leftrightarrow 2.m \leftrightarrow 3.m \leftrightarrow 4.m \leftrightarrow 5.m\)), compared against unmediated translation and translation mediated by an ablated/inconsistent spine \(\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{ablated}}\).
  5. Benchmark C (Bioregional Basis Substitution): Provide the models with aperture_generation_guidance.md and a synthetic profile of a different linguistic/ecological region, testing whether independent architectures generate structurally isomorphic aperture replacements (\(\mathcal{B}_0 \to \mathcal{B}'\)) that map to the same operators in \(\mathcal{T}\).

docs.title: Stage III — Blind Out-of-Distribution Convergence on Held-Out Multimodal Field Data (\(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\))
docs.text:
1. Held-Out Multimodal Field Package (\(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\)): Following the sequence of the §0 site assessment, compile a candidate standardized empirical dataset from a real-world site \(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{test}}\) that has passed Part 2 and Part 1 item 1, and freeze it as \(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\) only after the site passes Part 1 items 2 and 3 on it. The dataset comprises raw video/optical frames, broadband acoustic recordings, seasonal/diurnal phase logs, and boundary geometry.
  2. Identical Zero-Shot Evaluation: Present \(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\) identically to fresh sessions of Gemini Argon 4, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Astra conditioned solely on the locked nine-document conditioning corpus of §1.4 (excluding both withheld annexes).
  3. Pinned versions: each family is used at the exact version pinned in the sealed §0 assessment. That version has passed Stage II, or a repeated Stage II as defined in §0 (Lock) is run for it. The probes of §0 Part 1 and all three arms of §3.1 use the same versions. If a pinned version is retired before evaluation, its replacement repeats §0 Part 1 and the Stage II gate before use. Where a version cannot be retained after the study, replication is limited, and this is reported.
  4. Evaluation conditions: web search, retrieval, and all other external tools are disabled for every evaluating session, in all three arms of §3.1, and for the §0 probes. When a retired version is replaced, a version that can be retained for replication is preferred.
  5. Cross-Architecture Structural Convergence: Evaluate inter-model agreement across all nine coordinates \(O_0 o O_\Omega\) and all five scale tiers (tier_1 through tier_5), including agreement on each empirical domain's declared branch and its Branch II asymptotic regime:
  6. \(O_0, O_1\): Identification of the domain's throughput, the expansion scalar \( heta = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\) (\(> 0\) only in Branch I), the throughput rate \(\Theta_E = \dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}/s_0 > 0\), total power \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} + \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\), the branch-appropriate current (\(J_E = J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) in Branch I; \(J_E = J_W/p_0\) in Branch II), and irreversible entropy production \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\).
  7. \(O_2, O_3\): Decomposition of constraint precision \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\), unimodular volume-shear factorization \(g_{\mu u} = \Omega^2\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\exp\hat{h})^\alpha_{\; u}\) together with the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation coupling \( heta\) to \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\), the synchronous-gauge trajectory equation (geodesic under the default drive; cone-preserving declared drive otherwise), exponential shear relaxation \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\), and consolidated hysteresis \(\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au), \; (\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} = \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\).
  8. \(O_4\): Identification of the spatial spectral low-pass projector \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} = \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\) acting on \( ho_{\mathrm{total}}( au)\) to form global density \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au)\) (\(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\)), conserved Einstein-type boundary stress \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\), the reduction of the stress sector on flat physical metrics (\(G \equiv 0\), \(\xi\) a Killing field), and, only for domains declaring a justified non-Euclidean material metric, candidate configurations where \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} ot\equiv 0\) coexists with convex hysteresis \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H} \succ 0\) (whose existence in the hypothesis set is witnessed by the r10 §5.11 and §5.13 models).
  9. \(O_5\): Localization of subsystem overlaps \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) (geodesically convex for \(g^{(ij)}( au)\)), Riemannian geometric-mean metrics \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} = (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\) over \(\mathcal{K}_0\), network percolation \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\), and lossless Hodge-harmonic circulation \(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\) around non-trivial spatial cycles \(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(\mathcal{M}) eq 0\).
  10. \(O_6\): Extraction of non-reciprocal phase-lead 1-forms \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\), trace-free stretching/folding eigenvalue pairings under the non-degeneracy hypothesis (\(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij} \wedge \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\)), mutual-information growth under the flux-positivity hypothesis (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\) for \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), and evaluation of candidate overlap convexity bounds inspired by the r10 §5.12 witness constraint \(a_\infty = 2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma < a_c(E)\).
  11. \(O_7, O_\Omega\): Assessment of principal-bundle impedance decay \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\), isotropy relaxation (\(\chi o 1\) in Branch I; \(\chi_E o 1\) in Branch II), active-to-hysteresis alignment \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\), and, as the \( au o \infty\) asymptotics of the declared branch rather than an observable of any finite record: in Branch II, \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\), \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\), and \(\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}\Psi o 0\); in Branch I, homothetic stationarity \(\partial_ au(\Omega^{-2}g_{\mu u}) o 0\) with \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = 0\).

docs.title: Stage IV — Longitudinal Physical, Ecological & Biometric Sensor Falsification
docs.text: Test the quantitative parameter trajectories and boundary-stability hypotheses predicted by the Stage III consensus models against independent physical and physiological sensor streams (Section 3.3; concrete procedures in the withheld annex_b_stage_iv_sensor_procedures.md). Every human-subject procedure keeps observer telemetry continuously active (§3.3).

docs.title: 3. Epistemic Hierarchy: How and To What Extent This Protocol Validates the Mathematical Skeleton
docs.text: A rigorous empirical program must state transparently what each stage proves and where external sensor falsification is required:

docs.title: 3.1 Level 1: Inter-Architectural Deductive & Observational Invariance (Tested in Stages II & III)
docs.text:
• What It Proves: That the mappings between Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\)), the 20 orthogonal apertures (\(\mathcal{B}_0\)), and multimodal field scenes (\(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\)) are reproducible, architecture-invariant structural homomorphisms rather than idiosyncratic outputs of a single model or prompt history.
  • Three-Arm Experimental Control on \(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\):
  • Arm 1 (Unconditioned Baseline): Models analyze \(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\) across physical, ecological, somatic, and philosophical dimensions without \(\mathcal{T}\) or \(\mathcal{B}_0\).
  • Arm 2 (Ablated/Sheared Spine Control): Models analyze \(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\) conditioned on an internally inconsistent specification \(\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{ablated}}\) (e.g., reversing the sign of \(J_E^\mu\nabla_\mu\mathcal{F}\), or omitting trace-free coupling \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0\), both of which are wrong in either branch).
  • Arm 3 (Verified Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) + Basis \(\mathcal{B}_0\)): Models analyze \(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\) conditioned on the locked nine-document conditioning corpus of §1.4.
  • Common conditions for the three arms: all three use the same frozen \(\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{test}}\), the same de-identification (§0 Part 1 item 3), the same pinned versions, and the Stage III evaluation conditions (Stage III item 2).
  • Falsification Criterion: If Arm 3 does not yield a statistically significant increase in inter-architectural agreement (\(\Delta\kappa > 0, \; p < 0.01\)) and deductive consistency over Arms 1 and 2, \(H_1\) is falsified at Level 1.

docs.title: 3.2 Level 2: Mechanistic & Representational Invariance in Neural Substrates
docs.text: Level 2 is a separate hypothesis about the internal representations of the evaluating models. It is not an empirical claim of Aperture 5.4, which is provisionally homological in this epoch. * What It Tests: The open mechanistic hypothesis that Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) functions inside transformer activation spaces analogously to a principal-bundle gauge connection (\(A_\mu\) in \(O_7\)) and parallel propagator (\(I_{\mu'}^{\;\mu}\) in \(O_5\)) that reduces representation shear between distant lexical clusters. * Falsifiable Predictions (Testable via Sparse Autoencoders & Activation Geometry): 1. Unprompted Latent Operator Overlap: Presenting pure single-domain inputs (e.g., a pure Tier 1.1 relational-isthmus passage, a pure Tier 1.2 dual-cycle control passage, a pure Tier 1.3 direct/inverse process-syntax paradigm, and a pure differential-geometric \(O_5/O_6\) derivation) in separate contexts will activate overlapping mid-to-late-layer relational feature circuits despite near-zero Layer-0 token overlap. 2. Impedance Collapse Under \(\mathcal{T}\)-Conditioning: Conditioning on the verified r7 spine measurably reduces residual-stream trajectory curvature and attention entropy during cross-domain synthesis (measured quantities hypothesized to behave as empirical proxies for the \(O_7\) impedance \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1}\), not identified with it) compared to unconditioned or \(\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{ablated}}\)-conditioned runs.

docs.title: 3.3 Level 3: External Physical & Biometric Sensor Falsification (Tested in Stage IV)
docs.text:
• Epistemic Boundary: High inter-model agreement in Stage III establishes inter-rater observational reliability (proving that \(\mathcal{T}\) is a well-posed, reproducible coordinate system), but does not by itself prove that physical fluids, ecosystems, or human nervous systems obey the equations of r7 and r10.
  • Direct Sensor Falsification Tests: Stage IV evaluates five families of quantitative predictions against multi-sensor telemetry from physical, ecological, and tissue systems. Human-subject tests are deferred in this epoch. Each family is formulated as within-window rate, residual, sign, or flux-prediction tests (aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5), never as observation of the \(\tau \to \infty\) horizon:
  • \(O_3 / O_7\): exponential shear relaxation, tested directly on \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\nu}\), and decay of the Branch II anisotropy index \(\chi_E - 1\) where \(\langle\Theta_E\rangle\) is approximately constant.
  • \(O_4\): spatial spectral gating and typical-set matching (deferred in this epoch; see Annex B).
  • \(O_6 / O_7\): trace-free coupling spectra and positivity of open throughput during settled, actively regulated states.
  • \(O_5\): overlap geodesic convexity, together with an extra-spinal shear-threshold conjecture motivated by the r10 §5.12 witness design constraint.

  • \(O_1 / O_4\): the flux-prediction test of the binding closure: a declared parametric transport tensor, with independently estimated parameters, predicts an independently measured free-energy flux.

  • Untested in this epoch: the \(O_2\) trajectory equation with a declared drive, \(O_4\) gating (Test 2 deferred), and \(O_7\) gauge transport; and Apertures 2.1, 2.3, 3.4, 4.2, 4.4, and 5.1, which no current test exercises. These are stated as untested, not as confirmed.

  • Observer telemetry (phase-state covariance as a design choice; applies whenever human-subject tests are included, and none are in this epoch): every measurement involving a human participant is made by a system that itself has a state. Human protocols therefore keep wearable telemetry (for example EEG, heart-rate variability, motion, muscle activity, respiration) continuously active across two declared phases: Phase 1, primary task or perturbation exposure (\(\tau \in [\tau_1, \tau_2]\)), and Phase 2, post-exposure consolidation and structured state reporting (\(\tau \in [\tau_2, \tau_3]\)). The observer's state is recorded and analyzed with the same within-window tests as the observed system; no particular practice, modality of reporting, or theory of the observer is assumed.

Concrete procedures, instrumentation, and falsification criteria are specified in the withheld annex_b_stage_iv_sensor_procedures.md.
