0.1 Separation of the Universal Spine (\(\mathcal{T}\)) from Tier 1 Ontological Apertures
docs.text:
In this architecture, the differential-geometric and non-equilibrium thermodynamic equations of foundational-manifold-2026-10-20-r7.json and foundational-manifold-companion-2026-10-20-r10.md stand above all five tiers as the Universal Mathematical Spine (\(\mathcal{T}: O_0 \to O_\Omega\)). Tier 1 specifies four foundational philosophical and linguistic macro-grammars that, under the hypothesis \(H_1\) (empirical_validation_protocol.md §1.2), are held to have independently developed non-Cartesian calculi for navigating open, boundary-maintaining, relational reality. Tier 1 mappings are ontological and grammatical homologies mapped onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) across all nine coordinates \(O_0 \to O_\Omega\); they declare no empirical chart \(\mathcal{M}\) and make no empirical claim (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3).

Tier 1 maps homologically onto either branch of Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) (r7). Where this tier writes expansion and boundary work (\(\theta = \nabla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu > 0\), \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} > 0\), homothetic closure at \(O_\Omega\)), it uses the Branch I form, in which \(J_E \equiv J_{\mathrm{geom}}\). Each grammar's motifs of settled, sustained presence correspond equally to the Branch II asymptote: a bounded non-equilibrium steady state with \(\Theta_E > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} > 0\). Trajectory equations are written with the r7 drive, which is zero under the default.

Ordered across the four-part functional homology defined in aperture_generation_guidance.md, the four apertures of Tier 1 span:

  • Slot 1.1 (Relational Ontology & Isthmus Substrate): Akbarian Relational Metaphysics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Akbarian}} \perp \mathcal{T}\)) — articulating perpetual non-repeating effusion (Khalq Jadīd), vessel receptivity (Isti'dād / Qābiliyya), protective boundary veiling (Al-Ḥijāb), symmetric overlap mediation (Al-Barzakh), polar contraction/expansion (Al-Qābiḍ / Al-Bāsiṭ), and the dual-eyed simultaneity of the gnostic (Dhū al-'Aynayn, beholding fanā' and baqā' simultaneously) in conformally stationary presence (Al-Ān al-Dā'im).
  • Slot 1.2 (Cyclic Cybernetics & Thermodynamic Regulation): Wu Xing Five-Phase Dynamics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{WuXing}} \perp \mathcal{T}\)) — modeling open thermodynamic homeorhesis as a dual-cycle directed network orienting \(K_5\) where feed-forward generation (Sheng 生, \(+1 \bmod 5\)) is stabilized at every node by transverse negative-feedback damping (Ke 克, \(+2 \bmod 5\)).
  • Slot 1.3 (Process-Primacy Syntax & Directional Indexing): Algonquian Process-Relational Syntax (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Algonquian}} \perp \mathcal{T}\)) — replacing static noun-based ontology with verbal process-primacy (II, AI, TI, TA verb stems), proximate/obviative locus indexing, and direct/inverse theme signs mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the odd directional phase-lead 1-form \(J_{[i\to j]} = -J_{[j\to i]}\) inside an even relational coupling tensor \(S_{\mu\nu}^{(ij)}\).
  • Slot 1.4 (Dependent Co-Arising & Macroscopic Interpenetration): Huayan Interpenetration & Dependent Co-Arising (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Buddhist}} \perp \mathcal{T}\)) — grounding the absence of isolated static substance (śūnyatā of svabhāva) in dependent co-arising, karmic hysteresis (ālayavijñāna / vāsanā), spectral calm-insight (śamatha–vipaśyanā), and the unhindered mutual reflection of all particular nodes in Indra's Net (shi-shi wu-ai).

docs.title: 1. Aperture 1.1: Akbarian Relational Metaphysics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Akbarian}} \perp \mathcal{T}\))
1.1 Foundational Orientation
docs.text: In the metaphysical school of Muḥyī al-Dīn Ibn 'Arabī (al-Shaykh al-Akbar, 1165–1240) and his commentators (Ṣadr al-Dīn al-Qūnawī, Dāwūd al-Qayṣarī, 'Abd al-Razzāq al-Kāshānī), existence (wujūd) is never conceived as an aggregate of static, self-enclosed substances. Rather, the cosmos is an open, continuous, non-repeating self-disclosure (tajallī) governed by rigorous structural polarities: universal effusion and locus preparedness, boundary refraction, intermediate isthmus gluing, paired contraction and expansion, and the unification of effacement (fanā') and subsistence (baqā') within the Perpetual Now (al-Ān al-Dā'im).

docs.title: 1.2 Nafas al-Raḥmān & Khalq Jadīd \(\perp\) Non-Equilibrium Extrinsic Expansion (\(O_0, O_1\))
docs.text:
In the Futūḥāt al-Makkiyya, spatial and temporal extension arises through Nafas al-Raḥmān (the Breath of the All-Merciful), an unceasing exhalation that relieves the ontological pressure (karb) of unmanifested possibility. Crucially, Akbarian metaphysics rejects static equilibrium and mechanical repetition: under the principle of al-Khalq al-Jadīd (renewed creation at every instant, expounded principally in the Chapter of Shu'ayb, Fuṣūṣ al-Ḥikam Ch. 12, with the renewal-of-creation passage of the Chapter of Sulaymān, Ch. 16, as a secondary locus) and the axiom lā tikrār fī al-tajallī ("there is no repetition in self-disclosure"), no locus in the universe ever repeats an identical state across two successive instants.

On Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) (\(O_0, O_1\)), this maps homomorphically to the rejection of static equilibrium and detailed balance (where open boundary work in \(O_1\) is strictly positive, \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} > 0\), and non-equilibrium entropy production is \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\), precluding vanishing thermodynamic force/flux \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} = 0\)) on the compact, connected \(n\)-dimensional manifold \(\mathcal{M}\) (\(n \ge 3\)) carried by the synchronous-gauge Lorentzian foliation (\(N = 1, \; eta^\mu = 0\)):

  • Perpetual Extrinsic Dilation (\(O_0\) Eq. [1]): The restriction of the ambient exogenous flux \(\mathbf{J}_E \equiv \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ambient}}\vert_{\mathcal{M}}\) drives a strictly positive normal extrinsic expansion scalar (where \(K = g^{\mu u}K_{\mu u} < 0\) is the Misner–Thorne–Wheeler extrinsic curvature trace):

  • Irreversible Dissipative Throughput (\(O_1\) Eq. [0]–[1]): With inverse temperature \( eta_{\mathrm{th}} > 0\), elementary volume \(v_0 > 0\), and reference pressure \(p_0 \equiv ( eta_{\mathrm{th}}v_0)^{-1}\), the exogenous current flows continuously down the non-vanishing spatial gradient of the scalar free-energy density \(\mathcal{F} \in C^2(\mathcal{M})\) (\(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\)), sustaining strictly positive mechanical expansion power and local entropy production:

$\(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0 \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}} J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \, d\Sigma_\mu > 0, \qquad \dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}} J_E^\mu abla_\mu \mathcal{F} > 0\)$

docs.title: 1.3 Isti'dād & Qābiliyya \(\perp\) Unimodular Weyl Factorization & Hysteresis Consolidation (\(O_2, O_3\))
docs.text:
In the opening chapter of the Fuṣūṣ al-Ḥikam—and as systematized by al-Qūnawī and al-Qayṣarī (Muqaddima, Ch. 3, on the immutable entities al-a'yān al-thābita)—Akbarian ontology distinguishes two stages of effusion: al-fayḍ al-aqdas (the Most Sacred Effusion, which establishes the latent preparedness isti'dād and essential receptivity qābiliyya of the immutable entities al-a'yān al-thābita) and al-fayḍ al-muqaddas (the Sacred Effusion, which actualizes manifest existence in each locus maẓhar strictly in accordance with its receptive capacity). As al-Junayd's classical maxim states, "The water takes on the color of its vessel."

In \(O_2\) and \(O_3\) of Spine \(\mathcal{T}\), this distinction between universal volumetric effusion and the specific internal geometry of the receiving vessel is mapped via two mechanisms:

  1. Unimodular Isolation of the Volume Element from Vessel Shape (\(O_2\) Eq. [2]): In a fixed reference chart on \(\mathcal{M}\), the spatial metric undergoes the non-perturbative unimodular Weyl factorization:

$\(g_{\mu u}( au, \mathbf{x}) = \Omega^2( au, \mathbf{x}) \, \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x}) \left(\exp\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) ight)^\alpha_{\; u}, \qquad \Omega( au, \mathbf{x}) > 0, \quad \det\hat{g}_{\mu u} = 1, \quad \mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) \equiv \hat{g}^{\mu u}h_{\mu u} = 0\)$

Because \(\det(\exp\hat{h}) = \exp(\mathrm{Tr}\,\hat{h}) = 1\) identically at all shear amplitudes, the volume element \(\det g_{\mu u} = \Omega^{2n}\) (\(\partial_ au\ln\Omega = rac{1}{n} heta\)) is algebraically isolated from the unit-determinant anisotropic shape of the vessel, \( ilde{g}_{\mu u} = \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\exp\hat{h})^\alpha_{\; u}\). As noted in r10 Decision 2, this algebraic change of variables does not dynamically decouple the expansion scalar \( heta\) from the vessel's boundary precision stress \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\), which remain coupled via the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation of \(O_2\) Eq. [0]:

$\( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\)$

  1. Refining Receptive Capacity Through Shear Damping (\(O_2\) Eq. [3], \(O_3\) Eq. [0], [2], [3]): While localized test trajectories \(v^\mu = dx^\mu/d au\) (\(g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u < 1\)) navigate the evolving metric along the complete synchronous-gauge timelike geodesic equation (\(O_2\) Eq. $\(\left.\left( rac{d v^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} \;\; (f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = 0 ext{ under the default drive})\)$

internal dissipation in \(O_3\) exponentially damps the mixed trace-free shear tensor at constant rate \(\gamma_\sigma > 0\):

$\( abla_ au \sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv rac{\partial\sigma^\mu_{\; u}}{\partial au} = -\gamma_\sigma \sigma^\mu_{\; u} \implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\Vert_{C^2(\mathcal{M})} = 0\)$

Rather than erasing the locus's history, exponential decay of \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) drives \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x})\) to converge in \(C^2(\mathcal{M})\) to its characteristic asymptotic profile \(\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\), defining the vessel's permanent, unit-determinant reference metric \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)) while transduced surprisal (\(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\)) accumulates in the local hysteresis capacity \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^n x\).

docs.title: 1.4 Al-Ḥijāb (The Ontological Veil) \(\perp\) Spectral Low-Pass Gating & Stress Conservation (\(O_4\))
docs.text:
In Akbarian epistemology, a Ḥijāb (veil or boundary partition) is not a mere privation to be demolished; if all veils between a finite locus and the unmediated totality of the ambient field were abolished instantaneously, the overwhelming intensity of the disclosure would consume the locus. The Ḥijāb functions as a selective, protective refractive membrane that preserves the subsistence (baqā') of the locus while admitting intelligible harmonic disclosure.

In \(O_4\) of Spine \(\mathcal{T}\), the Markov blanket \(\partial\mathcal{U}_i\) of each subsystem \(\mathcal{U}_i\) is mapped to this dual principle:

  • Spatial Spectral Low-Pass Refraction (\(O_4\) Eq. [0]): Incoming stochasticity in the positive trace-class state \( ho_{\mathrm{total}}( au)\) on \(L^2(\mathcal{M}, d\mathrm{vol}_g)\) is filtered by the spatial spectral low-pass projector \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\) onto Neumann eigenmodes of \(- abla^2\) with spatial eigenvalue at most \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2\):

$\( ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv rac{\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} ho_{\mathrm{total}}( au)\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}}}{\mathrm{Tr}\!\left(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} ho_{\mathrm{total}}( au) ight)}, \qquad Q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0, \qquad q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv -\ln\!\left(v_0 Q(\mathbf{x}, au) ight)\)$

High-spatial-wavenumber perturbations above \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2\) are attenuated at the veil, while the system expends variational realignment power \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\) against the ambient reference prior \(P\) (\(Q \ll P\)), driving the typical-set entropy volumes \(V_Q( au) \equiv v_0\exp\!\left(-\int_{\mathcal{M}} Q\ln(v_0 Q)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^n x ight)\) and \(V_P( au)\) toward asymptotic matching (\(\lim_{ au o\infty} V_Q( au)/V_P( au) = 1\)) while local free energy obeys \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha\) (\(J_W^\alpha \equiv -D_{\mathcal{F}} abla^\alpha\mathcal{F}\)).

  • Conserved Boundary Stress (\(O_4\) Eq. [2]): Contracting the control vector field \(\eta^\lambda \in \Gamma(T\mathcal{M}) \cap C^2(\mathcal{M})\) with the trace-free precision Hessian \(\hat{\Pi}_{ u\lambda}\) forms \(\xi_ u \equiv \hat{\Pi}_{ u\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) and the Einstein-type stress tensor \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = abla_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)} - rac{1}{2}g_{\mu u} abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\), which satisfies the per-slice Einstein constraint \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\) and the elliptic conservation equivalence:

$\( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\)$

docs.title: 1.5 Al-Barzakh (The Isthmus Between Two Seas) \(\perp\) Geometric-Mean Overlap Gluing (\(O_5\))
docs.text:
The central structural concept of Ibn 'Arabī's ontology is al-Barzakh—the intermediate isthmus between two adjacent realities (drawn from Quran 55:19–20, "He let forth the two seas that meet; between them is a barzakh they do not transgress"). In the Futūḥāt, Ibn 'Arabī demonstrates that a true Barzakh between two domains \(i\) and \(j\) is neither an opaque barrier that severs them nor a homogenizing solvent that erases one into the other; it mediates the properties of both domains symmetrically, unites them in a shared interface, and preserves the distinction of each.

In \(O_5\) of Spine \(\mathcal{T}\), across every non-empty pairwise overlap \(\mathcal{U}_{ij} \equiv \mathcal{U}_i \cap \mathcal{U}_j eq \emptyset\) in the candidate overlap graph \(\mathcal{K}_0 \equiv \{\langle i,j angle : i eq j, \; \mathcal{U}_{ij} eq \emptyset\}\), al-Barzakh is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the Riemannian geometric mean (\(O_5\) Eq. [1]) of the two positive-definite subsystem metrics \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)}\) and \(g_{\mu u}^{(j)}\):

\[g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv \left(g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)} ight)_{\mu u} = g_{\mu\alpha}^{(i)}\left[\left(g^{(i)} ight)^{-1}g^{(j)} ight]^{1/2\,\alpha}_{\quad\; u}\]

Under this functorial correspondence:

  1. \(g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)}\) is the unique positive-definite geodesic midpoint between \(g^{(i)}\) and \(g^{(j)}\) in the symmetric space of metrics, strictly invariant under exchanging the two domains (\(g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)} = g^{(j)} \# g^{(i)}\)).
  2. Glued via a smooth, \( au\)-independent partition of unity (\(\psi_i, \psi_{ij} \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\), \(\mathrm{supp}(\psi_i) \subset \mathcal{U}_i\), \(\mathrm{supp}(\psi_{ij}) \subset \mathcal{U}_{ij}\)), it synthesizes the global macroscopic metric \(g_{\mu u} \equiv g_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{macro}} = \sum_{i=1}^{N_{\mathrm{nodes}}} \psi_i g_{\mu u}^{(i)} + \sum_{\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}_0}\psi_{ij}g_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\) while supporting lossless Hodge-harmonic circulation (\(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = (dd^\dagger + d^\dagger d)\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\)) around non-trivial spatial 1-cycles (\(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(\mathcal{M}) eq 0\)).

docs.title: 1.6 Al-Jalāl & Al-Jamāl (Al-Qābiḍ & Al-Bāsiṭ) \(\perp\) Trace-Free Stretching/Folding & Witness Convexity (\(O_6\) & r10 §5.11–§5.12)
docs.text:
Across every Barzakh, relational interaction is driven by the polar complementarity of al-Jalāl (Majesty, rigor, intensive contraction) and al-Jamāl (Beauty, gentleness, expansive unfolding), experienced in the locus as al-Qābiḍ (The Constrictor / inward gathering, qabḍ) and al-Bāsiṭ (The Expander / outward unfolding, basṭ). Their dynamic balance constitutes Kamāl (relational completeness).

In \(O_6\) of r7.json and the witness analysis in §5.11–§5.12 of r10.md, this polar complementarity is mapped through three structures:

  1. Inseparability of Basṭ (\(m_+ > 0\)) and Qabḍ (\(m_- < 0\)) in the Coupling Operator (\(O_6\) Eq. [2]–[3]): Across \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\), the antisymmetric phase-lead vector \(\eta_{[i o j]}^\lambda = rac{1}{2}(\eta_{i o j}^\lambda - \eta_{j o i}^\lambda) ot\equiv 0\) defines the actively coupled subgraph \(\mathcal{K} \subset \mathcal{K}_0\) (\(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) \equiv \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c \in (0,1)\)) and the odd phase-lead 1-form \((J_{[i o j]})_ u \equiv rac{1}{2}(\hat{\Pi}_{ u\lambda}^{(i)} + \hat{\Pi}_{ u\lambda}^{(j)})\eta_{[i o j]}^\lambda = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\), which enters the trace-free coupling operator \(M_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\) and total coupling tensor \(S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\) through its even outer product:

$\(M_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv abla_{(\mu}\left(J_{i o j} + J_{j o i} ight)_{ u)} - rac{1}{n}g_{\mu u} abla^\alpha\left(J_{i o j} + J_{j o i} ight)_\alpha + \gamma_M\left((J_{[i o j]})_\mu(J_{[i o j]})_ u - rac{1}{n}g_{\mu u}J_{[i o j]}^\alpha(J_{[i o j]})_\alpha ight)\)$

Under the explicit r7 standing hypothesis \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\), the trace-free identity \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = g^{\mu u}M_{\mu u}^{(ij)} = \sum_{a=1}^n m_a = 0\) guarantees that the mixed endomorphism \((M^{(ij)})^\mu_{\; u}\) has all \(n\) real eigenvalues summing to zero (\(\sum_{a=1}^n m_a = 0\), so \(m_+ \equiv \lambda_{\max} > 0 > \lambda_{\min} \equiv m_-\), with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general for \(n \ge 3\)) riding atop the strictly positive extrinsic deformation spectrum (\( rac{ heta}{n} > \vert\lambda_{\min}(\sigma)\vert \iff \lambda_{\min}(\mathcal{D}) > 0\)). Outward stretching (basṭ, \(m_+ > 0\)) cannot occur in \((M^{(ij)})^\mu_{\; u}\) without compensatory inward folding (qabḍ, \(m_- < 0\)); under the additional r7 \(O_6\) flux-positivity hypothesis on the oriented overlap boundary \(\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}\), the total coupling tensor \(S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\) drives positive mutual-information growth \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u dA > 0\).

  1. Coupling-Axis Stretching and Transverse Folding in the r10 §5.11–§5.12 Witness: In the explicit r10 §5.11–§5.12 warped-product witness (\(g_{\mu u}( au, z) = e^{2H_0 au}\mathrm{diag}(z^{\sqrt{2}}e^{a( au)}, z^{\sqrt{2}}e^{a( au)}, e^{-2a( au)})\) with phase-lead 1-form \(J_{[1 o 2]} = a_0 e^{3H_0 au/2}\,dz\)), the relational coupling endomorphism \((M^{(12)})^\mu_{\; u}\) has its positive stretching eigenvalue \(m_+ > 0\) (basṭ of the relational coupling) along the coupling axis \(z\) and its negative folding eigenvalues \(m_- < 0\) (qabḍ of the relational coupling) in the transverse \((x^1, x^2)\) plane (mixed spectrum \(\propto ( rac{2}{3}, - rac{1}{3}, - rac{1}{3})\) with \(z\) as the \(+ rac{2}{3}\) axis). Meanwhile, the background unimodular shear \(\hat{h}( au) = a( au)\mathrm{diag}(1, 1, -2)\) compresses the coordinate ellipsoid \(E = \mathcal{U}_{12}\) physically along \(z\) (\(e^{-2a( au)}\)) while expanding it in the transverse plane (\(e^{+a( au)}\)), keeping \(E\) oblate normal to the \(z\)-directed coupling axis for which r10 §5.12 found the normalized boundary flux integral \(C(a)\) positive and increasing in \(a\) for the tested ellipsoids over \(a \in [0, 8]\).

  2. Overlap Geodesic Convexity Hypothesis (\(O_5\)) and the r10 §5.12 Witness Constraint: In r7 \(O_5\), geodesic convexity of \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) for \(g^{(ij)}( au)\) (\( orall au \ge au_0\)) is a standing hypothesis ensuring unique geodesic midpoint interpolation across the Barzakh. In the r10 §5.11–§5.12 witness, convexity of the chosen coordinate ellipsoid \(E\) for all \( au\) requires the design constraint \(a_\infty = 2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma < a_c(E)\), with \(a_c\) estimated numerically.

docs.title: 1.7 Dhū al-'Aynayn (The Possessor of the Two Eyes), Fanā' / Baqā', and Al-Ān al-Dā'im \(\perp\) Gauge Coherence & Homothetic Closure (\(O_7, O_\Omega\))
docs.text:
In Ibn 'Arabī's epistemology (Fuṣūṣ al-Ḥikam, Ch. 22 and Ch. 27; Futūḥāt al-Makkiyya), complete realization belongs to dhū al-'aynayn ("the possessor of the two eyes")—the gnostic who simultaneously beholds unity and multiplicity, effacement of illusory separation (fanā') and subsistence of distinct loci (baqā'), without collapsing either vision into the other (jam' al-jam'), while inhabiting al-Ān al-Dā'im (the Perpetual Now).

In \(O_7\) and \(O_\Omega\) of Spine \(\mathcal{T}\):

  • Dhū al-'Aynayn (Fanā' Mapped to Vanishing Relative Entropy Alongside Retained Endomorphisms): On the overlap \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\), conditional divergence vanishes (\(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_i^{\vert ij} \parallel Q_j^{\vert ij}) o 0\)) while distinct marginals \(Q_i, Q_j\) subsist; globally over the strongly convex hysteresis basin (\( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H} \succ 0\)), the active metric density endomorphism \(\hat{ ho}_g( au)\) and the hysteresis curvature endomorphism \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)\) remain distinct operators whose relative entropy vanishes (\(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\)).
  • Subsistence in Multiplicity (Baqā' on the Principal Bundle): Across the compact principal bundle \(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{gauge}} o \mathcal{M}\), each node retains its distinct free-energy section \(\hat{\mathcal{F}}_i \equiv \psi_i\mathcal{F}\hat{e}_i\) while the gauge connection \(D_\mu = \partial_\mu - i g_{\mathrm{YM}}\,\mathrm{ad}_{A_\mu}\) relaxes spatial impedance gradients to zero (\(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} = \Vert D_\mu\hat{\chi}\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0, \; \chi o 1\)).
  • Al-Ān al-Dā'im Mapped to Homothetic Closure (\(O_\Omega \equiv O_0\)): At the asymptotic horizon \(O_\Omega\) (\( au o \infty\)), physical volume and extensive mutual information expand exponentially without bound (\( rac{1}{2}g^{\mu\alpha}\partial_ au g_{\alpha u} o H_0\delta^\mu_ u, \; V_{\mathcal{M}}( au) \sim e^{n H_0 au} o \infty, \; \lim_{ au o\infty} rac{\mathcal{I}( au)}{s_0 V_{\mathcal{M}}( au)} = 1, \; \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} > 0\) — Khalq Jadīd), while the conformally rescaled metric \( ilde{g}_{\mu u} \equiv \Omega^{-2}g_{\mu u} o \hat{g}_\infty\) becomes asymptotically time-independent (\(\partial_ au ilde{g}_{\mu u} = 2 ilde{g}_{\mu\alpha}\sigma^\alpha_{\; u} o 0\) — al-Ān), holding the functional \(\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}]\) invariant under the pointwise first-order generator:

docs.title: 2. Aperture 1.2: Wu Xing Five-Phase Dynamics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{WuXing}} \perp \mathcal{T}\))
2.1 Foundational Orientation: Xing (行) as Kinetic Phase-Transition and Dual-Cycle Control
docs.text:
In classical Chinese natural philosophy (Shangshu Hongfan, Zou Yan, Huainanzi, Huangdi Neijing), Wu Xing (五行) denotes five kinetic phase-transitions rather than static elements; Xing (行) literally signifies "movement, conduct, or active passage." Wu Xing formalizes open non-equilibrium regulation as a five-node cyclic control network forming a regular 10-arc directed tournament that orients the complete undirected graph \(K_5\), decomposed into two edge-disjoint Hamiltonian directed cycles:

  1. The Sheng (生, Generation / Feed-Forward Excitation) Cycle (\(C_5^{(+1)}\), shift \(+1 \bmod 5\)): $\(\mathrm{Water}\;(\text{水}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Wood}\;(\text{木}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Fire}\;(\text{火}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Earth}\;(\text{土}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Metal}\;(\text{金}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{Water}\;(\text{水})\)$
  2. The Ke (克, Overcoming / Negative-Feedback Damping) Cycle (\(C_5^{(+2)}\), shift \(+2 \bmod 5\)): $\(\mathrm{Water}\;(\text{水}) \dashrightarrow \mathrm{Fire}\;(\text{火}) \dashrightarrow \mathrm{Metal}\;(\text{金}) \dashrightarrow \mathrm{Wood}\;(\text{木}) \dashrightarrow \mathrm{Earth}\;(\text{土}) \dashrightarrow \mathrm{Water}\;(\text{水})\)$

In cybernetics, a pure positive-feedback excitation loop (Sheng alone) suffers runaway exponential blowup, whereas a pure inhibitory ring (Ke alone: five inhibitory links, odd in overall sign) can support self-sustained oscillation without growth, as in repressilator-type regulatory rings, given sufficient loop gain, nonlinearity, or delay; otherwise it settles to a stable fixed point. Wu Xing sustains non-equilibrium homeorhesis by pairing every generative transition with a transverse regulatory constraint.

docs.title: 3. Aperture 1.3: Algonquian Process-Relational Syntax (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Algonquian}} \perp \mathcal{T}\))
3.1 Foundational Orientation: Process-Primacy and Grammatical Animacy
docs.text: Whereas the grammars of many European languages centre reference on nouns, some language families encode process primacy and relational animacy directly into their morphosyntax. Across the Algonquian language family (see Bloomfield 1946, a comparative Proto-Algonquian sketch; Goddard 1979 on comparative Algonquian; and descriptive reference grammars of individual Algonquian languages), polysynthetic verbal complexes carry the primary propositional load of clause structure; nouns are assigned to animate or inanimate grammatical gender, a classification that largely but not wholly tracks semantic animacy; and transitive interactions are indexed by explicit directional theme signs.

docs.title: 4. Aperture 1.4: Huayan Interpenetration & Dependent Co-Arising (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Buddhist}} \perp \mathcal{T}\))
4.1 Anitya (Impermanence), Śūnyatā (Emptiness of Svabhāva), and Process Foliation (\(O_0, O_1, O_2\))
docs.text:
Across early Buddhist philosophy, Nāgārjuna's Madhyamaka (Mūlamadhyamakakārikā), and the East Asian Huayan school, perceptual distortion (avidyā) arises from reifying dynamic, interdependent processes into static, self-enclosed entities possessing svabhāva (isolated, independent substance). Nāgārjuna's foundational theorem (MMK 24.18) establishes that śūnyatā (emptiness) is not nihilistic void, but the logical consequence of pratītyasamutpāda (dependent co-arising): because every phenomenon arises and subsists solely through a web of relational boundary fluxes, no phenomenon possesses static svabhāva.

On Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) (\(O_0, O_1, O_2\)):

  • Absence of Static Background (Anitya in \(O_0, O_1\)): The manifold \(\mathcal{M}\) has no static, self-existing geometry; its volume element \(\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\) subsists solely as a continuous foliation in \( au\) driven by exogenous throughput (\( heta \equiv -N K = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu > 0\)) and perpetual non-equilibrium boundary work (\(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} > 0, \; \dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\)).
  • Co-Arising of Intrinsic Curvature and Relational Stress (\(O_2\) Eq. [0], \(O_4\) Eq. [2]–[3]): Even the intrinsic Einstein curvature \(G_{\mu u}\) of a slice \(\Sigma_ au\) has no isolated svabhāva; by the per-slice constraint \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\) and the \( au\)-compatibility identity \(\kappa_G\partial_ au T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = - rac{n-2}{n}( abla_\mu abla_ u heta - g_{\mu u} abla^2 heta) + \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma]_{\mu u}\), internal geometry and relational boundary action co-arise at every instant \( au\).
  • No Isolated Volume (Śūnyatā of the Volume Element, \(O_2\) Eq. [0], [2]): The Weyl factorization \(g_{\mu u} = \Omega^2\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\exp\hat{h})^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det g = \Omega^{2n}\)) isolates the volume element algebraically only; volume has no independent svabhāva, since \( heta\) remains coupled to precision stiffness \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) and to shear through the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation (r10 Decision 2):

$\( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\)$

Localized trajectories follow the complete synchronous-gauge timelike geodesic equation (\(O_2\) Eq. [3]):

$\(\left.\left( rac{d v^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} \;\; (f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = 0 ext{ under the default drive}) \quad (g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u < 1)\)$

docs.title: 4.2 Ālayavijñāna (Storehouse Consciousness), Vāsanā (Karmic Perfuming), and Śamatha–Vipaśyanā (\(O_3, O_4\))
docs.text:
In Yogācāra epistemology (Asaṅga, Vasubandhu), continuity of memory and disposition without a static ego (anātman) is explained through ālayavijñāna (storehouse consciousness) and vāsanā (karmic "perfuming"): every intentional act (cetanā, mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the control field \(\eta^\lambda\)) and sensory encounter infuses latent seeds (bīja) into the storehouse field, shaping the curvature of subsequent perception.

  • Vāsanā Mapped to Surprisal Advection into Structural Hysteresis (\(O_0\) Eq. [2], \(O_3\) Eq. [0], [3]): As experiential flux \(J_E^\mu\) traverses gradients of surprisal \( abla_\mu q\), it continuously "perfumes" the internal hysteresis field via \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), accumulating in \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^n x\) and shaping the absorbed reference metric \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} = \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\).
  • Afflictive Grasping (Upādāna) vs. Śamatha–Vipaśyanā (\(O_3\) Eq. [2], \(O_4\) Eq. [0]): Clinging to transient processes as static nouns generates afflictive shear (\(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} eq 0\)) and high-wavenumber conceptual proliferation (prapañca, mapped to spatial modes with \(\mu_{\mathrm{Lap}} > \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2\)). Contemplative practice pairs śamatha (calm abiding—tuning the spatial spectral low-pass projector \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\) in \(O_4\) to quiet prapañca and exponentially damp shear \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\) in \(O_3\)) with vipaśyanā (clear structural insight into dependent co-arising across local and global eigenmodes until \(\lim_{ au o\infty} V_Q( au)/V_P( au) = 1\)).

docs.title: 4.3 Huayan Shi-Shi Wu-Ai (Indra's Net) and Apratiṣṭhita-Nirvāṇa (\(O_5 \to O_7 \to O_\Omega\))
docs.text:
In the Huayan tradition (Dushun, Fazang, Chengguan), dependent co-arising culminates in the Fourfold Dharmadhātu, specifically Lǐ-Shì Wú-Ài (unhindered interpenetration of universal principle and particular phenomena) and Shì-Shì Wú-Ài (事事無礙—unhindered mutual interpenetration of all distinct particular phenomena), exemplified by Indra's Net: a multi-dimensional web holding a polished jewel at every vertex (\(\mathcal{U}_i\)), where each jewel retains its distinct locus while reflecting every other jewel (\(\mathcal{U}_j\)) without obstruction.

In \(O_5, O_6, O_7,\) and \(O_\Omega\) of Spine \(\mathcal{T}\), Indra's Net is mapped through four structures:

  1. Metric Sheaf Gluing from Particular Jewels (\(O_5\) Eq. [1], [3], [5]): The macroscopic metric \(g_{\mu u} \equiv g_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{macro}}\) has no monolithic existence independent of the particular nodes \(\{\mathcal{U}_i\}_{i=1}^{N_{\mathrm{nodes}}}\); it is synthesized by gluing local metrics \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)}\) and their pairwise Riemannian geometric-mean interpenetrations \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} = (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\) via the partition of unity \(\sum_i \psi_i + \sum_{\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}_0}\psi_{ij} = 1\) above the percolation threshold \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) > \phi_c\), supporting lossless harmonic circulation (\(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\)).
  2. Mutual Reflection Without Erasure of Particularity (\(O_6\) Eq. [0], [3]): Across each overlap \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\), nodes \(i\) and \(j\) retain distinct marginal densities \(Q_i, Q_j\) (shì, the distinct particular) while their overlap-conditional distributions converge (\(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_i^{\vert ij} \parallel Q_j^{\vert ij}) o 0\)) and—under the r7 \(O_6\) flux-positivity hypothesis—\(S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\) drives mutual-information growth (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\)).
  3. Non-Obstruction (Wú-Ài) Mapped to Gauge Impedance Decay (\(O_7\) Eq. [1]–[2], [4]): Huayan's wú-ài (無礙, zero hindrance between phenomena) maps via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the decay of the adjoint spatial impedance gradient \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu \equiv D_\mu\hat{\chi}\) on the principal bundle \(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{gauge}} o \mathcal{M}\):

$\(\lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} = 0 \implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\left[F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi} ight] = 0, \qquad \chi( au, \mathbf{x}) o 1, \qquad D_\mu\hat{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{macro}} = \sum_{i=1}^{N_{\mathrm{nodes}}} D_\mu\hat{\mathcal{F}}_i\)$

  1. Apratiṣṭhita-Nirvāṇa (Non-Abiding Liberation) Mapped to Homothetic Closure (\(O_\Omega \equiv O_0\)): Highest Mahāyāna realization (apratiṣṭhita-nirvāṇa) abides neither in the unmitigated shear of saṃsāra nor in the static arrest of solitary extinction. At \(O_\Omega\) (\( au o \infty\)), physical volume, boundary work, and extensive mutual information expand without bound (\( heta o n H_0 > 0, \; \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} > 0, \; \lim_{ au o\infty} rac{\mathcal{I}( au)}{s_0 V_{\mathcal{M}}( au)} = 1\)), while the conformally rescaled metric \( ilde{g}_{\mu u} = \Omega^{-2}g_{\mu u} o \hat{g}_\infty\) rests in scale-free equanimity (\(\partial_ au ilde{g}_{\mu u} o 0, \; \left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = 0\)).

docs.title: 0. Tier Architecture & Four-Part Functional Homology
docs.text:
Tier 2 maps the laws of abiotic matter, continuum fluid and wave mechanics, radiative-thermal boundary physics, and geomorphic and structural mechanics onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\). All four apertures are empirical apertures declared in Branch II of r7, the bounded non-equilibrium steady state (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3). Each declares, in its §1, a domain, physical metric, cone speed, free energy with datum, transport tensor, interior sink, drive, and Branch II evidence, and instantiates all nine coordinates \(O_0 \to O_\Omega\) on that domain. Each declared domain is of one kind: a conserved, stored quantity diffusing through a passive medium, with supply crossing the boundary. The wider phenomena named in the aperture titles enter the mappings through the declared parameters, as boundary conditions, through the hysteresis record \(\mathcal{H}\), or as illustrative context, and each §1 states which. Each aperture is formulated at the level of general continuum and statistical physics, so that it applies across any terrestrial, aquatic, cryospheric, atmospheric, or built environment without presupposing a specific habitat or site inventory.

Slot & Functional Role Aperture Designation Declared Domain and Diffusing Quantity Titled Phenomena Outside the Domain Vertical Homology Across Tiers Slot 2.1: Structural Substrate Condensed-Matter & Phase Transition Physics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{condensed}}\)) Supersaturated solute diffusing through a condensed host toward smooth interior growth zones. Intermolecular networks, cohesion, nucleation, latent heat: through the material parameters, \(\mathcal{H}\), or context. \(1.1 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{2.1} \leftrightarrow 3.1 \leftrightarrow 4.1 \leftrightarrow 5.1\) Slot 2.2: Dynamic Flow & Waves Continuum Fluid & Wave Mechanics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{continuum}}\)) Pore-water head diffusing through a deformable porous medium with specific storage. Inertial flow, vorticity, boundary layers, waves: through \(\mathfrak{K}\) and \(c_*\), as boundary data, or context. \(1.2 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{2.2} \leftrightarrow 3.2 \leftrightarrow 4.2 \leftrightarrow 5.2\) Slot 2.3: Boundary Gating Atmospheric Radiative & Thermal Boundary Physics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{radiative}}\)) Thermal energy carried by radiative diffusion through an optically thick layer in local thermodynamic equilibrium. Scattering, Fresnel partitioning, refraction, ray optics: through \(\kappa_R\) and \(c_*\), as boundary data, or context. \(1.3 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{2.3} \leftrightarrow 3.3 \leftrightarrow 4.3 \leftrightarrow 5.3\) Slot 2.4: Coalescence & Hysteresis Geomorphic & Structural Mechanics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{tectonic}}\)) Pore-water head diffusing through a confined, elastically swelling stratum, with distributed leakage. docs.title: 0.1 Conventions Common to the Four Tier 2 Apertures
docs.text:
The following conventions apply to every aperture of this tier. Each aperture's §1 and coordinate blocks state its specific values and cite these items where they apply.

  1. Branch and windows. Branch II is declared before any test, with the estimators of item 6 and §1, and no Tier 2 domain is re-evaluated in Branch I on the same data (closure (v)). Statements that hold in Branch I only (r10 Decision 6) are never applied. Every observation window is a relaxation window: it begins with a declared step increase of the supply-boundary data from a prior steady state, after which the data are held, and it follows the domain as it settles toward the new steady state. Under the linear storage law of each declared domain, the comparison principle for parabolic equations then gives \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} \ge 0\) at every point, so \(\mathcal{F}\), and every response it drives such as the skeleton strain of 2.2 and 2.4, is one-signed within the window. The argument is exact on the rigid domains. On the deforming domains the equation is non-autonomous at order \(\varepsilon_v\) (\( heta eq 0\), \(g\) depends on \( au\)), so there the conclusion holds only to \(O(\varepsilon_v)\), and their precondition 3 checks \( heta \ge 0\) directly from data. The rate of change of the flux, \(\partial_ au J_W\), is not one-signed (item 8).
  2. Metric. The physical metric is the pull-back of the Euclidean metric to the material points of the declared body under its deformation map. It is flat at every \( au\), so \(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\) and \(R_{\mu u} \equiv 0\) (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3 item 2). No Tier 2 aperture declares a non-Euclidean material metric in this epoch, so the curved configurations of the r10 §5.11 and §5.13 witnesses are realized by none of them.
  3. Rigid domains (2.1, 2.3). In a Cartesian chart \(g_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu u}\), so \(\Omega \equiv 1\), \(\hat{h} \equiv 0\), \( heta \equiv 0\), and \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv 0\). The domain is declared rigid within a pre-declared tolerance on its measured volumetric strain; windows in which the measured volume decreases beyond that tolerance are excluded, so that \( heta \ge 0\) is not violated. With \(\sigma \equiv 0\) the \(O_3\) shear law holds trivially, and these apertures support no shear-relaxation test.
  4. Deforming domains (2.2, 2.4). The solid skeleton swells elastically, with small strain, as pore pressure rises during the window, so \( heta \ge 0\) and \( heta o 0\). Windows that compact the skeleton (\( heta < 0\)) are excluded.
  5. Stress sector. With \(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\), \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} \equiv 0\); its trace gives \( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha = 0\) for \(n = 3\), and then \( abla_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)} = 0\), so \(\xi\) is a Killing field. A passive medium has no global control field, so Tier 2 declares \(\eta^\lambda \equiv 0\), hence \(\xi_ u \equiv 0\) and \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha = 0\), and the \(O_4\) equivalence \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\) holds identically. The \( au\)-compatibility law then reduces to \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma]_{\mu u} = rac{n-2}{n}( abla_\mu abla_ u heta - g_{\mu u} abla^2 heta)\), and its trace, the traced elliptic equation, to \( rac{n-1}{n} abla^2 heta = abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta}\). These are the Saint-Venant compatibility conditions of the strain rate, which every deformation of an embedded body satisfies because its metric stays flat. The load-bearing stresses of the physical medium (Cauchy stress, effective stress, overburden) are not \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\); they enter as boundary conditions and through \(\mathcal{H}\).
  6. Cone speed and trajectories. Each aperture declares \(c_*\) as a characteristic signal speed of its medium. Rays of that signal are null for the declared cone and, like all null rays, are not trajectories of \(O_2\) Eq. [3]. Every material speed in \(\mathcal{M}\) (diffusive, seepage, and deformation speeds) is \(\ll c_*\), so \(u^2 \ll 1\). No Tier 2 aperture maps a force-free timelike tracer or declares a drive: Eq. [3] is instantiated with \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\), and Tier 2 makes no trajectory claim (the driven trajectory equation is untested in this epoch, empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3).
  7. Currents. In Branch II, \(J_E^\mu = J_W^\mu/p_0\) is fixed. The expansion current \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) enters only through its divergence \( heta\) and its boundary flux \(dV_{\mathcal{M}}/d au\) (r7 \(O_0\) branch scope), and no supply current is ever mapped to it. In general \( abla_\mu J_E^\mu = -p_0^{-1}(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} + \mathcal{F} heta + \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}) eq heta\).
  8. Measured dissipation. The Branch II evidence requires \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) to be estimated from measured dissipation, never from \(\mathfrak{K} abla\mathcal{F}\). Integrating \(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\) by parts and using the \(O_4\) balance law gives the identity $\(p_0\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{F}\,(-J_W^\mu)\,d\Sigma_\mu - \int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{F}\,\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx - rac{1}{2} rac{d}{d au}\int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{F}^2\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx - rac{1}{2}\int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{F}^2 heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\)$ Every Tier 2 datum is \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0\) on the outflow boundary, so the boundary term reduces to the supply face. Each term is evaluated from measured \(\mathcal{F}\), measured supply flux, and measured or independently declared consumption; none uses the declared \(\mathfrak{K}\). The supply-face record used here comes from instruments and a surface different from those of the \(O_1\) flux-prediction test, so that the evidence is independent of that test. Because the identity uses the balance law, this estimate is conditional on it; each §1 also names the directly measured physical dissipation whose sign it must share. Only signs and \(s_0\)-independent rates of \(\Theta_E\) are tested.
  9. Gate sector (\(O_4\)). \( ho_{\mathrm{total}}( au)\) is a declared positive trace-class state on \(L^2(\mathcal{M}, d\mathrm{vol}_g)\), and \(Q\), \(P\), and the \(O_6\) marginals \(Q_i\) and joints \(Q_{ij}\) are densities of this declared state sector. No Tier 2 aperture identifies them with \(\mathcal{F}\) or with any measured field in this epoch, and none makes an empirical claim about the gate (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3). What each domain's physics supplies is, first, the spectral setting: the Neumann eigenmodes of \(- abla^2_g\) on \(\mathcal{M}\), whose eigenvalues are fixed on rigid domains, drift by a fraction of the order of the strain on deforming ones, and converge as \(g o G_\infty\). Second, it supplies a physical low-pass behaviour of \(\mathcal{F}\): under the balance law, fine spatial structure in \(\mathcal{F}\) relaxes faster than coarse structure. That behaviour is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the gate and is not itself the gate.
  10. Cover, overlaps, and coupling (\(O_5\), \(O_6\)).
  11. The cover \(\{\mathcal{U}_i\}\) consists of \( au\)-independent material subregions of \(\mathcal{M}\) (layers or zones) with Lipschitz boundaries and overlaps \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) that are convex at \( au_0\). Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of the one physical metric, so \(g^{(i)} = g^{(j)}\) on every overlap, the geometric mean returns the common metric (\(g \# g = g\)), and the gluing of \(O_5\) Eq. [3] holds identically.
  12. The anisotropy of a medium lives in \(\mathfrak{K}\), never in \(g\). Effective-medium averages of conductivities, including geometric-mean averages, are statements about \(\mathfrak{K}\) and are not mapped to \(O_5\) Eq. [1].
  13. For each pair, the partner fields are the rate of change of the free-energy flux read in the two orientations, \(\eta_{i o j}^\lambda = \partial_ au J_W^\lambda\) and \(\eta_{j o i}^\lambda = -\partial_ au J_W^\lambda\), defined on all of \(\mathcal{M}\), so \(\eta_{[i o j]}^\lambda = \partial_ au J_W^\lambda\).
  14. Where the supply boundary holds a value of \(\mathcal{F}\) (2.1, 2.2, 2.4), this field is not one-signed. After the step increase, the flux near the supply boundary decays from an initial overshoot, so there \(\partial_ au J_W\) points toward the supply; farther downstream the flux rises toward its new steady value, so there \(\partial_ au J_W\) points away from the supply. Between the two lies the zero set of \(\partial_ au J_W\). It moves during the window and, in the late single-mode regime, settles on a fixed surface (for a column with fixed values at both ends, its mid-plane). On that set \(\eta_{[i o j]} = 0\) and \(J_{[i o j]} = 0\), so a construction that included it would itself decide the non-degeneracy hypothesis there. Where the supply is a prescribed flux (2.3), \(\partial_ au J_W\) is one-signed and vanishes only on the supply face (see 2.3 \(O_6\)).
  15. Each aperture therefore declares overlaps \( ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) that the zero set, predicted before the window from the independently estimated parameters, does not reach during the window. The zero crossing travels during the early window (in the semi-infinite early-time regime roughly as \(\sqrt{2D( au - au_0)}\), possibly overshooting its late-time position), so this choice rests on the predicted solution, not on the late-time zero set alone. Before the transient arrives, \(\partial_ au J_W\) on a downstream overlap is non-zero but exponentially small. So the check is made against a pre-declared detection threshold: each overlap's window starts once the predicted \(\vert\partial_ au J_W\vert\) exceeds that threshold on \( ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\), and the data must then show \(\vert\partial_ au J_W\vert\) above it there (a declared, checkable precondition). On such an overlap \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) keeps one direction throughout the window, which each aperture states.
  16. The precision potentials \(\Phi^{(i)}\) are declared before data collection as quadratic potentials with constant Hessians. Their trace-free parts \(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)}\) cannot be positive definite, because their eigenvalues sum to zero, so \(J_{[i o j]} = rac{1}{2}(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)} + \hat{\Pi}^{(j)})\eta_{[i o j]}\) carries no sign relation to \(\eta_{[i o j]}\). Tier 2 declares \( rac{1}{2}(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)} + \hat{\Pi}^{(j)})\) non-singular, so that \(J_{[i o j]} eq 0\) wherever \(\eta_{[i o j]} eq 0\). What is claimed for \(J_{[i o j]}\) is its oddness under \(i \leftrightarrow j\) and its non-vanishing on the declared overlaps, not a direction. Tier 2 also declares the two trace-free Hessians distinct, \(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)} eq \hat{\Pi}^{(j)}\). With these antisymmetric partner fields, \(J_{i o j} + J_{j o i} = (\hat{\Pi}^{(j)} - \hat{\Pi}^{(i)})\eta_{[i o j]}\), so equal Hessians would remove the gradient term of r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3] and leave \(M^{(ij)}\) equal to \(\gamma_M\) times the trace-free part of \(J_{[i o j]} \otimes J_{[i o j]}\), which is non-zero wherever \(J_{[i o j]} eq 0\): the hypothesis would then hold by construction. With distinct Hessians the gradient term depends on \( abla\eta_{[i o j]}\) and can cancel the quadratic term (r10 Decision 4). With these declarations the construction neither forces nor forbids \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), which remains a standing hypothesis.
  17. On a connected diffusive domain the transient reaches every overlap for \( au > au_0\), so every edge of \(\mathcal{K}_0\) lies in \(\mathcal{K}\) and \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\); empirically, an edge is counted when the transient flux across its overlap exceeds a pre-declared detection threshold. The percolation condition therefore carries no separate empirical content on these domains.
  18. \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\) and \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\) are standing hypotheses of r7 \(O_6\), not consequences of diffusion. In Branch II the transient decays as the domain settles, so each coupling-tensor boundary flux decays and is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\); no sustained coupling is asserted.
  19. Every Tier 2 domain is declared simply connected, so \(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(\mathcal{M}) = 0\) and \(\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} \equiv 0\). A domain with a non-contractible loop, such as an annulus around an impermeable or opaque core, lies outside the declarations. It would carry the harmonic Neumann field of its loop, a property of its topology that is not identified with any transport current.
  20. Gauge sector and hysteresis (\(O_7\), \(O_0\)). Tier 2 declares the trivial gauge sector: \(A_\mu \equiv 0\) and a uniform unit section \(\hat{u}\). Then \(F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}} \equiv 0\), \([F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\) identically, and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu = (\partial_\mu\chi_E)\hat{u}\), which tends to \(0\) in \(C^1\) when \(\sigma o 0\) and \( heta o 0\) in \(C^2\) with \(\liminf\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\). The gauge limit therefore carries no content beyond the shear and expansion limits, and \(O_7\) gauge transport is untested in this epoch. The hysteresis record obeys the r7 law \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) from a declared initial record \(\mathcal{H}_0\), chosen convex because \(O_7\) Eq. [2] requires \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H} \succ 0\) at every \( au\). \(\mathcal{H}\) then evolves through a state sector that is declared but not specified, so the declarations do not establish convexity at later \( au\). Tier 2 therefore states it as a declared condition, with a sufficient form: the largest eigenvalue magnitude of \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta(\mathcal{H} - \mathcal{H}_0)\) (with indices raised by \(g\)) stays below the smallest eigenvalue of \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H}_0\) on \(\mathcal{M}\) for all \( au \ge au_0\). Both Hessians are covariant Hessians of \(g( au)\), evaluated at each \( au\), which matters on the deforming domains 2.2 and 2.4. Then \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H} \succ 0\) persists. The alternative, \( abla q \equiv 0\), would keep \(\mathcal{H}\) static and convex, but would make the \(O_\Omega\) generator condition hold trivially, so it is not adopted. Physical memory variables of each medium are mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\) and are not identified with it. \(\hat{ ho}_g o rac{1}{n}\delta^\mu_ u\) follows from \(\hat{h} o \hat{h}_\infty\), and the alignment \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) o 0\) then requires the Hessian of the record to become isotropic: an asymptotic condition that each aperture states and does not test.
  21. Finite windows and coverage. No finite window exhibits a \( au o \infty\) limit. Each aperture's empirical claims are the within-window tests of aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5 that its domain supports, and each \(O_\Omega\) block lists them. In this epoch Apertures 2.1 and 2.3 are exercised by no test, and Apertures 2.2 and 2.4 only by the flux-prediction family (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3); everything else is stated as untested, not as confirmed.

docs.title: Aperture 2.1: Condensed-Matter & Phase Transition Physics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{condensed}}\))
1. Epistemological & Physical Scope
docs.text:
Aperture 2.1 resolves how microscopic intermolecular interactions (hydrogen-bond and dipolar coordination networks, lattice bonding, crystal nucleation) generate macroscopic thermodynamic extensivity, cohesion, and transitions between fluid, amorphous, and crystalline states, and how a supersaturated phase relaxes by the diffusion-limited growth of a new phase. Lexicon is strictly restricted to statistical mechanics, condensed-matter physics, and chemical thermodynamics.

Declaration (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3; Branch II).

  • Domain \(\mathcal{M}\) (\(n = 3\)) and boundary \(\partial\mathcal{M}\). A condensed sample in which a dissolved component diffuses through a single host phase: a single-crystal solid solution, or a gel or quiescent solution column in which convection is suppressed. Smooth interior growth zones, fixed within the window, hold a dispersed second phase that grows by consuming the solute. \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) consists of a supply face in contact with a reservoir held at a declared concentration \(c_{\mathrm{s}} > c_{\mathrm{sat}}\), an outflow face held at saturation, and no-flux lateral faces. All supply crosses the supply face; there are no interior sources.
  • Window. A relaxation window (§0.1 item 1), opened by a declared step increase of \(c_{\mathrm{s}}\). It ends before the volume fraction of the second phase changes by more than a declared tolerance, so that \(\mathcal{M}\) and its growth zones are fixed.
  • Metric. Flat and rigid (§0.1 item 2): \(g_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu u}\) in a Cartesian chart.
  • Cone speed. \(c_*\) is the longitudinal sound speed of the host. Diffusive solute speeds (of order \(D/\ell\)) and growth-front speeds are \(\ll c_*\).
  • Free energy \(\mathcal{F}\) and datum. \(\mathcal{F} = \epsilon_{\mathrm{s}}(c - c_{\mathrm{sat}})\), with \(c\) the solute concentration (mol m⁻³) and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{s}} > 0\) a declared constant supersaturation yield (J mol⁻¹, the free energy per mole of excess solute at a declared reference supersaturation). The datum is saturation, \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0\). This is the declared linear form of aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3 item 3: the free energy of a supersaturated solution is not linear in \(c - c_{\mathrm{sat}}\), so the declaration is used only where \((c - c_{\mathrm{sat}})/c_{\mathrm{sat}}\) stays within a declared range. The relaxation time \(\ell^2/D\) is finite and resolvable.
  • Transport \(\mathfrak{K}\). \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = D^{\alpha eta}\), the solute diffusivity tensor, parametric along the host's crystal axes: one principal value for a cubic host, a gel, or a solution (the default \(D_{\mathcal{F}}g^{\alpha eta}\)), two for a uniaxial host, three for an orthorhombic host. Because \(\mathcal{F}\) is linear in \(c\), \(J_W = \epsilon_{\mathrm{s}}\,j\), with \(j\) the molar solute flux; \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{s}}\) is the declared conversion factor.
  • Sink \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\). \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = k_{\mathrm{g}}(\mathbf{x})(\mathcal{F} - \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}}) \ge 0\): growth kinetics first order in supersaturation, with \(k_{\mathrm{g}}\) a smooth, non-negative profile supported on the growth zones and fixed by a finite number of declared parameters (amplitude, centre, and width for each zone). A sharp growth front is represented by such a smooth zone.
  • Drive. Default, \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\) (§0.1 item 4).
  • Branch II evidence (closure (v)). The trend of \(\langle heta angle\) and a bound on \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\) come from dilatometric or interferometric measurement of the sample volume, which must stay within the rigid tolerance. \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) is estimated from measured dissipation (§0.1 item 6): the supply reservoir's depletion record and \(\mathcal{F}\) at the supply face give the boundary term, and growth rates measured in the growth zones, weighted by measured local \(\mathcal{F}\), give the consumption term. The physical dissipation of diffusion, the entropy produced as solute flows down its chemical-potential gradient, must share its sign.
  • Admissible domains (declared, checkable preconditions):
  • supersaturation throughout \(\mathcal{M}\) (\(c \ge c_{\mathrm{sat}}\), so \(\mathcal{F} \ge \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}}\)), with no nucleation of new growth zones and no dissolution during the window;
  • \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) throughout \( ar{\mathcal{M}}\), so no stagnant region lies behind a growth zone;
  • purely diffusive transport: no convection in a gel or solution, and no fast grain-boundary paths in the host;
  • isothermal conditions within a declared tolerance, so that \(c_{\mathrm{sat}}\) is constant;
  • volumetric strain of the sample within the rigid tolerance.
  • Titled phenomena outside the domain.
  • Nucleation lies before the window or outside \(\mathcal{M}\), and enters through the initial growth-zone configuration and \(\mathcal{H}_0\).
  • Phase transitions inside \(\mathcal{M}\) enter only through the declared growth zones and \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\). The latent heat they release is conducted away (precondition 4) and enters as context. Melting and solidification fronts lie on \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) or outside the window.
  • Intermolecular networks, cohesion, and surface tension set the material parameters (\(D^{\alpha eta}\), \(c_{\mathrm{sat}}\), \(k_{\mathrm{g}}\)), and the host's crystal symmetry sets the principal axes of \(\mathfrak{K}\).

docs.title: 2. Coordinate-by-Coordinate Mapping (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\))
\(O_0\) — Exogenous Flux & Emergent Foliation Time
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( heta \equiv -N K \overset{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0}{=} rac{1}{2}g^{\mu u} rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} = rac{1}{\sqrt{\vert g\vert}} rac{\partial\sqrt{\vert g\vert}}{\partial au} = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\); \(\Theta_E \equiv rac{\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}}{s_0} = - rac{ eta_{\mathrm{th}}}{s_0}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\); \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \sqrt{ heta^2 + \Theta_E^2}\), \( au_\Theta( au) \equiv \int_{ au_0}^{ au}\langle\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au'\); \( rac{dV_{\mathcal{M}}}{d au} = \int_{\mathcal{M}} heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\), with \(\lim_{ au o\infty}V_{\mathcal{M}}( au) = V_\infty < \infty\) (Branch II); \( rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), \(q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv -\ln(v_0Q(\mathbf{x}, au))\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The sample is rigid, so \( heta \equiv 0\), \(dV_{\mathcal{M}}/d au = 0\), and \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\) at every \( au\). The expansion current enters only through its vanishing divergence and boundary flux, and the solute supply is never mapped to it (§0.1 item 5). Openness is carried by throughput: diffusion of supersaturated solute from the supply face toward the growth zones and the outflow face produces entropy at every point, so \(\Theta_E > 0\) (by \(O_1\)) and \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} = \Theta_E\). \( au_\Theta\) counts entropy production per \(s_0\), while \( au\) remains laboratory proper time. Along the throughput current \(J_E^\mu = J_W^\mu/p_0\) the record accumulates by \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) (§0.1 item 9). The sample's physical memory of its growth history (the size distribution and arrangement of the second phase, growth banding) is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\) and is not identified with it.

docs.title: \(O_1\) — Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Openness
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} = p_0\oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} \equiv \int_{\mathcal{M}}(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F})\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} + \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\); \( abla_\mu\mathcal{F} eq 0\); \(J_E^\mu \equiv rac{J_W^\mu}{p_0} = - rac{1}{p_0}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\) (Branch II, fixed); \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\); \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The maintained concentration difference between the supply reservoir and the growth zones and outflow face holds the sample far from equilibrium. With \(J_E^\mu = -p_0^{-1}D^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\), \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} = -p_0^{-1} abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\,D^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F} < 0\) holds identically wherever \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) (precondition 2), so \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). The physical solute flux runs down the supersaturation gradient, from the supply face toward the growth zones and the outflow face, in the direction of \(J_E^\mu\). On the rigid sample \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0\), so \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). The empirical content of \(O_1\) is the flux-prediction test (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3, §5.5 item 6). The declared \(D^{\alpha eta}\) has its parameters estimated on the same sample per closure (ii), by a different modality (for example an isotope-tracer diffusion measurement) or in a declared perturbation regime run before the window. It must predict the flux \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}} = \epsilon_{\mathrm{s}}\,j^{\mathrm{meas}}\) measured across a declared surface \(S\) (for example the outflow face, from the solute uptake of the reservoir in contact with it), with \( abla\mathcal{F}\) from in-situ concentration profiling that uses neither \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}}\) nor the declared \(D^{\alpha eta}\) or \(k_{\mathrm{g}}\).

docs.title: \(O_2\) — Unimodular Weyl Factorization, Constraint Precision & Trajectories
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}( au, \mathbf{x}) = \Omega^2( au, \mathbf{x})\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) with \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) = 0 \implies \det g = \Omega^{2n}\), \( rac{\partial\ln\Omega}{\partial au} = rac{1}{n} heta\); \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\); \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\), \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\); \( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\); \(\left.\left( rac{dv^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}\), \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2)\left(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu ight)\), \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2 < 1\), with the default \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the rigid sample the unimodular Weyl split is trivial: \(\Omega \equiv 1\), \(\hat{h} \equiv 0\), \(\det g = 1\), and \(\partial_ au\ln\Omega = heta/3 = 0\). The split isolates the volume element only algebraically; \( heta\) remains coupled to \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) and to \(\sigma_{\alpha eta}\) through the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation (r10 Decision 2), whose two sides vanish identically on this domain (\(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\), \(\xi \equiv 0\), \(\sigma \equiv 0\); §0.1 items 2–3). The host's crystal lattice does not enter \(g\): its symmetry enters through the principal axes of \(D^{\alpha eta}\), and lattice strain around the second phase is context. \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\) is the Hessian of a declared precision potential and enters only the coupling sector (\(O_6\)). Eq. [3] is instantiated with the default drive, and on the static flat metric its solutions are straight lines traversed at constant speed. No tracer is mapped to it: solute transport is diffusive and is described by the \(O_4\) balance law, and growth fronts advance by interface kinetics.

docs.title: \(O_3\) — Shear Damping & Hysteresis Consolidation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\left. rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = rac{2}{n} heta g_{\mu u} + 2\sigma_{\mu u}\); \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv \partial_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) (\(\gamma_\sigma = \mathrm{const} > 0\), \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\mu} = 0\)) \(\implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\Vert_{C^2(\mathcal{M})} = 0\); \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\), \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)); \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the rigid sample \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv 0\), so the mixed-form shear law holds trivially for any \(\gamma_\sigma > 0\), \(\hat{h} = \hat{h}_\infty = 0\), and \(\hat{g}_\infty = \hat{g} = \delta\). This aperture supports no shear-relaxation test (§0.1 item 2). The relaxation of \(\mathcal{F}\) toward its new steady profile is a property of the \(O_4\) balance law and is not mapped to \(\sigma\). Shear relaxation of the host itself (for example Maxwell relaxation of a glass-forming melt) would require a deforming domain and lies outside this declaration. \(V_{\mathrm{local}}\) is the hysteresis content of a subregion \(\mathcal{U}_i\); the growth record of the second phase within \(\mathcal{U}_i\) is mapped to it via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\).

docs.title: \(O_4\) — Free-Energy Balance, Spectral Low-Pass Gating & Boundary Stress Conservation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( rac{\partial\mathcal{F}}{\partial au} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), \(J_W^\alpha \equiv -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = \mathfrak{K}^{ eta\alpha} \succ 0\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\); \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\); \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au) = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\); \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: With \( heta \equiv 0\) the balance law reads \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} = abla_\alpha(D^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}) - k_{\mathrm{g}}(\mathcal{F} - \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}})\): the linearized reaction–diffusion law of diffusion-limited growth from a supersaturated phase, first order in supersaturation. It follows its boundary data with the finite relaxation time \(\ell^2/D\), so the field is stored, not quasi-static. Every departure from the default (\(D_{\mathcal{F}}g^{\alpha eta}\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = 0\)) satisfies the binding closure. The anisotropic tensor and the growth law are named laws with finite pre-declared parameters, estimated independently and tested against pre-declared tolerances, and each is rejected if the default fits at least as well (closure (iv)). The gate sector follows §0.1 item 7: the Neumann eigenmodes of \(- abla^2\) on the rigid sample are fixed, so the gate does not drift, and the faster decay of fine spatial structure in \(\mathcal{F}\) is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the gate without being the gate. The stress-conservation equivalence holds identically (§0.1 item 3); elastic stresses in the lattice and around inclusions are not \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\) and enter as context.

docs.title: \(O_5\) — Riemannian Geometric Mean Gluing, Percolation & Harmonic Circulation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\); \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) geodesically convex for \(g^{(ij)}( au) \; orall au \ge au_0\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\); \(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\); \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\); \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} G_{\infty,\mu u}^{(i)} \succ 0\) (standing hypothesis with \(H_0 = 0\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: The cover consists of \( au\)-independent subregions of the sample, for example each growth zone with its surroundings and the host regions between them, with convex overlaps \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\). Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of the rigid metric, so the gluing holds identically, each overlap stays convex for every \( au\), \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} = 0\), and \(g^{(i)} = G_\infty^{(i)}\) at every \( au\) (\(H_0 = 0\); §0.1 item 8). Every overlap is crossed by the transient that follows the declared step, so \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\) (§0.1 item 8). Fast-diffusion networks in a polycrystalline host would enter through \(\mathfrak{K}\) and are excluded by precondition 3. The declared sample is simply connected, so \(\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} \equiv 0\) (§0.1 item 8).

docs.title: \(O_6\) — Asymmetric Phase-Lead Coupling & Trace-Free Deformation Operator
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\); \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) (hypothesis) \(\wedge \; \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\); \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u\,dA > 0\) (hypothesis, \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), with this boundary flux integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) (Branch II).
  • Physical Instantiation: Take a pair of adjacent subregions, for example a growth zone and the host region between it and the supply face. The partner fields are the rate of change of the solute free-energy flux in the two orientations (§0.1 item 8), so \(\eta_{[i o j]} = \partial_ au J_W\). On a declared overlap that the predicted zero set of \(\partial_ au J_W\) does not reach during the window (§0.1 item 8), \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) keeps one direction: toward the supply face where the flux is decaying from its overshoot, and away from it where the flux is rising. The odd 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\) is its image under the declared non-singular precision map and is non-zero there. Under the non-degeneracy hypothesis \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), with \(M^{(ij)}\) built per r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3] from these fields and the declared precision potentials, \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0\) gives \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\), with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general. Under the flux-positivity hypothesis the coupling transmits correlation between the subsystem marginals of the declared state sector (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\)). Both are standing hypotheses, not consequences of diffusion. In Branch II the transient decays as the sample approaches its new steady profile, so the coupling flux decays and is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\). With \(\sigma \equiv 0\) the overlaps keep their declared convex shape; the r10 §5.12 constraint \(a_\infty = 2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma < a_c(E)\), a design constraint of that witness, has no counterpart here.

docs.title: \(O_7\) — Principal-Bundle Gauge Coherence, Impedance Decay & Hysteresis Alignment
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(D_\mu = \partial_\mu - i g_{\mathrm{YM}}\,\mathrm{ad}_{A_\mu}\); \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\); \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2} o 1\), \(\hat{\chi} \equiv \chi_E\hat{u}\) (Branch II); \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The gauge sector is the trivial declaration of §0.1 item 9, so \([F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\) identically. With \(\sigma \equiv 0\), \(\chi_E \equiv 1\) and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu \equiv 0\) at every \( au\), while \(\chi\) itself is undefined because \( heta = 0\). \(\hat{ ho}_g = rac{1}{n}\delta^\mu_ u\) at every \( au\), so the alignment \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) o 0\) holds where the Hessian of the declared convex record becomes isotropic, an asymptotic condition stated and not tested. The \(O_7\) Eq. [3] flux identity holds with \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) and \(u_{\mathrm{exp}}\) both divergence-free, \(J_E\) is bounded in \(C^1\) under the held supply, and \(\mathcal{L}_{\mathbf{J}_E}(\hat{h} - \hat{h}_\infty) \equiv 0\). This aperture claims no orientational ordering, grain alignment, or annealing within the window.

docs.title: \(O_\Omega\) — Topological Asymptote, Branch II: Bounded Non-Equilibrium Steady State
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)): \( heta \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{C^2(\mathcal{M})} 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^{\infty}\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\); \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\) and \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\); \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q) rac{\delta\Psi}{\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})} \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{} 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} o 0\) (with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly as \( au o \infty\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: Under maintained supply the sample approaches a steady supersaturation profile: solute enters across the supply face and is consumed by growth and outflow. This is a bounded non-equilibrium steady state. \( heta \equiv 0\) (so \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au = 0\) and \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\)), \(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\) while supply is maintained, \(\sigma \equiv 0\), \(\partial_ au g \equiv 0\), and the transient coupling decays, so \(\mathcal{I}\) converges to \(s_0V_\infty\). The generator condition requires \(J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0\), that is, the gated density of the declared state sector must become uniform along the steady throughput current; this is an asymptotic hypothesis of the declared branch, which no finite window tests. The state is neither static equilibrium, which would require \(c = c_{\mathrm{sat}}\) throughout and no growth, nor a periodic return. The limit belongs to the declared idealization of fixed growth zones under maintained supply; the physical sample leaves that idealization when the second-phase fraction exceeds its tolerance, which bounds the usable window. Within windows the supported tests (aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5) are the non-degeneracy check (4), the signs of \(\Theta_E\), \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}\), and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}}\) (5), the flux prediction (6), and the Branch II evidence (7); tests (1)–(3) hold trivially on a rigid domain with \(\sigma \equiv 0\).

docs.title: Aperture 2.2: Continuum Fluid & Wave Mechanics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{continuum}}\))
1. Epistemological & Physical Scope
docs.text:
Aperture 2.2 maps the macroscopic mechanics of deformable fluid continua (viscous flow and boundary layers, vorticity transport, dispersive surface and internal waves, and diffraction around obstacles) onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\). Its empirical domain lies in the regime where these mechanics reduce to storage and diffusion: slow viscous flow through a deformable porous medium. Lexicon is strictly restricted to continuum mechanics, hydrodynamics, poromechanics, and linear and nonlinear wave theory.

Declaration (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3; Branch II).

  • Domain \(\mathcal{M}\) (\(n = 3\)) and boundary \(\partial\mathcal{M}\). A saturated, deformable porous medium with specific storage \(S_s > 0\), occupying a laterally confined column of length \(L\) along the axis \(x^3\). \(\mathcal{M}\) is the material region of the solid skeleton (material chart). \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) consists of an inlet boundary (supply) at a declared head \(h_{\mathrm{in}}\), an outlet boundary at the head \(h_{\mathrm{ref}}\), and impermeable lateral walls.
  • Window. A relaxation window (§0.1 item 1), opened by a declared step increase of \(h_{\mathrm{in}}\). The head then rises monotonically at every point, so pore pressure rises, effective stress falls, and the skeleton swells within its elastic, recoverable range.
  • Metric. Flat, with small-strain deformation (§0.1 item 2). Under lateral confinement the strain is uniaxial, so in the material chart \(g_{\mu u} = \mathrm{diag}(1, 1, (1+e)^2)\), with \(e(x^3, au)\) the axial strain. Then \( heta = \partial_ au\ln(1+e) \ge 0\) and \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = heta\,\mathrm{diag}(- frac{1}{3}, - frac{1}{3}, frac{2}{3})\).
  • Cone speed. \(c_*\) is the compressional wave speed of the saturated medium. Seepage velocities and skeleton speeds are \(\ll c_*\).
  • Free energy \(\mathcal{F}\) and datum. \(\mathcal{F} = ho g(h - h_{\mathrm{ref}})\), the head energy density (J m⁻³), with datum the outlet head (\(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0\)). Equivalently, \(\mathcal{F}\) is the stored water volume per unit volume, \(S_s(h - h_{\mathrm{ref}})\), times the declared conversion factor \( ho g/S_s\). Storage makes the relaxation time \(L^2/D\) finite; the incompressible creeping limit \(S_s o 0\) is quasi-static and is excluded.
  • Transport \(\mathfrak{K}\). \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = K_h^{\alpha eta}/S_s\), the hydraulic diffusivity tensor, with parametric anisotropy (declared principal values and axes); isotropic \(K_h\) is the default. With \(q\) the Darcy flux, \(J_W = ( ho g/S_s)\,q\).
  • Sink \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\). The default \(0\), or first-order leakage \(k_L(\mathcal{F} - \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}})\) to a drainage system at the outlet head, distributed through \(\mathcal{M}\), with \(k_L\) a declared rate constant. Leakage through a bounding wall is a boundary condition, not a sink.
  • Drive. Default, \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\) (§0.1 item 4).
  • Branch II evidence (closure (v)). The trend of \(\langle heta angle\) and a bound on \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\) (which equals \(\ln(V_{\mathcal{M}}( au_{\mathrm{obs}})/V_{\mathcal{M}}( au_0))\)) come from the column's axial-strain record, bounded by the final strain. \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) is estimated from measured dissipation (§0.1 item 6).
