Its leading term is the hydraulic power delivered at the inlet, \(( ho g/S_s)\, ho g(h_{\mathrm{in}} - h_{\mathrm{ref}})\,Q_{\mathrm{in}}\), with \(Q_{\mathrm{in}}\) from inlet flow metering and \(h_{\mathrm{in}}\) from an inlet transducer, not from the outlet volumetry and piezometers of the \(O_1\) test. The physical viscous dissipation of the through-flow, \( ho g K_h\vert abla h\vert^2\) per unit volume for isotropic \(K_h\), must share its sign.
  • Admissible domains (declared, checkable preconditions):
  • Darcy regime: pore Reynolds number \(\ll 1\), so inertia and recirculation are negligible;
  • \(h \ge h_{\mathrm{ref}}\) throughout (so \(\mathcal{F} \ge \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}}\)) and \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) throughout \( ar{\mathcal{M}}\);
  • elastic, recoverable skeleton deformation with volumetric strain \(\varepsilon_v \ll 1\) and \( heta \ge 0\) throughout the window, verified from the strain record. The linear storage equation and the r7 balance law then differ by terms of relative order \(\varepsilon_v\) (the \(\mathcal{F} heta\) term among them), and the pre-declared flux tolerance must exceed them. Windows that compact the skeleton are excluded;
  • no change of \(K_h\) or \(S_s\) within the window (no migration of fines or clogging beyond tolerance);
  • laterally uniform response, so that the strain is uniaxial.
  • Titled phenomena outside the domain.
  • Inertial flow governed by the full Navier–Stokes equations (boundary layers, vorticity transport, turbulence) lies outside the Darcy regime; pore-scale viscous flow is the microscale origin of \(K_h\) and enters through \(\mathfrak{K}\).
  • Waves enter in two ways: the compressional wave speed sets \(c_*\), and pressure waves arriving at the inlet are boundary data. Wave propagation through the column obeys a wave equation, not the storage–diffusion balance law, and lies outside the domain; wave rays are null or dispersive and are not trajectories of \(O_2\) Eq. [3].
  • Diffraction around obstacles and free-surface waves are illustrative context.

docs.title: 2. Coordinate-by-Coordinate Mapping (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\))
\(O_0\) — Exogenous Flux & Emergent Foliation Time
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( heta \equiv -N K \overset{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0}{=} rac{1}{2}g^{\mu u} rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} = rac{1}{\sqrt{\vert g\vert}} rac{\partial\sqrt{\vert g\vert}}{\partial au} = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\); \(\Theta_E \equiv rac{\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}}{s_0} = - rac{ eta_{\mathrm{th}}}{s_0}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\); \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \sqrt{ heta^2 + \Theta_E^2}\), \( au_\Theta( au) \equiv \int_{ au_0}^{ au}\langle\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au'\); \( rac{dV_{\mathcal{M}}}{d au} = \int_{\mathcal{M}} heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\), with \(\lim_{ au o\infty}V_{\mathcal{M}}( au) = V_\infty < \infty\) (Branch II); \( rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), \(q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv -\ln(v_0Q(\mathbf{x}, au))\).
  • Physical Instantiation: During the window the skeleton swells as pore pressure rises, so \( heta = \partial_ au\ln(1+e) \ge 0\). The volume growth \(dV_{\mathcal{M}}/d au = \int heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^3x \ge 0\) equals the boundary flux of an expansion current \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) of divergence \( heta\), of which only that divergence and boundary flux are used (§0.1 item 5); the inflow of water across the inlet is throughput and is never mapped to \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\). As the head approaches its new steady profile, \( heta o 0\) and \(V_{\mathcal{M}}\) approaches a finite \(V_\infty\). Openness is carried by throughput: viscous dissipation of the through-flow at every point gives \(\Theta_E > 0\) (by \(O_1\)). During the transient \( au_\Theta\) is driven by both \( heta\) and \(\Theta_E\), and by \(\Theta_E\) alone as \( heta o 0\). The record accumulates by \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) along the throughput current. Lasting changes of the porous fabric from earlier flow events (rearranged grains, altered pore structure) are mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\) and are not identified with it; within the window such changes are excluded (precondition 4).

docs.title: \(O_1\) — Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Openness
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} = p_0\oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} \equiv \int_{\mathcal{M}}(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F})\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} + \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\); \( abla_\mu\mathcal{F} eq 0\); \(J_E^\mu \equiv rac{J_W^\mu}{p_0} = - rac{1}{p_0}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\) (Branch II, fixed); \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\); \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The maintained head difference between inlet and outlet holds the medium far from equilibrium. With \(J_E^\mu = -p_0^{-1}(K_h^{\mu u}/S_s) abla_ u\mathcal{F}\), \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\) holds identically wherever \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\). The Darcy flux runs down the head gradient from inlet to outlet, in the direction of \(J_E^\mu\), so \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). The expansion work \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} \ge 0\) is positive during swelling and tends to \(0\), so \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} > 0\) is carried asymptotically by \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}}\). Measured hydraulic power tests the signs of \(\Theta_E\), \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}\), and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}}\) and is never identified with \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}}\). The empirical content of \(O_1\) is the flux-prediction test (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3, §5.5 item 6). The declared \(K_h^{\alpha eta}/S_s\) is estimated on the same specimen per closure (ii), for example from a pressure-pulse decay run as a declared perturbation regime before the window, with \(S_s\) from the specimen's measured compressibility. It must predict \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}} = ( ho g/S_s)\,q^{\mathrm{meas}}\) across a declared section \(S\), with \(q^{\mathrm{meas}}\) from outlet volumetry and \( abla\mathcal{F}\) from piezometers that use neither \(q^{\mathrm{meas}}\) nor \(\mathfrak{K}\).

docs.title: \(O_2\) — Unimodular Weyl Factorization, Constraint Precision & Trajectories
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}( au, \mathbf{x}) = \Omega^2( au, \mathbf{x})\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) with \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) = 0 \implies \det g = \Omega^{2n}\), \( rac{\partial\ln\Omega}{\partial au} = rac{1}{n} heta\); \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\); \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\), \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\); \( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\); \(\left.\left( rac{dv^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}\), \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2)\left(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu ight)\), \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2 < 1\), with the default \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The physical metric is the flat metric of the swelling skeleton, \(g_{\mu u} = \mathrm{diag}(1, 1, (1+e)^2)\) in the material chart. Its Weyl split has \(\Omega = (1+e)^{1/3}\) (so \(\det g = \Omega^6\)) and \(\hat{h}\) equal to the trace-free part of the logarithmic axial stretch, and \(\partial_ au\ln\Omega = heta/3\). The split isolates the volume element only algebraically; \( heta\) remains coupled to \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) and \(\sigma_{\alpha eta}\) through the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation (r10 Decision 2). On this domain (\(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\), \(\xi \equiv 0\); §0.1 item 3) it reduces to \( rac{2}{3} abla^2 heta = abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta}\), which the uniaxial strain rate satisfies identically because the metric stays flat. The anisotropy of the pore fabric is carried by \(\mathfrak{K}\), not by \(g\), and walls and grains enter as boundary data and through \(K_h\). \(\Pi_{\mu u}\) is the Hessian of a declared precision potential and enters only the coupling sector (\(O_6\)). Eq. [3] is instantiated with the default drive and maps no tracer. Fluid parcels in Darcy flow are driven by pressure gradients against drag, which is forced motion; no drag-law drive is declared in this epoch, so their paths are not trajectories of Eq. [3]. Wave rays are excluded (§0.1 item 4).

docs.title: \(O_3\) — Shear Damping & Hysteresis Consolidation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\left. rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = rac{2}{n} heta g_{\mu u} + 2\sigma_{\mu u}\); \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv \partial_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) (\(\gamma_\sigma = \mathrm{const} > 0\), \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\mu} = 0\)) \(\implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\Vert_{C^2(\mathcal{M})} = 0\); \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\), \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)); \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\).
  • Physical Instantiation: Under lateral confinement the trace-free strain rate is \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = heta\,\mathrm{diag}(- frac{1}{3}, - frac{1}{3}, frac{2}{3})\), so all its components share one time dependence. After the step, the head transient is a sum of decaying modes of the column. Once the higher modes have decayed below a declared tolerance, the slowest mode dominates and \(\sigma\) decays exponentially at a single constant rate. The aperture declares that rate as \(\gamma_\sigma = D_{33}\mu_1 + k_L\), with \(D_{33} = K_{33}/S_s\) and \(\mu_1 = \pi^2/L^2\) the lowest eigenvalue of \(-\partial_3^2\) on the column with fixed heads at inlet and outlet, all estimated independently before the window. Because the head rises monotonically, \(\sigma\) keeps one sign and does not oscillate. The shear rate decays while the accumulated deformation increases monotonically to its final value, so \(\hat{h} o \hat{h}_\infty\) (the final trace-free logarithmic stretch) and \((\hat{g}_\infty)_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu\alpha}(\exp\hat{h}_\infty)^\alpha_{\; u}\), with unit determinant. The late part of the window therefore supports the shear-rate test of aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5 item 1, with \(\gamma_\sigma\) predicted in advance, to within a declared residual from the higher modes; this aperture is not among the systems of the current shear-relaxation test (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3). \(V_{\mathrm{local}}\) is the hysteresis content of a layer; elastic recovery leaves no plastic record within the window.

docs.title: \(O_4\) — Free-Energy Balance, Spectral Low-Pass Gating & Boundary Stress Conservation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( rac{\partial\mathcal{F}}{\partial au} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), \(J_W^\alpha \equiv -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = \mathfrak{K}^{ eta\alpha} \succ 0\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\); \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\); \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au) = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\); \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the declared domain the balance law reads \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} + \mathcal{F} heta = abla_\alpha((K_h^{\alpha eta}/S_s) abla_ eta\mathcal{F}) - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\): the groundwater storage equation in energy-density form, with the \(\mathcal{F} heta\) term of relative order \(\varepsilon_v\) (precondition 3). Specific storage gives the finite relaxation time. Departures from the default (anisotropic \(K_h\), leakage) satisfy the binding closure, and each is rejected if the default fits at least as well (closure (iv)). The gate sector follows §0.1 item 7: the Neumann spectrum of \(- abla^2_g\) changes with \(g\) by a fraction of the order of the strain across the window, which is negligible, and it converges as \(g o G_\infty\). The faster decay of fine spatial structure in the head field is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the gate without being the gate. The stress-conservation equivalence holds identically (§0.1 item 3). The effective stress of the skeleton is not \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\); it enters through the boundary conditions and \(\mathcal{H}\).

docs.title: \(O_5\) — Riemannian Geometric Mean Gluing, Percolation & Harmonic Circulation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\); \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) geodesically convex for \(g^{(ij)}( au) \; orall au \ge au_0\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\); \(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\); \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\); \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} G_{\infty,\mu u}^{(i)} \succ 0\) (standing hypothesis with \(H_0 = 0\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: The cover consists of \( au\)-independent material layers of the column, with slab-shaped overlaps \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) perpendicular to its axis. Under laterally uniform uniaxial strain, planes perpendicular to the axis stay planar, so each overlap stays convex for \(g( au)\) at every \( au\). Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of \(g\), so the gluing holds identically (§0.1 item 8). \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} = heta\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\), and \(g^{(i)} o G_\infty^{(i)}\) as the strain approaches its final value (\(H_0 = 0\)). Every overlap is crossed by the transient, so \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\). The connectivity of the pore space is a property of the medium that enters through \(K_h\): a medium below its pore-percolation threshold has no continuum \(K_h\) and is not an admissible domain. That connectivity is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the condition \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} > \phi_c\) and is not identified with it. The declared column is simply connected, so \(\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} \equiv 0\) (§0.1 item 8). An annular column around an impermeable core, an illustration outside this declaration, would carry the harmonic Neumann field of its loop. Under isotropic \(K_h\) the Darcy flux is the gradient of a single-valued head and has no circulation around that loop, so that field would not be identified with it.

docs.title: \(O_6\) — Asymmetric Phase-Lead Coupling & Trace-Free Deformation Operator
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\); \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) (hypothesis) \(\wedge \; \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\); \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u\,dA > 0\) (hypothesis, \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), with this boundary flux integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) (Branch II).
  • Physical Instantiation: Take two layers of differing permeability that share a transition zone \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\). The partner fields are the rate of change of the head free-energy flux in the two orientations (§0.1 item 8), so \(\eta_{[i o j]} = \partial_ au J_W\): a spatially resolved flux field, not a temporal lag between scalar signals. With fixed heads at both ends, the late-time zero set of \(\partial_ au J_W\) is the column's mid-plane. Upstream of it \(\partial_ au J_W\) points toward the inlet, and downstream of it away from the inlet. The declared overlap is one that the predicted zero set does not reach during the window (§0.1 item 8), for example a transition zone in the downstream half that the predicted zero crossing, which travels downstream during the early window, never reaches. There the flux rises throughout the window and \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) points away from the inlet. The odd 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\) is its image under the declared non-singular precision map and is non-zero there. Under the non-degeneracy hypothesis \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), built per r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3] from these fields and the declared precision potentials, \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0\) gives \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\), with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general. The eigendirections are directions of the operator \(M^{(ij)}\); in the laterally confined column the transverse ones carry no flow. Under the flux-positivity hypothesis the coupling transmits correlation between the subsystem marginals of the declared state sector (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\)). Both are standing hypotheses. In Branch II the transient decays at the rate \(\gamma_\sigma\) of \(O_3\), so the coupling flux is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) and no sustained coupling is asserted. The planar overlaps remain convex at every \( au\), so the r10 §5.12 constraint \(a_\infty = 2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma < a_c(E)\), a design constraint of a curved witness overlap, does not apply. Any convexity threshold for curved overlaps in a deforming porous medium would be an aperture-level empirical conjecture mapped to that witness criterion, and none is asserted here.

docs.title: \(O_7\) — Principal-Bundle Gauge Coherence, Impedance Decay & Hysteresis Alignment
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(D_\mu = \partial_\mu - i g_{\mathrm{YM}}\,\mathrm{ad}_{A_\mu}\); \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\); \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2} o 1\), \(\hat{\chi} \equiv \chi_E\hat{u}\) (Branch II); \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The gauge sector is the trivial declaration of §0.1 item 9, so \([F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\) identically and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu o 0\) as \(\sigma o 0\). Here \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu} = rac{2}{3} heta^2\), so \(\chi_E - 1 = 2 heta^2/( heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle^2) o 0\) as \( heta o 0\) with \(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\). Once \( heta^2 \ll \langle\Theta_E angle^2\), late in the window, \(\chi_E - 1\) decays at \(2\gamma_\sigma\). Because \(\langle\Theta_E angle\) depends on \(s_0\), the onset of that regime is not \(s_0\)-independent, so the aperture's \(s_0\)-independent observable is the decay rate of \(\sigma\) itself (\(O_3\)). \(\chi\) is undefined where \( heta = 0\) and is not used. \(\hat{ ho}_g = e^{-\hat{h}_\infty}e^{\hat{h}}/\mathrm{Tr}(e^{-\hat{h}_\infty}e^{\hat{h}}) o rac{1}{n}\delta^\mu_ u\) as \(\hat{h} o \hat{h}_\infty\), a residual that decays at \(\gamma_\sigma\) and can be computed from the strain record. Alignment with \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}\) requires the Hessian of the record to become isotropic, an asymptotic condition stated and not tested. In \(O_7\) Eq. [3], \(u_{\mathrm{exp}}\) and \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) share the divergence \( heta\), so the boundary-flux identity holds; \(J_E\) is bounded in \(C^1\) and \(\hat{h} o \hat{h}_\infty\), so \(\mathcal{L}_{\mathbf{J}_E}(\hat{h} - \hat{h}_\infty) o 0\). No alignment of the flow with the porous fabric is claimed beyond what \(\mathfrak{K}\) declares.

docs.title: \(O_\Omega\) — Topological Asymptote, Branch II: Bounded Non-Equilibrium Steady State
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)): \( heta \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{C^2(\mathcal{M})} 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^{\infty}\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\); \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\) and \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\); \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q) rac{\delta\Psi}{\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})} \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{} 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} o 0\) (with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly as \( au o \infty\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: Under a maintained head difference the column approaches a steady head profile with continuing through-flow and dissipation: a bounded non-equilibrium steady state. Swelling ceases (\( heta o 0\)), \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\) is bounded by the final volumetric strain, \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\), \(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\), \(\sigma o 0\), and \(\partial_ au g o 0\). The transient coupling decays, so \(\mathcal{I} o s_0V_\infty\). The generator condition requires \(J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0\), an asymptotic hypothesis on the declared state sector that no finite window tests. The state is neither static equilibrium, which would require a uniform head and no flow, nor a periodic return. Within windows the supported tests (aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5) are the shear-rate test (1); decaying \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u}\) residuals at the rate \(\gamma_\sigma\) (3); the non-degeneracy check (4); the signs of \(\Theta_E\), \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}\), and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}}\) (5); the flux prediction (6); and the Branch II evidence (7). The \(\chi_E\) rate test (2) is not among them: its late-window regime has an \(s_0\)-dependent onset (see \(O_7\)), so \(\chi_E\) may be reported only as a quantity that is not \(s_0\)-independent.

docs.title: Aperture 2.3: Atmospheric Radiative & Thermal Boundary Physics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{radiative}}\))
1. Epistemological & Physical Scope
docs.text:
Aperture 2.3 maps the physics of electromagnetic radiation in matter and of atmospheric and other radiative-thermal boundary layers (absorption and emission, Rayleigh and Mie scattering, Fresnel partitioning at interfaces, refraction, and the coupling of radiation to sensible heat) onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\). Its empirical domain lies in the regime where radiative transfer becomes a storage–diffusion process: an optically thick layer in local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE). Lexicon is strictly restricted to radiative transfer, atmospheric physics, non-equilibrium thermodynamics, and geometrical and physical optics.

Declaration (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3; Branch II).

  • Domain \(\mathcal{M}\) (\(n = 3\)) and boundary \(\partial\mathcal{M}\). An optically thick layer in LTE through which radiation diffuses: a translucent condensed or particulate medium, or an optically thick, convectively stable gas layer. The layer's upper face, the irradiated boundary (supply), lies several extinction lengths below the physical surface on which radiation is incident, at a depth where the incident radiation has been absorbed. The absorbed flux therefore enters \(\mathcal{M}\) across this face, and the absorption layer above it lies outside \(\mathcal{M}\). The lower boundary is held at the temperature \(T_{\mathrm{ref}}\), and the lateral faces are adiabatic. The absorbed flux is laterally uniform across the supply face, so the declared problem is one-dimensional in \(x^3\).
  • Window. A relaxation window (§0.1 item 1), opened by a declared step increase of the absorbed flux. The temperature then rises monotonically at every point, so any residual thermal expansion is non-negative.
  • Metric. Flat and rigid (§0.1 item 2): \(g_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu u}\) in a Cartesian chart, with thermal expansion within the rigid tolerance.
  • Cone speed. \(c_* = c/n_r\), the speed of radiation in the medium, with \(n_r\) its refractive index. Radiation rays are null for this cone; all material speeds are \(\ll c_*\).
  • Free energy \(\mathcal{F}\) and datum. \(\mathcal{F} = ho c_{\mathrm{eff}}(T - T_{\mathrm{ref}})\), the effective thermal energy density, linearized about the datum \(T_{\mathrm{ref}}\) of the lower boundary (\(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0\)). Storage is dominated by the heat capacity of the matter: the radiation's own heat capacity per unit volume, \(4aT^3\), is negligible against \( ho c_{\mathrm{eff}}\). The relaxation time \(\ell^2/D_R\) is finite and resolvable.
  • Transport \(\mathfrak{K}\). \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = D_R(x^3)\,g^{\alpha eta}\), with \(D_R = 16\sigma_{\mathrm{SB}}T_{\mathrm{ref}}^3/(3\kappa_R ho c_{\mathrm{eff}})\), the effective radiative diffusivity. \(\kappa_R(x^3)\) is the Rosseland mean extinction coefficient (m⁻¹), stratified with a declared parametric profile, and \(T^3\) is evaluated at the declared reference; constant \(\kappa_R\) is the default. Then \(J_W = -D_R abla\mathcal{F} = -k_R abla T\), with \(k_R = 16\sigma_{\mathrm{SB}}T_{\mathrm{ref}}^3/(3\kappa_R)\): the radiative heat flux (W m⁻²), so the only conversion factor is \( ho c_{\mathrm{eff}}\).
  • Sink \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\). Default, \(0\): in LTE local emission balances local absorption, so there is no net interior loss.
  • Drive. Default, \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\) (§0.1 item 4).
  • Branch II evidence (closure (v)). The trend of \(\langle heta angle\) and a bound on \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\) come from dilatometric or thickness measurement of the layer, which must stay within the rigid tolerance. \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) is estimated from measured dissipation (§0.1 item 6), using a heat-flux and temperature record at the supply face, separate from the interior section and sensors of the \(O_1\) test. The physical entropy production of heat flowing down a temperature gradient, \(k_R\vert abla T\vert^2/T^2\) per unit volume, must share its sign.
  • Admissible domains (declared, checkable preconditions):
  • optical depth \(\gg 1\) across \(\mathcal{M}\) and on the scale of its temperature gradients, so the diffusion approximation holds. The error it makes within about one extinction length of each boundary falls within the declared tolerance, which requires the extinction length to be small against the layer thickness;
  • LTE, with no phase change and no chemical heat release in \(\mathcal{M}\) (no interior source or sink);
  • no convection or other advection;
  • \(\vert T - T_{\mathrm{ref}}\vert \ll T_{\mathrm{ref}}\), so that the \(T^3\) linearization holds within tolerance, and radiative transport dominates conduction by the matter, so that \(D_R\) is the effective diffusivity within tolerance;
  • \(T \ge T_{\mathrm{ref}}\) throughout (so \(\mathcal{F} \ge \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}}\)) and \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) throughout \( ar{\mathcal{M}}\);
  • thermal expansion within the rigid tolerance, and \(\kappa_R\) constant in time (no sintering, recrystallization, or compositional change within the window).
  • laterally uniform absorbed flux, checked by radiometry across the supply face to within a declared tolerance.
  • Titled phenomena outside the domain.
  • Rayleigh and Mie scattering and spectral absorption enter only through \(\kappa_R\), the Rosseland mean of the medium's extinction spectrum.
  • Fresnel partitioning, refraction, and the absorption of the incident beam at and above the supply face enter as boundary data, through the absorbed flux.
  • Geometrical-optics rays, caustics, and refracted beams are null and are not trajectories of \(O_2\) Eq. [3].
  • Optically thin atmospheric layers, convective boundary layers, and turbulent exchange lie outside the diffusion regime and enter as boundary conditions or context. Latent-heat exchange at a two-medium boundary lies on or outside \(\partial\mathcal{M}\).

docs.title: 2. Coordinate-by-Coordinate Mapping (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\))
\(O_0\) — Exogenous Flux & Emergent Foliation Time
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( heta \equiv -N K \overset{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0}{=} rac{1}{2}g^{\mu u} rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} = rac{1}{\sqrt{\vert g\vert}} rac{\partial\sqrt{\vert g\vert}}{\partial au} = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\); \(\Theta_E \equiv rac{\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}}{s_0} = - rac{ eta_{\mathrm{th}}}{s_0}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\); \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \sqrt{ heta^2 + \Theta_E^2}\), \( au_\Theta( au) \equiv \int_{ au_0}^{ au}\langle\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au'\); \( rac{dV_{\mathcal{M}}}{d au} = \int_{\mathcal{M}} heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\), with \(\lim_{ au o\infty}V_{\mathcal{M}}( au) = V_\infty < \infty\) (Branch II); \( rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), \(q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv -\ln(v_0Q(\mathbf{x}, au))\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The layer is rigid, so \( heta \equiv 0\), \(dV_{\mathcal{M}}/d au = 0\), and \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\); the absorbed supply is throughput and is never mapped to \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) (§0.1 item 5). Radiative diffusion of energy from the supply face to the lower boundary produces entropy at every point, so \(\Theta_E > 0\) (by \(O_1\)), \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} = \Theta_E\), and \( au_\Theta\) counts entropy production per \(s_0\). The record accumulates by \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) along the throughput current. Lasting changes of the medium under its irradiation history, such as sintering or recrystallization of a particulate layer, are mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\) and are not identified with it; within the window they are excluded (precondition 6). The temperature profile itself is \(\mathcal{F}\), not the record.

docs.title: \(O_1\) — Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Openness
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} = p_0\oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} \equiv \int_{\mathcal{M}}(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F})\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} + \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\); \( abla_\mu\mathcal{F} eq 0\); \(J_E^\mu \equiv rac{J_W^\mu}{p_0} = - rac{1}{p_0}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\) (Branch II, fixed); \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\); \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The layer sits between the absorbed supply and the colder lower boundary and is held far from equilibrium by the energy flux between them. With \(J_E^\mu = -p_0^{-1}D_R abla^\mu\mathcal{F}\), \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} = -p_0^{-1}D_R\vert abla\mathcal{F}\vert^2 < 0\) holds identically wherever \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\). The radiative heat flux runs down the temperature gradient from the supply face to the lower boundary, in the direction of \(J_E^\mu\), so \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). On the rigid layer \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). The empirical content of \(O_1\) is the flux-prediction test (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3, §5.5 item 6). The parameters of \(\kappa_R(x^3)\) are estimated on the specimen itself by a different modality, for example spectral transmission measurements averaged with the Rosseland weight, and \(c_{\mathrm{eff}}\) by calorimetry. The declared law must then predict the heat flux \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}}\) measured across a declared interior section \(S\), with \( abla T\) from embedded thermometry that uses neither \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}}\) nor \(\kappa_R\). No current test exercises this aperture (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3).

docs.title: \(O_2\) — Unimodular Weyl Factorization, Constraint Precision & Trajectories
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}( au, \mathbf{x}) = \Omega^2( au, \mathbf{x})\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) with \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) = 0 \implies \det g = \Omega^{2n}\), \( rac{\partial\ln\Omega}{\partial au} = rac{1}{n} heta\); \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\); \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\), \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\); \( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\); \(\left.\left( rac{dv^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}\), \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2)\left(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu ight)\), \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2 < 1\), with the default \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the rigid layer the unimodular Weyl split is trivial (\(\Omega \equiv 1\), \(\hat{h} \equiv 0\), \(\partial_ au\ln\Omega = 0\)). The split isolates the volume element only algebraically; \( heta\) remains coupled to \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) and \(\sigma_{\alpha eta}\) through the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation (r10 Decision 2), whose two sides vanish identically here (§0.1 items 2–3). The refractive-index field and any birefringence do not enter \(g\). The optical (Fermat) metric of ray optics is a different object from the physical metric and is not mapped to \(g_{\mu u}\); the refractive index enters only through \(c_*\), \(\kappa_R\), and the boundary data. Dielectric interfaces, where Snell's law and Fresnel partitioning apply, lie on or outside \(\partial\mathcal{M}\). \(\Pi_{\mu u}\) is the Hessian of a declared precision potential and enters only the coupling sector (\(O_6\)). Eq. [3] is instantiated with the default drive and maps no tracer. Radiation is null for the declared cone, dispersive wavepackets follow Hamiltonian ray equations (\(\dot{x}^\mu = \partial\omega/\partial k_\mu\)), and the diffusing energy is described by the \(O_4\) balance law; none of these is a timelike trajectory of Eq. [3].

docs.title: \(O_3\) — Shear Damping & Hysteresis Consolidation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\left. rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = rac{2}{n} heta g_{\mu u} + 2\sigma_{\mu u}\); \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv \partial_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) (\(\gamma_\sigma = \mathrm{const} > 0\), \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\mu} = 0\)) \(\implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\Vert_{C^2(\mathcal{M})} = 0\); \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\), \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)); \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the rigid layer \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv 0\), so the shear law holds trivially, \(\hat{h} = \hat{h}_\infty = 0\), and \(\hat{g}_\infty = \hat{g} = \delta\); this aperture supports no shear-relaxation test (§0.1 item 2). The relaxation of the temperature profile toward its new steady state, which proceeds through modes decaying at rates set by \(D_R\) and the layer thickness, is a property of the \(O_4\) balance law and is not mapped to \(\sigma\). Thermal-stress deformation of the layer lies outside the rigid declaration. \(V_{\mathrm{local}}\) is the hysteresis content of a layer \(\mathcal{U}_i\).

docs.title: \(O_4\) — Free-Energy Balance, Spectral Low-Pass Gating & Boundary Stress Conservation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( rac{\partial\mathcal{F}}{\partial au} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), \(J_W^\alpha \equiv -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = \mathfrak{K}^{ eta\alpha} \succ 0\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\); \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\); \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au) = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\); \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: With \( heta \equiv 0\) and \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = 0\) the balance law reads \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} = abla_\alpha(D_R(x^3) abla^\alpha\mathcal{F})\): linearized radiative diffusion in the Rosseland approximation, with heat storage in the matter. The stratified \(\kappa_R(x^3)\) departs from the default constant diffusivity and satisfies the binding closure; it is rejected if the constant default fits at least as well (closure (iv)). The gate sector follows §0.1 item 7: the Neumann eigenmodes of \(- abla^2\) on the rigid layer are fixed, so the gate does not drift, and the faster decay of fine spatial structure in the temperature field is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the gate without being the gate. The gate is a spatial filter and is distinct from any spectral (wavelength) filtering of the incident beam above the supply face. The stress-conservation equivalence holds identically (§0.1 item 3).

docs.title: \(O_5\) — Riemannian Geometric Mean Gluing, Percolation & Harmonic Circulation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\); \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) geodesically convex for \(g^{(ij)}( au) \; orall au \ge au_0\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\); \(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\); \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\); \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} G_{\infty,\mu u}^{(i)} \succ 0\) (standing hypothesis with \(H_0 = 0\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: The cover consists of \( au\)-independent layers of differing \(\kappa_R\), with slab-shaped overlaps \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) that stay convex on the rigid metric. Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of \(g\), so the gluing holds identically, \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} = 0\), and \(g^{(i)} = G_\infty^{(i)}\) at every \( au\) (\(H_0 = 0\); §0.1 item 8). Every overlap is crossed by the transient, so \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\). In a particulate medium the connectivity of radiative pathways between particles enters through \(\kappa_R\); it is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the percolation condition and is not identified with it. The declared layer is simply connected, so \(\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} \equiv 0\) (§0.1 item 8).

docs.title: \(O_6\) — Asymmetric Phase-Lead Coupling & Trace-Free Deformation Operator
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\); \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) (hypothesis) \(\wedge \; \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\); \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u\,dA > 0\) (hypothesis, \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), with this boundary flux integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) (Branch II).
  • Physical Instantiation: Take two layers of differing \(\kappa_R\) that share a transition zone \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\). The partner fields are the rate of change of the radiative heat flux in the two orientations (§0.1 item 8): a spatially resolved flux field across the zone, not a temporal lag between scalar signals. Because the supply is a prescribed absorbed flux, after the step the flux at the supply face is held constant, so \(\partial_ au J_W = 0\) there. The lower boundary is held at fixed temperature, so the flux has zero gradient there. With a laterally uniform supply (precondition 7) the flux \(J = -D_R\partial_3\mathcal{F}\) obeys the autonomous parabolic law \(\partial_ au J = D_R\partial_3^2 J\). The prior uniform flux is a subsolution for the raised supply flux, so comparison gives \(J(\cdot, au_0 + h) \ge J(\cdot, au_0)\), and time-translation invariance then gives \(J(\cdot, au + h) \ge J(\cdot, au)\), that is, \(\partial_ au J_W \ge 0\). The strong maximum principle, with Hopf's lemma at the lower face, makes it positive everywhere except on the supply face. Its zero set is therefore the supply face itself, and on every declared overlap away from that face \(\eta_{[i o j]} = \partial_ au J_W\) points away from the supply face throughout the window (§0.1 item 8). The odd 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\) is its image under the declared non-singular precision map and is non-zero there. Under the non-degeneracy hypothesis \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), built per r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3], \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0\) gives \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\), with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general. The eigendirections are directions of the operator \(M^{(ij)}\), not of separate fluxes; in the laterally adiabatic layer the transverse ones carry no flux. Under the flux-positivity hypothesis the coupling transmits correlation between the subsystem marginals of the declared state sector (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\)). Both are standing hypotheses. In Branch II the transient decays as the layer settles, so the coupling flux is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\). With \(\sigma \equiv 0\) the overlaps keep their declared convex shape, and the r10 §5.12 constraint has no counterpart here. Sensible and latent heat exchange across a boundary between two different media lies on or outside \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) (precondition 2).

docs.title: \(O_7\) — Principal-Bundle Gauge Coherence, Impedance Decay & Hysteresis Alignment
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(D_\mu = \partial_\mu - i g_{\mathrm{YM}}\,\mathrm{ad}_{A_\mu}\); \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\); \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2} o 1\), \(\hat{\chi} \equiv \chi_E\hat{u}\) (Branch II); \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The gauge sector is the trivial declaration of §0.1 item 9, so \([F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\) identically. With \(\sigma \equiv 0\), \(\chi_E \equiv 1\) and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu \equiv 0\) at every \( au\), and \(\chi\) is undefined (\( heta = 0\)). \(\hat{ ho}_g = rac{1}{n}\delta^\mu_ u\) at every \( au\), and alignment with \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}\) holds where the Hessian of the declared convex record becomes isotropic, an asymptotic condition stated and not tested. The \(O_7\) Eq. [3] identities hold with divergence-free \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) and \(u_{\mathrm{exp}}\), bounded \(J_E\), and \(\hat{h} \equiv \hat{h}_\infty\). No alignment of the energy distribution with a stored profile is claimed beyond these declarations.

docs.title: \(O_\Omega\) — Topological Asymptote, Branch II: Bounded Non-Equilibrium Steady State
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)): \( heta \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{C^2(\mathcal{M})} 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^{\infty}\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\); \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\) and \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\); \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q) rac{\delta\Psi}{\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})} \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{} 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} o 0\) (with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly as \( au o \infty\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: Under maintained irradiation the layer approaches a steady temperature profile that carries a steady energy flux from the supply face to the lower boundary: a bounded non-equilibrium steady state. \( heta \equiv 0\), \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\), \(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\) while the absorbed flux is maintained, \(\sigma \equiv 0\), \(\partial_ au g \equiv 0\), and the transient coupling decays, so \(\mathcal{I} o s_0V_\infty\). The generator condition requires \(J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0\), an asymptotic hypothesis on the declared state sector that no finite window tests. The state is neither thermodynamic equilibrium at a uniform temperature, which would carry no flux, nor a periodic return. Within windows the supported tests (aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5) are the non-degeneracy check (4), the signs of \(\Theta_E\), \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}\), and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}}\) (5), the flux prediction (6), and the Branch II evidence (7); tests (1)–(3) hold trivially on the rigid layer.

docs.title: Aperture 2.4: Geomorphic & Structural Mechanics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{tectonic}}\))
1. Epistemological & Physical Scope
docs.text:
Aperture 2.4 maps the mechanics of solid-earth substrates and load-bearing bodies (landform evolution, sediment transport and bedform memory, consolidation and swelling of saturated soils and rocks, and the stress fields of structures) onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\). Its empirical domain is the saturated stratum of a landform or load-bearing earth body, where pore-pressure diffusion couples groundwater flow to the deformation of the solid skeleton. Lexicon is strictly restricted to geomorphology, sedimentology, hydrogeology, geotechnical engineering, and structural mechanics.

Declaration (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3; Branch II).

  • Domain \(\mathcal{M}\) (\(n = 3\)) and boundary \(\partial\mathcal{M}\). A confined aquifer stratum within a landform or load-bearing earth body: a saturated, deformable porous stratum bounded above and below by confining layers, which lie outside \(\mathcal{M}\) and are treated as no-flow boundaries. \(\mathcal{M}\) is the material region of the stratum's skeleton (material chart). \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) consists of a recharge boundary (supply) at a declared head, a drain boundary at the drain level \(h_{\mathrm{ref}}\), and the no-flow confining surfaces.
  • Window. A relaxation window (§0.1 item 1), opened by a declared increase of the recharge-boundary head from a prior steady state, after which the head is held. Pore pressure then rises monotonically at every point and the stratum swells elastically, which is the recoverable rebound counterpart of consolidation. Windows that compact the stratum (consolidation under added load, or a declining head) give \( heta < 0\) and are excluded.
  • Metric. Flat, with small-strain deformation (§0.1 item 2): the pull-back of the Euclidean metric under the measured displacement field of the skeleton. For a laterally extensive stratum the strain is approximately uniaxial and normal to the bedding, and \( heta \ge 0\).
  • Cone speed. \(c_*\) is the compressional wave speed of the saturated stratum. Seepage velocities and deformation speeds are \(\ll c_*\).
  • Free energy \(\mathcal{F}\) and datum. \(\mathcal{F} = ho g(h - h_{\mathrm{ref}})\), the head energy density, with datum the drain level (\(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0\)): the stored water volume per unit volume, \(S_s(h - h_{\mathrm{ref}})\), times the declared conversion factor \( ho g/S_s\). Storage makes the relaxation time finite and resolvable.
  • Transport \(\mathfrak{K}\). Layered hydraulic diffusivity, \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = \mathrm{diag}(D_H, D_H, D_V)\) in a chart aligned with the bedding, with \(D_H = K_H/S_s\) and \(D_V = K_V/S_s\) (two declared parameters, plus the declared bedding orientation). With \(q\) the Darcy flux, \(J_W = ( ho g/S_s)\,q\).
  • Sink \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\). \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = k_L(\mathcal{F} - \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}}) \ge 0\): distributed leakage through interbedded semi-confining layers to a drainage system at the drain level, with \(k_L\) a declared rate constant. In this quasi-three-dimensional idealization \(k_L\) is of order \(K'/(b'bS_s)\), for semi-confining layers of conductivity \(K'\) and thickness \(b'\) in a stratum of thickness \(b\). Leakage across a bounding confining layer is a boundary condition, not a sink.
  • Drive. Default, \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\) (§0.1 item 4).
  • Branch II evidence (closure (v)). The trend of \(\langle heta angle\) and a bound on \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au = \ln(V_{\mathcal{M}}( au_{\mathrm{obs}})/V_{\mathcal{M}}( au_0))\) come from geodetic surface uplift and borehole extensometers, bounded by the final uplift. \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) is estimated from measured dissipation (§0.1 item 6). The boundary term uses the recharge-boundary record (recharge rate and head), and the leakage term uses the declared, independently estimated \(k_L\) with \(\mathcal{F}\) from a set of piezometers not used for the \(O_1\) gradient. The physical viscous dissipation of the groundwater flow must share its sign.
  • Admissible domains (declared, checkable preconditions):
  • Darcy regime;
  • \(h \ge h_{\mathrm{ref}}\) throughout (so \(\mathcal{F} \ge \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}}\)) and \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) throughout \( ar{\mathcal{M}}\);
  • elastic, recoverable swelling with volumetric strain \(\varepsilon_v \ll 1\) and \( heta \ge 0\) throughout the window, verified from the deformation record. The linear storage equation and the r7 balance law then differ by terms of relative order \(\varepsilon_v\), which the pre-declared flux tolerance must exceed;
  • no erosion, deposition, or change of load on \(\mathcal{M}\) within the window; these act on \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) or between windows;
  • \(K_H\), \(K_V\), \(S_s\), and \(k_L\) constant within the window.
  • Titled phenomena outside the domain.
  • Landform evolution acts at the ground surface, outside \(\mathcal{M}\), and between windows: erosion, deposition, and the divergence-form Exner sediment balance. It enters through changed loads and boundary heads and through \(\mathcal{H}\).
  • Bedforms, granular bedload, and saltation are forced transport outside the domain; no drive is declared for them in this epoch.
  • Consolidation under loading (\( heta < 0\)) and visco-plastic creep lie outside the declared windows.
  • Structural stress fields (overburden, effective stress, the stresses of load-bearing spans) and their principal-stress lines, arches, and catenaries are equilibrium objects. They enter through the boundary conditions and \(\mathcal{H}\), not through \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\) or \(O_2\) Eq. [3].
  • Granular force-chain networks in the skeleton set its compressibility, and hence \(S_s\) and \(\mathfrak{K}\), and enter otherwise as context. Fault and contact-zone mechanics lie outside the domain.

docs.title: 2. Coordinate-by-Coordinate Mapping (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\))
\(O_0\) — Exogenous Flux & Emergent Foliation Time
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( heta \equiv -N K \overset{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0}{=} rac{1}{2}g^{\mu u} rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} = rac{1}{\sqrt{\vert g\vert}} rac{\partial\sqrt{\vert g\vert}}{\partial au} = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\); \(\Theta_E \equiv rac{\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}}{s_0} = - rac{ eta_{\mathrm{th}}}{s_0}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\); \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \sqrt{ heta^2 + \Theta_E^2}\), \( au_\Theta( au) \equiv \int_{ au_0}^{ au}\langle\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au'\); \( rac{dV_{\mathcal{M}}}{d au} = \int_{\mathcal{M}} heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\), with \(\lim_{ au o\infty}V_{\mathcal{M}}( au) = V_\infty < \infty\) (Branch II); \( rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), \(q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv -\ln(v_0Q(\mathbf{x}, au))\).
  • Physical Instantiation: During the window the stratum swells as pore pressure rises, so \( heta \ge 0\), and the surface rises. The volume growth equals the boundary flux of an expansion current of divergence \( heta\), of which only that divergence and boundary flux are used (§0.1 item 5); recharge is throughput and is never mapped to \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\). As the head approaches its new steady field, \( heta o 0\) and \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\). Openness is carried by throughput: groundwater flow from recharge to drain and leakage dissipates energy at every point, so \(\Theta_E > 0\) (by \(O_1\)), and \( au_\Theta\) is driven by \( heta\) and \(\Theta_E\) during the transient and by \(\Theta_E\) alone as \( heta o 0\). The record accumulates by \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) along the throughput current. The stratum's consolidation and stress history (its preconsolidation state, fabric, and stratigraphic record) is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\), and enters each window through the declared \(\mathcal{H}_0\). The sediment mass balance at the surface is the Exner equation; its memory content is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the hysteresis law, which is not itself the Exner equation.

docs.title: \(O_1\) — Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Openness
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} = p_0\oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} \equiv \int_{\mathcal{M}}(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F})\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} + \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\); \( abla_\mu\mathcal{F} eq 0\); \(J_E^\mu \equiv rac{J_W^\mu}{p_0} = - rac{1}{p_0}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\) (Branch II, fixed); \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\); \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The maintained head difference between the recharge and drain boundaries holds the stratum far from equilibrium. With \(J_E^\mu = -p_0^{-1}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\) for the layered \(\mathfrak{K}\), \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\) holds identically wherever \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\). Groundwater flows down the head gradient from recharge to drain, in the direction of \(J_E^\mu\), so \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} \ge 0\) is positive during uplift and tends to \(0\), so \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} > 0\) is carried asymptotically by \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}}\). The empirical content of \(O_1\) is the flux-prediction test (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3, §5.5 item 6). \(D_H\) and \(D_V\) are estimated per closure (ii) from a declared hydraulic perturbation test on the same stratum before the window, with the skeleton part of \(S_s\) from the stratum's measured strain response to a known head change and the water-compressibility part from tabulated values. The declared law must predict \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}} = ( ho g/S_s)\,q^{\mathrm{meas}}\) across a declared section \(S\), for example from measured drain discharge, with \( abla\mathcal{F}\) from piezometers that use neither \(q^{\mathrm{meas}}\) nor \(\mathfrak{K}\).

docs.title: \(O_2\) — Unimodular Weyl Factorization, Constraint Precision & Trajectories
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}( au, \mathbf{x}) = \Omega^2( au, \mathbf{x})\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) with \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) = 0 \implies \det g = \Omega^{2n}\), \( rac{\partial\ln\Omega}{\partial au} = rac{1}{n} heta\); \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\); \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\), \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\); \( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\); \(\left.\left( rac{dv^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}\), \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2)\left(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu ight)\), \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2 < 1\), with the default \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The physical metric is the flat pull-back metric of the swelling skeleton. Its Weyl split puts the local volume ratio in \(\Omega^n = \sqrt{\det g}\) and the trace-free part of the logarithmic strain in \(\hat{h}\), with \(\partial_ au\ln\Omega = heta/3\). The split isolates the volume element only algebraically; \( heta\) remains coupled to \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) and \(\sigma_{\alpha eta}\) through the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation (r10 Decision 2). On this domain (\(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\), \(\xi \equiv 0\); §0.1 item 3) it reduces to \( rac{2}{3} abla^2 heta = abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta}\), the traced Saint-Venant compatibility, which the skeleton's strain rate satisfies because its metric stays flat. Bedrock strata and load-bearing spans do not curve the physical metric: their stresses balance applied load in the Cauchy sense, which is not \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\). \(\Pi_{\mu u}\) is the Hessian of a declared precision potential and enters only the coupling sector (\(O_6\)). Eq. [3] is instantiated with the default drive and maps no tracer. Principal-stress lines are integral curves of eigenvector fields of the stress, and funicular arches and catenaries solve equilibrium problems, so neither is a trajectory of Eq. [3]. Bedload is forced and frictional, and saltating grains are accelerated by gravity and drag; no drive is declared for them in this epoch.

docs.title: \(O_3\) — Shear Damping & Hysteresis Consolidation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\left. rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = rac{2}{n} heta g_{\mu u} + 2\sigma_{\mu u}\); \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv \partial_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) (\(\gamma_\sigma = \mathrm{const} > 0\), \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\mu} = 0\)) \(\implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\Vert_{C^2(\mathcal{M})} = 0\); \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\), \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)); \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The trace-free part of the skeleton's strain rate is \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\); for approximately uniaxial strain normal to the bedding it is proportional to \( heta\), with \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu} \approx rac{2}{3} heta^2\). After the declared increase, the head transient is a sum of decaying modes of the stratum. Once the higher modes have decayed below a declared tolerance, the slowest mode dominates and \(\sigma\) decays exponentially at a single constant rate. The aperture declares that rate as \(\gamma_\sigma = \lambda_1\), the lowest eigenvalue of \(- abla_\alpha(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\,\cdot\,) + k_L\) on the stratum, with fixed heads on the recharge and drain boundaries and no flow across the confining surfaces, computed from the independently estimated parameters. This is the swelling counterpart of Terzaghi consolidation. The head rises monotonically, so \(\sigma\) keeps one sign. The shear rate decays while the accumulated strain increases monotonically to its final value, so \(\hat{h} o \hat{h}_\infty\) and \((\hat{g}_\infty)_{\mu u} = \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\exp\hat{h}_\infty)^\alpha_{\; u}\), with unit determinant. The late part of the window supports the shear-rate test of aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5 item 1, with \(\gamma_\sigma\) predicted in advance, to within a declared residual from the higher modes; this aperture is not among the systems of the current shear-relaxation test. Elastic swelling leaves no plastic record in the window, so \(V_{\mathrm{local}}\), the hysteresis content of a stratum, carries the earlier plastic history entered through \(\mathcal{H}_0\).

docs.title: \(O_4\) — Free-Energy Balance, Spectral Low-Pass Gating & Boundary Stress Conservation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( rac{\partial\mathcal{F}}{\partial au} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), \(J_W^\alpha \equiv -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = \mathfrak{K}^{ eta\alpha} \succ 0\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\); \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\); \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au) = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\); \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the declared domain the balance law reads \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} + \mathcal{F} heta = abla_\alpha(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}) - k_L(\mathcal{F} - \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}})\): the leaky confined-aquifer storage equation in energy-density form, with the \(\mathcal{F} heta\) term of relative order \(\varepsilon_v\) (precondition 3). The layered \(\mathfrak{K}\) and the leakage law depart from the default and satisfy the binding closure, and each is rejected if the default fits at least as well (closure (iv)). The gate sector follows §0.1 item 7: the Neumann spectrum of \(- abla^2_g\) drifts by a fraction of the order of the strain, which is negligible within the window, and it converges as \(g o G_\infty\). The faster decay of fine spatial structure in the head field is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the gate without being the gate. Seismic and vibrational filtering by the landform involves elastic waves, which lie outside the storage–diffusion domain, and is not mapped to the gate. The stress-conservation equivalence holds identically (§0.1 item 3). Effective stress and overburden are not \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\), and vertically stratified stiffness and confinement profiles do not make \(G_{\mu u} ot\equiv 0\) on this flat domain; they enter through the boundary conditions, \(S_s\), and \(\mathcal{H}\).

docs.title: \(O_5\) — Riemannian Geometric Mean Gluing, Percolation & Harmonic Circulation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\); \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) geodesically convex for \(g^{(ij)}( au) \; orall au \ge au_0\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\); \(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\); \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\); \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} G_{\infty,\mu u}^{(i)} \succ 0\) (standing hypothesis with \(H_0 = 0\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: The cover consists of \( au\)-independent material strata, with overlaps \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) across bedding contacts or an unconformity, convex at \( au_0\) in \(g\). Under the small, approximately uniaxial strain they stay convex, and the aperture checks this on the measured metric. Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of \(g\), so the gluing holds identically (§0.1 item 8). \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} = heta\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\), and \(g^{(i)} o G_\infty^{(i)}\) as the strain approaches its final value (\(H_0 = 0\)). Every overlap is crossed by the transient, so \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\). The rigidity percolation of force chains in a granular skeleton is a microstructural property that sets the skeleton's compressibility; it is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the percolation condition only as context. The declared stratum is simply connected, so \(\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} \equiv 0\) (§0.1 item 8); self-equilibrated stress states of the body are structural stresses outside \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\).

docs.title: \(O_6\) — Asymmetric Phase-Lead Coupling & Trace-Free Deformation Operator
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\); \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) (hypothesis) \(\wedge \; \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\); \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u\,dA > 0\) (hypothesis, \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), with this boundary flux integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) (Branch II).
  • Physical Instantiation: Take two strata that share a bedding contact or unconformity \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\). The partner fields are the rate of change of the groundwater free-energy flux in the two orientations (§0.1 item 8): a spatially resolved flux field transmitted from one stratum into the other, not a temporal lag between recharge and response. With fixed heads on the recharge and drain boundaries, the late-time zero set of \(\partial_ au J_W\) is an interior surface between them: nearer the recharge boundary \(\partial_ au J_W\) points toward it, and nearer the drain away from it. On a declared overlap that the predicted zero set of \(\partial_ au J_W\) does not reach during the window (§0.1 item 8), \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) keeps one direction, which the declaration states from the predicted solution. The odd 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\) is its image under the declared non-singular precision map and is non-zero there. Under the non-degeneracy hypothesis \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), built per r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3] from these fields and the declared precision potentials, \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0\) gives \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\), with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general. Under the flux-positivity hypothesis the coupling transmits correlation between the subsystem marginals of the declared state sector (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\)). Both are standing hypotheses. In Branch II the transient decays at the rate \(\gamma_\sigma\) of \(O_3\), so the coupling flux is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) and no sustained coupling is asserted. For a curved contact, any threshold of accumulated strain beyond which the overlap would lose convexity is an aperture-level empirical conjecture mapped to the r10 §5.12 witness criterion \(a_\infty = 2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma < a_c(E)\), which is a design constraint of that witness. No such threshold is asserted, and convexity is checked on the measured metric.

docs.title: \(O_7\) — Principal-Bundle Gauge Coherence, Impedance Decay & Hysteresis Alignment
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(D_\mu = \partial_\mu - i g_{\mathrm{YM}}\,\mathrm{ad}_{A_\mu}\); \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\); \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2} o 1\), \(\hat{\chi} \equiv \chi_E\hat{u}\) (Branch II); \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The gauge sector is the trivial declaration of §0.1 item 9, so \([F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\) identically and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu o 0\) as \(\sigma o 0\). With \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu} \approx rac{2}{3} heta^2\), \(\chi_E - 1 \approx 2 heta^2/( heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle^2) o 0\) as swelling ceases. As in Aperture 2.2, its late-window decay rate \(2\gamma_\sigma\) applies only once \( heta^2 \ll \langle\Theta_E angle^2\), whose onset depends on \(s_0\), so the \(s_0\)-independent observable is the decay rate of \(\sigma\) (\(O_3\)). \(\chi\) is not used. \(\hat{ ho}_g o rac{1}{n}\delta^\mu_ u\) as \(\hat{h} o \hat{h}_\infty\), a residual computable from the deformation record. Alignment with \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}\) requires the Hessian of the record to become isotropic, an asymptotic condition stated and not tested. The \(O_7\) Eq. [3] identities hold as in Aperture 2.2. The aperture claims no smoothing of stress concentrations or alignment of load paths with the consolidated morphology; those belong to the structural stress field, which lies outside \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\).

docs.title: \(O_\Omega\) — Topological Asymptote, Branch II: Bounded Non-Equilibrium Steady State
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)): \( heta \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{C^2(\mathcal{M})} 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^{\infty}\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\); \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\) and \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\); \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q) rac{\delta\Psi}{\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})} \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{} 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} o 0\) (with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly as \( au o \infty\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: Under maintained recharge the stratum approaches a steady head field with continuing recharge, leakage, and drain discharge: a bounded non-equilibrium steady state. Uplift ceases (\( heta o 0\)), \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\) is bounded by the final volumetric strain, \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\), \(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\), \(\sigma o 0\), and \(\partial_ au g o 0\). The transient coupling decays, so \(\mathcal{I} o s_0V_\infty\). The generator condition requires \(J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0\), an asymptotic hypothesis on the declared state sector that no finite window tests. The state is neither static equilibrium, which would require a uniform head at the drain level and no flow, nor a periodic return. The limit belongs to the window's held boundary data. A physical landform keeps evolving by erosion and deposition at its surface between windows, which changes the boundary data and opens a new window; this is never read as a return. Within windows the supported tests (aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5) are the same as for Aperture 2.2: (1) and (3) with the predicted \(\gamma_\sigma\), and (4)–(7). The \(\chi_E\) rate test (2) is not among them, because its regime has an \(s_0\)-dependent onset.
