docs.title: 0. Tier Architecture & Four-Part Functional Homology
docs.text:
Tier 3 maps vascular plant physiology, movement ecology, benthic and edaphic biogeochemistry, and chronobiology onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\). All four apertures are empirical apertures declared in Branch II of r7, the bounded non-equilibrium steady state (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3). Each declares, in its §1, a domain, physical metric, cone speed, storage coefficient, free energy with datum, transport tensor, interior sink, drive, and Branch II evidence, and instantiates all nine coordinates \(O_0 \to O_\Omega\) on that domain. Each declared domain is of one kind: a stored quantity (xylem water, prey biomass, a dissolved oxidant, a signal molecule) spreading through a living or biologically structured medium, with supply crossing the boundary and consumption, where declared, by a named interior sink. The wider phenomena named in the aperture titles enter the mappings through the declared parameters, as boundary conditions, through the hysteresis record \(\mathcal{H}\), or as illustrative context, and each §1 states which. Each aperture is formulated at the level of general physiology, ecology, and biogeochemistry, so that it applies across terrestrial, freshwater, and marine ecosystems without presupposing a specific habitat or site inventory.

Slot & Functional Role Aperture Designation Declared Domain and Diffusing Quantity Titled Phenomena Outside the Domain Vertical Homology Across Tiers Slot 3.1: Structural Substrate Vascular Plant Physiology & Rhizosphere Coupling (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{botanical}}\)) Water in the conducting xylem of the main stem, moving from the root collar to the crown base down its water-potential gradient. Rhizosphere and mycorrhizal uptake, crown and leaf storage, stomatal regulation, phloem transport, growth, stem sway, reaction wood: as boundary data, through \(\mathcal{H}\), or context. \(1.1 \leftrightarrow 2.1 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{3.1} \leftrightarrow 4.1 \leftrightarrow 5.1\) Slot 3.2: Dynamic Flow & Waves Movement Ecology & Ecotone Foraging Dynamics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{trophic}}\)) Prey biomass dispersing into a three-dimensional foraging volume across an ecotone and consumed by predators, whose trajectories follow a declared taxis drive. Foraging decisions, population cycles, prey reproduction, migration, learned routes: through the declared parameters, as boundary data, through \(\mathcal{H}\), or context. \(1.2 \leftrightarrow 2.2 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{3.2} \leftrightarrow 4.2 \leftrightarrow 5.2\) Slot 3.3: Boundary Gating Benthic & Edaphic Biogeochemical Metabolism (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{metabolic}}\)) A dissolved oxidant diffusing from overlying water through the diffusive boundary layer into a sediment column, consumed by microbial respiration. The sequence of other electron acceptors, bioturbation, humification, extracellular enzymes: through the declared parameters, the lower boundary, \(\mathcal{H}\), or context. \(1.3 \leftrightarrow 2.3 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{3.3} \leftrightarrow 4.3 \leftrightarrow 5.3\) Slot 3.4: Coalescence & Hysteresis Chronobiology & Phenological Synchrony (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{chrono}}\)) A humoral or paracrine entraining signal diffusing into an avascular target tissue from cells outside it, and degraded there. Pacemaker oscillators, entrainment and phase response, dormancy, vernalization, mast seeding, succession: as boundary data, through \(\mathcal{H}\), or context. \(1.4 \leftrightarrow 2.4 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{3.4} \leftrightarrow 4.4 \leftrightarrow 5.4\)

docs.title: 0.1 Conventions Common to the Four Tier 3 Apertures
docs.text:
The following conventions apply to every aperture of this tier. Each aperture's §1 and coordinate blocks state its specific values and cite these items where they apply. Where an item repeats a convention of tier_2_abiotic_continuum_physics.md §0.1, it is restated here so that this tier can be read on its own.

  1. Branch and windows. Branch II is declared before any test, with the estimators of item 7 and §1, and no Tier 3 domain is re-evaluated in Branch I on the same data (closure (v)). Statements that hold in Branch I only (r10 Decision 6) are never applied. Every observation window is a relaxation window: it begins at a declared \( au_0\) from a prior steady state, a declared transient starts at \( au_0\), the external data are then held within declared tolerances, and the window follows the domain as it settles.
  2. In 3.1, 3.3, and 3.4 the transient is a declared step of the boundary data in the direction that raises \(\mathcal{F}\): a step decrease of evaporative demand at the leaves (3.1), and a step increase of the oxidant concentration of the overlying water (3.3) or of the signal concentration at the supply interface (3.4). Each declared balance law is a scalar parabolic equation whose sink is Lipschitz and non-decreasing in \(\mathcal{F}\) (zero, first order, Michaelis–Menten), so the comparison principle holds. The prior steady state is a subsolution for the raised data, so \(\mathcal{F}(\cdot, au_0 + h) \ge \mathcal{F}(\cdot, au_0)\); the held data make the problem invariant under time translation, so \(\mathcal{F}(\cdot, au + h) \ge \mathcal{F}(\cdot, au)\), that is, \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} \ge 0\) at every point. Where the step is in fact a ramp (non-decreasing boundary data that reach their held value over a finite rise time, as for secretion in 3.4), the same conclusion follows without time translation: \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F}\) obeys the linearized equation with zero initial data (the prior steady state) and non-negative boundary data, so it stays non-negative. In 3.1 the xylem also exchanges water with capacitive living tissue outside the \(\mathcal{F}\) field; that coupled linear system is cooperative, and the same conclusion holds for it (3.1 §1). The argument is exact on rigid domains. Under the optional torsional perturbation of 3.1 the operator depends on \( au\) through \(g( au)\) at the order of the shear strain, so there the conclusion holds only to that order, and 3.1 checks it from its water-potential record.
  3. In 3.2 the prey data are held at their prior steady values, so \(\mathcal{F}\) is steady within the window, which aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3 item 3 admits. The transient is the mixing of two predator groups, labelled at \( au_0\) by the patch each animal occupies (item 9 and 3.2 \(O_6\)).
  4. The rate of change of the flux, \(\partial_ au J_W\), is not one-signed in general (item 9).
  5. Metric. The physical metric is the pull-back of the Euclidean metric to the material points of the declared body under its deformation map (for 3.2, to a fixed region of space). It is flat at every \( au\), so \(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\) and \(R_{\mu u} \equiv 0\) (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3 item 2). No Tier 3 aperture declares a non-Euclidean material metric in this epoch: the growth material metric that the master table admits for 3.1 is discussed in 3.1 §1 and not declared. The curved configurations of the r10 §5.11 and §5.13 witnesses are therefore realized by none of these apertures, and r7's curvature sector is exercised by no Tier 3 aperture.
  6. Rigid domains (3.2, 3.3, 3.4). In a Cartesian chart \(g_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu u}\), so \(\Omega \equiv 1\), \(\hat{h} \equiv 0\), \( heta \equiv 0\), and \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv 0\). For 3.2 this holds by construction, because the declared domain is a fixed region of space. For 3.3 and 3.4 the body is declared rigid within a pre-declared tolerance on its measured volumetric strain, and windows in which the measured volume decreases beyond that tolerance are excluded, so that \( heta \ge 0\) is not violated. With \(\sigma \equiv 0\) the \(O_3\) shear law holds trivially, and these apertures support no shear-relaxation test.
  7. Volume-rigid domain (3.1). The volumetric strain of the conducting xylem stays within a declared tolerance, so \( heta \equiv 0\) in the declared metric. Without the optional torsional perturbation, the shear strain also stays within tolerance and 3.1 is treated as rigid. With it, the metric is the pull-back under an isochoric twist: in a Cartesian material chart \(g( au) = \mathbf{F}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{F}\) with \(\det\mathbf{F} = 1\), so \(\Omega \equiv 1\), \( heta \equiv 0\), \(\exp\hat{h} = g\), and \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} eq 0\). On that deforming domain every covariant quantity (Laplacian, Hessians, convexity, harmonic fields) is evaluated with \(g( au)\).
  8. Storage. The r7 \(O_4\) balance law carries unit storage: \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F}\) is the rate of change of the stored quantity per unit volume. A living medium stores its diffusing quantity \(u\) with a coefficient \(s\) (stored amount per unit volume per unit of \(u\)): the hydraulic capacitance of stem sapwood in 3.1, unity in 3.2, the sediment porosity in 3.3, and the extracellular volume fraction times a binding retardation factor in 3.4. With \(s\) uniform, the physical balance \(s\,\partial_ au u = abla_\alpha(k^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta u) - r\) becomes the r7 law for \(\mathcal{F} = \epsilon u\) (with \(\epsilon\) a declared constant yield), \(\mathfrak{K} = k/s\), and \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = \epsilon r/s\), and the r7 flux is \(J_W = (\epsilon/s)\,j\), with \(j = -k abla u\) the physical flux. The factor \(\epsilon/s\) is a declared conversion factor, estimated independently (closure (ii)). If \(s\) varies in space, \(s^{-1} abla_\alpha(k^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta u) = abla_\alpha(s^{-1}k^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta u) + s^{-2}k^{\alpha eta} abla_\alpha s\, abla_ eta u\), and the last term is a drift term that the r7 balance law does not contain. Each aperture therefore declares \(s\) uniform on \(\mathcal{M}\) within a tolerance (a declared, checkable precondition), or, in 3.3, states where the declared law departs from the physical one and bounds that departure.
  9. Stress sector. With \(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\), \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} \equiv 0\); its trace gives \( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha = 0\) for \(n = 3\), and then \( abla_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)} = 0\), so \(\xi\) is a Killing field. No Tier 3 medium has an identified global control field in this epoch, so Tier 3 declares \(\eta^\lambda \equiv 0\), hence \(\xi_ u \equiv 0\) and \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha = 0\), and the \(O_4\) equivalence \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\) holds identically. The \( au\)-compatibility law then reduces to \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma]_{\mu u} = rac{n-2}{n}( abla_\mu abla_ u heta - g_{\mu u} abla^2 heta)\), and its trace, the traced elliptic equation, to \( rac{n-1}{n} abla^2 heta = abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta}\). These are the Saint-Venant compatibility conditions of the strain rate, which every deformation of an embedded body satisfies because its metric stays flat; with \( heta \equiv 0\) (all Tier 3 domains) they read \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma] = 0\) and \( abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} = 0\). The mechanical stresses of living media (turgor, growth stresses in wood, tissue and sediment stresses) are not \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\); they enter as boundary conditions, through the declared parameters, and through \(\mathcal{H}\). The partner fields \(\eta_{i o j}\) of \(O_6\) (item 9) are distinct objects from the global \(\eta\) of \(O_4\).
  10. Cone speed and trajectories. Each aperture declares \(c_*\) as a characteristic signal speed of its medium (a sound or pressure-wave speed). Rays of that signal are null for the declared cone and, like all null rays, are not trajectories of \(O_2\) Eq. [3]. Every material and animal speed in \(\mathcal{M}\) is \(\ll c_*\), so \(u^2 \ll 1\) and \(f_{\mathrm{drive}} \approx a_{\mathrm{d}}\). The trajectory equation is displayed in physical units: both \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2\) and the projection term \(c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu\) carry \(c_*\), and with \(c_* = 1\) the display reduces to the r7 form. Apertures 3.1, 3.3, and 3.4 instantiate Eq. [3] with \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\) and map no tracer. Aperture 3.2 declares a taxis drive for predator trajectories; the driven trajectory equation is untested in this epoch (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3).
  11. Currents. In Branch II, \(J_E^\mu = J_W^\mu/p_0\) is fixed. The expansion current \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) enters only through its divergence \( heta\) and its boundary flux \(dV_{\mathcal{M}}/d au\) (r7 \(O_0\) branch scope), and no supply current is ever mapped to it. In general \( abla_\mu J_E^\mu = -p_0^{-1}(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} + \mathcal{F} heta + \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}) eq heta\).
  12. Measured dissipation. The Branch II evidence requires \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) to be estimated from measured dissipation, never from \(\mathfrak{K} abla\mathcal{F}\). Integrating \(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\) by parts and using the \(O_4\) balance law gives the identity $\(p_0\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{F}\,(-J_W^\mu)\,d\Sigma_\mu - \int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{F}\,\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx - rac{1}{2} rac{d}{d au}\int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{F}^2\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx - rac{1}{2}\int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{F}^2 heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\)$
  13. Where an outflow face is held at the datum \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0\) (3.2, 3.3, 3.4), it contributes nothing and the boundary term reduces to the supply face. The outflow faces of 3.1 (crown base, cambial interface) are not at the datum, and their terms are evaluated from the measured outflow and the measured \(\mathcal{F}\) there.
  14. Each term is evaluated from measured \(\mathcal{F}\), measured boundary fluxes, and measured or independently declared consumption; none uses the declared \(\mathfrak{K}\). Each §1 names instruments and surfaces different from those of the \(O_1\) flux-prediction test, so that the evidence is independent of that test; 3.3 states where this independence is weaker.
  15. Because the identity uses the balance law, the estimate is conditional on it. Each §1 also names a directly measured physical dissipation whose sign the estimate must share. Every such dissipation is non-negative, by the second law (3.1, 3.3, 3.4) or because a living system's metabolic power is positive (3.2), so this comparison tests only the sign of the identity-based estimate, and it is stated as such. Only signs and \(s_0\)-independent rates of \(\Theta_E\) are tested.
  16. Gate sector (\(O_4\)). \( ho_{\mathrm{total}}( au)\) is a declared positive trace-class state on \(L^2(\mathcal{M}, d\mathrm{vol}_g)\), and \(Q\), \(P\), and the \(O_6\) marginals \(Q_i\) and joints \(Q_{ij}\) are densities of this declared state sector. No Tier 3 aperture identifies them with \(\mathcal{F}\) or with any measured field in this epoch, and none makes an empirical claim about the gate (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3). What each domain's physics supplies is, first, the spectral setting: the Neumann eigenmodes of \(- abla^2_g\) on \(\mathcal{M}\), whose eigenvalues are fixed on rigid domains, drift by a fraction of the order of the shear strain under the torsional perturbation of 3.1, and converge as \(g o G_\infty\). Second, it supplies a physical low-pass behaviour of \(\mathcal{F}\): under the balance law, fine spatial structure in \(\mathcal{F}\) relaxes faster than coarse structure. That behaviour is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the gate and is not itself the gate. Temporal smoothing of fluctuating supply by the medium is a property in time and is not the spatial gate.
  17. Cover, overlaps, and coupling (\(O_5\), \(O_6\)).
  18. The cover \(\{\mathcal{U}_i\}\) consists of \( au\)-independent material subregions of \(\mathcal{M}\) (for 3.2, fixed subregions of space) with Lipschitz boundaries, and every overlap \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) is convex at \( au_0\). Where \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) has concave parts (the core boundary of the conducting xylem in 3.1), each concave part lies in a single cover set, which need not be convex: r7 requires convex overlaps, not convex cover sets. Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of the one physical metric, so \(g^{(i)} = g^{(j)}\) on every overlap, the geometric mean returns the common metric (\(g \# g = g\)), and the gluing of \(O_5\) Eq. [3] holds identically.
  19. The anisotropy of a medium lives in \(\mathfrak{K}\), never in \(g\). Effective-medium averages of conductivities or diffusivities, including geometric-mean averages, are statements about \(\mathfrak{K}\) and are not mapped to \(O_5\) Eq. [1].
  20. Partner fields. In 3.1, 3.3, and 3.4 the partner fields are the rate of change of the free-energy flux read in the two orientations, \(\eta_{i o j}^\lambda = \partial_ au J_W^\lambda\) and \(\eta_{j o i}^\lambda = -\partial_ au J_W^\lambda\), defined on all of \(\mathcal{M}\), so \(\eta_{[i o j]}^\lambda = \partial_ au J_W^\lambda\). In 3.2 they are the movement-flux fields of the two labelled predator groups (3.2 \(O_6\)), which are not antisymmetric by construction.
  21. Zero sets. \(\partial_ au J_W\) is not one-signed in general. Where the supply boundary holds a value of \(\mathcal{F}\) (3.3, 3.4), the flux near the supply decays after the step from an initial overshoot, so there \(\partial_ au J_W\) points toward the supply, while farther downstream the flux rises toward its new steady value, so there it points away from the supply. Between the two lies the zero set of \(\partial_ au J_W\). It travels during the early window, possibly overshooting its late position, and in the late single-mode regime it settles on a fixed surface. In a laterally uniform column, a precondition that 3.3 and 3.4 declare for this purpose, that surface is the level at which the slowest relaxation mode of the linearized problem peaks; without lateral uniformity it is located only by the predicted solution. In 3.1 the boundary data are of mixed kind (3.1 \(O_6\)), and the zero set is located only by the predicted solution. On the zero set \(\eta_{[i o j]} = 0\) and \(J_{[i o j]} = 0\), so a construction that included it would itself decide the non-degeneracy hypothesis there.
  22. Each aperture therefore declares overlaps \( ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) that the zero set, predicted before the window from the independently estimated parameters, does not reach during the window. Before the transient arrives, the partner field on a downstream overlap is non-zero but exponentially small, so the check is made against a pre-declared detection threshold: each overlap's window starts once the predicted \(\vert\eta_{[i o j]}\vert\) exceeds that threshold on \( ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\), and the data must then show \(\vert\eta_{[i o j]}\vert\) above it there (a declared, checkable precondition). On such an overlap \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) keeps one direction throughout the overlap's window, which each aperture states.
  23. Precision potentials. The potentials \(\Phi^{(i)}\) are declared before data collection as quadratic potentials (in a Cartesian chart, or in the Cartesian material chart for 3.1, with Hessians computed with \(g( au)\) under the torsional perturbation). Their trace-free parts \(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)}\) cannot be positive definite, because their eigenvalues sum to zero, so \(J_{[i o j]} = rac{1}{2}(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)} + \hat{\Pi}^{(j)})\eta_{[i o j]}\) carries no sign relation to \(\eta_{[i o j]}\). Tier 3 declares \( rac{1}{2}(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)} + \hat{\Pi}^{(j)})\) non-singular, so that \(J_{[i o j]} eq 0\) wherever \(\eta_{[i o j]} eq 0\). What is claimed for \(J_{[i o j]}\) is its oddness under \(i \leftrightarrow j\) and its non-vanishing on the declared overlaps, not a direction.
  24. Tier 3 also declares the two trace-free Hessians distinct, \(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)} eq \hat{\Pi}^{(j)}\). With antisymmetric partner fields, \(J_{i o j} + J_{j o i} = (\hat{\Pi}^{(j)} - \hat{\Pi}^{(i)})\eta_{[i o j]}\). Equal Hessians would therefore remove the gradient term of r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3] and leave \(M^{(ij)}_{\mu u} = \gamma_M ig((J_{[i o j]})_\mu(J_{[i o j]})_ u - rac{1}{n}g_{\mu u}J_{[i o j]}^\alpha(J_{[i o j]})_\alpha ig)\), the trace-free part of a rank-one tensor, which is non-zero wherever \(J_{[i o j]} eq 0\): the hypothesis would hold by construction. With distinct Hessians the gradient term depends on \( abla\eta_{[i o j]}\) and can cancel the quadratic term (r10 Decision 4), so the construction neither forces nor forbids \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), which remains a standing hypothesis. The labelled fields of 3.2 are not antisymmetric by construction, but their sum is small under its uniform-density precondition, so the same declaration is made there.
  25. On a connected domain the declared transient reaches every overlap for \( au > au_0\) (in 3.2, the labelled groups mix across every overlap), so every edge of \(\mathcal{K}_0\) lies in \(\mathcal{K}\) and \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\); empirically, an edge is counted when its partner field exceeds a pre-declared detection threshold on its overlap. The percolation condition therefore carries no separate empirical content on these domains.
  26. \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\) and \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\) are standing hypotheses of r7 \(O_6\), not consequences of diffusion or of movement. In Branch II the transient decays as the domain settles (in 3.2, as the groups mix), so each coupling-tensor boundary flux decays and is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\); no sustained coupling is asserted.
  27. Topology. The domains of 3.2, 3.3, and 3.4 are declared simply connected, so \(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(\mathcal{M}) = 0\) and \(\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} \equiv 0\). The conducting xylem of 3.1 generally surrounds a non-conducting core (pith or heartwood), so its first Betti number \(b_1(\mathcal{M})\) is at least one and the space of harmonic Neumann fields \(\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}}\) of r7 \(O_5\) Eq. [5] is non-trivial: a property of the domain's topology, computed slice-wise with \(g( au)\). Tier 3 identifies no transport current or measured field with it and makes no claim about it.
  28. Gauge sector and hysteresis (\(O_7\), \(O_0\)). Tier 3 declares the trivial gauge sector: \(A_\mu \equiv 0\) and a uniform unit section \(\hat{u}\). Then \(F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}} \equiv 0\), \([F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\) identically, and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu = (\partial_\mu\chi_E)\hat{u}\), which tends to \(0\) in \(C^1\) when \(\sigma o 0\) and \( heta o 0\) in \(C^2\) with \(\liminf\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\). The gauge limit therefore carries no content beyond the shear and expansion limits, and \(O_7\) gauge transport is untested in this epoch. In particular, no Tier 3 aperture makes a synchronization, alignment, or collective-coherence claim: such claims would belong to gauge transport (aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5), not to \(\chi_E\). The hysteresis record obeys the r7 law \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) from a declared initial record \(\mathcal{H}_0\), chosen convex because \(O_7\) Eq. [2] requires \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H} \succ 0\) at every \( au\). \(\mathcal{H}\) then evolves through a state sector that is declared but not specified, so the declarations do not establish convexity at later \( au\). Tier 3 therefore states it as a declared condition, with a sufficient form: the largest eigenvalue magnitude of \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta(\mathcal{H} - \mathcal{H}_0)\) (with indices raised by \(g\)) stays below the smallest eigenvalue of \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H}_0\) on \(\mathcal{M}\) for all \( au \ge au_0\). Both Hessians are covariant Hessians of \(g( au)\), evaluated at each \( au\), which matters for 3.1 under the torsional perturbation. Then \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H} \succ 0\) persists. The alternative, \( abla q \equiv 0\), would keep \(\mathcal{H}\) static and convex, but would make the \(O_\Omega\) generator condition hold trivially, so it is not adopted. Biological memory variables of each system (wood anatomy, learned routes, a sediment's chemical record, an entrained clock phase) are mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\) and are not identified with it. \(\hat{ ho}_g o rac{1}{n}\delta^\mu_ u\) follows from \(\hat{h} o \hat{h}_\infty\), and the alignment \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) o 0\) then requires the Hessian of the record to become isotropic: an asymptotic condition that each aperture states and does not test.
  29. Finite windows and coverage. No finite window exhibits a \( au o \infty\) limit. Each aperture's empirical claims are the within-window tests of aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5 that its domain supports, and each \(O_\Omega\) block lists them. In this epoch Aperture 3.1 is exercised by the shear-relaxation and flux-prediction families, 3.2 by the coupling family, 3.3 by the flux-prediction family, and 3.4 by no test (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3). Everything else is stated as untested, not as confirmed.

docs.title: 0.2 Coordinates That Hold Trivially or by Construction
docs.text:
On these declared domains several coordinates hold identically and carry no empirical content. They are listed here so that no block below is read as evidence for them.

docs.title: Aperture 3.1: Vascular Plant Physiology & Rhizosphere Coupling (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{botanical}}\))
1. Epistemological & Biological Scope
docs.text:
Aperture 3.1 resolves how vascular plants lift water from the soil, through the rhizosphere, roots, and conducting xylem, to the leaves, where it is transpired: water moves under the tension that evaporation generates (the cohesion–tension mechanism), is buffered by the water stored in tissues, is regulated at the leaves by stomata, and is coupled at the roots to the rhizosphere and its mycorrhizal symbionts. Lexicon is strictly restricted to plant physiology, plant hydraulics, dendrology, plant biomechanics, and rhizosphere and mycorrhizal ecology.

Declaration (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3; Branch II).

  • Domain \(\mathcal{M}\) (\(n = 3\)) and boundary \(\partial\mathcal{M}\). The conducting xylem (sapwood) of the main stem, between the root collar and the crown base: the functional conduits and fibres of a single organ class, with the living ray and axial parenchyma embedded among them, treated at the tissue scale as a porous continuum. The domain is confined to one organ class because xylem capacitance per unit volume differs systematically between trunk, branches, petioles, and veins: a capacitance jump at an organ junction would make \(J_W = q/C\) discontinuous where \(q\) is continuous, which the unit-storage balance law reads as an interface source or sink (§0.1 item 3). \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) consists of:
  • the root collar (supply face), across which water enters from the root system;
  • the crown-base cross-section (outflow), across which water leaves \(\mathcal{M}\) for the crown: the branch, petiole, and vein xylem and the leaf mesophyll, from which it is transpired, all of which lie outside \(\mathcal{M}\);
  • the cambial interface with the bark, across which water is exchanged with the bark's living tissue;
  • the boundary with the non-conducting core (pith or heartwood), which is impermeable.

All supply crosses the root collar; there are no interior sources. The soil, the rhizosphere, and the roots lie outside \(\mathcal{M}\) and enter through the root-collar boundary condition: water enters at the rate set by the soil water potential, held during the window, and by declared root and rhizosphere conductances. For predictions (as in \(O_6\)) the crown (its xylem and leaf storage, with transpiration leaving it) and the bark are represented as capacitive compartments outside \(\mathcal{M}\), with declared capacitances and conductances estimated independently. * Window. A relaxation window (§0.1 item 1), opened from a prior steady state by a declared step decrease of evaporative demand at the leaves (for example a step increase of air humidity around an enclosed shoot), after which evaporative demand, stomatal conductance, and soil water potential are held within declared tolerances. Water potential then rises at every point and tension relaxes, so no conduit embolizes, and water flows from the xylem into the living tissue, which it refills. Windows in which demand rises are excluded: there the xylem contracts as tension rises (\( heta < 0\)), and living tissue discharges water into the xylem, which would be an interior source. The window is fixed: growth (new conduits, extension, radial increment) stays within a declared tolerance throughout it. * Coupled compartments. The stem xylem, the parenchyma embedded in it, and the bark and crown compartments form a linear system in which each compartment gains water from the others in proportion to their potential differences. Such a system is cooperative, so a step of the external data in the direction that raises potentials raises every potential monotonically: \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} \ge 0\) throughout \(\mathcal{M}\), and every compartment's potential stays below the xylem potential that feeds it, so its exchange with the xylem is one-signed, into the living tissue. * Optional torsional perturbation. A stem segment may be twisted and released at \( au_0\) within such a window. The recovery of the twist then supplies a shear transient (\(O_3\)), while transpiration-driven flow continues to supply the throughput. * Metric. Flat and volume-rigid (§0.1 item 2): the volumetric strain of the conducting xylem stays within a declared tolerance (checked by point dendrometers anchored in the xylem), so \( heta \equiv 0\). Without the torsional perturbation the shear strain also stays within tolerance, and \(g_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu u}\) in a Cartesian material chart. With it, \(g( au) = \mathbf{F}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{F}\) is the pull-back under the twist, with \(\det\mathbf{F} = 1\). For a segment twisted about its axis by an angle \(\Phi_{\mathrm{tw}}(z, au)\), the deformation \((r, \varphi, z) \mapsto (r, \varphi + \Phi_{\mathrm{tw}}, z)\) is isochoric and maps each cylinder \(r = \mathrm{const}\) and each cross-section onto itself. * Cone speed. \(c_*\) is the speed of pressure waves in the sap-filled conduits, set by the compressibility of sap and the compliance of conduit walls. Sap velocities and twist-recovery speeds are \(\ll c_*\). * Storage. The hydraulic capacitance \(C\) of the stem sapwood: the water released per unit volume per unit decrease of water potential (m³ m⁻³ Pa⁻¹), from capillary and elastic storage in conduits and fibres and from the apoplast of the embedded parenchyma. It is declared uniform over \(\mathcal{M}\) within a tolerance and linear over the window's range of potentials (§0.1 item 3). * Free energy \(\mathcal{F}\) and datum. \(\mathcal{F} = \psi_{\mathrm{h}} - \psi_{\mathrm{ref}}\) (J m⁻³). Here \(\psi_{\mathrm{h}}\) is the water potential of the xylem sap in hydraulic form: pressure plus gravitational potential \( ho_w g z\). The osmotic component of xylem sap is small, does not drive flow through the conduit network, and is declared constant within tolerance; psychrometric readings are corrected for it and for the gravitational term. The datum \(\psi_{\mathrm{ref}}\) is the declared window minimum of leaf water potential, in the same hydraulic form. Potentials only rise during the window, so that minimum is the lowest leaf value of the prior steady state, measured at \( au_0\) and fixed before the window opens. Water flows from the root collar toward the leaves, so the leaves hold the lowest potentials, and \(\mathcal{F} \ge 0\) throughout \(\mathcal{M}\). \(\mathcal{F}\) is linear in the stored water: the water stored per unit volume above the datum is \(C\mathcal{F}\), so \(\mathcal{F}\) is that stored water times the declared conversion factor \(1/C\). The relaxation time \(\ell^2C/k\) is finite and resolvable. * Transport \(\mathfrak{K}\). \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = k^{\alpha eta}/C\), with \(k^{\alpha eta}\) the hydraulic conductivity tensor of the conducting xylem, parametric: axial and radial (and, if declared, tangential) conductivities along the stem's axes. The master table's "conductances" are these conductivities per unit area and gradient. Isotropic \(k\) is the default. With \(q\) the volumetric sap flux density (m s⁻¹), \(J_W = q/C\); \(1/C\) is the declared conversion factor. * Sink \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\). The default \(0\), or a declared lateral loss to the living parenchyma embedded in \(\mathcal{M}\), first order relative to the datum: \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = k_{\mathrm{p}}(\mathcal{F} - \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}}) \ge 0\), with \(k_{\mathrm{p}}\) a declared rate constant. The physical exchange is driven by the difference between the xylem potential and the lagging potential of the parenchyma, so the first-order datum form is a declared idealization. It is admitted only under the binding closure, and it is rejected if the default fits at least as well (closure (iv)). Exchange with the bark across the cambial interface is a boundary flux, not a sink. * Drive. Default, \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\) (§0.1 item 5). * Growth material metric (not declared in this epoch). The master table admits an optional incompatible-growth material metric for this aperture. It is not declared, for three reasons. 1. Within a fixed window growth is excluded, so a growth metric would be \( au\)-independent: \( heta = \sigma = 0\) in it. The imposed twist, an elastic or viscoelastic deformation, would not appear in it at all, so the shear-relaxation test of this aperture requires the physical metric. 2. r7 ties curvature to the control field. With \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_GT^{\mathrm{mat}}_{\mu u}\) and \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\) (\(O_2\) Eq. [0]), \(T^{\mathrm{mat}}_{\mu u} = abla_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)} - rac{1}{2}g_{\mu u} abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\) gives \(R_{\mu u} = \kappa_G abla_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)}\), with \(\xi_ u = \hat{\Pi}_{ u\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) (\(O_4\) Eq. [2]). No plant-physiological field is identified as the global control field \(\eta\). A \(\xi\) constructed from a declared growth metric so as to satisfy this equation would satisfy the stress sector by construction. 3. The incompatibility of a growth metric (its curvature) is carried by residual growth strains, whose measurement by release cuts is destructive and so cannot be made on the intact plants that the tests require.

A future declaration would need a growth tensor whose incompatibility is estimated by an independent modality; an identified control field for which \(R_{\mu u} = \kappa_G abla_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)}\) is a tested hypothesis rather than a construction; and a statement, coordinate by coordinate, of which metric is used. Until then the stress sector of this aperture is that of §0.1 item 4. * Branch II evidence (closure (v)). * The trend of \(\langle heta angle\) and a bound on \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\) come from the xylem dendrometers, which must stay within the volume tolerance; for this volume-rigid domain the evidence is that tolerance check. * \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) is estimated from measured dissipation (§0.1 item 7). The supply term uses the root-collar inflow, from a stem heat-balance gauge at the collar, and \(\mathcal{F}\) there, from a collar psychrometer. The crown-base term uses the outflow into the crown, from a second stem heat-balance gauge at the crown base, with \(\mathcal{F}\) there from a crown-base psychrometer. The cambial term uses bark dendrometry with \(\mathcal{F}\) at the cambium. The storage term uses \(\mathcal{F}\) along the flow path. None of these are the heat-pulse sensors or stem psychrometers of the \(O_1\) section. * The physical dissipation is the viscous dissipation of sap flow, \(q\cdot(- abla\psi_{\mathrm{h}})\) per unit volume. Under the declarations it equals the r7 dissipation density \(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\) times the positive constant \(p_0C\), and its measured sign must agree with that of the estimate. * Admissible domains (declared, checkable preconditions): 1. intact conduit network: no new embolism and no refilling of embolized conduits within the window, checked by a declared method (for example acoustic emission for new embolism and a conductance or imaging check for refilling), so that \(k\) and \(C\) are constant; 2. \(\psi_{\mathrm{h}} \ge \psi_{\mathrm{ref}}\) throughout (so \(\mathcal{F} \ge \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}}\)) and \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) throughout \( ar{\mathcal{M}}\); 3. volumetric strain of the conducting xylem within the volume tolerance. Without the torsional perturbation, shear strain is also within tolerance. With it, the twist is recoverable, with shear strain \(\ll 1\), and \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} \ge 0\) is checked from the psychrometer record (§0.1 item 1); 4. exchange with living tissue (embedded parenchyma, bark) one-signed into the tissue, checked by bark dendrometry: living tissue never discharges into the xylem within the window; 5. evaporative demand, stomatal conductance, and soil water potential held within tolerance after the step, checked by gas exchange and a soil or root-collar psychrometer; 6. capacitance and sap osmotic potential uniform over the stem sapwood within tolerance (§0.1 item 3), checked against pressure–volume measurements at two or more heights; a stem whose sapwood capacitance varies with height beyond tolerance is not admissible; 7. growth within tolerance throughout the window. * Titled phenomena outside the domain. * Rhizosphere coupling. Soil water potential and the conductances of roots and rhizosphere, including the extension of the absorbing surface by mycorrhizal hyphae, set the root-collar boundary condition. The soil, roots, and fungal networks lie outside \(\mathcal{M}\); common mycorrhizal networks between plants are context. * Leaves and stomata. The crown lies outside \(\mathcal{M}\): stomatal regulation and transpiration, with the storage of the crown's xylem and leaves, set the crown-base boundary data. * Phloem. Pressure-driven phloem transport in the bark lies outside \(\mathcal{M}\) and enters only through the cambial exchange. * Growth and wood. Growth, wood formation, reaction wood, conduit dimensions, and the history of cavitation lie between windows; they enter through the declared parameters and \(\mathcal{H}_0\). * Canopy mechanics. Stem and canopy sway is underdamped oscillation, which the mixed-form shear law excludes, so it lies outside the declared windows. Canopy architecture and spacing between crowns are context.

docs.title: 2. Coordinate-by-Coordinate Mapping (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\))
\(O_0\) — Exogenous Flux & Emergent Foliation Time
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( heta \equiv -N K \overset{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0}{=} rac{1}{2}g^{\mu u} rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} = rac{1}{\sqrt{\vert g\vert}} rac{\partial\sqrt{\vert g\vert}}{\partial au} = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\); \(\Theta_E \equiv rac{\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}}{s_0} = - rac{ eta_{\mathrm{th}}}{s_0}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\); \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \sqrt{ heta^2 + \Theta_E^2}\), \( au_\Theta( au) \equiv \int_{ au_0}^{ au}\langle\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au'\); \( rac{dV_{\mathcal{M}}}{d au} = \int_{\mathcal{M}} heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\), with \(\lim_{ au o\infty}V_{\mathcal{M}}( au) = V_\infty < \infty\) (Branch II); \( rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), \(q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv -\ln(v_0Q(\mathbf{x}, au))\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The conducting xylem is volume-rigid, so \( heta \equiv 0\), \(dV_{\mathcal{M}}/d au = 0\), and \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\) at every \( au\); under the torsional perturbation the twist is isochoric, so this still holds. The expansion current enters only through its vanishing divergence and boundary flux. The water entering at the root collar and leaving at the crown base is throughput and is never mapped to it (§0.1 item 6). Openness is carried by throughput: sap flow down the water-potential gradient dissipates energy at every point, so \(\Theta_E > 0\) (by \(O_1\)), \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} = \Theta_E\), and \( au_\Theta\) counts entropy production per \(s_0\), while \( au\) remains laboratory proper time. Along the throughput current \(J_E^\mu = J_W^\mu/p_0\) the record accumulates by \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) (§0.1 item 10). The plant's hydraulic memory (conduit dimensions and their vulnerability to embolism, the history of cavitation, reaction wood) is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\) and is not identified with it. Within the window such changes are excluded (preconditions 1 and 7), and they enter through \(\mathcal{H}_0\).

docs.title: \(O_1\) — Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Openness
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} = p_0\oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} \equiv \int_{\mathcal{M}}(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F})\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} + \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\); \( abla_\mu\mathcal{F} eq 0\); \(J_E^\mu \equiv rac{J_W^\mu}{p_0} = - rac{1}{p_0}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\) (Branch II, fixed); \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\); \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The maintained difference between the soil's water potential and the atmosphere's evaporative demand holds the shoot far from equilibrium. With \(J_E^\mu = -p_0^{-1}(k^{\mu u}/C) abla_ u\mathcal{F}\), \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\) holds identically wherever \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) (precondition 2), so \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). Sap flows down the gradient of \(\psi_{\mathrm{h}}\), from the root collar toward the leaves and into the refilling tissue, in the direction of \(J_E^\mu\). On the volume-rigid xylem \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0\), so \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). The empirical content of \(O_1\) is the flux-prediction test (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3, §5.5 item 6), which exercises this aperture in the current epoch (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3). The parameters of \(k^{\alpha eta}\) are estimated on the intact test plant per closure (ii), from its water-potential response to a declared step change of transpiration run as a perturbation regime before the window, with transpiration from gas exchange. \(C\), the stem-sapwood capacitance, comes from water-release (pressure–volume) curves on sapwood cores from the test stem itself, taken after the window at the heights of precondition 6 (or by a non-destructive method), never from another plant. The declared law must predict \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}} = q^{\mathrm{meas}}/C\) across a declared stem section \(S\), with \(q^{\mathrm{meas}}\) from heat-pulse sap-flux sensors, and with \( abla\mathcal{F}\) from stem psychrometers at two heights, with the gravitational term added; neither \( abla\mathcal{F}\) nor \(q^{\mathrm{meas}}\) uses the other or the declared \(k^{\alpha eta}\).

docs.title: \(O_2\) — Unimodular Weyl Factorization, Constraint Precision & Trajectories
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}( au, \mathbf{x}) = \Omega^2( au, \mathbf{x})\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) with \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) = 0 \implies \det g = \Omega^{2n}\), \( rac{\partial\ln\Omega}{\partial au} = rac{1}{n} heta\); \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\); \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\), \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\); \( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\); \(\left.\left( rac{dv^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}\), \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2)\left(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu ight)\), \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2 < 1\), with the default \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: Without the torsional perturbation the unimodular Weyl split is trivial: \(\Omega \equiv 1\), \(\hat{h} \equiv 0\), and \(\partial_ au\ln\Omega = heta/3 = 0\). Under it, in the Cartesian material chart \(\hat{g} = \delta\), \(\Omega \equiv 1\) because the twist is isochoric (\(\det g = 1\)), and \(\exp\hat{h} = g( au)\), so \(\hat{h}\) is the logarithm of the right Cauchy–Green tensor of the twist, trace-free. The split isolates the volume element only algebraically; \( heta\) remains coupled to \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) and \(\sigma_{\alpha eta}\) through the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation (r10 Decision 2). On this domain (\(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\), \(\xi \equiv 0\), \( heta \equiv 0\); §0.1 items 2 and 4) it reduces to \( abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} = 0\), and the full law to \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma] = 0\): the Saint-Venant compatibility of an isochoric strain rate, which the twist satisfies because its metric stays flat. Lignified walls and turgid tissue carry Cauchy stresses (bending stresses, growth stresses), which are not \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\). The tendency of stems to grow toward uniform surface stress is an adaptive growth rule and is context, not \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_GT_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\). Grain and fibre lines are integral curves of material fields, not trajectories. \(\Pi_{\mu u}\) is the Hessian of a declared precision potential and enters only the coupling sector (\(O_6\)). Eq. [3] is instantiated with the default drive and maps no tracer. Sap is driven by pressure gradients against viscous drag, which is forced motion; no drag-law drive is declared in this epoch. The paths of material points under the twist are prescribed by the deformation, not by Eq. [3].

docs.title: \(O_3\) — Shear Damping & Hysteresis Consolidation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\left. rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = rac{2}{n} heta g_{\mu u} + 2\sigma_{\mu u}\); \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv \partial_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) (\(\gamma_\sigma = \mathrm{const} > 0\), \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\mu} = 0\)) \(\implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\Vert_{C^2(\mathcal{M})} = 0\); \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\), \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)); \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\).
  • Physical Instantiation: Without the torsional perturbation, \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) stays within tolerance of \(0\), the shear law holds trivially for any \(\gamma_\sigma > 0\), \(\hat{h} = \hat{h}_\infty = 0\), and the aperture supports no shear-relaxation test. The hydraulic relaxation of \(\mathcal{F}\) is a property of the \(O_4\) balance law and is not mapped to \(\sigma\). Under the perturbation, \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = rac{1}{2}g^{\mu\alpha}\partial_ au g_{\alpha u}\) is the isochoric strain rate of the recovering segment, trace-free because \( heta \equiv 0\). If the twist recovers as a single overdamped exponential at a constant rate, every component of \(\sigma\) decays at that rate, and the mixed-form shear law holds to first order in the twist strain; the second-order terms fall within a declared residual. That rate is \(\gamma_\sigma\). It is not predicted from independent parameters: it is estimated per recovery trajectory, and the test is whether one constant rate fits within each trajectory, with the pre-declared precondition that \(\sigma\) does not change sign during the window (the mixed-form law forbids oscillation, so underdamped sway is excluded). This is the aperture's contribution to the shear-relaxation family (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3). As the twist recovers, \(\hat{h} o \hat{h}_\infty\), the logarithmic strain of any residual twist (set), and \((\hat{g}_\infty)_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu\alpha}(\exp\hat{h}_\infty)^\alpha_{\; u}\) has unit determinant. \(V_{\mathrm{local}}\) is the hysteresis content of a cover set. Lasting responses of wood to loading, such as permanent set or reaction-wood formation, lie between windows and enter through \(\mathcal{H}_0\).

docs.title: \(O_4\) — Free-Energy Balance, Spectral Low-Pass Gating & Boundary Stress Conservation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( rac{\partial\mathcal{F}}{\partial au} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), \(J_W^\alpha \equiv -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = \mathfrak{K}^{ eta\alpha} \succ 0\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\); \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\); \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au) = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\); \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: With \( heta \equiv 0\) the balance law reads \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} = abla_\alpha((k^{\alpha eta}/C) abla_ eta\mathcal{F}) - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\): the storage–conductance equation of plant water transport in water-potential form, the continuum version of capacitance–resistance models of the soil–plant–atmosphere continuum. Capacitance gives the finite relaxation time, so the field is stored, not quasi-static. Every departure from the default (organ-wise anisotropic \(k\), lateral loss) satisfies the binding closure: each is a named law with finite pre-declared parameters, estimated independently and tested against pre-declared tolerances, and each is rejected if the default fits at least as well (closure (iv)). Under the torsional perturbation the Laplacian and \(J_W\) are evaluated with \(g( au)\). The gate sector follows §0.1 item 8: the Neumann spectrum of \(- abla^2_g\) is fixed on the volume-rigid xylem and drifts by a fraction of the order of the shear strain under the perturbation, which is negligible within the window. The faster decay of fine spatial structure in the water potential is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the gate without being the gate. The stress-conservation equivalence holds identically (§0.1 item 4); stresses in wood are not \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\).

docs.title: \(O_5\) — Riemannian Geometric Mean Gluing, Percolation & Harmonic Circulation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\); \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) geodesically convex for \(g^{(ij)}( au) \; orall au \ge au_0\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\); \(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\); \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\); \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} G_{\infty,\mu u}^{(i)} \succ 0\) (standing hypothesis with \(H_0 = 0\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: The cover consists of \( au\)-independent material subregions of the conducting xylem. A single cover set, a thin shell, contains the concave part of \(\partial\mathcal{M}\): the boundary with the non-conducting core. The other cover sets are intersections of \(\mathcal{M}\) with strictly convex bodies that stay clear of those concave parts. Every overlap is then an intersection of strictly convex bodies with the convex side of a cylinder \(r = \mathrm{const}\) or of a cross-section, so it is convex at \( au_0\) (§0.1 item 9). The twist maps each cylinder \(r = \mathrm{const}\) and each cross-section onto itself, and strictly convex parts stay convex for twist strains below a declared bound. Convexity for \(g( au)\) is checked on the measured metric. Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of \(g\), so the gluing holds identically, \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} = 0\), and \(g^{(i)} o G_\infty^{(i)}\) as the twist recovers (\(H_0 = 0\)). Every overlap is crossed by the hydraulic transient, so \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\). The connectivity of the conduit network through inter-conduit pits is a property of the tissue that enters through \(k\); a network below its percolation threshold has no continuum conductivity and is not an admissible domain. That connectivity is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the condition \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} > \phi_c\) and is not identified with it. The conducting xylem surrounds a non-conducting core, so \(b_1(\mathcal{M}) \ge 1\). On an annular stem segment the harmonic Neumann field is the angular field around the core, computed with \(g( au)\). No transport current is identified with it, and no claim is made about it (§0.1 item 9).

docs.title: \(O_6\) — Asymmetric Phase-Lead Coupling & Trace-Free Deformation Operator
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\); \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) (hypothesis) \(\wedge \; \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\); \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u\,dA > 0\) (hypothesis, \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), with this boundary flux integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) (Branch II).
  • Physical Instantiation: Take two adjacent cover sets along the flow path, for example a lower and an upper stem region that share an overlap \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\), or an outer and an inner sapwood region of differing conductivity. The partner fields are the rate of change of the sap free-energy flux in the two orientations (§0.1 item 9), so \(\eta_{[i o j]} = \partial_ au J_W\): a spatially resolved flux field, not a temporal lag between scalar signals. The boundary data are of mixed kind:
  • at the root collar the inflow declines as the collar potential rises;
  • at the crown base the outflow changes continuously: the step acts on transpiration inside the crown compartment, so at \( au_0^+\) the crown-base outflow still equals the old transpiration rate, and it then declines toward the new rate as the crown's xylem and leaf tissue refill;
  • at the cambial interface water flows outward into the bark as it refills.

Whether \(\partial_ au J_W\) changes sign in the stem is not decided by these descriptions: it may be one-signed or not, and its zero set, if any, has no simple form. The sign structure comes from the prediction. The zero set is predicted before the window from the declared model, using the independently estimated \(k\), \(C\), and \(k_{\mathrm{p}}\), the root and rhizosphere conductances, and the declared crown and bark compartments. The declared overlap is one that the predicted zero set does not reach during the overlap's window, with the detection threshold of §0.1 item 9. On it \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) keeps one direction, which the declaration states from the predicted solution; typically it points toward the root collar where the flux is declining. The odd 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\) is its image under the declared non-singular precision map, with distinct Hessians, and is non-zero there. Under the non-degeneracy hypothesis \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), built per r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3] from these fields and the declared precision potentials, \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0\) gives \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\), with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general. Under the flux-positivity hypothesis the coupling transmits correlation between the subsystem marginals of the declared state sector (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\)). Both are standing hypotheses, not consequences of sap flow, and this aperture is not among the systems of the current coupling test. In Branch II the hydraulic transient decays as the shoot settles, so the coupling flux is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\). Under the torsional perturbation the overlaps are convex for \(g( au)\) (\(O_5\)). Any threshold of twist beyond which an overlap would lose convexity is an aperture-level empirical conjecture mapped to the r10 §5.12 witness criterion \(a_\infty = 2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma < a_c(E)\), which is a design constraint of that witness. No such threshold is asserted.

docs.title: \(O_7\) — Principal-Bundle Gauge Coherence, Impedance Decay & Hysteresis Alignment
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(D_\mu = \partial_\mu - i g_{\mathrm{YM}}\,\mathrm{ad}_{A_\mu}\); \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\); \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2} o 1\), \(\hat{\chi} \equiv \chi_E\hat{u}\) (Branch II); \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The gauge sector is the trivial declaration of §0.1 item 10, so \([F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\) identically. Without the torsional perturbation, \(\chi_E \equiv 1\) and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu \equiv 0\). Under it, \( heta \equiv 0\) gives \(\chi_E - 1 = 3\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}/\langle\Theta_E angle^2\). The slope of \(\ln(\chi_E - 1)\) is then \(-2\gamma_\sigma - 2\,d\ln\langle\Theta_E angle/d au\), and the second term is a relative rate of measured dissipation, so the slope contains no \(s_0\). On sub-intervals where measured dissipation is constant within a pre-declared relative tolerance, \(\chi_E - 1\) decays at \(2\gamma_\sigma\). Under the declarations this is equivalent to the shear-rate test of \(O_3\) and adds no separate content. Its \(s_0\)-independence also rests on the declared \( heta \equiv 0\): whether the measured residual volumetric strain rate is negligible against \(\langle\Theta_E angle\) depends on \(s_0\). \(\chi\) is undefined (\( heta = 0\)) and is not used. \(\hat{ ho}_g = e^{-\hat{h}_\infty}e^{\hat{h}}/\mathrm{Tr}(e^{-\hat{h}_\infty}e^{\hat{h}}) o rac{1}{n}\delta^\mu_ u\) as the twist recovers, a residual computable from the twist record. Alignment with \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}\) requires the Hessian of the record to become isotropic, an asymptotic condition stated and not tested. The \(O_7\) Eq. [3] identities hold with divergence-free \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) and \(u_{\mathrm{exp}}\), \(J_E\) bounded in \(C^1\) under the held data, and \(\hat{h} o \hat{h}_\infty\), so \(\mathcal{L}_{\mathbf{J}_E}(\hat{h} - \hat{h}_\infty) o 0\). The aperture claims no alignment of flow with conduit orientation beyond what \(\mathfrak{K}\) declares, and no synchrony of canopy motion.

docs.title: \(O_\Omega\) — Topological Asymptote, Branch II: Bounded Non-Equilibrium Steady State
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)): \( heta \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{C^2(\mathcal{M})} 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^{\infty}\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\); \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\) and \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\); \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q) rac{\delta\Psi}{\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})} \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{} 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} o 0\) (with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly as \( au o \infty\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: Under held evaporative demand and soil water potential, the shoot approaches a steady water-potential field that carries a steady transpiration stream from the root collar to the leaves: a bounded non-equilibrium steady state. \( heta \equiv 0\) (so \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au = 0\) and \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\)). \(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\) while transpiration is maintained. \(\sigma o 0\) as any imposed twist recovers, and \(\partial_ au g o 0\). The transient coupling decays, so \(\mathcal{I}\) converges to \(s_0V_\infty\). The generator condition requires \(J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0\), an asymptotic hypothesis on the declared state sector that no finite window tests. The state is neither static equilibrium, which would require a hydrostatic potential field with no transpiration, nor a periodic return: repeated cycles of evaporative demand form a sequence of windows, each settling toward its own held data, and are never mapped to \( heta\) or read as a return. The limit belongs to the declared idealization of a non-growing shoot under held data; the physical plant leaves that idealization as it grows, which bounds the usable window.
  • Within windows the supported tests (aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5) are the shear-rate test (1) under the torsional perturbation, with \(\gamma_\sigma\) estimated per trajectory; the non-degeneracy check (4); the signs of \(\Theta_E\), \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}\), and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}}\) (5); the flux prediction (6); and the Branch II evidence (7).
  • Under the perturbation the \(\chi_E\) rate test (2) and the residual test (3) (\(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} = 2\sigma_{\mu u}\)) are equivalent to (1) and are not counted separately. Without it, tests (1)–(3) hold trivially.

docs.title: Aperture 3.2: Movement Ecology & Ecotone Foraging Dynamics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{trophic}}\))
1. Epistemological & Biological Scope
docs.text:
Aperture 3.2 maps the movement ecology of foraging animals (random search, area-restricted search, taxis toward resources, and movement across habitat edges and ecotones) and the trophic dynamics of predator and prey onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\). Its empirical domain is the redistribution and consumption of mobile prey in a three-dimensional foraging volume. There, random prey dispersal is a storage–diffusion process and predation is an interior sink, while the predators' trajectories follow a declared taxis drive. Lexicon is strictly restricted to movement ecology, behavioural ecology, trophic dynamics, and spatial population biology.

Declaration (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3; Branch II).

  • Domain \(\mathcal{M}\) (\(n = 3\)) and boundary \(\partial\mathcal{M}\). A three-dimensional foraging volume within one habitat (a layer of vegetation canopy or a body of the water column), fixed in space over one foraging window. \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) consists of:
  • an ecotone boundary with an adjacent prey-source habitat (supply), across which prey disperse into \(\mathcal{M}\);
  • an outflow boundary with a habitat into which prey that cross are lost to \(\mathcal{M}\) without return, so that prey density there is held at the datum within tolerance;
  • closed faces with no prey flux.

No prey reproduce inside \(\mathcal{M}\) and none enter except across the ecotone boundary, so all supply crosses \(\partial\mathcal{M}\). Within \(\mathcal{M}\), patches of differing structure (vegetation strata or plant types, or water layers) meet along internal transition zones. * Window. A foraging window (§0.1 item 1). It begins from a prior steady prey distribution, with prey supply at the ecotone, predator numbers, and habitat structure held within declared tolerances, so that \(\mathcal{F}\) is steady within the window. At \( au_0\) each tracked predator is labelled by the patch it occupies, and the window follows the mixing of the two labelled groups. The window is shorter than the prey's generation time and than the time over which predator numbers respond to prey. * Metric. Flat and rigid (§0.1 item 2): the domain is a fixed region of space, with \(g_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu u}\) in a Cartesian chart, so \( heta \equiv 0\) and \(\sigma \equiv 0\) by construction. Vegetation or water moving within the region is part of the medium and enters through \(\mathfrak{K}\) and as context. * Cone speed. \(c_*\) is the speed of sound in the ambient medium (air or water). Prey and predator speeds are \(\ll c_*\). * Storage. Unity: \(\mathcal{F}\) is itself the stored prey energy per unit volume, so no storage factor enters (§0.1 item 3). * Free energy \(\mathcal{F}\) and datum. \(\mathcal{F} = \epsilon_{\mathrm{p}}b\) (J m⁻³), with \(b\) the prey biomass density (g m⁻³) and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{p}}\) the declared energy content of prey biomass (J g⁻¹), from calorimetry of the prey population. The datum is zero (\(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0\)), and \(\mathcal{F} \ge 0\) holds trivially. \(\mathcal{F}\) is linear in prey biomass. The relaxation time \(\ell^2/D\) of prey dispersal across the volume is finite and resolvable. * Transport \(\mathfrak{K}\). \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = D_{\mathrm{p}}^{\alpha eta}\), the prey dispersal tensor, parametric: for example one horizontal and one vertical dispersal coefficient in a canopy layer or water column. Isotropic dispersal is the default. With \(j_b\) the prey biomass flux, \(J_W = \epsilon_{\mathrm{p}}j_b\). * Sink \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\). Predation with a type II functional response: $\(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = rac{aP\,\mathcal{F}}{1 + (ah/\epsilon_{\mathrm{p}})\,\mathcal{F}}\)$ Here \(a\) is the attack rate (volume searched per predator per unit time), \(h\) the handling time, and \(P\) the predator density, uniform within the window at an independently estimated value. \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\) is continuous, non-negative, non-decreasing in \(\mathcal{F}\), and zero at the datum. \(a\) and \(h\) are estimated from functional-response trials with the same predator individuals in a declared perturbation regime before the window (controlled prey densities), and \(P\) from a census, per closure (ii). * Drive. Predator taxis toward prey gradients, a named law (linear taxis with velocity relaxation, the deterministic part of a biased Ornstein–Uhlenbeck movement model): $\(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = au_v^{-1}\left(\chi_{\mathrm{P}}\,g^{\mu u} abla_ u b - v^\mu ight)\)$ Predators relax their velocity, at the rate \( au_v^{-1}\), toward a taxis velocity proportional to the prey-density gradient. The taxis sensitivity \(\chi_{\mathrm{P}}\) (the measured sensitivity of the master table) and \( au_v\) are estimated per closure (ii) from the same individuals' responses to an imposed prey gradient, in a declared perturbation regime before the window, never from the trajectories the law predicts. \(b \in C^2\) on the steady prey field of the window, so \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}}\) is jointly continuous and locally Lipschitz in \((\mathbf{x}, v)\), as r7 \(O_2\) Eq. [3] requires. * Eq. [3] is deterministic, so the declared reading is that \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}\) is the mean acceleration of predators conditional on position and velocity. The variability of search about that mean lies outside Eq. [3] and is not mapped. * The drive acts on individual trajectories. The uniform predator density declared for the sink is compatible with it only where taxis-driven redistribution of predators within the window stays below the uniformity tolerance (precondition 3). * Coupling-sector data. A predator search diffusivity \(D_{\mathrm{P}}\), estimated from predator tracks in a declared period before the window, is used, with the drive, only to predict the labelled-flux fields of \(O_6\) and their zero set. * Branch II evidence (closure (v)). * The trend of \(\langle heta angle\) and \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\) are zero by construction for a fixed region of space; this part of the evidence holds trivially and is stated as such. * \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) is estimated from measured dissipation (§0.1 item 7): * the supply term uses the prey flux across the ecotone boundary, from bidirectional interception traps or counts at that boundary, with \(\mathcal{F}\) there from a census; * the outflow face, at the datum, contributes nothing; * the consumption term uses predation rates from observed kills or feeding records of tracked predators, weighted by the local \(\mathcal{F}\); * the storage term is checked to be zero by repeated census.

None of these instruments or surfaces is that of the $O_1$ section.
  • \(\mathcal{F}\) is a resource energy density, not a thermodynamic potential of the dispersing medium, so \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}\) is the entropy production of the declared mapping, not a measured physical entropy production. The physical dissipation named for the sign comparison is the metabolic power of the foraging community (by respirometry or isotope turnover), which is positive in any living system. The comparison therefore holds trivially and is stated as such.
  • Admissible domains (declared, checkable preconditions):
  • prey movement is unbiased random dispersal at the declared scale, with no drift from predator avoidance or resource tracking beyond tolerance, and prey numbers are large enough for a continuum density;
  • no prey reproduction, immigration other than across the ecotone boundary, or mortality other than predation within the window;
  • predator density uniform within tolerance and predator numbers constant throughout the window, checked by census. Sustained taxis on the steady prey field would drive predators toward a profile \(P \propto \exp(\chi_{\mathrm{P}}b/D_{\mathrm{P}})\), so the relative non-uniformity it can produce is about \(\chi_{\mathrm{P}}\Delta b/D_{\mathrm{P}}\), with \(\Delta b\) the range of prey density over \(\mathcal{M}\). This number is computed before the window from the declared parameters and must lie below the uniformity tolerance;
  • \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) throughout \( ar{\mathcal{M}}\): prey density decreases from the ecotone boundary toward the predation zones and the outflow boundary;
  • prey density at the outflow boundary at the datum within tolerance;
  • habitat structure, and hence \(D_{\mathrm{p}}\), fixed within the window;
  • for the one-dimensional statement of \(O_6\) only: patches and data laterally uniform across the transition zone, and taxis drift negligible across it (\(\chi_{\mathrm{P}}\vert abla b\vert\ell_{ij}/D_{\mathrm{P}}\) below a declared tolerance, with \(\ell_{ij}\) the width of the zone), because a spatially varying drift can break the monotonicity of the label densities.
  • Titled phenomena outside the domain.
  • Foraging decisions (patch choice, giving-up rules, the ideal free distribution) redistribute predators between windows. Within the window predator density is declared uniform, and the decisions enter only through the drive's parameters and as context.
  • Predator–prey population cycles and prey reproduction lie between windows. Their oscillations are never mapped to \( heta\) or \(\sigma\).
  • Migration, home ranges, and learned routes are context, and enter each window through \(\mathcal{H}_0\).
  • The ecotone is the supply boundary only; the boundaries between patches inside \(\mathcal{M}\) are called internal transition zones, never ecotones. Edge effects on prey supply enter as boundary data.

docs.title: 2. Coordinate-by-Coordinate Mapping (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\))
\(O_0\) — Exogenous Flux & Emergent Foliation Time
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( heta \equiv -N K \overset{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0}{=} rac{1}{2}g^{\mu u} rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} = rac{1}{\sqrt{\vert g\vert}} rac{\partial\sqrt{\vert g\vert}}{\partial au} = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\); \(\Theta_E \equiv rac{\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}}{s_0} = - rac{ eta_{\mathrm{th}}}{s_0}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\); \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \sqrt{ heta^2 + \Theta_E^2}\), \( au_\Theta( au) \equiv \int_{ au_0}^{ au}\langle\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au'\); \( rac{dV_{\mathcal{M}}}{d au} = \int_{\mathcal{M}} heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\), with \(\lim_{ au o\infty}V_{\mathcal{M}}( au) = V_\infty < \infty\) (Branch II); \( rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), \(q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv -\ln(v_0Q(\mathbf{x}, au))\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The domain is a fixed region of space, so \( heta \equiv 0\), \(dV_{\mathcal{M}}/d au = 0\), and \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\) by construction. The prey supply across the ecotone is throughput and is never mapped to \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) (§0.1 item 6). Openness is carried by throughput: prey disperse down their density gradient and are consumed, so \(\Theta_E > 0\) (by \(O_1\)), \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} = \Theta_E\), and \( au_\Theta\) counts the entropy production of the declared mapping per \(s_0\). The record accumulates by \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) along the throughput current. The spatial memory of predators (learned routes, remembered patch quality) is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\) and is not identified with it; it enters each window through \(\mathcal{H}_0\).

docs.title: \(O_1\) — Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Openness
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} = p_0\oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} \equiv \int_{\mathcal{M}}(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F})\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} + \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\); \( abla_\mu\mathcal{F} eq 0\); \(J_E^\mu \equiv rac{J_W^\mu}{p_0} = - rac{1}{p_0}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\) (Branch II, fixed); \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\); \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: Prey supply across the ecotone, set against consumption by predators and loss across the outflow boundary, holds the volume far from equilibrium; equilibrium would be a uniform prey density with no supply, no flux, and no predation. With \(J_E^\mu = -p_0^{-1}D_{\mathrm{p}}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\), \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\) holds identically wherever \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) (precondition 4), so \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). The prey biomass flux runs down the density gradient, from the ecotone toward the predation zones and the outflow boundary, in the direction of \(J_E^\mu\). \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0\), so \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). The empirical content of \(O_1\) is the flux-prediction test (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3, §5.5 item 6). \(D_{\mathrm{p}}^{\alpha eta}\) is estimated per closure (ii) from marked prey (mark–release–recapture or tracking) released in a declared perturbation regime before the window. It must predict \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}} = \epsilon_{\mathrm{p}}j_b^{\mathrm{meas}}\) across a declared interior section \(S\), with \(j_b^{\mathrm{meas}}\) from bidirectional interception or counts of prey crossing \(S\), and \( abla\mathcal{F}\) from prey census on both sides of \(S\); neither uses the other or the declared \(D_{\mathrm{p}}\). This aperture is not among the systems of the current flux-prediction test.

docs.title: \(O_2\) — Unimodular Weyl Factorization, Constraint Precision & Trajectories
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}( au, \mathbf{x}) = \Omega^2( au, \mathbf{x})\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) with \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) = 0 \implies \det g = \Omega^{2n}\), \( rac{\partial\ln\Omega}{\partial au} = rac{1}{n} heta\); \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\); \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\), \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\); \( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\); \(\left.\left( rac{dv^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}\), \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2)\left(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu ight)\), \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2 < 1\), with the default \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the fixed region the unimodular Weyl split is trivial (\(\Omega \equiv 1\), \(\hat{h} \equiv 0\), \(\partial_ au\ln\Omega = 0\)). The split isolates the volume element only algebraically; \( heta\) remains coupled to \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) and \(\sigma_{\alpha eta}\) through the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation (r10 Decision 2), whose two sides vanish identically here (§0.1 items 2 and 4). Vegetation structure and water layering enter through \(D_{\mathrm{p}}\), the drive's parameters, and the geometry of \(\mathcal{M}\), not through \(g\). Least-cost movement paths are geodesics of a separate cost-of-transport metric, which is not \(g_{\mu u}\). \(\Pi_{\mu u}\) is the Hessian of a declared precision potential and enters only the coupling sector (\(O_6\)). Eq. [3] is instantiated with the declared taxis drive. On the static flat metric, in the Cartesian chart, \(\Gamma = 0\) and \(\partial_ au g = 0\), so Eq. [3] reduces to \(dv^\mu/d au = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} \approx a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = au_v^{-1}(\chi_{\mathrm{P}}\,\partial^\mu b - v^\mu)\), with \(u^2 \ll 1\): predators relax toward a taxis velocity up the prey gradient. This conditional mean acceleration is the aperture's trajectory claim, and the driven trajectory equation is untested in this epoch (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3). Prey paths are random dispersal, described by the \(O_4\) balance law, and are not trajectories of Eq. [3].

docs.title: \(O_3\) — Shear Damping & Hysteresis Consolidation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\left. rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = rac{2}{n} heta g_{\mu u} + 2\sigma_{\mu u}\); \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv \partial_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) (\(\gamma_\sigma = \mathrm{const} > 0\), \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\mu} = 0\)) \(\implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\Vert_{C^2(\mathcal{M})} = 0\); \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\), \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)); \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the fixed region \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv 0\), so the shear law holds trivially for any \(\gamma_\sigma > 0\), \(\hat{h} = \hat{h}_\infty = 0\), and \(\hat{g}_\infty = \hat{g} = \delta\); this aperture supports no shear-relaxation test (§0.1 item 2). Behavioural recovery after a disturbance, and the settling of the prey field, are not mapped to \(\sigma\): the first lies in \(\mathcal{H}\) and context, the second in the \(O_4\) balance law. \(V_{\mathrm{local}}\) is the hysteresis content of a patch \(\mathcal{U}_i\).
