docs.title: \(O_4\) — Free-Energy Balance, Spectral Low-Pass Gating & Boundary Stress Conservation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( rac{\partial\mathcal{F}}{\partial au} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), \(J_W^\alpha \equiv -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = \mathfrak{K}^{ eta\alpha} \succ 0\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\); \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\); \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au) = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\); \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: With \( heta \equiv 0\) the balance law reads \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} = abla_\alpha(D_{\mathrm{p}}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}) - aP\mathcal{F}/(1 + (ah/\epsilon_{\mathrm{p}})\mathcal{F})\): the reaction–diffusion equation of dispersing prey under type II predation, steady within the window. Its finite relaxation time makes the field stored, not quasi-static. Both departures from the default (anisotropic dispersal, predation) satisfy the binding closure, and each is rejected if the default fits at least as well (closure (iv)). The gate sector follows §0.1 item 8: the Neumann eigenmodes of \(- abla^2\) on the fixed region are fixed, so the gate does not drift, and the faster decay of fine spatial structure in the prey field is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the gate without being the gate. The stress-conservation equivalence holds identically (§0.1 item 4).

docs.title: \(O_5\) — Riemannian Geometric Mean Gluing, Percolation & Harmonic Circulation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\); \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) geodesically convex for \(g^{(ij)}( au) \; orall au \ge au_0\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\); \(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\); \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\); \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} G_{\infty,\mu u}^{(i)} \succ 0\) (standing hypothesis with \(H_0 = 0\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: The cover consists of fixed subregions of the volume: the patches and their surroundings, with convex overlaps \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) along the internal transition zones. Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of the flat metric, so the gluing holds identically, each overlap stays convex, \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} = 0\), and \(g^{(i)} = G_\infty^{(i)}\) at every \( au\) (\(H_0 = 0\); §0.1 item 9). The labelled predator groups mix across every overlap of the connected volume, so \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\). Habitat connectivity (gaps, corridors, and barriers to movement) enters through \(D_{\mathrm{p}}\) and the predator movement parameters. It is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the condition \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} > \phi_c\) and is not identified with it. The declared volume is simply connected, so \(\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} \equiv 0\) (§0.1 item 9). A volume pierced by an impassable obstacle lies outside this declaration.

docs.title: \(O_6\) — Asymmetric Phase-Lead Coupling & Trace-Free Deformation Operator
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\); \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) (hypothesis) \(\wedge \; \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\); \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u\,dA > 0\) (hypothesis, \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), with this boundary flux integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) (Branch II).
  • Physical Instantiation: Take two adjacent patches \(\mathcal{U}_i\) and \(\mathcal{U}_j\) that share a transition zone \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\). The partner fields are the movement-flux fields of the two labelled predator groups: \(\eta_{i o j}^\lambda\) is the flux density of the predators labelled \(i\) at \( au_0\) (animals per unit area per unit time), and \(\eta_{j o i}^\lambda\) that of the predators labelled \(j\). Both are estimated from individual tracks with a declared smoothing kernel, so they are defined on all of \(\mathcal{M}\) and lie in \(C^2\). They are spatially resolved flux fields, not temporal lead–lag statistics between scalar signals.
  • The two fields are not antisymmetric by construction. Their sum is the net predator flux, which is small under precondition 3, so \(\eta_{[i o j]} = rac{1}{2}(\eta_{i o j} - \eta_{j o i})\) is close to each group's own flux.
  • As the groups mix after \( au_0\), predators labelled \(i\) cross the transition zone toward \(\mathcal{U}_j\) and those labelled \(j\) toward \(\mathcal{U}_i\), so on the zone \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) points from \(\mathcal{U}_i\) toward \(\mathcal{U}_j\). The zero set of \(\eta_{[i o j]}\), where the two group fluxes balance, is predicted before the window from \(D_{\mathrm{P}}\) and the declared drive. The declared overlap is one that the predicted zero set does not reach, with the detection threshold of §0.1 item 9.
  • Where the patches and data are laterally uniform across the zone (precondition 7), each label density starts as a step across the zone and, with taxis drift negligible across the zone, stays monotone under diffusive mixing with closed ends. The label flux then keeps one direction in the interior, and the zero set lies on the closed faces. Without lateral uniformity no such argument is claimed.

The odd 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\) is the image of \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) under the declared non-singular precision map, with distinct Hessians (§0.1 item 9), and is non-zero on the overlap. Under the non-degeneracy hypothesis \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), built per r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3] from these fields and the declared precision potentials, \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0\) gives \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\), with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general. The eigendirections are directions of the operator \(M^{(ij)}\), not of aggregation or spreading of animals. Under the flux-positivity hypothesis the coupling transmits correlation between the subsystem marginals of the declared state sector (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\)). Both are standing hypotheses, not consequences of movement, and this pair is the aperture's system in the current coupling test (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3, family 3).

In Branch II the labelled fluxes decay as the groups mix, at the rate of the slowest mixing mode, so the coupling flux is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) and no sustained coupling is asserted. What decays is the difference between the groups' fluxes, not movement itself: the predators keep moving and foraging. The overlaps are fixed and convex, so the r10 §5.12 constraint \(a_\infty = 2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma < a_c(E)\), a design constraint of a deforming witness overlap, has no counterpart here.

docs.title: \(O_7\) — Principal-Bundle Gauge Coherence, Impedance Decay & Hysteresis Alignment
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(D_\mu = \partial_\mu - i g_{\mathrm{YM}}\,\mathrm{ad}_{A_\mu}\); \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\); \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2} o 1\), \(\hat{\chi} \equiv \chi_E\hat{u}\) (Branch II); \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The gauge sector is the trivial declaration of §0.1 item 10, so \([F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\) identically. With \(\sigma \equiv 0\), \(\chi_E \equiv 1\) and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu \equiv 0\) at every \( au\), and \(\chi\) is undefined (\( heta = 0\)). \(\hat{ ho}_g = rac{1}{n}\delta^\mu_ u\) at every \( au\), and alignment with \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}\) holds where the Hessian of the declared convex record becomes isotropic, an asymptotic condition stated and not tested. The \(O_7\) Eq. [3] identities hold with divergence-free \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) and \(u_{\mathrm{exp}}\), bounded \(J_E\), and \(\hat{h} \equiv \hat{h}_\infty\). Collective alignment of moving animals (schooling, flocking) is not mapped to the gauge connection; it is context, and no alignment or synchrony claim is made.

docs.title: \(O_\Omega\) — Topological Asymptote, Branch II: Bounded Non-Equilibrium Steady State
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)): \( heta \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{C^2(\mathcal{M})} 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^{\infty}\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\); \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\) and \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\); \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q) rac{\delta\Psi}{\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})} \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{} 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} o 0\) (with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly as \( au o \infty\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: Under maintained prey supply and a held predator density, the volume holds a steady prey distribution that carries a steady prey flux from the ecotone into the predation zones and across the outflow boundary: a bounded non-equilibrium steady state. \( heta \equiv 0\), \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\), \(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\) while supply is maintained, \(\sigma \equiv 0\), and \(\partial_ au g \equiv 0\). The labelled-group coupling decays as the groups mix, so \(\mathcal{I} o s_0V_\infty\). The generator condition requires \(J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0\), an asymptotic hypothesis on the declared state sector that no finite window tests. The state is neither static equilibrium, which would require uniform prey density with no supply, flux, or predation, nor a periodic return: predator–prey cycles lie between windows and are never read as a return. The limit belongs to the declared idealization of constant, uniform predators and non-reproducing prey; the physical community leaves it as prey reproduce or predators respond, which bounds the usable window.
  • Within windows the supported tests (aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5) are the non-degeneracy check (4), the signs of \(\Theta_E\), \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}\), and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}}\) (5), the flux prediction (6), and the Branch II evidence (7).
  • Tests (1)–(3) hold trivially on the fixed region.

docs.title: Aperture 3.3: Benthic & Edaphic Biogeochemical Metabolism (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{metabolic}}\))
1. Epistemological & Biological Scope
docs.text:
Aperture 3.3 maps the metabolism of sediments and water-saturated soils onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\): microbial respiration, the sequence of terminal electron acceptors, redox stratification, the decomposition of detritus, and the exchange of solutes across the sediment–water interface. Its empirical domain is the supply of a dissolved oxidant from overlying water, across the diffusive boundary layer (DBL), into a sediment column where microbes consume it. Lexicon is strictly restricted to biogeochemistry, microbial ecology, aquatic and soil metabolism, and bioenergetics.

Declaration (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3; Branch II).

  • Domain \(\mathcal{M}\) (\(n = 3\)) and boundary \(\partial\mathcal{M}\). A column of sediment or water-saturated soil, for example an intact core, with the DBL of water above its surface. \(\mathcal{M}\) is the DBL together with the sediment down to a declared lower face. \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) consists of:
  • the top of the DBL, where the overlying water is well mixed (supply), held at a declared oxidant concentration \(c_w\);
  • the lower face, at the base of the zone that the oxidant penetrates, where it is consumed by reduced species diffusing up from below in a thin reaction zone outside \(\mathcal{M}\), so that the oxidant concentration is held at zero there (outflow at the datum);
  • closed lateral walls.

The sediment–water interface lies inside \(\mathcal{M}\), with a declared smooth transition zone. There are no interior sources: all oxidant crosses the supply face. * Window. A relaxation window (§0.1 item 1), opened by a declared step increase of \(c_w\) from a prior steady state, after which \(c_w\) is held within tolerance. The window ends before the lower face moves beyond a declared tolerance, and before microbial activity changes beyond tolerance. * Metric. Flat and rigid (§0.1 item 2): \(g_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu u}\) in a Cartesian chart, with compaction and swelling of the sediment within the rigid tolerance. * Cone speed. \(c_*\) is the compressional wave speed of the water-saturated sediment. Diffusive speeds are \(\ll c_*\). * Storage. In the sediment the oxidant's storage coefficient is the porosity \(\varphi_{\mathrm{s}}\), declared uniform over the sediment part of \(\mathcal{M}\) within tolerance; in the DBL it is unity. The declared law is normalized by \(\varphi_{\mathrm{s}}\) (§0.1 item 3). It is then exact in the sediment and keeps \(J_W\) continuous across the interface, as the physical flux is. Its only departure from the physical law is in the DBL, where it stores oxidant with the coefficient \(\varphi_{\mathrm{s}}\) instead of \(1\). Relative to the oxidant stored in the sediment, about \(\varphi_{\mathrm{s}}c\,\ell_{\mathrm{p}}\) per unit area against the excess \((1 - \varphi_{\mathrm{s}})c\,\delta\), that departure is of relative order \((1 - \varphi_{\mathrm{s}})\delta/(\varphi_{\mathrm{s}}\ell_{\mathrm{p}})\) in the storage rate, with \(\delta\) the DBL thickness and \(\ell_{\mathrm{p}}\) the oxidant penetration depth, and the pre-declared flux tolerance must exceed it (precondition 3). * Free energy \(\mathcal{F}\) and datum. \(\mathcal{F} = c\,(-\Delta G_r^{\circ\prime})\) (J m⁻³), with \(c\) the pore-water (or, in the DBL, water) concentration of the oxidant (mol m⁻³) and \(-\Delta G_r^{\circ\prime} > 0\) the declared standard-state free-energy yield per mole of oxidant reduced in the declared respiration reaction (J mol⁻¹), taken from tabulated standards. This is the declared linear form of aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3 item 3: the actual reaction free energy depends on the concentrations, and the standard-state yield is used as a declared constant. The datum is zero (\(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0\)), and \(\mathcal{F} \ge 0\) holds trivially. The relaxation time \(\ell_{\mathrm{p}}^2/D_{\mathrm{s}}\) is finite and resolvable. * Transport \(\mathfrak{K}\). In the sediment, \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = D_{\mathrm{s}}^{\alpha eta}\), the effective (tortuosity-corrected) pore-water diffusion tensor, parametric with layering: \(\mathrm{diag}(D_{\mathrm{H}}, D_{\mathrm{H}}, D_{\mathrm{V}})\) in a chart aligned with the bedding for laminated sediment, with isotropic \(D_{\mathrm{s}}\) as the default. In the DBL, \(\mathfrak{K} = (D_0/\varphi_{\mathrm{s}})\,g^{\alpha eta}\), with \(D_0\) the molecular diffusivity of the oxidant in water, tabulated at the declared temperature and salinity. The two are joined smoothly across the declared transition zone, so \(\mathfrak{K} \in C^1\). With \(j\) the molar oxidant flux per unit bulk area, \(J_W = (-\Delta G_r^{\circ\prime})\,j/\varphi_{\mathrm{s}}\). The conversion factor \((-\Delta G_r^{\circ\prime})/\varphi_{\mathrm{s}}\) is declared, with \(\varphi_{\mathrm{s}}\) measured independently on the same column, for example from the water content and density of its sediment after the window, or from electrical resistivity. * Sink \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\). Microbial consumption with Michaelis–Menten kinetics, \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = V_{\mathrm{m}}\mathcal{F}/(K_{\mathcal{F}} + \mathcal{F})\), with \(K_{\mathcal{F}} = K_{\mathrm{m}}(-\Delta G_r^{\circ\prime})\) and \(V_{\mathrm{m}}\) in the storage-normalized units of the declared law. \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\) is continuous, non-negative, non-decreasing in \(\mathcal{F}\), and spread over the oxic sediment, with no sharp front inside \(\mathcal{M}\). \(V_{\mathrm{m}}\) and \(K_{\mathrm{m}}\) are estimated per closure (ii): from the consumption response of the same column to declared changes of overlying-water oxidant before the window (a declared perturbation regime), or from incubations of its own sediment after the window. * Drive. Default, \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\) (§0.1 item 5). * Branch II evidence (closure (v)). * The trend of \(\langle heta angle\) and a bound on \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\) come from the measured elevation of the sediment surface and the column length, which must stay within the rigid tolerance. * \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) is estimated from measured dissipation (§0.1 item 7): * the supply term uses the oxidant supply to the overlying water and \(\mathcal{F}\) there, from a second, independent set of overlying-water sensors (or discrete samples by a different analytical method); * the lower face, at the datum, contributes nothing; * the consumption term uses the declared, independently estimated \(V_{\mathrm{m}}\) and \(K_{\mathrm{m}}\) with \(\mathcal{F}\) from a second set of microsensor profiles; * the storage term uses repeated profiles. * Weaker independence. The only boundary at which \(\mathcal{F} eq 0\) is the supply face, and the \(O_1\) test measures the flux across the sediment–water interface. The two surfaces are separated only by the DBL, so the two flux records differ only by the DBL's storage change. The evidence is therefore independent of the \(O_1\) measurement (different instruments) but not of the quantity that it measures, which is weaker than the separation of surfaces in Tier 2. * The physical dissipation is the entropy production of oxidant diffusion, which is non-negative by the second law, so the comparison tests only the sign of the estimate. * Admissible domains (declared, checkable preconditions): 1. no bioturbation, bioirrigation, ebullition, or advective pore-water flow within the window (a defaunated or naturally quiescent column, checked by inert-tracer profiles); 2. no oxidant production in \(\mathcal{M}\) (no benthic photosynthesis or other oxidant-producing process), and \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) throughout \( ar{\mathcal{M}}\); 3. porosity uniform over the sediment part of \(\mathcal{M}\) within tolerance, and the DBL departure of relative order \((1 - \varphi_{\mathrm{s}})\delta/(\varphi_{\mathrm{s}}\ell_{\mathrm{p}})\) within the flux tolerance; 4. a fixed lower face: oxidant at the lower face below a pre-declared detection threshold, and its depth constant within tolerance, throughout the window. A step increase of \(c_w\) pushes the oxic boundary down unless the upward flux of reduced species absorbs the extra oxidant, so the step size is chosen before the window such that the shift of the lower face, predicted from the declared parameters and a declared, independently measured upward flux of reduced species, stays within that tolerance; and \(V_{\mathrm{m}}\), \(K_{\mathrm{m}}\) constant (no growth or decline of microbial activity beyond tolerance); 5. isothermal conditions within tolerance, so that \(D_0\), \(D_{\mathrm{s}}\), \(V_{\mathrm{m}}\), and \(K_{\mathrm{m}}\) are constant; 6. compaction and swelling within the rigid tolerance; 7. for the one-dimensional statements of \(O_6\) only: a laterally uniform supply and sediment, so that the problem is one-dimensional in depth. * Titled phenomena outside the domain. * Redox sequence. The other electron acceptors (nitrate, manganese and iron oxides, sulfate) and methanogenesis lie below the lower face, or enter as context; each window declares one oxidant. The reduced species that consume it at the lower face enter as the outflow boundary condition. * Organic matter. Extracellular enzymatic hydrolysis and the humification of organic matter set the supply of electron donors, and so \(V_{\mathrm{m}}\) and \(K_{\mathrm{m}}\); they enter through the declared parameters and \(\mathcal{H}\). * Fauna and resuspension. Bioturbation, bioirrigation, and resuspension are excluded within windows (precondition 1). Between windows they rework the sediment and enter through \(\mathcal{H}\). * Unsaturated soils. Gas-phase diffusion in unsaturated soils is outside this declaration; it would need its own storage coefficient (the air-filled porosity) and is context here. * Persistence. Long-term persistence of buried metabolism below the lower face is context.

docs.title: 2. Coordinate-by-Coordinate Mapping (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\))
\(O_0\) — Exogenous Flux & Emergent Foliation Time
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( heta \equiv -N K \overset{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0}{=} rac{1}{2}g^{\mu u} rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} = rac{1}{\sqrt{\vert g\vert}} rac{\partial\sqrt{\vert g\vert}}{\partial au} = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\); \(\Theta_E \equiv rac{\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}}{s_0} = - rac{ eta_{\mathrm{th}}}{s_0}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\); \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \sqrt{ heta^2 + \Theta_E^2}\), \( au_\Theta( au) \equiv \int_{ au_0}^{ au}\langle\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au'\); \( rac{dV_{\mathcal{M}}}{d au} = \int_{\mathcal{M}} heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\), with \(\lim_{ au o\infty}V_{\mathcal{M}}( au) = V_\infty < \infty\) (Branch II); \( rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), \(q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv -\ln(v_0Q(\mathbf{x}, au))\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The column is rigid, so \( heta \equiv 0\), \(dV_{\mathcal{M}}/d au = 0\), and \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\). The oxidant supplied across the top of the DBL is throughput and is never mapped to \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) (§0.1 item 6). Diffusion of oxidant from the overlying water to the respiring sediment and the lower face produces entropy at every point, so \(\Theta_E > 0\) (by \(O_1\)), \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} = \Theta_E\), and \( au_\Theta\) counts entropy production per \(s_0\). The record accumulates by \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) along the throughput current. The sediment's chemical and biological record (layers of oxides and sulfides, organic content, the structure of the microbial community) is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\) and is not identified with it. Within the window it is held fixed (precondition 4), and it enters through \(\mathcal{H}_0\). The oxidant profile itself is \(\mathcal{F}\), not the record.

docs.title: \(O_1\) — Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Openness
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} = p_0\oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} \equiv \int_{\mathcal{M}}(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F})\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} + \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\); \( abla_\mu\mathcal{F} eq 0\); \(J_E^\mu \equiv rac{J_W^\mu}{p_0} = - rac{1}{p_0}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\) (Branch II, fixed); \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\); \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The maintained difference in oxidant between the overlying water and the lower face, together with consumption, holds the column far from equilibrium. With \(J_E^\mu = -p_0^{-1}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\), \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\) holds identically wherever \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) (precondition 2), so \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). The oxidant flux runs down its gradient, from the overlying water into the sediment, in the direction of \(J_E^\mu\). \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0\), so \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). The empirical content of \(O_1\) is the flux-prediction test (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3, §5.5 item 6), which exercises this aperture in the current epoch (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3). \(D_{\mathrm{s}}^{\alpha eta}\) is estimated on the same column per closure (ii), from an inert-tracer diffusion experiment (a different modality), and \(\varphi_{\mathrm{s}}\) independently as above. The declared law must predict \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}} = (-\Delta G_r^{\circ\prime})\,j^{\mathrm{meas}}/\varphi_{\mathrm{s}}\) across a declared section \(S\) just beneath the sediment–water interface. Here \(j^{\mathrm{meas}}\) is the oxidant uptake measured from the decline of overlying-water oxidant in a chamber (with the DBL's storage change negligible, precondition 3), and \( abla\mathcal{F}\) comes from microsensor profiles across \(S\); neither uses the other or the declared \(D_{\mathrm{s}}\) or \(V_{\mathrm{m}}\). The redox potential \(E_h\), a potential in volts, is not mapped to \(\mathcal{F}\), and electron transport within the reactions is not \(J_E^\mu\).

docs.title: \(O_2\) — Unimodular Weyl Factorization, Constraint Precision & Trajectories
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}( au, \mathbf{x}) = \Omega^2( au, \mathbf{x})\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) with \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) = 0 \implies \det g = \Omega^{2n}\), \( rac{\partial\ln\Omega}{\partial au} = rac{1}{n} heta\); \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\); \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\), \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\); \( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\); \(\left.\left( rac{dv^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}\), \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2)\left(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu ight)\), \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2 < 1\), with the default \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the rigid column the unimodular Weyl split is trivial (\(\Omega \equiv 1\), \(\hat{h} \equiv 0\), \(\partial_ au\ln\Omega = 0\)). The split isolates the volume element only algebraically; \( heta\) remains coupled to \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) and \(\sigma_{\alpha eta}\) through the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation (r10 Decision 2), whose two sides vanish identically here (§0.1 items 2 and 4). The fabric and tortuosity of the sediment enter through \(D_{\mathrm{s}}\), not through \(g\), and the topography of the sediment surface enters through the declared geometry of \(\mathcal{M}\) and its DBL. \(\Pi_{\mu u}\) is the Hessian of a declared precision potential and enters only the coupling sector (\(O_6\)). Eq. [3] is instantiated with the default drive and maps no tracer. Solute transport is diffusive and is described by the \(O_4\) balance law, and microbes are not mapped as tracers.

docs.title: \(O_3\) — Shear Damping & Hysteresis Consolidation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\left. rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = rac{2}{n} heta g_{\mu u} + 2\sigma_{\mu u}\); \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv \partial_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) (\(\gamma_\sigma = \mathrm{const} > 0\), \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\mu} = 0\)) \(\implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\Vert_{C^2(\mathcal{M})} = 0\); \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\), \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)); \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the rigid column \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv 0\), so the shear law holds trivially for any \(\gamma_\sigma > 0\), \(\hat{h} = \hat{h}_\infty = 0\), and \(\hat{g}_\infty = \hat{g} = \delta\); this aperture supports no shear-relaxation test (§0.1 item 2). The relaxation of the oxidant profile toward its new steady state is a property of the \(O_4\) balance law and is not mapped to \(\sigma\). Compaction and consolidation of sediment lie outside the declared windows. \(V_{\mathrm{local}}\) is the hysteresis content of a layer \(\mathcal{U}_i\).

docs.title: \(O_4\) — Free-Energy Balance, Spectral Low-Pass Gating & Boundary Stress Conservation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( rac{\partial\mathcal{F}}{\partial au} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), \(J_W^\alpha \equiv -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = \mathfrak{K}^{ eta\alpha} \succ 0\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\); \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\); \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au) = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\); \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: With \( heta \equiv 0\) the balance law reads \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} = abla_\alpha(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}) - V_{\mathrm{m}}\mathcal{F}/(K_{\mathcal{F}} + \mathcal{F})\): the reaction–diffusion (early-diagenesis) equation of oxidant uptake without advection, normalized by the sediment porosity. Its finite relaxation time makes the field stored, not quasi-static. The layered \(D_{\mathrm{s}}\) and the Michaelis–Menten law depart from the default and satisfy the binding closure, and each is rejected if the default fits at least as well (closure (iv)). The gate sector follows §0.1 item 8: the Neumann eigenmodes of \(- abla^2\) on the rigid column are fixed, so the gate does not drift, and the faster decay of fine spatial structure in the oxidant profile is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the gate without being the gate. The selective uptake of particular solutes by microbial membranes and enzymes is a property of the reactions, set through \(V_{\mathrm{m}}\) and \(K_{\mathrm{m}}\), and is not the spatial gate. The stress-conservation equivalence holds identically (§0.1 item 4).

docs.title: \(O_5\) — Riemannian Geometric Mean Gluing, Percolation & Harmonic Circulation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\); \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) geodesically convex for \(g^{(ij)}( au) \; orall au \ge au_0\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\); \(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\); \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\); \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} G_{\infty,\mu u}^{(i)} \succ 0\) (standing hypothesis with \(H_0 = 0\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: The cover consists of \( au\)-independent horizontal layers of the column (the DBL, the uppermost sediment, and deeper oxic layers), with slab-shaped overlaps \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) that stay convex on the rigid metric. Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of \(g\), so the gluing holds identically, \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} = 0\), and \(g^{(i)} = G_\infty^{(i)}\) at every \( au\) (\(H_0 = 0\); §0.1 item 9). Every overlap is crossed by the transient, so \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\). The connectivity of the pore space is a property of the sediment that enters through \(D_{\mathrm{s}}\): a sediment whose pore space does not percolate has no continuum diffusivity and is not an admissible domain. That connectivity is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the condition \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} > \phi_c\) and is not identified with it. The declared column is simply connected, so \(\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} \equiv 0\) (§0.1 item 9). A column pierced by tubes or burrows lies outside this declaration (precondition 1). Cycles in the reaction network are not \(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(\mathcal{M})\).

docs.title: \(O_6\) — Asymmetric Phase-Lead Coupling & Trace-Free Deformation Operator
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\); \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) (hypothesis) \(\wedge \; \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\); \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u\,dA > 0\) (hypothesis, \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), with this boundary flux integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) (Branch II).
  • Physical Instantiation: Take two layers that share a transition zone \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\), for example the DBL and the uppermost sediment across the interface transition, or two sediment layers of differing tortuosity. The partner fields are the rate of change of the oxidant free-energy flux in the two orientations (§0.1 item 9), so \(\eta_{[i o j]} = \partial_ au J_W\): a spatially resolved flux field, not a temporal lag between scalar signals.
  • The supply face holds a value of \(\mathcal{F}\) and the lower face holds the datum, so after the step the flux near the supply decays from an initial overshoot, while farther down it rises. There \(\partial_ au J_W\) points toward the supply and away from it, respectively, and the zero set between them travels downward during the early window.
  • In a laterally uniform column (precondition 7) the late zero set is the level at which the slowest relaxation mode of the problem linearized about its new steady state peaks. Without lateral uniformity it is located only by the predicted solution.
  • The declared overlap is one that the predicted zero set does not reach during the overlap's window, with the detection threshold of §0.1 item 9; on it \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) keeps one direction, which the declaration states from the predicted solution. Where the sediment is laterally heterogeneous, the transition zones between patches of differing demand are overlaps too, with partner fields from the lateral components of the same \(\partial_ au J_W\).

The odd 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\) is its image under the declared non-singular precision map, with distinct Hessians, and is non-zero there. Under the non-degeneracy hypothesis \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), built per r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3], \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0\) gives \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\), with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general. The eigendirections are directions of the operator \(M^{(ij)}\), not of separate fluxes; in a laterally uniform column the transverse ones carry no flux. Under the flux-positivity hypothesis the coupling transmits correlation between the subsystem marginals of the declared state sector (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\)). Both are standing hypotheses, not consequences of diffusion, and this aperture is not among the systems of the current coupling test. In Branch II the transient decays as the column settles, so the coupling flux is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\). With \(\sigma \equiv 0\) the overlaps keep their declared convex shape, and the r10 §5.12 constraint has no counterpart here.

docs.title: \(O_7\) — Principal-Bundle Gauge Coherence, Impedance Decay & Hysteresis Alignment
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(D_\mu = \partial_\mu - i g_{\mathrm{YM}}\,\mathrm{ad}_{A_\mu}\); \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\); \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2} o 1\), \(\hat{\chi} \equiv \chi_E\hat{u}\) (Branch II); \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The gauge sector is the trivial declaration of §0.1 item 10, so \([F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\) identically. With \(\sigma \equiv 0\), \(\chi_E \equiv 1\) and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu \equiv 0\) at every \( au\), and \(\chi\) is undefined (\( heta = 0\)). \(\hat{ ho}_g = rac{1}{n}\delta^\mu_ u\) at every \( au\), and alignment with \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}\) holds where the Hessian of the declared convex record becomes isotropic, an asymptotic condition stated and not tested. The \(O_7\) Eq. [3] identities hold with divergence-free \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) and \(u_{\mathrm{exp}}\), bounded \(J_E\), and \(\hat{h} \equiv \hat{h}_\infty\). No alignment of the oxidant field with the sediment's stored record is claimed beyond these declarations.

docs.title: \(O_\Omega\) — Topological Asymptote, Branch II: Bounded Non-Equilibrium Steady State
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)): \( heta \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{C^2(\mathcal{M})} 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^{\infty}\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\); \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\) and \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\); \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q) rac{\delta\Psi}{\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})} \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{} 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} o 0\) (with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly as \( au o \infty\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: Under a held overlying-water concentration the column approaches a steady oxidant profile that carries a steady flux from the overlying water into the respiring sediment and the lower face: a bounded non-equilibrium steady state. \( heta \equiv 0\), \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\), \(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\) while supply is maintained, \(\sigma \equiv 0\), and \(\partial_ au g \equiv 0\). The transient coupling decays, so \(\mathcal{I} o s_0V_\infty\). The generator condition requires \(J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0\), an asymptotic hypothesis on the declared state sector that no finite window tests. The state is neither static equilibrium, which would require a uniform concentration with no consumption and no flux, nor a periodic return: natural cycles of supply form a sequence of windows and are never read as a return. The limit belongs to the declared idealization of fixed microbial activity and a fixed lower face; the physical column leaves it as the community and the reduced pools change, which bounds the usable window.
  • Within windows the supported tests (aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5) are the non-degeneracy check (4), the signs of \(\Theta_E\), \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}\), and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}}\) (5), the flux prediction (6), and the Branch II evidence (7).
  • Tests (1)–(3) hold trivially on the rigid column.

docs.title: Aperture 3.4: Chronobiology & Phenological Synchrony (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{chrono}}\))
1. Epistemological & Biological Scope
docs.text:
Aperture 3.4 maps the temporal organization of living systems onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\): circadian and other endogenous oscillators, their entrainment by environmental cues, the humoral and paracrine signals by which pacemaker tissues synchronize peripheral tissues, and the seasonal timing of development (dormancy, vernalization, flowering, mast seeding). Its empirical domain is the spatial delivery of an entraining signal into a target tissue: a signal molecule secreted by pacemaker cells outside the tissue diffuses into it and is degraded there. The oscillators and their phase dynamics lie outside the domain, and temporal cycles are never mapped to spatial operators. Lexicon is strictly restricted to chronobiology, the endocrinology of timing signals, phenology, nonlinear oscillator theory, and dynamical systems ecology.

Declaration (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3; Branch II).

  • Domain \(\mathcal{M}\) (\(n = 3\)) and boundary \(\partial\mathcal{M}\). An avascular layer of target tissue, or a tissue slice or explant, that receives a humoral or paracrine entraining signal secreted by cells outside \(\mathcal{M}\). \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) consists of:
  • a supply interface (vascular or fluid) at which the signal concentration is set by the secretory output of the pacemaker cells and held during the window;
  • a drainage interface (vascular, lymphatic, or fluid) that holds the signal at the datum within tolerance (in a two-chamber explant preparation, the receiving medium);
  • closed faces.

The tissue contains no cells that secrete the signal and no capillaries, so there are no interior sources and all supply crosses \(\partial\mathcal{M}\). * Window. A relaxation window (§0.1 item 1), opened by a declared step increase of the signal concentration at the supply interface from a prior steady state, after which the concentration is held at its new level within tolerance. In vivo the step is the rise of secretion at a declared phase of the pacemaker's cycle, which is a ramp with a finite rise time; \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} \ge 0\) then follows from the ramp form of the comparison argument (§0.1 item 1), not from time translation. In vitro it is a change of the supplying medium. The window ends before the pacemaker's output changes again. Each window therefore covers one monotone segment of the signal's cycle. The cycle itself is a sequence of windows and is never mapped to \( heta\) or read as a return. * Metric. Flat and rigid (§0.1 item 2): \(g_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu u}\) in a Cartesian chart, with swelling or shrinkage of the tissue within the rigid tolerance. * Cone speed. \(c_*\) is the longitudinal sound speed of the tissue. Diffusive speeds are \(\ll c_*\). * Storage. \(s = \alpha(1 + B)\): the extracellular volume fraction \(\alpha\) times the retardation factor \(1 + B\) of fast, linear, reversible binding of the signal (to extracellular matrix or to receptors). It is declared uniform over \(\mathcal{M}\) within tolerance (§0.1 item 3); saturable binding is excluded. * Free energy \(\mathcal{F}\) and datum. \(\mathcal{F} = RT\,c\) (J m⁻³), with \(c\) the extracellular concentration of the free signal (mol m⁻³) and the declared constant yield \(RT\) (J mol⁻¹) at the declared tissue temperature \(T\). \(RT\,c\) is the van 't Hoff osmotic pressure of the signal, an energy density linear in \(c\). It is the declared linear form of aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3 item 3; the chemical potential itself is logarithmic in \(c\). The datum is zero (\(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0\)), and \(\mathcal{F} \ge 0\) holds trivially. The relaxation time \(\ell^2/D^*\) across the layer is finite and resolvable. * Transport \(\mathfrak{K}\). \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = D^{*\alpha eta}/(1 + B)\), with \(D^{*\alpha eta}\) the effective extracellular diffusivity tensor (the free diffusivity reduced by the tortuosity of the extracellular space). It is parametric along declared tissue axes (for example a fibre direction), with isotropic diffusivity as the default. With \(j\) the molar flux per unit tissue area, \(J_W = RT\,j/s\). The conversion factor \(RT/s\) is declared. \(\alpha\) and \(D^*\) are estimated per closure (ii) on the same tissue, for example from the real-time diffusion of an inert probe ion (a different modality), and \(B\) from binding assays of the same tissue after the window. * Sink \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\). Enzymatic degradation, first order: \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = k_{\mathrm{d}}\mathcal{F}\), with \(k_{\mathrm{d}} = \ln 2/t_{1/2}\) from the measured half-life of the signal in the same tissue, after its supply is removed in a declared perturbation regime. \(k_{\mathrm{d}}\) is the effective rate in the storage-normalized law: the degradation rate of free signal divided by \(1 + B\) if bound signal is protected. Cellular uptake and receptor internalization are included in \(k_{\mathrm{d}}\) where they are first order, and otherwise must be negligible. * Drive. Default, \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\) (§0.1 item 5). * Branch II evidence (closure (v)). * The trend of \(\langle heta angle\) and a bound on \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\) come from measurements of tissue thickness (optical or acoustic), which must stay within the rigid tolerance. * \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) is estimated from measured dissipation (§0.1 item 7): * the supply term uses the depletion record of the supplying compartment (or, in vivo, the difference between arterial and venous concentrations times the flow), with \(\mathcal{F}\) at the supply interface; * the drainage interface, at the datum, contributes nothing; * the consumption term uses the declared \(k_{\mathrm{d}}\) with \(\mathcal{F}\) from tissue concentration measurements that are not those of the \(O_1\) profile; * the storage term uses repeated measurements.

The $O_1$ test uses the drainage interface, a different surface.
  • The physical dissipation is the entropy production of the signal's diffusion, which is non-negative by the second law, so the comparison tests only the sign of the estimate.
  • Admissible domains (declared, checkable preconditions):
  • an avascular tissue with no secretion of the signal and no other interior source;
  • \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) throughout \( ar{\mathcal{M}}\);
  • uniform \(\alpha\) and fast, linear, reversible binding with constant \(B\) (or none), and no saturable uptake, within tolerance;
  • supply-interface concentration held at its new level, and drainage interface at the datum, within tolerance;
  • tissue dimensions within the rigid tolerance, and isothermal conditions within tolerance;
  • purely diffusive extracellular transport, with interstitial convection below tolerance;
  • for the one-dimensional statements of \(O_6\) only: a laterally uniform supply and tissue.
  • Titled phenomena outside the domain.
  • Pacemakers. The pacemaker oscillators and their cycles lie outside \(\mathcal{M}\), and their output sets the supply data window by window. Oscillator phase, period, and amplitude are temporal quantities and are not mapped to \( heta\), \(\sigma\), or any spatial operator.
  • Entrainment. The entrainment of the target cells' own clocks by the delivered signal (phase response, phase locking) is a response in the target cells. It enters through \(\mathcal{H}\) and as context, and no synchronization claim is made (§0.1 item 10).
  • Environmental cues. Cues that entrain the pacemakers act outside \(\mathcal{M}\) and are context.
  • Phenology. Dormancy, vernalization, flowering time, and mast seeding are seasonal developmental timing, between windows. The memory of accumulated cues (for example accumulated chilling) is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\) and is not identified with it.
  • Long cycles. Succession and multi-year cycles are context.

docs.title: 2. Coordinate-by-Coordinate Mapping (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\))
\(O_0\) — Exogenous Flux & Emergent Foliation Time
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( heta \equiv -N K \overset{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0}{=} rac{1}{2}g^{\mu u} rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} = rac{1}{\sqrt{\vert g\vert}} rac{\partial\sqrt{\vert g\vert}}{\partial au} = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\); \(\Theta_E \equiv rac{\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}}{s_0} = - rac{ eta_{\mathrm{th}}}{s_0}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\); \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \sqrt{ heta^2 + \Theta_E^2}\), \( au_\Theta( au) \equiv \int_{ au_0}^{ au}\langle\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au'\); \( rac{dV_{\mathcal{M}}}{d au} = \int_{\mathcal{M}} heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\), with \(\lim_{ au o\infty}V_{\mathcal{M}}( au) = V_\infty < \infty\) (Branch II); \( rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), \(q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv -\ln(v_0Q(\mathbf{x}, au))\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The tissue is rigid, so \( heta \equiv 0\), \(dV_{\mathcal{M}}/d au = 0\), and \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\). The signal supplied across the supply interface is throughput and is never mapped to \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) (§0.1 item 6). Diffusion of the signal from the supply interface toward the drainage interface, with degradation along the way, produces entropy at every point, so \(\Theta_E > 0\) (by \(O_1\)), \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} = \Theta_E\), and \( au_\Theta\) counts entropy production per \(s_0\). \( au\) remains laboratory proper time, and the oscillators' cycles run outside \(\mathcal{M}\) within this foliation; they are not \( heta\), which never changes sign. The record accumulates by \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) along the throughput current. The entrainment state of the target tissue (the phase of its cellular clocks) and its memory of accumulated seasonal cues are mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\) and are not identified with it; they enter each window through \(\mathcal{H}_0\).

docs.title: \(O_1\) — Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Openness
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} = p_0\oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} \equiv \int_{\mathcal{M}}(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F})\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} + \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\); \( abla_\mu\mathcal{F} eq 0\); \(J_E^\mu \equiv rac{J_W^\mu}{p_0} = - rac{1}{p_0}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\) (Branch II, fixed); \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\); \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The maintained difference in signal concentration between the supply and drainage interfaces, together with degradation, holds the tissue far from equilibrium. With \(J_E^\mu = -p_0^{-1}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\), \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\) holds identically wherever \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) (precondition 2), so \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). The signal flux runs down its gradient from the supply interface toward the drainage interface, in the direction of \(J_E^\mu\). \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0\), so \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). The empirical content of \(O_1\) is the flux-prediction test (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3, §5.5 item 6). \(D^*\), \(\alpha\), and \(B\) are estimated on the same tissue as declared above. The declared law must predict \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}} = RT\,j^{\mathrm{meas}}/s\) at the drainage interface, with \(j^{\mathrm{meas}}\) from the accumulation of the signal in the receiving compartment, and \( abla\mathcal{F}\) from a profiling method within the window that uses neither \(j^{\mathrm{meas}}\) nor the declared \(D^*\) or \(k_{\mathrm{d}}\). No current test exercises this aperture (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3). Each oscillator outside \(\mathcal{M}\) is a dissipative limit cycle that requires a continuous supply of free energy; that is context, not a coordinate of the declared domain.

docs.title: \(O_2\) — Unimodular Weyl Factorization, Constraint Precision & Trajectories
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}( au, \mathbf{x}) = \Omega^2( au, \mathbf{x})\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) with \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) = 0 \implies \det g = \Omega^{2n}\), \( rac{\partial\ln\Omega}{\partial au} = rac{1}{n} heta\); \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\); \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\), \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\); \( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\); \(\left.\left( rac{dv^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}\), \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2)\left(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu ight)\), \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2 < 1\), with the default \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the rigid tissue the unimodular Weyl split is trivial (\(\Omega \equiv 1\), \(\hat{h} \equiv 0\), \(\partial_ au\ln\Omega = 0\)). The split isolates the volume element only algebraically; \( heta\) remains coupled to \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) and \(\sigma_{\alpha eta}\) through the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation (r10 Decision 2), whose two sides vanish identically here (§0.1 items 2 and 4). Tissue architecture enters through the axes of \(D^*\), not through \(g\). \(\Pi_{\mu u}\) is the Hessian of a declared precision potential and enters only the coupling sector (\(O_6\)). Eq. [3] is instantiated with the default drive and maps no tracer: signal transport is diffusive and is described by the \(O_4\) balance law. Developmental and life-history trade-offs are not mapped to \(\hat{h}\).

docs.title: \(O_3\) — Shear Damping & Hysteresis Consolidation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\left. rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = rac{2}{n} heta g_{\mu u} + 2\sigma_{\mu u}\); \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv \partial_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) (\(\gamma_\sigma = \mathrm{const} > 0\), \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\mu} = 0\)) \(\implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\Vert_{C^2(\mathcal{M})} = 0\); \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\), \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)); \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the rigid tissue \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv 0\), so the shear law holds trivially for any \(\gamma_\sigma > 0\), \(\hat{h} = \hat{h}_\infty = 0\), and \(\hat{g}_\infty = \hat{g} = \delta\); this aperture supports no shear-relaxation test (§0.1 item 2). The relaxation of the signal profile toward its new steady state is a property of the \(O_4\) balance law and is not mapped to \(\sigma\). The phase relationships that the target tissue retains after entrainment lie in \(\mathcal{H}\). \(V_{\mathrm{local}}\) is the hysteresis content of a layer \(\mathcal{U}_i\).

docs.title: \(O_4\) — Free-Energy Balance, Spectral Low-Pass Gating & Boundary Stress Conservation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( rac{\partial\mathcal{F}}{\partial au} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), \(J_W^\alpha \equiv -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = \mathfrak{K}^{ eta\alpha} \succ 0\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\); \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\); \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au) = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\); \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: With \( heta \equiv 0\) the balance law reads \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} = abla_\alpha(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}) - k_{\mathrm{d}}\mathcal{F}\): the reaction–diffusion equation of a signal delivered across a boundary and degraded in the tissue, normalized by its storage coefficient. Its finite relaxation time makes the field stored, not quasi-static. The anisotropic \(D^*\) and the degradation law depart from the default and satisfy the binding closure, and each is rejected if the default fits at least as well (closure (iv)). The gate sector follows §0.1 item 8: the Neumann eigenmodes of \(- abla^2\) on the rigid tissue are fixed, so the gate does not drift, and the faster decay of fine spatial structure in the signal field is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the gate without being the gate. The tissue also attenuates fast temporal fluctuations of its supply; that is a filter in time, distinct from the spatial gate, and it is not mapped to it. The stress-conservation equivalence holds identically (§0.1 item 4).

docs.title: \(O_5\) — Riemannian Geometric Mean Gluing, Percolation & Harmonic Circulation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\); \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) geodesically convex for \(g^{(ij)}( au) \; orall au \ge au_0\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\); \(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\); \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\); \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} G_{\infty,\mu u}^{(i)} \succ 0\) (standing hypothesis with \(H_0 = 0\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: The cover consists of \( au\)-independent layers of the tissue at increasing distance from the supply interface, with slab-shaped overlaps \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) that stay convex on the rigid metric. Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of \(g\), so the gluing holds identically, \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} = 0\), and \(g^{(i)} = G_\infty^{(i)}\) at every \( au\) (\(H_0 = 0\); §0.1 item 9). Every overlap is crossed by the transient, so \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\). The connectivity of the extracellular space is a property of the tissue that enters through \(D^*\): a tissue whose extracellular space does not percolate has no continuum diffusivity and is not an admissible domain. That connectivity is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the condition \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} > \phi_c\) and is not identified with it. The declared tissue is simply connected, so \(\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} \equiv 0\) (§0.1 item 9).

docs.title: \(O_6\) — Asymmetric Phase-Lead Coupling & Trace-Free Deformation Operator
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\); \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) (hypothesis) \(\wedge \; \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\); \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u\,dA > 0\) (hypothesis, \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), with this boundary flux integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) (Branch II).
  • Physical Instantiation: Take two layers that share a transition zone \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\). The partner fields are the rate of change of the signal's free-energy flux in the two orientations (§0.1 item 9), so \(\eta_{[i o j]} = \partial_ au J_W\): a spatially resolved flux field. Temporal phase lags between oscillators are not spatial 1-forms and are not used as partner fields.
  • The supply interface holds a value of \(\mathcal{F}\) and the drainage interface holds the datum, so after the step the flux near the supply decays from an initial overshoot, while farther in it rises. There \(\partial_ au J_W\) points toward the supply and away from it, respectively, and the zero set between them travels inward during the early window.
  • In a laterally uniform layer (precondition 7) the late zero set is the level at which the slowest relaxation mode peaks. Without lateral uniformity it is located only by the predicted solution.
  • The declared overlap is one that the predicted zero set does not reach during the overlap's window, with the detection threshold of §0.1 item 9; on it \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) keeps one direction, which the declaration states from the predicted solution.

The odd 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\) is its image under the declared non-singular precision map, with distinct Hessians, and is non-zero there. Under the non-degeneracy hypothesis \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), built per r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3], \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0\) gives \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\), with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general. The eigendirections are directions of the operator \(M^{(ij)}\), not directions of enhanced or suppressed signalling. Under the flux-positivity hypothesis the coupling transmits correlation between the subsystem marginals of the declared state sector (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\)). Both are standing hypotheses, not consequences of diffusion. In Branch II the transient decays as the tissue settles, so the coupling flux is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\). With \(\sigma \equiv 0\) the overlaps keep their declared convex shape, and the r10 §5.12 constraint has no counterpart here.

docs.title: \(O_7\) — Principal-Bundle Gauge Coherence, Impedance Decay & Hysteresis Alignment
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(D_\mu = \partial_\mu - i g_{\mathrm{YM}}\,\mathrm{ad}_{A_\mu}\); \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\); \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2} o 1\), \(\hat{\chi} \equiv \chi_E\hat{u}\) (Branch II); \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The gauge sector is the trivial declaration of §0.1 item 10, so \([F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\) identically. With \(\sigma \equiv 0\), \(\chi_E \equiv 1\) and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu \equiv 0\) at every \( au\), and \(\chi\) is undefined (\( heta = 0\)). \(\hat{ ho}_g = rac{1}{n}\delta^\mu_ u\) at every \( au\), and alignment with \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}\) holds where the Hessian of the declared convex record becomes isotropic, an asymptotic condition stated and not tested. The \(O_7\) Eq. [3] identities hold with divergence-free \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) and \(u_{\mathrm{exp}}\), bounded \(J_E\), and \(\hat{h} \equiv \hat{h}_\infty\). Synchrony between the pacemaker and the target tissue's clocks is a phase property of oscillators outside the declared field. Synchronization claims would belong to gauge transport, which is trivial and untested here, so the aperture makes no synchrony claim; the "synchrony" of its title enters as context.

docs.title: \(O_\Omega\) — Topological Asymptote, Branch II: Bounded Non-Equilibrium Steady State
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)): \( heta \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{C^2(\mathcal{M})} 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^{\infty}\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\); \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\) and \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\); \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q) rac{\delta\Psi}{\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})} \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{} 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} o 0\) (with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly as \( au o \infty\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: Under a held supply concentration the tissue approaches a steady signal profile that carries a steady flux from the supply interface, partly degraded within the tissue and partly drained: a bounded non-equilibrium steady state. \( heta \equiv 0\), \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\), \(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\) while supply is maintained, \(\sigma \equiv 0\), and \(\partial_ au g \equiv 0\). The transient coupling decays, so \(\mathcal{I} o s_0V_\infty\). The generator condition requires \(J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0\), an asymptotic hypothesis on the declared state sector that no finite window tests. The state is neither static equilibrium, which would require a uniform concentration with no degradation and no flux, nor a periodic return. While the pacemaker keeps cycling, successive windows settle toward successive held levels, and that sequence is never mapped onto the spine as a return.
  • Within windows the supported tests (aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5) are the non-degeneracy check (4), the signs of \(\Theta_E\), \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}\), and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}}\) (5), the flux prediction (6), and the Branch II evidence (7).
  • Tests (1)–(3) hold trivially on the rigid tissue.
  • No current test exercises this aperture.

docs.title: 0. Tier Architecture & Four-Part Functional Homology
docs.text:
Tier 4 maps the mechanics and nutrition of load-bearing connective tissue, the physiology of balance and support contact, neuro-attentional and autonomic regulation, and the regulation of affect through the microcirculation onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\). Three apertures (4.1, 4.2, 4.4) are empirical apertures declared in Branch II of r7, the bounded non-equilibrium steady state (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3). Each declares, in its §1, a domain, physical metric, cone speed, storage coefficient, free energy with datum, transport tensor, interior sink, drive, and Branch II evidence, and instantiates all nine coordinates \(O_0 \to O_\Omega\) on that domain. Each declared domain is of one kind: a stored quantity (dissolved oxygen, or blood held in a compliant capillary bed) spreading through a living tissue, with supply crossing the boundary and consumption or loss, where declared, by a named interior sink. Aperture 4.3 is provisionally homological in this epoch: it declares no domain, maps all nine coordinates as conceptual correspondences, like Tier 1, and makes no empirical claim (§0.1 item 12).

The wider phenomena named in the aperture titles (posture, balance, attention, autonomic regulation, affect, resilience) enter the empirical mappings as boundary conditions, through the declared parameters, through the hysteresis record \(\mathcal{H}\), or as illustrative context, and each §1 states which. No Tier 4 aperture claims that attention, affect, or any interior state obeys a spine law. Each aperture is formulated at the level of general physiology, biomechanics, and neuroscience, for vertebrate and mammalian tissues and for human populations studied at cohort level, without presupposing a single practitioner, practice, or site. No human-subject test is included in this epoch (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3).

Slot & Functional Role Aperture Designation Declared Domain and Diffusing Quantity Titled Phenomena Outside the Domain Vertical Homology Across Tiers Slot 4.1: Structural Substrate Myofascial Biotensegrity & Postural Mechanics (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{somatic}}\)) Oxygen diffusing through an explant of avascular articular cartilage of a single zone, from a supply chamber to a receiving chamber held at the datum, consumed by chondrocytes. The myofascial continuum and its tensegrity, posture and joint loading, synovial lubrication, remodelling, the intervertebral disc: as boundary data, through the parameters, through \(\mathcal{H}\), or context. \(1.1 \leftrightarrow 2.1 \leftrightarrow 3.1 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{4.1} \leftrightarrow 5.1\) Slot 4.2: Dynamic Flow & Waves Vestibular Equilibrium & Sensorimotor Contact (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{kinesthetic}}\)) Oxygen diffusing through the viable epidermis at an occluded support contact, from the dermal–epidermal junction toward the contact, consumed by keratinocytes. Vestibular sensing, balance control and postural sway, contact loading, cutaneous mechanoreception, callus formation: as boundary data, through \(\mathcal{H}\), or context. \(1.2 \leftrightarrow 2.2 \leftrightarrow 3.2 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{4.2} \leftrightarrow 5.2\) Slot 4.3: Boundary Gating Neuro-Attentional & Autonomic Regulation (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{neuro}}\)) None declared: provisionally homological (quasi-static bioelectric potentials). All of its phenomena are mapped as conceptual correspondences only. \(1.3 \leftrightarrow 2.3 \leftrightarrow 3.3 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{4.3} \leftrightarrow 5.3\) Slot 4.4: Coalescence & Hysteresis Affective Regulation & Psychophysiological Resilience (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{affective}}\)) Blood pressure energy in a capillary bed treated as a porous medium, from the feeding arterioles to the draining venules, with transcapillary filtration as the sink. Affect and its regulation, autonomic outflow and arteriolar tone, cardiac and respiratory rhythms, vascular adaptation, recovery after stressors: as boundary data, through \(\mathcal{H}\), or context. \(1.4 \leftrightarrow 2.4 \leftrightarrow 3.4 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{4.4} \leftrightarrow 5.4\)

docs.title: 0.1 Conventions Common to the Tier 4 Apertures
docs.text:
The following conventions apply to every empirical aperture of this tier (4.1, 4.2, 4.4); item 12 states how the provisionally homological Aperture 4.3 is mapped. Each aperture's §1 and coordinate blocks state its specific values and cite these items where they apply. Where an item repeats a convention of tier_3_ecological_living_networks.md §0.1, it is restated here so that this tier can be read on its own.

  1. Branch and windows. Branch II is declared before any test, with the estimators of item 7 and §1, and no Tier 4 domain is re-evaluated in Branch I on the same data (closure (v)). Statements that hold in Branch I only (r10 Decision 6) are never applied. Every observation window is a relaxation window: it begins at a declared \( au_0\) from a prior steady state, a declared transient starts at \( au_0\), the external data are then held within declared tolerances, and the window follows the domain as it settles.
  2. In every empirical aperture the transient is a declared step of the boundary data in the direction that raises \(\mathcal{F}\): a step increase of the supply-chamber oxygen (4.1), of the oxygen supplied at the dermal–epidermal junction (4.2), or of the pressure at the arteriolar boundary (4.4). Each declared balance law is a scalar parabolic equation whose sink is Lipschitz and non-decreasing in \(\mathcal{F}\) (Michaelis–Menten, first order), so the comparison principle holds. The prior steady state is a subsolution for the raised data, so \(\mathcal{F}(\cdot, au_0 + h) \ge \mathcal{F}(\cdot, au_0)\); the held data make the problem invariant under time translation, so \(\mathcal{F}(\cdot, au + h) \ge \mathcal{F}(\cdot, au)\), that is, \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} \ge 0\) at every point. Where the step is in fact a ramp (non-decreasing boundary data that reach their held value over a finite rise time, as for the in-vivo supply of 4.2 and the arteriolar dilation of 4.4), the same conclusion follows without time translation: \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F}\) obeys the linearized equation with zero initial data and non-negative boundary data, so it stays non-negative. Robin data (4.2's outflow face) do not change the argument, and the duct lumens of 4.2, which receive oxygen only from the tissue, form with it a cooperative system, for which the comparison principle also holds. The argument is exact on rigid domains. Under the optional torsional perturbation of 4.1 the operator depends on \( au\) through \(g( au)\) at the order of the shear strain, so there the conclusion holds only to that order, and 4.1 checks it from its oxygen record.
  3. Direction. The opposite direction is excluded in each aperture, because it would break a declaration. In 4.4 a fall of capillary pressure shrinks the tissue (\( heta < 0\)), which alone excludes it; physically it can also turn filtration into reabsorption, an interior source, which the declared datum form of the sink cannot represent (4.4 §1). In 4.2 a change of contact load compresses the epidermis (\( heta < 0\)) or, on unloading, is followed by a reactive hyperaemia whose overshoot makes the supply data non-monotone. In 4.1 an oxygen step is osmotically negligible, so either direction keeps the volume; the raising direction is declared for the comparison argument, and a glucose step is not declared because it changes the bath's osmolarity, and a rise of osmolarity deswells cartilage (\( heta < 0\)).
  4. Boundary and lateral exchange. Every exchange of the declared field across an internal or lateral boundary is one-signed, out of \(\mathcal{M}\): transcapillary filtration in 4.4 is a sink and never reabsorption (4.4 §1), and exchange across the walls of the epidermal ducts in 4.2 runs from the tissue into lumens that receive oxygen from nowhere else (4.2 §1). No compartment outside \(\mathcal{M}\) discharges into it within a window, except across the declared supply faces.
  5. The rate of change of the flux, \(\partial_ au J_W\), is not one-signed in general (item 9).
  6. Metric. The physical metric is the pull-back of the Euclidean metric to the material points of the declared body under its deformation map. It is flat at every \( au\), so \(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\) and \(R_{\mu u} \equiv 0\) (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3 item 2). No Tier 4 aperture declares a non-Euclidean material metric in this epoch: the growth or remodelling material metric that the master table admits for 4.1 is weighed in 4.1 §1 and not declared. The curved configurations of the r10 §5.11 and §5.13 witnesses are therefore realized by none of these apertures, and r7's curvature sector is exercised by no Tier 4 aperture; with Tiers 2 and 3, it is exercised by no empirical aperture of Tiers 2–4.
  7. Rigid domains (4.2, 4.4). In a Cartesian chart \(g_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu u}\), so \(\Omega \equiv 1\), \(\hat{h} \equiv 0\), \( heta \equiv 0\), and \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv 0\). The tissue is declared rigid within a pre-declared tolerance on its measured volumetric strain. In the declared window direction any residual volume change is non-negative (epidermal thickness under held load in 4.2; vascular distension and filtration in 4.4), and windows in which the measured volume decreases beyond the tolerance are excluded, so that \( heta \ge 0\) is not violated. With \(\sigma \equiv 0\) the \(O_3\) shear law holds trivially, and these apertures support no shear-relaxation test.
  8. Volume-rigid domain (4.1). The volumetric strain of the explant stays within a declared tolerance, so \( heta \equiv 0\) in the declared metric. Without the optional torsional perturbation, the shear strain also stays within tolerance and 4.1 is treated as rigid. With it, the metric is the pull-back under an isochoric twist: in a Cartesian material chart \(g( au) = \mathbf{F}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{F}\) with \(\det\mathbf{F} = 1\), so \(\Omega \equiv 1\), \( heta \equiv 0\), \(\exp\hat{h} = g\), and \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} eq 0\). On that deforming domain every covariant quantity (Laplacian, Hessians, convexity) is evaluated with \(g( au)\).
  9. Storage. The r7 \(O_4\) balance law carries unit storage: \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F}\) is the rate of change of the stored quantity per unit volume. A living medium stores its diffusing quantity \(u\) with a coefficient \(s\) (stored amount per unit volume per unit of \(u\)): for dissolved oxygen in 4.1 and 4.2, the tissue's water volume fraction times the partition coefficient of oxygen between tissue and bath water, with \(u\) the bath-equivalent oxygen concentration (oxygen tension times its solubility in bath water), which is continuous across the tissue's faces; in 4.4, the compliance of the capillary bed per unit tissue volume. With \(s\) uniform, the physical balance \(s\,\partial_ au u = abla_\alpha(k^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta u) - r\) becomes the r7 law for \(\mathcal{F} = \epsilon u\) (with \(\epsilon\) a declared constant yield), \(\mathfrak{K} = k/s\), and \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = \epsilon r/s\), and the r7 flux is \(J_W = (\epsilon/s)\,j\), with \(j = -k abla u\) the physical flux. The factor \(\epsilon/s\) is a declared conversion factor, estimated independently (closure (ii)). If \(s\) varies in space, \(s^{-1} abla_\alpha(k^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta u) = abla_\alpha(s^{-1}k^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta u) + s^{-2}k^{\alpha eta} abla_\alpha s\, abla_ eta u\), and the last term is a drift term that the r7 balance law does not contain. Each aperture therefore declares a single storage class: \(s\) uniform on \(\mathcal{M}\) within a tolerance (a declared, checkable precondition). Adjacent media with a different coefficient (other zones of the cartilage in 4.1; the stratum corneum and the dermis in 4.2; arterioles, venules, and the interstitium in 4.4) lie outside \(\mathcal{M}\) and enter as boundary data or compartments, because a jump in \(s\) would make \(J_W\) discontinuous where the physical flux is continuous, which the unit-storage law reads as an interface source or sink.
  10. Stress sector. With \(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\), \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} \equiv 0\); its trace gives \( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha = 0\) for \(n = 3\), and then \( abla_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)} = 0\), so \(\xi\) is a Killing field. No Tier 4 medium has an identified global control field in this epoch, so Tier 4 declares \(\eta^\lambda \equiv 0\), hence \(\xi_ u \equiv 0\) and \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha = 0\), and the \(O_4\) equivalence \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\) holds identically. The \( au\)-compatibility law then reduces to \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma]_{\mu u} = rac{n-2}{n}( abla_\mu abla_ u heta - g_{\mu u} abla^2 heta)\), and its trace, the traced elliptic equation, to \( rac{n-1}{n} abla^2 heta = abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta}\). These are the Saint-Venant compatibility conditions of the strain rate, which every deformation of an embedded body satisfies because its metric stays flat; with \( heta \equiv 0\) (all Tier 4 domains) they read \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma] = 0\) and \( abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} = 0\). The mechanical stresses of tissues (the swelling prestress of cartilage, myofascial tension, contact pressure, vessel-wall stress) are not \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\); they enter as boundary conditions, through the declared parameters, and through \(\mathcal{H}\). The partner fields \(\eta_{i o j}\) of \(O_6\) (item 9) are distinct objects from the global \(\eta\) of \(O_4\).
  11. Cone speed and trajectories. Each aperture declares \(c_*\) as the longitudinal sound speed of its tissue. Rays of that signal are null for the declared cone and, like all null rays, are not trajectories of \(O_2\) Eq. [3]. Every material speed in \(\mathcal{M}\) (diffusive speeds, twist-recovery speeds, blood velocities) is \(\ll c_*\), so \(u^2 \ll 1\). The trajectory equation is displayed in physical units: both \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2\) and the projection term \(c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu\) carry \(c_*\), and with \(c_* = 1\) the display reduces to the r7 form. All three empirical apertures instantiate Eq. [3] with \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\) and map no tracer. Bodily movement, postural sway, and the motion of blood cells are forced motions that no declared drive describes in this epoch.
  12. Currents. In Branch II, \(J_E^\mu = J_W^\mu/p_0\) is fixed.
