Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of \(g\), so the gluing holds identically, \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} = 0\), and \(g^{(i)} = G_\infty^{(i)}\) at every \( au\) (\(H_0 = 0\)). Every overlap is crossed by the transient, so \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\). The connectivity of the tissue's intercellular and intracellular paths for oxygen enters through \(D\); it is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the condition \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} > \phi_c\) and is not identified with it. Each duct that passes through the epidermis adds a non-contractible loop, so \(b_1(\mathcal{M})\) equals the number of ducts and follicles in the declared area, and the harmonic Neumann fields that circulate around them are non-trivial. No transport current is identified with them, and no claim is made about them (§0.1 item 9).

docs.title: \(O_6\) — Asymmetric Phase-Lead Coupling & Trace-Free Deformation Operator
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\); \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) (hypothesis) \(\wedge \; \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\); \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u\,dA > 0\) (hypothesis, \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), with this boundary flux integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) (Branch II).
  • Physical Instantiation: Take two adjacent cover sets that share an overlap \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\), for example a deeper and a more superficial region of the spinous layer between ducts. The partner fields are the rate of change of the oxygen free-energy flux in the two orientations (§0.1 item 9), so \(\eta_{[i o j]} = \partial_ au J_W\): a spatially resolved flux field, not a temporal lag between scalar signals such as sway and muscle activity.
  • The junction holds the raised supply and the outer face drains through the stratum corneum to the datum, so after the increase the flux near the junction decays from an initial overshoot while nearer the surface it rises, and the zero set between them travels outward during the early window.
  • The ducts and the undulating junction break lateral uniformity, so the zero set is located only by the predicted solution, from the independently estimated parameters, the declared junction data, and \(h_{\mathrm{SC}}\).
  • The declared overlap is one that the predicted zero set does not reach during the overlap's window, with the detection threshold of §0.1 item 9; on it \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) keeps one direction, which the declaration states from the predicted solution.

The odd 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\) is its image under the declared non-singular precision map, with distinct Hessians, and is non-zero there. Under the non-degeneracy hypothesis \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), built per r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3], \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0\) gives \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\), with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general. The eigendirections are directions of the operator \(M^{(ij)}\), not directions of postural stability or instability. Under the flux-positivity hypothesis the coupling transmits correlation between the subsystem marginals of the declared state sector (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\)). Both are standing hypotheses, not consequences of diffusion. In Branch II the transient decays as the epidermis settles, so the coupling flux is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\). With \(\sigma \equiv 0\) the overlaps keep their declared convex shape, and the r10 §5.12 constraint has no counterpart here.

docs.text:
• Spine Equations: Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)): \( heta \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{C^2(\mathcal{M})} 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^{\infty}\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\); \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\) and \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\); \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q) rac{\delta\Psi}{\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})} \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{} 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} o 0\) (with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly as \( au o \infty\)).

The state is neither static equilibrium, which would require a uniform oxygen concentration with no consumption and no flux, nor a periodic return: the alternation of loading and unloading in standing and walking lies between windows and is never read as a return. The limit belongs to the declared idealization of held load and supply; the physical skin leaves it as load shifts, which bounds the usable window.

docs.title: Aperture 4.3: Neuro-Attentional & Autonomic Regulation (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{neuro}}\); provisionally homological)
1. Epistemological & Physiological Scope
docs.text:
Aperture 4.3 maps how nervous systems select and regulate: attention, which selects among competing signals and sets their gain; arousal and its neuromodulatory control; and the autonomic nervous system, whose sympathetic and parasympathetic branches regulate the internal milieu through reflex loops such as the baroreflex, and whose afferents carry interoceptive signals to the brain. Lexicon is strictly restricted to cognitive neuroscience, electrophysiology, neurodynamics, and autonomic and interoceptive physiology.

Status (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3; provisionally homological). This aperture declares no empirical domain and makes no empirical claim in this epoch (§0.1 item 12). The systems it describes do not fit r7's balance law literally. The electrical potentials of neural tissue are quasi-static: in volume conduction the potential follows its current sources without a storage term, so it is not a stored field with a finite relaxation time, which aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3 item 3 requires. Attention and autonomic regulation are, besides, properties of whole circuits and of the body, not fields on one declared tissue domain. Each coordinate is therefore mapped as a conceptual correspondence, mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) and never a reductive identity. Populations are described at cohort level; practices that train attention or regulate arousal are context and are not mapped. Test 2 (spatial gating) remains deferred while this aperture is homological (Annex B).

docs.title: 2. Coordinate-by-Coordinate Mapping (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\))
\(O_0\) — Exogenous Flux & Emergent Foliation Time
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( heta \equiv -N K \overset{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0}{=} rac{1}{2}g^{\mu u} rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} = rac{1}{\sqrt{\vert g\vert}} rac{\partial\sqrt{\vert g\vert}}{\partial au} = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\); \(\Theta_E \equiv rac{\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}}{s_0} = - rac{ eta_{\mathrm{th}}}{s_0}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\); \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \sqrt{ heta^2 + \Theta_E^2}\), \( au_\Theta( au) \equiv \int_{ au_0}^{ au}\langle\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au'\); \( rac{dV_{\mathcal{M}}}{d au} = \int_{\mathcal{M}} heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\), with \(\lim_{ au o\infty}V_{\mathcal{M}}( au) = V_\infty < \infty\) (Branch II); \( rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), \(q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv -\ln(v_0Q(\mathbf{x}, au))\).
  • Homological Mapping: Neural tissue never rests in equilibrium: it is sustained by a continuous supply of oxygen and glucose, and most of its energy is spent restoring the ionic gradients that signalling runs down. That sustained metabolic throughput corresponds to the throughput rate \(\Theta_E\) of a Branch II state, in which openness is carried by throughput and not by expansion (\( heta o 0\)). Brain volume is bounded; no expansion of tissue is mapped to \( heta\), and the cyclic swelling of tissue with the pulse is not \( heta\). The accumulation of learned expectations from surprising input corresponds to the record law \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), with prediction error read as a correspondence of the surprisal gradient \( abla q\); this is a correspondence with predictive-processing accounts of perception, not an identity.

docs.title: \(O_1\) — Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Openness
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} = p_0\oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} \equiv \int_{\mathcal{M}}(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F})\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} + \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\); \( abla_\mu\mathcal{F} eq 0\); \(J_E^\mu \equiv rac{J_W^\mu}{p_0} = - rac{1}{p_0}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\) (Branch II, fixed); \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\); \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\).
  • Homological Mapping: The energy budget of signalling (ion pumping against the leak of action and synaptic potentials) corresponds to the dissipative power \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\) and to positive entropy production. In neural tissue the potential that drives currents is an electrical potential in volts, which is not an energy density and is never \(\mathcal{F}\); in the homology, \(\mathcal{F}\) corresponds to the free energy stored in ionic and metabolic gradients. The sign condition \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\) corresponds to currents that run down those gradients and must be restored by metabolism. No flux prediction is made.

docs.title: \(O_2\) — Unimodular Weyl Factorization, Constraint Precision & Trajectories
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}( au, \mathbf{x}) = \Omega^2( au, \mathbf{x})\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) with \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) = 0 \implies \det g = \Omega^{2n}\), \( rac{\partial\ln\Omega}{\partial au} = rac{1}{n} heta\); \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\); \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\), \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\); \( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\); \(\left.\left( rac{dv^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}\), \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2)\left(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu ight)\), \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2 < 1\), with the default \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\).

That notion corresponds to the precision Hessian \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\) and its trace-free part \(\hat{\Pi}\), which weights the control 1-form \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\); the correspondence is between roles, not between quantities, and no precision potential is estimated from neural data. docs.title: \(O_3\) — Shear Damping & Hysteresis Consolidation

• Spine Equations: \(\left. rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = rac{2}{n} heta g_{\mu u} + 2\sigma_{\mu u}\); \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv \partial_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) (\(\gamma_\sigma = \mathrm{const} > 0\), \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\mu} = 0\)) \(\implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\Vert_{C^2(\mathcal{M})} = 0\); \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\), \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)); \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\).

docs.title: \(O_4\) — Free-Energy Balance, Spectral Low-Pass Gating & Boundary Stress Conservation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( rac{\partial\mathcal{F}}{\partial au} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), \(J_W^\alpha \equiv -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = \mathfrak{K}^{ eta\alpha} \succ 0\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\); \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\); \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au) = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\); \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\).
  • Homological Mapping: Attentional selection, which passes some signals and suppresses others, corresponds to the gate \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}}\) that forms the gated density \(Q\) from \( ho_{\mathrm{total}}\), with the variational power \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}}\) as the cost of keeping \(Q\) apart from the reference \(P\). The breadth of attentional scope corresponds to the spatial cutoff \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}\): a broad scope to a low cutoff that keeps coarse structure, a narrow scope to a high cutoff. The gate is a spatial projector onto Neumann eigenmodes; it does not correspond to temporal frequency bands of neural rhythms, and the smoothing of conducted potentials by volume conduction is a physical property of the conductor, not the gate. The balance law corresponds to the restoration of ionic gradients against their dissipation. The autonomic baroreflex, which holds blood pressure near a set point by opposing deviations, corresponds to the regulation of \(Q\) toward \(P\) and is not mapped to the stress-conservation equivalence \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\), which has no counterpart here.

docs.title: \(O_5\) — Riemannian Geometric Mean Gluing, Percolation & Harmonic Circulation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\); \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) geodesically convex for \(g^{(ij)}( au) \; orall au \ge au_0\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\); \(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\); \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\); \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} G_{\infty,\mu u}^{(i)} \succ 0\) (standing hypothesis with \(H_0 = 0\)).
  • Homological Mapping: Large-scale brain networks join specialized regions through shared connections without erasing their specializations; that pattern corresponds to the gluing of local metrics over overlaps by the geometric mean, \(g^{(ij)} = g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)}\), which keeps each cover set's metric. The integration of a network whose connections exceed a threshold of density corresponds to the percolation condition \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) > \phi_c\). Recurrent loops of connectivity correspond to non-trivial first cohomology and to harmonic circulation around closed cycles, as a correspondence between a graph's cycles and a manifold's topology, not an identity. No connectivity estimate is mapped to \(\mathcal{K}\).

docs.title: \(O_6\) — Asymmetric Phase-Lead Coupling & Trace-Free Deformation Operator
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\); \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) (hypothesis) \(\wedge \; \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\); \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u\,dA > 0\) (hypothesis, \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), with this boundary flux integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) (Branch II).
  • Homological Mapping: Directed influence between brain regions (effective connectivity, in which one region's activity shapes another's more than the reverse) corresponds to the odd phase-lead 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\), which reverses sign when the pair is read the other way. Temporal lead–lag statistics between scalar recordings are not spatial 1-form fields, and the correspondence implies no estimator. The paired antagonism of the sympathetic and parasympathetic branches, which act in opposite senses on the same organs, corresponds to the opposite-signed extreme eigenvalues \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\) of the trace-free operator \(M^{(ij)}\) under the non-degeneracy hypothesis, with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general, as autonomic balance is not a symmetric see-saw. The growth of shared information between coupled regions corresponds to the flux-positivity hypothesis \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\). Both remain standing hypotheses of r7, and in the Branch II form the coupling must be transient (integrable), so the correspondence is with episodes of coupling that resolve, not with sustained coupling.

docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(D_\mu = \partial_\mu - i g_{\mathrm{YM}}\,\mathrm{ad}_{A_\mu}\); \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\); \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2} o 1\), \(\hat{\chi} \equiv \chi_E\hat{u}\) (Branch II); \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\).

The alignment \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) o 0\) corresponds to the convergence of current processing with what has been learned, as expectations come to match the statistics of the environment.

docs.title: \(O_\Omega\) — Topological Asymptote, Branch II: Bounded Non-Equilibrium Steady State
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)): \( heta \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{C^2(\mathcal{M})} 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^{\infty}\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\); \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\) and \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\); \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q) rac{\delta\Psi}{\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})} \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{} 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} o 0\) (with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly as \( au o \infty\)).

That state corresponds to the Branch II limit: bounded volume, sustained throughput (\(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\)), decaying shear and coupling transients, and a record whose growth stops when expectations no longer meet surprise (\(J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0\)). The correspondence makes no claim about any state of attention or awareness, and no test exercises this aperture in this epoch.

docs.title: Aperture 4.4: Affective Regulation & Psychophysiological Resilience (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{affective}}\))
1. Epistemological & Physiological Scope
docs.text:
Aperture 4.4 maps the bodily side of affect onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\): the autonomic expression of emotion and arousal, its regulation, and the capacity of physiological systems to recover after stressors (psychophysiological resilience). A principal route by which affective and autonomic states act on tissues is the tone of small arteries and arterioles, which sets how blood is distributed through the microcirculation. Its empirical domain is the perfusion of a capillary bed: blood enters from the feeding arterioles, spreads through the capillary network, which stores blood in its compliance, and leaves through the draining venules, while part of the plasma filters into the tissue. Lexicon is strictly restricted to affective neuroscience, autonomic psychophysiology, and microvascular physiology.

Declaration (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3; Branch II).

  • Domain \(\mathcal{M}\) (\(n = 3\)) and boundary \(\partial\mathcal{M}\). A tissue region containing a capillary bed, treated at the network scale as a porous medium, with the lumens and walls of the feeding arterioles and draining venules that run through it excised from \(\mathcal{M}\), together with any larger vessels. The capillaries and the post-capillary segments of a single compliance class form the medium. \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) consists of:
  • the arteriolar boundary (supply): the walls of the terminal arterioles where the capillaries arise, across which blood enters at a pressure set by arteriolar tone;
  • the venular boundary (outflow at the datum): the walls of the collecting venules into which the capillaries drain, at venular pressure \(p_{\mathrm{ven}}\), held within tolerance;
  • the remaining boundary, closed: tissue surfaces, or surfaces across which no blood crosses within tolerance, located by a declared perfusion measurement.

All supply crosses the arteriolar boundary; the capillary bed contains no other inflow, so there are no interior sources. The arterioles, venules, and interstitium have compliance or storage of a different class (§0.1 item 3) and lie outside \(\mathcal{M}\); the interstitium receives the filtrate, which lymphatics drain outside \(\mathcal{M}\). The domain may be observed in vivo by intravital microscopy, or in an isolated perfused tissue preparation. * Window. A relaxation window (§0.1 item 1), opened from a prior steady state by a declared step (or monotone ramp) increase of the pressure at the arteriolar boundary, after which arteriolar pressure, venular pressure, and temperature are held within tolerance. The increase may come from dilation of the feeding arterioles (withdrawal of vasoconstrictor tone, or a vasodilator applied to the feeding arterioles only) or, in a perfused preparation, from a raised perfusion pressure. Capillary pressure then rises at every point, so filtration rises and remains a sink, and the tissue's volume change is non-negative (vascular distension and filtrate). Windows that open with a fall of arteriolar pressure are excluded, because falling capillary pressure shrinks the tissue (\( heta < 0\)); that alone justifies the exclusion. Physically, a fall can also turn filtration into reabsorption from the interstitium, an interior source. The declared datum form cannot show this: with \(p_{\mathrm{f}} = p_{\mathrm{ven}}\) and \(p \ge p_{\mathrm{ven}}\) the declared filtration never reverses. This second reason therefore rests on the physical Starling balance, not on the declared law, and it is why the declared form would misrepresent such a window. Windows in which myogenic or metabolic autoregulation returns the arteriolar pressure beyond tolerance are excluded. * Metric. Flat and rigid (§0.1 item 2): \(g_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu u}\) in a Cartesian chart, with the tissue volume, measured by plethysmography or tissue thickness, within the rigid tolerance; any residual change is non-negative in the declared direction. * Cone speed. \(c_*\) is the longitudinal sound speed of the tissue. Blood velocities in the microcirculation are \(\ll c_*\). * Storage. \(C_{\mathrm{v}}\): the compliance of the capillary bed per unit tissue volume, the blood volume stored per unit volume per unit rise of capillary pressure (m³ m⁻³ Pa⁻¹). It is declared uniform over \(\mathcal{M}\) within tolerance and linear over the window's range of pressures (§0.1 item 3). * Free energy \(\mathcal{F}\) and datum. \(\mathcal{F} = p - p_{\mathrm{ven}}\) (J m⁻³), with \(p\) the network-scale capillary blood pressure. The datum is the venular pressure, held at the venular boundary. Blood flows from the arteriolar to the venular boundary, so \(p \ge p_{\mathrm{ven}}\) throughout \(\mathcal{M}\) is a checkable precondition (precondition 2), not a triviality. \(\mathcal{F}\) is linear in the stored blood: the blood stored per unit volume above the datum is \(C_{\mathrm{v}}\mathcal{F}\), so \(\mathcal{F}\) is that stored blood times the declared conversion factor \(1/C_{\mathrm{v}}\). The relaxation time \(\ell^2C_{\mathrm{v}}/k_{\mathrm{b}}\) is finite, and it is required to exceed the time resolution of the pressure instruments by a declared factor (precondition 8). * Transport \(\mathfrak{K}\). \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = k_{\mathrm{b}}^{\alpha eta}/C_{\mathrm{v}}\), with \(k_{\mathrm{b}}^{\alpha eta}\) the network-scale (Darcy) conductance tensor of the capillary bed for blood at its effective viscosity, parametric: for example one conductance along and one across the dominant capillary orientation (as along muscle fibres), with isotropic conductance as the default. With \(q\) the Darcy blood flux (m s⁻¹), \(J_W = q/C_{\mathrm{v}}\); \(1/C_{\mathrm{v}}\) is the declared conversion factor. * Sink \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\). Transcapillary filtration, first order relative to the datum: \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = k_{\mathrm{f}}(\mathcal{F} - \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{ref}}) \ge 0\), with \(k_{\mathrm{f}} = L_{\mathrm{p}}S_{\mathrm{v}}/C_{\mathrm{v}}\) (\(L_{\mathrm{p}}\) the hydraulic conductivity of the capillary wall, \(S_{\mathrm{v}}\) the capillary surface area per unit tissue volume). The physical filtration follows the Starling balance of hydrostatic and oncotic pressures across the wall, which vanishes at some capillary pressure \(p_{\mathrm{f}}\); the first-order datum form declares \(p_{\mathrm{f}} = p_{\mathrm{ven}}\) within tolerance, a declared idealization. It is admitted only under the binding closure, and it is rejected if the default fits at least as well (closure (iv)). \(L_{\mathrm{p}}S_{\mathrm{v}}\) is estimated per closure (ii) by a declared method on the same tissue (for example the filtration response to venous pressure steps before the window, a declared perturbation regime), and \(p_{\mathrm{f}}\) is checked against \(p_{\mathrm{ven}}\) in the same regime. * Drive. Default, \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\) (§0.1 item 5). Red cells move with the blood under pressure and drag; no drag drive is declared, and no cell is mapped as a tracer. * Branch II evidence (closure (v)). * The trend of \(\langle heta angle\) and a bound on \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\) come from the measured tissue volume, which must stay within the rigid tolerance. * \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) is estimated from measured dissipation (§0.1 item 7): * the supply term uses the inflow through the feeding arterioles (red-cell velocimetry times lumen cross-section in vivo, or the perfusion flow of a perfused preparation) and \(\mathcal{F}\) at the arteriolar boundary from servo-null micropressure measurement; * the venular boundary, at the datum, contributes nothing; * the consumption term uses the declared, independently estimated \(k_{\mathrm{f}}\) with \(\mathcal{F}\) from a second set of capillary pressure measurements; * the storage term uses repeated pressure measurements.

The $O_1$ test uses an interior section and its own instruments.
  • The physical dissipation is the viscous dissipation of blood flow, \(q\cdot(- abla p)\) per unit volume. Under the declarations it equals the r7 dissipation density \(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\) times the positive constant \(p_0C_{\mathrm{v}}\), and its measured sign must agree with that of the estimate.
  • Admissible domains (declared, checkable preconditions):
  • no interior inflow (no arteriovenous shunts or feeding vessels inside \(\mathcal{M}\) beyond the excised ones), and \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) throughout \( ar{\mathcal{M}}\);
  • capillary pressure above venular pressure throughout \(\mathcal{M}\), and net filtration non-negative everywhere (no reabsorption), with interstitial hydrostatic and oncotic pressures constant within tolerance over the window;
  • a single compliance class: \(C_{\mathrm{v}}\) uniform within tolerance, checked by the blood-volume response to a pressure step in two or more subregions;
  • no capillary recruitment or derecruitment within the window (perfused capillary density constant within tolerance, by intravital microscopy), and a steady distribution of haematocrit, so that \(k_{\mathrm{b}}\) is constant;
  • arteriolar and venular boundary pressures held within tolerance after the step, with residual cardiac pulsation, respiratory modulation, and vasomotion at the arteriolar boundary within tolerance; windows with vasomotion beyond tolerance are excluded;
  • tissue volume within the rigid tolerance, isothermal conditions within tolerance;
  • the closed parts of the boundary carry no blood flux within tolerance;
  • a relaxation time \(\ell^2C_{\mathrm{v}}/k_{\mathrm{b}}\) that exceeds the time resolution of the pressure instruments by a declared factor, so that the field is resolvably stored and not quasi-static.
  • Titled phenomena outside the domain.
  • Affect and its regulation. Emotions, their appraisal, and their regulation are processes of the person, outside \(\mathcal{M}\); they are context. Their autonomic expression reaches the bed through sympathetic vasoconstrictor tone on the feeding arterioles, which sets the arteriolar boundary data. Within windows those data are held, so affect enters only through their held level and through the step that opens the window.
  • Autonomic rhythms. Heart-rate variability, respiratory modulation, and vasomotion are temporal quantities; they are excluded from windows by tolerance and are never mapped to \( heta\), \(\sigma\), or any spatial operator.
  • Psychophysiological resilience. Recovery of physiological variables after a stressor is a property of the person's regulatory systems, outside \(\mathcal{M}\). It is not mapped to \(\gamma_\sigma\), to the relaxation of the pressure field, or to any rate of this aperture. Repeated stress shapes the microvasculature between windows (remodelling, changes of capillary density), which enters through the declared parameters and is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\), not identified with it.
  • Lymphatic drainage and oedema. Drainage of the filtrate and the accumulation of interstitial fluid lie outside \(\mathcal{M}\); windows end before interstitial pressure changes beyond tolerance (precondition 2).

docs.title: 2. Coordinate-by-Coordinate Mapping (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\))
\(O_0\) — Exogenous Flux & Emergent Foliation Time
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( heta \equiv -N K \overset{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0}{=} rac{1}{2}g^{\mu u} rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} = rac{1}{\sqrt{\vert g\vert}} rac{\partial\sqrt{\vert g\vert}}{\partial au} = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\); \(\Theta_E \equiv rac{\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}}{s_0} = - rac{ eta_{\mathrm{th}}}{s_0}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\); \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \sqrt{ heta^2 + \Theta_E^2}\), \( au_\Theta( au) \equiv \int_{ au_0}^{ au}\langle\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au'\); \( rac{dV_{\mathcal{M}}}{d au} = \int_{\mathcal{M}} heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\), with \(\lim_{ au o\infty}V_{\mathcal{M}}( au) = V_\infty < \infty\) (Branch II); \( rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), \(q(\mathbf{x}, au) \equiv -\ln(v_0Q(\mathbf{x}, au))\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The tissue is rigid within tolerance, so \( heta \equiv 0\), \(dV_{\mathcal{M}}/d au = 0\), and \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\). The blood entering across the arteriolar boundary is throughput and is never mapped to \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) (§0.1 item 6); the cyclic pulsation of vessels with the heartbeat is not \( heta\). Viscous flow of blood down its pressure gradient dissipates energy at every point, so \(\Theta_E > 0\) (by \(O_1\)), \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} = \Theta_E\), and \( au_\Theta\) counts entropy production per \(s_0\). The record accumulates by \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) along the throughput current. The bed's structural adaptation (capillary density, vessel calibre, the history of its tone) is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\) and is not identified with it; it enters each window through \(\mathcal{H}_0\).

docs.title: \(O_1\) — Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamic Openness
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} = p_0\oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu \ge 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} \equiv \int_{\mathcal{M}}(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F})\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} \equiv \dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} + \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\); \( abla_\mu\mathcal{F} eq 0\); \(J_E^\mu \equiv rac{J_W^\mu}{p_0} = - rac{1}{p_0}\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}\) (Branch II, fixed); \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\); \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} > 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The maintained arteriovenous pressure difference, together with filtration, holds the bed far from equilibrium. With \(J_E^\mu = -p_0^{-1}(k_{\mathrm{b}}^{\mu u}/C_{\mathrm{v}}) abla_ u\mathcal{F}\), \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\) holds identically wherever \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) (precondition 1), so \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). Blood flows down its pressure gradient from the arteriolar to the venular boundary, in the direction of \(J_E^\mu\). \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0\), so \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} > 0\). The empirical content of \(O_1\) is the flux-prediction test (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3, §5.5 item 6). \(k_{\mathrm{b}}\) is estimated per closure (ii) from the bed's pressure–flow relation at several steady perfusion pressures before the window (a declared perturbation regime), and \(C_{\mathrm{v}}\) from the blood-volume response to a pressure step measured optically (a different modality). The declared law must predict \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}} = q^{\mathrm{meas}}/C_{\mathrm{v}}\) across a declared interior section \(S\), with \(q^{\mathrm{meas}}\) from the summed flows of the capillaries crossing \(S\) (red-cell velocity and lumen cross-section by intravital microscopy, per unit area), and \( abla\mathcal{F}\) from micropressure measurements on both sides of \(S\); neither uses the other or the declared \(k_{\mathrm{b}}\) or \(k_{\mathrm{f}}\). No current test exercises this aperture (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3).

docs.title: \(O_2\) — Unimodular Weyl Factorization, Constraint Precision & Trajectories
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}( au, \mathbf{x}) = \Omega^2( au, \mathbf{x})\hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) with \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) = 0 \implies \det g = \Omega^{2n}\), \( rac{\partial\ln\Omega}{\partial au} = rac{1}{n} heta\); \(\Pi_{\mu u} = abla_\mu abla_ u\Phi\); \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\), \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\); \( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G rac{\partial( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha)}{\partial au} + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\); \(\left.\left( rac{dv^\mu}{d au} + \Gamma^\mu_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + g^{\mu\lambda}\left( rac{\partial g_{\lambda u}}{\partial au} ight)v^ u - rac{1}{2}\left( rac{\partial g_{ ho\epsilon}}{\partial au}v^ ho v^\epsilon ight)v^\mu ight) ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}\), \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2)\left(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu ight)\), \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2 < 1\), with the default \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the rigid tissue the unimodular Weyl split is trivial (\(\Omega \equiv 1\), \(\hat{h} \equiv 0\), \(\partial_ au\ln\Omega = 0\)). The split isolates the volume element only algebraically; \( heta\) remains coupled to \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\) and \(\sigma_{\alpha eta}\) through the traced elliptic \( au\)-compatibility equation (r10 Decision 2), whose two sides vanish identically here (§0.1 items 2 and 4). Vessel-wall stresses and the tone of vascular smooth muscle are Cauchy stresses and active tensions, not \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\); tone acts through the arteriolar boundary data. The architecture of the network enters through \(k_{\mathrm{b}}\) and the declared geometry of \(\mathcal{M}\), not through \(g\). \(\Pi_{\mu u}\) is the Hessian of a declared precision potential and enters only the coupling sector (\(O_6\)). Eq. [3] is instantiated with the default drive and maps no tracer.

docs.title: \(O_3\) — Shear Damping & Hysteresis Consolidation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\left. rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = rac{2}{n} heta g_{\mu u} + 2\sigma_{\mu u}\); \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv \partial_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) (\(\gamma_\sigma = \mathrm{const} > 0\), \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\mu} = 0\)) \(\implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\Vert_{C^2(\mathcal{M})} = 0\); \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\), \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)); \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\).
  • Physical Instantiation: On the rigid tissue \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv 0\), so the shear law holds trivially for any \(\gamma_\sigma > 0\), \(\hat{h} = \hat{h}_\infty = 0\), and \(\hat{g}_\infty = \hat{g} = \delta\); this aperture supports no shear-relaxation test (§0.1 item 2). The relaxation of the pressure field toward its new steady state is a property of the \(O_4\) balance law and is not mapped to \(\sigma\). The haemodynamic shear stress on vessel walls is a stress, not the shear rate \(\sigma\) of the metric. Recovery after a stressor lies outside \(\mathcal{M}\) and is not mapped here. \(V_{\mathrm{local}}\) is the hysteresis content of a cover set.

docs.title: \(O_4\) — Free-Energy Balance, Spectral Low-Pass Gating & Boundary Stress Conservation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( rac{\partial\mathcal{F}}{\partial au} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), \(J_W^\alpha \equiv -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = \mathfrak{K}^{ eta\alpha} \succ 0\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\); \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\); \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au) = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\); \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: With \( heta \equiv 0\) the balance law reads \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} = abla_\alpha((k_{\mathrm{b}}^{\alpha eta}/C_{\mathrm{v}}) abla_ eta\mathcal{F}) - k_{\mathrm{f}}\mathcal{F}\): the storage–conductance equation of a compliant porous capillary bed with first-order filtration, in pressure form. Compliance gives the finite relaxation time, so the field is stored, not quasi-static (precondition 8). The anisotropic \(k_{\mathrm{b}}\) and the filtration law depart from the default and satisfy the binding closure, and each is rejected if the default fits at least as well (closure (iv)). The gate sector follows §0.1 item 8: the Neumann eigenmodes of \(- abla^2\) on the rigid tissue are fixed, so the gate does not drift, and the faster decay of fine spatial structure in the pressure field is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the gate without being the gate. The selective permeability of the capillary wall to water and solutes is a property of the sink's parameters, not the spatial gate. The stress-conservation equivalence holds identically (§0.1 item 4).

docs.title: \(O_5\) — Riemannian Geometric Mean Gluing, Percolation & Harmonic Circulation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\); \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) geodesically convex for \(g^{(ij)}( au) \; orall au \ge au_0\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\); \(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\); \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\); \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} G_{\infty,\mu u}^{(i)} \succ 0\) (standing hypothesis with \(H_0 = 0\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: The cover consists of \( au\)-independent subregions of the tissue: one cover set around each excised vessel segment, containing its wall (a concave part of \(\partial\mathcal{M}\)), and further sets that are intersections of \(\mathcal{M}\) with strictly convex bodies clear of those walls. Every overlap is declared clear of the concave parts and convex on the rigid metric (§0.1 item 9). Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of \(g\), so the gluing holds identically, \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} = 0\), and \(g^{(i)} = G_\infty^{(i)}\) at every \( au\) (\(H_0 = 0\)). Every overlap is crossed by the transient, so \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\). The connectivity of the capillary network is a property of the bed that enters through \(k_{\mathrm{b}}\): a network below its percolation threshold has no network-scale conductance and is not an admissible domain. That connectivity is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the condition \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} > \phi_c\) and is not identified with it; anastomoses between vascular territories are context. Each excised vessel segment that passes through \(\mathcal{M}\) adds a non-contractible loop, so \(b_1(\mathcal{M}) \ge 1\) in general, and harmonic Neumann fields circulate around these segments. No blood flow or measured field is identified with them, and no claim is made about them (§0.1 item 9).

docs.title: \(O_6\) — Asymmetric Phase-Lead Coupling & Trace-Free Deformation Operator
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\); \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) (hypothesis) \(\wedge \; \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\); \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u\,dA > 0\) (hypothesis, \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), with this boundary flux integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) (Branch II).
  • Physical Instantiation: Take two adjacent cover sets along the flow path between a feeding arteriole and a draining venule, sharing an overlap \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\). The partner fields are the rate of change of the free-energy flux of blood in the two orientations (§0.1 item 9), so \(\eta_{[i o j]} = \partial_ au J_W\): a spatially resolved flux field, not a temporal lag between scalar signals such as heart rate and blood pressure.
  • The arteriolar boundary holds the raised pressure and the venular boundary the datum, so after the step the flux near the arterioles decays from an initial overshoot while nearer the venules it rises, and the zero set between them travels toward the venules during the early window.
  • The excised vessels make the geometry far from a slab, so the zero set is located only by the predicted solution, from the independently estimated \(k_{\mathrm{b}}\), \(C_{\mathrm{v}}\), and \(k_{\mathrm{f}}\) and the declared boundary data.
  • The declared overlap is one that the predicted zero set does not reach during the overlap's window, with the detection threshold of §0.1 item 9; on it \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) keeps one direction, which the declaration states from the predicted solution.

The odd 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\) is its image under the declared non-singular precision map, with distinct Hessians, and is non-zero there. Under the non-degeneracy hypothesis \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), built per r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3], \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0\) gives \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\), with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general. The eigendirections are directions of the operator \(M^{(ij)}\), not sympathetic and parasympathetic influences, and not directions of enhanced or suppressed perfusion. Under the flux-positivity hypothesis the coupling transmits correlation between the subsystem marginals of the declared state sector (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\)). Both are standing hypotheses, not consequences of perfusion. In Branch II the transient decays as the bed settles, so the coupling flux is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\). With \(\sigma \equiv 0\) the overlaps keep their declared convex shape, and the r10 §5.12 constraint has no counterpart here. No range of autonomic perturbation, clinical or otherwise, is mapped to a convexity threshold.

docs.title: \(O_7\) — Principal-Bundle Gauge Coherence, Impedance Decay & Hysteresis Alignment
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(D_\mu = \partial_\mu - i g_{\mathrm{YM}}\,\mathrm{ad}_{A_\mu}\); \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\); \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2} o 1\), \(\hat{\chi} \equiv \chi_E\hat{u}\) (Branch II); \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\).
  • Physical Instantiation: The gauge sector is the trivial declaration of §0.1 item 10, so \([F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\) identically. With \(\sigma \equiv 0\), \(\chi_E \equiv 1\) and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu \equiv 0\) at every \( au\), and \(\chi\) is undefined (\( heta = 0\)). \(\hat{ ho}_g = rac{1}{n}\delta^\mu_ u\) at every \( au\), and alignment with \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}\) holds where the Hessian of the declared convex record becomes isotropic, an asymptotic condition stated and not tested. The \(O_7\) Eq. [3] identities hold with divergence-free \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) and \(u_{\mathrm{exp}}\), bounded \(J_E\), and \(\hat{h} \equiv \hat{h}_\infty\). Coherence between cardiac, respiratory, and vasomotor rhythms, and physiological synchrony between persons, are not mapped to the gauge connection; they are context, and no coherence or synchrony claim is made.

docs.title: \(O_\Omega\) — Topological Asymptote, Branch II: Bounded Non-Equilibrium Steady State
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)): \( heta \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{C^2(\mathcal{M})} 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^{\infty}\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\); \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\) and \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\); \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q) rac{\delta\Psi}{\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})} \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{} 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} o 0\) (with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly as \( au o \infty\)).
  • Physical Instantiation: Under held arteriolar and venular pressures, the bed approaches a steady pressure field that carries a steady flow of blood from the arterioles to the venules, with steady filtration: a bounded non-equilibrium steady state. \( heta \equiv 0\), \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\), \(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\) while perfusion is maintained, \(\sigma \equiv 0\), and \(\partial_ au g \equiv 0\). The transient coupling decays, so \(\mathcal{I} o s_0V_\infty\). The generator condition requires \(J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0\), an asymptotic hypothesis on the declared state sector that no finite window tests. The state is neither static equilibrium, which would require uniform pressure with no flow and no filtration (the arrest of circulation), nor a periodic return: the cardiac and respiratory cycles are excluded from windows by tolerance, and successive changes of autonomic tone form a sequence of windows. A calm or regulated affective state of the person is not mapped to this limit. The limit belongs to the declared idealization of held tone and constant interstitial pressures; the physical bed leaves it as tone changes or oedema develops, which bounds the usable window.
  • Within windows the supported tests (aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5) are the non-degeneracy check (4), the signs of \(\Theta_E\), \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}\), and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}}\) (5), the flux prediction (6), and the Branch II evidence (7).
  • Tests (1)–(3) hold trivially on the rigid tissue.
  • No current test exercises this aperture.

docs.title: 0. Tier Architecture & Four-Part Functional Homology
docs.text:
Tier 5 maps the physics of sound in the environment and its relation to rhythm, the prosody and comprehension of verse, the movement of persons in space and in relation to one another, and the association of heterogeneous agents onto Spine \(\mathcal{T}\). One aperture (5.1) is an empirical aperture declared in Branch II of r7, the bounded non-equilibrium steady state (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3). It declares, in its §1, a domain, physical metric, cone speed, storage coefficient, free energy with datum, transport tensor, interior sink, drive, and Branch II evidence, and instantiates all nine coordinates \(O_0 \to O_\Omega\) on that domain: the energy of a diffuse sound field, supplied across the surface of an excised source region, spreading through the air of an enclosure by repeated reflection and scattering, and absorbed by the enclosure's bounding surfaces and, as a declared interior sink, by the air. Apertures 5.2, 5.3, and 5.4 are provisionally homological in this epoch: they declare no domain, map all nine coordinates as conceptual correspondences, like Tier 1, and make no empirical claim (§0.1 item 12).

The wider phenomena named in the aperture titles (rhythm and entrainment, verse and its meaning, choreography and the coordination of movement, inter-subjective and cross-substrate association) enter the empirical mapping of 5.1 as boundary conditions, through the declared parameters, through the hysteresis record \(\mathcal{H}\), or as illustrative context, and its §1 states which. No Tier 5 aperture claims that an expressive, aesthetic, or collective phenomenon obeys a spine law. Each aperture is formulated at the level of general physics, linguistics, movement science, and systems theory, for populations studied at cohort level, without presupposing a single practitioner, practice, work, or site. No human-subject test is included in this epoch (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3), and the declared domain of 5.1 is unoccupied within its windows.

Slot & Functional Role Aperture Designation Declared Domain and Diffusing Quantity Titled Phenomena Outside the Domain Vertical Homology Across Tiers Slot 5.1: Structural Substrate Environmental Acoustics & Rhythmic Entrainment (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{acoustic}}\)) The energy density of a diffuse sound field in the air of an unoccupied enclosure, supplied across the surface of an excised source region and absorbed by the bounding surfaces and the air. Sound sources and their resonance, direct sound, early reflections and low-frequency modes, outdoor propagation, hearing, rhythm and entrainment: as boundary data, through the parameters, through \(\mathcal{H}\), or context. \(1.1 \leftrightarrow 2.1 \leftrightarrow 3.1 \leftrightarrow 4.1 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{5.1}\) Slot 5.2: Dynamic Flow & Waves Poetic Prosody & Psycholinguistic Condensation (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{poetic}}\)) None declared: provisionally homological (inertial phonatory airflow). All of its phenomena are mapped as conceptual correspondences only. \(1.2 \leftrightarrow 2.2 \leftrightarrow 3.2 \leftrightarrow 4.2 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{5.2}\) Slot 5.3: Boundary Gating Spatial Choreography & Relational Kinesiology (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{choreographic}}\)) None declared: provisionally homological (advective goal-directed movement). All of its phenomena are mapped as conceptual correspondences only. \(1.3 \leftrightarrow 2.3 \leftrightarrow 3.3 \leftrightarrow 4.3 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{5.3}\) Slot 5.4: Coalescence & Hysteresis Inter-Subjective & Cross-Substrate Symbiosis (\(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{symbiotic}}\)) None declared: provisionally homological (quasi-static signal media). All of its phenomena are mapped as conceptual correspondences only. \(1.4 \leftrightarrow 2.4 \leftrightarrow 3.4 \leftrightarrow 4.4 \leftrightarrow \mathbf{5.4}\)

docs.title: 0.1 Conventions Common to the Tier 5 Apertures
docs.text:
The following conventions apply to the empirical aperture of this tier (5.1); item 12 states how the provisionally homological Apertures 5.2, 5.3, and 5.4 are mapped. Aperture 5.1's §1 and coordinate blocks state its specific values and cite these items where they apply. Where an item repeats a convention of tier_4_somatic_contemplative_interiority.md §0.1, it is restated here so that this tier can be read on its own.

  1. Branch and windows. Branch II is declared before any test, with the estimators of item 7 and 5.1 §1, and the domain of 5.1 is never re-evaluated in Branch I on the same data (closure (v)). Statements that hold in Branch I only (r10 Decision 6) are never applied. Every observation window is a relaxation window: it begins at a declared \( au_0\) from a prior steady state, a declared transient starts at \( au_0\), the external data are then held within declared tolerances, and the window follows the domain as it settles.
  2. The transient is a declared step increase of the source's acoustic power, from a held non-zero level to a higher held level. The supply data are the net inflow of acoustic power across the source surface (flux data, not a held value of \(\mathcal{F}\)); the bounding surfaces absorb through a Robin exchange (5.1 §1); and the sink, air absorption, is first order, Lipschitz, and non-decreasing in \(\mathcal{F}\). The declared balance law is a scalar parabolic equation, so the comparison principle holds. The prior steady state is a subsolution for the raised inflow, so \(\mathcal{F}(\cdot, au_0 + h) \ge \mathcal{F}(\cdot, au_0)\); the held data make the problem invariant under time translation, so \(\mathcal{F}(\cdot, au + h) \ge \mathcal{F}(\cdot, au)\), that is, \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} \ge 0\) at every point. The inflow reaches its held level over a short rise time (the response of the source and the travel of sound across the excised region), a non-decreasing ramp, for which the same conclusion follows without time translation: \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F}\) obeys the linearized equation with zero initial data and non-negative boundary data, so it stays non-negative. The Robin data do not change the argument. The argument is exact on the declared rigid domain.
  3. Direction. The opposite direction is excluded. When the source is switched off, the field relaxes to the datum: this is the decay from which reverberation time is measured, and it is not a Branch II window, because the throughput stops and \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle = 0\). A decrease to a lower non-zero power would keep every declaration; the raising direction is declared for the comparison argument, as for 4.1 in Tier 4. Sources whose power varies within the window (periodic, rhythmic, modulated, or intermittent signals) are excluded, because their supply data are not monotone.
  4. Boundary exchange. Every exchange of acoustic energy across the bounding surfaces is one-signed, out of \(\mathcal{M}\): absorption by the surfaces and transmission through them to the outside. No compartment outside \(\mathcal{M}\) discharges into it within a window, except across the declared supply surface: sound entering from outside the enclosure is held below a declared fraction of \(\mathcal{F}\) everywhere in \(\mathcal{M}\), the enclosure has no opening to another volume that could store sound and return it, the linings of the bounding surfaces store negligible energy, and the bounding surfaces are rigid within tolerance (5.1 preconditions 1, 3, 4, and 5).
  5. The rate of change of the flux, \(\partial_ au J_W\), is not one-signed in general (item 9).
  6. Metric. The domain is a fixed region of space, the air of a rigid enclosure minus the excised source region, with the Euclidean metric. It is flat at every \( au\), so \(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\) and \(R_{\mu u} \equiv 0\) (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3 item 2). In a Cartesian chart \(g_{\mu u} = \delta_{\mu u}\), so \(\Omega \equiv 1\), \(\hat{h} \equiv 0\), \( heta \equiv 0\), and \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv 0\). The enclosure is declared rigid within a pre-declared tolerance on its volume. The air in it has no reference configuration whose deformation \(g\) could record: the compressions and rarefactions of sound are oscillations at acoustic frequencies with zero mean, and the vibration of the bounding surfaces is cyclic; neither is \( heta\) (item 6). With \(\sigma \equiv 0\) the \(O_3\) shear law holds trivially, and 5.1 supports no shear-relaxation test. No non-Euclidean material metric is declared: a gas has no stress-free reference configuration from which one could be built. The curved configurations of the r10 §5.11 and §5.13 witnesses are therefore realized by no Tier 5 aperture, and r7's curvature sector, which no empirical aperture of Tiers 2–4 exercises, is exercised by no empirical aperture in this epoch.
  7. Storage. The r7 \(O_4\) balance law carries unit storage: \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F}\) is the rate of change of the stored quantity per unit volume. The diffusing quantity of 5.1 is the acoustic energy density \(u\) of the air, in a declared band and over a declared averaging time (5.1 §1). Where the enclosure contains distributed scatterers, which are treated at the continuum scale as part of the medium (5.1 §1), acoustic energy is stored only in the air between them, and the storage coefficient is \(s = \phi_{\mathrm{a}}\), the air volume fraction; without scatterers \(s = 1\). With \(s\) uniform, the physical balance \(s\,\partial_ au u = abla_\alpha(k^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta u) - r\) becomes the r7 law for \(\mathcal{F} = u\) (\(u\) is itself an energy density, so the declared yield is \(1\)), \(\mathfrak{K} = k/s\), and \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = r/s\), and the r7 flux is \(J_W = j/s\), with \(j\) the net acoustic intensity per unit bulk area. The factor \(1/s\) is a declared conversion factor, estimated independently (closure (ii)). If \(s\) varies in space, \(s^{-1} abla_\alpha(k^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta u) = abla_\alpha(s^{-1}k^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta u) + s^{-2}k^{\alpha eta} abla_\alpha s\, abla_ eta u\), and the last term is a drift term that the r7 balance law does not contain. Aperture 5.1 therefore declares a single storage class: \(s\) uniform on \(\mathcal{M}\) within a tolerance (a declared, checkable precondition). Media that store acoustic energy differently (porous or resonant linings of the bounding surfaces, other volumes coupled to the enclosure, the excised source region) lie outside \(\mathcal{M}\) and enter as boundary data (the Robin exchange at the bounding surfaces, the inflow at the source surface) or are excluded, because a jump in \(s\) would make \(J_W\) discontinuous where the physical intensity is continuous, which the unit-storage law reads as an interface source or sink.
  8. Stress sector. With \(G_{\mu u} \equiv 0\), \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} \equiv 0\); its trace gives \( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha = 0\) for \(n = 3\), and then \( abla_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)} = 0\), so \(\xi\) is a Killing field. No Tier 5 medium has an identified global control field in this epoch, so Tier 5 declares \(\eta^\lambda \equiv 0\), hence \(\xi_ u \equiv 0\) and \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha = 0\), and the \(O_4\) equivalence \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\) holds identically. The \( au\)-compatibility law then reduces to \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma]_{\mu u} = rac{n-2}{n}( abla_\mu abla_ u heta - g_{\mu u} abla^2 heta)\), and its trace, the traced elliptic equation, to \( rac{n-1}{n} abla^2 heta = abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta}\): the Saint-Venant compatibility conditions of the strain rate. On the rigid domain of 5.1 both sides vanish. The pressures and stresses of the domain (the static pressure of the air, the oscillating acoustic pressure, the radiation pressure of sound, and the stresses in the bounding surfaces) are not \(T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}}\); they enter as boundary conditions, through the declared parameters, and through \(\mathcal{H}\). The partner fields \(\eta_{i o j}\) of \(O_6\) (item 9) are distinct objects from the global \(\eta\) of \(O_4\).
  9. Cone speed and trajectories. Aperture 5.1 declares \(c_*\) as the speed of sound in the air at the declared temperature. In this aperture the declared quantity itself travels on the cone at the scale of the mean free path: between reflections and scatterings, sound energy propagates along rays at \(c_*\), which are null for the declared cone and, like all null rays, are not trajectories of \(O_2\) Eq. [3]. The diffusion law describes the energy only at scales large against the mean free path \(\lambda\), where the energy transport velocity \(\vert j\vert/(s\,u)\) is \(\ll c_*\); that is the condition \(\lambda\vert abla\mathcal{F}\vert \ll \mathcal{F}\) (5.1 precondition 2). The law's instantaneous propagation is outside its validity at points that sound from a change at the source surface could not yet have reached, which item 9 takes into account. Every material speed in \(\mathcal{M}\) (drifts of the air) is \(\ll c_*\), so \(u^2 \ll 1\). The trajectory equation is displayed in physical units: both \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u/c_*^2\) and the projection term \(c_*^{-2}(g_{\alpha eta}a^\alpha_{\mathrm{d}}v^ eta)v^\mu\) carry \(c_*\), and with \(c_* = 1\) the display reduces to the r7 form. Aperture 5.1 instantiates Eq. [3] with \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\) and maps no tracer. The movement of sources, persons, and objects is forced motion outside \(\mathcal{M}\), and within windows nothing moves (5.1 precondition 5).
  10. Currents. In Branch II, \(J_E^\mu = J_W^\mu/p_0\) is fixed. The expansion current \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\) enters only through its divergence \( heta\) and its boundary flux \(dV_{\mathcal{M}}/d au\) (r7 \(O_0\) branch scope), and no supply current is ever mapped to it: the acoustic power entering at the source surface is throughput. In general \( abla_\mu J_E^\mu = -p_0^{-1}(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} + \mathcal{F} heta + \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}) eq heta\). The cyclic volume changes of sound (the condensation of the air in each period) and of vibrating surfaces are outside the declared fields and are never mapped to \( heta\). The oscillating particle velocity of the air is not a current of the spine: \(J_W\) is built from the net intensity, averaged over the declared averaging time.
  11. Measured dissipation. The Branch II evidence requires \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) to be estimated from measured dissipation, never from \(\mathfrak{K} abla\mathcal{F}\). Integrating \(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\) by parts and using the \(O_4\) balance law gives the identity $\(p_0\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} = \oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{F}\,(-J_W^\mu)\,d\Sigma_\mu - \int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{F}\,\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx - rac{1}{2} rac{d}{d au}\int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{F}^2\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx - rac{1}{2}\int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{F}^2 heta\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\)$
  12. No face of \(\mathcal{M}\) is held at the datum. The source surface carries the held inflow, and its term is evaluated from the source's calibrated acoustic power and the measured \(\mathcal{F}\) there. The bounding surfaces absorb in proportion to \(\mathcal{F}\), and their term is evaluated from the measured normal intensity into them and the measured \(\mathcal{F}\) there (5.1 §1).
  13. Each term is evaluated from measured \(\mathcal{F}\), measured boundary fluxes, and measured or independently declared consumption; none uses the declared \(\mathfrak{K}\). 5.1 §1 names instruments and surfaces different from those of the \(O_1\) flux-prediction test, so that the evidence is independent of that test.
  14. Because the identity uses the balance law, the estimate is conditional on it. 5.1 §1 also names a directly measured physical dissipation whose sign the estimate must share: the conversion of acoustic energy into heat by the bounding surfaces and the air. It is non-negative by the second law, so this comparison tests only the sign of the identity-based estimate, and it is stated as such. Only signs and \(s_0\)-independent rates of \(\Theta_E\) are tested.
  15. Reflection and scattering conserve acoustic energy: no heat is produced where the energy density merely spreads. \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} = - eta_{\mathrm{th}}J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F}\) is therefore the entropy production of the declared mapping (the spreading of an incoherent field's energy down its gradient), not a measured heat production, as for Aperture 3.2 in Tier 3. Heat is produced only by the absorption.
  16. Gate sector (\(O_4\)). \( ho_{\mathrm{total}}( au)\) is a declared positive trace-class state on \(L^2(\mathcal{M}, d\mathrm{vol}_g)\), and \(Q\), \(P\), and the \(O_6\) marginals \(Q_i\) and joints \(Q_{ij}\) are densities of this declared state sector. No Tier 5 aperture identifies them with \(\mathcal{F}\) or with any measured field in this epoch, and none makes an empirical claim about the gate (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3). What the domain's physics supplies is, first, the spectral setting: the Neumann eigenmodes of \(- abla^2_g\) on \(\mathcal{M}\), whose eigenvalues are fixed on the rigid domain. On this domain these eigenmodes coincide in shape with the acoustic modes of a rigid-walled enclosure of the same shape. The gate is nonetheless a spatial projector acting on the declared state sector, never a filter in frequency: the declared field is an energy density averaged over a band above the frequency at which the modes of the enclosure overlap (5.1 precondition 2), so individual modes are not resolved in \(\mathcal{F}\), and \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}\) is never read in hertz. Second, the physics supplies a physical low-pass behaviour of \(\mathcal{F}\): under the balance law, fine spatial structure in \(\mathcal{F}\) relaxes faster than coarse structure. That behaviour is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to the gate and is not itself the gate. The stronger absorption of higher frequencies by surfaces and air is a property of the declared parameters across bands, not the spatial gate.
  17. Cover, overlaps, and coupling (\(O_5\), \(O_6\)).
  18. The cover \(\{\mathcal{U}_i\}\) consists of \( au\)-independent subregions of \(\mathcal{M}\) with Lipschitz boundaries, and every overlap \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) is convex at \( au_0\). \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) has concave parts: the source surface, which \(\mathcal{M}\) surrounds, and any re-entrant parts of the bounding surface. Each concave part lies in a single cover set, which need not be convex, and every overlap stays clear of the concave parts: r7 requires convex overlaps, not convex cover sets. Each \(g^{(i)}\) is the restriction of the one physical metric, so \(g^{(i)} = g^{(j)}\) on every overlap, the geometric mean returns the common metric (\(g \# g = g\)), and the gluing of \(O_5\) Eq. [3] holds identically.
  19. The anisotropy or inhomogeneity of a medium lives in \(\mathfrak{K}\), never in \(g\). Effective-medium averages of diffusion coefficients, including the combination of the mean free paths of the enclosure and of its scatterers, are statements about \(\mathfrak{K}\) and are not mapped to \(O_5\) Eq. [1].
  20. Partner fields. The partner fields are the rate of change of the free-energy flux read in the two orientations, \(\eta_{i o j}^\lambda = \partial_ au J_W^\lambda\) and \(\eta_{j o i}^\lambda = -\partial_ au J_W^\lambda\), defined on all of \(\mathcal{M}\), so \(\eta_{[i o j]}^\lambda = \partial_ au J_W^\lambda\). They decay with the transient, which gives the integrable coupling that Branch II requires; a steady flux would give \(\eta \equiv 0\), and a sustained coupling field is never declared.
  21. Zero sets. \(\partial_ au J_W\) is not one-signed in general. The supply of 5.1 is a held inflow, not a held value of \(\mathcal{F}\): after the step the normal flux at the source surface is held, and the flux near the supply does not decay from an initial overshoot, as it does under the held-value supplies of Tiers 3 and 4. In a one-dimensional configuration (an inflow uniform across a whole cross-section) and in a radially symmetric one, the flux obeys a parabolic equation of the same kind as \(\mathcal{F}\), with its held value at the supply and a non-decreasing value at the absorbing surface (the Robin outflow is proportional to \(\mathcal{F}\), which does not decrease); by the comparison principle the flux then rises at every interior point, so \(\partial_ au J_W\) points away from the supply throughout the interior of \(\mathcal{M}\) and vanishes only on the supply surface, where the held inflow fixes it. In general geometry the held inflow fixes the normal component of \(J_W\) on the supply surface, so the normal component of \(\partial_ au J_W\) vanishes there. Every overlap therefore stays clear of the supply surface, whatever its shape; in the declared enclosure it is also a concave part. The declared enclosure is in general neither one-dimensional nor radially symmetric, so any zero set of \(\partial_ au J_W\) in its interior is located only by the predicted solution. On a zero set \(\eta_{[i o j]} = 0\) and \(J_{[i o j]} = 0\), so a construction that included it would itself decide the non-degeneracy hypothesis there.
  22. 5.1 therefore declares overlaps \( ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) that the zero set, predicted before the window from the independently estimated parameters, does not reach during the window. Before the transient arrives, the partner field on a downstream overlap is non-zero in the diffusion law but exponentially small, so the check is made against a pre-declared detection threshold: each overlap's window starts once the predicted \(\vert\eta_{[i o j]}\vert\) exceeds that threshold on \( ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\), and no earlier than a declared margin after the time sound needs to travel from the source surface to the overlap plus several mean free times (item 5); the data must then show \(\vert\eta_{[i o j]}\vert\) above the threshold there (a declared, checkable precondition). On such an overlap \(\eta_{[i o j]}\) keeps one direction throughout the overlap's window, which 5.1 states from the predicted solution.
  23. Precision potentials. The potentials \(\Phi^{(i)}\) are declared before data collection as quadratic potentials in a Cartesian chart. Their trace-free parts \(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)}\) cannot be positive definite, because their eigenvalues sum to zero, so \(J_{[i o j]} = rac{1}{2}(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)} + \hat{\Pi}^{(j)})\eta_{[i o j]}\) carries no sign relation to \(\eta_{[i o j]}\). Tier 5 declares \( rac{1}{2}(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)} + \hat{\Pi}^{(j)})\) non-singular, so that \(J_{[i o j]} eq 0\) wherever \(\eta_{[i o j]} eq 0\). What is claimed for \(J_{[i o j]}\) is its oddness under \(i \leftrightarrow j\) and its non-vanishing on the declared overlaps, not a direction.
  24. Tier 5 also declares the two trace-free Hessians distinct, \(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)} eq \hat{\Pi}^{(j)}\). With antisymmetric partner fields, \(J_{i o j} + J_{j o i} = (\hat{\Pi}^{(j)} - \hat{\Pi}^{(i)})\eta_{[i o j]}\). Equal Hessians would therefore remove the gradient term of r7 \(O_6\) Eq. [3] and leave \(M^{(ij)}_{\mu u} = \gamma_M ig((J_{[i o j]})_\mu(J_{[i o j]})_ u - rac{1}{n}g_{\mu u}J_{[i o j]}^\alpha(J_{[i o j]})_\alpha ig)\), the trace-free part of a rank-one tensor, which is non-zero wherever \(J_{[i o j]} eq 0\): the hypothesis would hold by construction. With distinct Hessians the gradient term depends on \( abla\eta_{[i o j]}\) and can cancel the quadratic term (r10 Decision 4), so the construction neither forces nor forbids \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\), which remains a standing hypothesis.
  25. On a connected domain the declared transient reaches every overlap for \( au > au_0\), so every edge of \(\mathcal{K}_0\) lies in \(\mathcal{K}\) and \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\); empirically, an edge is counted when its partner field exceeds a pre-declared detection threshold on its overlap. The percolation condition therefore carries no separate empirical content on this domain.
  26. \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\) and \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\) are standing hypotheses of r7 \(O_6\), not consequences of diffusion. In Branch II the transient decays as the domain settles, so each coupling-tensor boundary flux decays and is integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\); no sustained coupling is asserted. Aperture 5.1 is not among the systems of the current coupling test.
  27. Topology. The harmonic field of r7 \(O_5\) Eq. [5] carries absolute boundary conditions (it is tangential to \(\partial\mathcal{M}\)), so its space has dimension \(b_1(\mathcal{M})\), the first Betti number. The excised source region does not by itself make \(b_1\) positive: attached to a bounding surface through its mounting, it is a concave dent in \(\partial\mathcal{M}\); free-standing, it is an interior cavity, which adds to the second Betti number, not the first. \(b_1(\mathcal{M}) > 0\) where a fixed body in the enclosure (the source mounting among them) joins two separate parts of the bounding surface, or where the enclosure's own shape has a handle; then \(\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}}\) is non-trivial, a property of the domain's topology. The scatterers, treated at the continuum scale, are not holes of \(\mathcal{M}\). Tier 5 identifies no transport current or measured field with the harmonic field and makes no claim about it. With the declared uniform, isotropic \(\mathfrak{K}\), the r7 flux is the exact 1-form \(J_W = -D\,d\mathcal{F}\), which is \(L^2\)-orthogonal to every tangential harmonic field (the Hodge–Morrey–Friedrichs decomposition), so the declared current has no harmonic component.
  28. Gauge sector and hysteresis (\(O_7\), \(O_0\)). Tier 5 declares the trivial gauge sector for 5.1: \(A_\mu \equiv 0\) and a uniform unit section \(\hat{u}\). Then \(F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}} \equiv 0\), \([F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\) identically, and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu = (\partial_\mu\chi_E)\hat{u}\), which tends to \(0\) in \(C^1\) when \(\sigma o 0\) and \( heta o 0\) in \(C^2\) with \(\liminf\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\). The gauge limit therefore carries no content beyond the shear and expansion limits, and \(O_7\) gauge transport is untested in this epoch. In particular, no Tier 5 aperture makes a synchronization, alignment, entrainment, or coherence claim (of sound fields, of rhythms, of persons, or of agents): such claims would belong to gauge transport (aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5), not to \(\chi_E\), and the homological apertures map such phenomena to gauge transport as correspondences only. The hysteresis record obeys the r7 law \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) from a declared initial record \(\mathcal{H}_0\), chosen convex because \(O_7\) Eq. [2] requires \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H} \succ 0\) at every \( au\). \(\mathcal{H}\) then evolves through a state sector that is declared but not specified, so the declarations do not establish convexity at later \( au\). Tier 5 therefore states it as a declared condition, with a sufficient form: the largest eigenvalue magnitude of \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta(\mathcal{H} - \mathcal{H}_0)\) (with indices raised by \(g\)) stays below the smallest eigenvalue of \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H}_0\) on \(\mathcal{M}\) for all \( au \ge au_0\). Then \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H} \succ 0\) persists. The alternative, \( abla q \equiv 0\), would keep \(\mathcal{H}\) static and convex, but would make the \(O_\Omega\) generator condition hold trivially, so it is not adopted. The acoustic history of the enclosure (changes of its surfaces, linings, and contents between windows) is mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) to \(\mathcal{H}\) and is not identified with it. \(\hat{ ho}_g = rac{1}{n}\delta^\mu_ u\) at every \( au\) on the rigid domain, and the alignment \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) o 0\) then requires the Hessian of the record to become isotropic: an asymptotic condition that 5.1 states and does not test.
  29. Finite windows and coverage. No finite window exhibits a \( au o \infty\) limit. The claims of 5.1 are the within-window tests of aperture_generation_guidance.md §5.5 that its domain supports, listed in its \(O_\Omega\) block. In this epoch Aperture 5.1 is exercised by no test (empirical_validation_protocol.md §3.3), and no human-subject test is included. Everything else is stated as untested, not as confirmed.
  30. The provisionally homological apertures (5.2, 5.3, 5.4). Apertures 5.2, 5.3, and 5.4 map their phenomena onto all nine coordinates as conceptual correspondences, like the Tier 1 grammars and Aperture 4.3 (aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3). They declare no domain, metric, storage, free energy, transport tensor, sink, drive, or Branch II evidence, and make no empirical claim. Each §1 states why r7's storage–diffusion balance law cannot represent its system literally: the airflow of phonation is inertial (5.2), goal-directed movement is advective (5.3), and the media through which agents signal are quasi-static or carry waves (5.4). For uniformity of the tier, each of their blocks carries the same r7 spine-equation line as the empirical blocks. The shared line is read as tier_4_somatic_contemplative_interiority.md §0.1 item 12 states: schematically, with no cone speed declared, so that the r7 form with \(c_* = 1\) applies to the trajectory equation, and with the entry \(J_E^\mu = J_W^\mu/p_0\) as the Branch II form being read, not a declared current. Their correspondences are read against the Branch II form, because the systems they describe (a speaker's airflow, a moving group, an association of agents) are bounded, are sustained by throughput, and do not expand without bound (a homological aperture may choose a branch form with a stated reason, aperture_generation_guidance.md §2.3); as homologies they declare no branch in the sense of closure (v), because nothing is evaluated. Their correspondences are mapped via Spine \(\mathcal{T}\) and are never reductive identities; none is evidence for a spine law, and none is used by an empirical aperture. Coordinates that hold only trivially or by construction in 5.1 carry no content in them either.
