docs.title: \(O_3\) — Shear Damping & Hysteresis Consolidation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(\left. rac{\partial g_{\mu u}}{\partial au} ight\vert_{N=1,\, eta^\mu=0} = rac{2}{n} heta g_{\mu u} + 2\sigma_{\mu u}\); \( abla_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} \equiv \partial_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) (\(\gamma_\sigma = \mathrm{const} > 0\), \(\sigma^\mu_{\;\mu} = 0\)) \(\implies \lim_{ au o\infty}\Vert\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\Vert_{C^2(\mathcal{M})} = 0\); \(\hat{h}( au, \mathbf{x}) \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x})\), \((\hat{g}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))_{\mu u} \equiv \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\mathbf{x})(\exp\hat{h}_\infty(\mathbf{x}))^\alpha_{\; u}\) (\(\det\hat{g}_\infty = \det\hat{g} = 1\)); \(V_{\mathrm{local}}( au) \equiv \int_{\mathcal{U}_i}\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x}, au)\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx\).
  • Homological Mapping: Agents that repeatedly exchange their estimates of a common quantity converge on a shared value (consensus); in linear consensus models the disagreement decays exponentially, at a rate set by the structure of the exchange network, while the agreed value is retained. That pairing of a decaying disagreement with a retained agreement corresponds to the decay of \(\sigma\) at a constant rate as \(\hat{h}\) settles to \(\hat{h}_\infty\), with \(V_{\mathrm{local}}\) holding the consolidated content. No rate of a collective process is mapped to \(\gamma_\sigma\).

docs.title: \(O_4\) — Free-Energy Balance, Spectral Low-Pass Gating & Boundary Stress Conservation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \( rac{\partial\mathcal{F}}{\partial au} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\), \(J_W^\alpha \equiv -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = \mathfrak{K}^{ eta\alpha} \succ 0\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\); \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}} \equiv \mathbf{1}_{(- abla^2 \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2)}\); \(Q(\mathbf{x}, au) = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}( au)\vert\mathbf{x} angle > 0\); \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} = rac{1}{t_0 eta_{\mathrm{th}}}D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\); \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0 \iff abla^\mu T_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\).
  • Homological Mapping: The shared model of the environment that an association maintains corresponds to the gated density \(Q\), and the environment's own statistics to the reference \(P\), with the divergence \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P)\) and its cost \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}}\) as the cost of the mismatch. Only features that many members can observe and confirm enter common ground, while the detail that each agent alone observes stays with it; that retention of broadly shared, coarse structure corresponds to the gate \(\hat{\mathcal{P}}_{\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}}\), which keeps low spatial modes, as a correspondence between roles. The balance law corresponds to the resources of a symbiosis, replenished across the association's boundary and drawn down by its members. The stress-conservation equivalence has no counterpart here.

docs.title: \(O_5\) — Riemannian Geometric Mean Gluing, Percolation & Harmonic Circulation
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} \equiv (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\); \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) geodesically convex for \(g^{(ij)}( au) \; orall au \ge au_0\); \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\); \(\Delta_{\mathrm{Hodge}}\mathbf{J}_{\mathcal{M}}^{\mathrm{harm}} = 0\); \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} \ge 0\); \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} G_{\infty,\mu u}^{(i)} \succ 0\) (standing hypothesis with \(H_0 = 0\)).
  • Homological Mapping: In a symbiosis each partner keeps its own organization while the partners share an interface across which they exchange; in a team of persons and artificial agents, each keeps its own model while they maintain a shared one. That association without annexation corresponds to the gluing of local metrics over overlaps by the geometric mean, \(g^{(ij)} = g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)}\), which keeps each cover set's metric. A network of agents becomes able to pass information across its whole extent once its density of links exceeds a threshold, which corresponds to the percolation condition \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) > \phi_c\). Closed chains of dependence, as when each member of a community of microorganisms feeds on what the next produces around a cycle (cross-feeding), correspond to non-trivial cycles and to harmonic circulation around them, as a correspondence between a network's cycles and a manifold's topology, not an identity.

docs.title: \(O_6\) — Asymmetric Phase-Lead Coupling & Trace-Free Deformation Operator
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \((J_{[i o j]})_ u = -(J_{[j o i]})_ u\); \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) (hypothesis) \(\wedge \; \mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0 \implies m_+ > 0 > m_-\); \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\oint_{\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}} S_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u\,dA > 0\) (hypothesis, \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\)), with this boundary flux integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\) (Branch II).
  • Homological Mapping: In most partnerships one partner's state shapes the other's more than the reverse, so that it is the other that adapts. That direction corresponds to the odd phase-lead 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\); a perfectly symmetric exchange carries no directional lead, as fully symmetric partner fields remove a pair from \(\mathcal{K}\) in r7. An association can benefit a partner in one respect and cost it in another, by unequal amounts; that pairing corresponds to the opposite-signed extreme eigenvalues \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\) of the trace-free operator \(M^{(ij)}\) under the non-degeneracy hypothesis, with \(m_+ eq -m_-\) in general. The growth of the information that partners share during an exchange corresponds to the flux-positivity hypothesis \( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) > 0\). Both remain standing hypotheses of r7, and in the Branch II form the coupling must be transient (integrable), so the correspondence is with episodes of exchange that resolve, not with sustained coupling.

docs.title: \(O_7\) — Principal-Bundle Gauge Coherence, Impedance Decay & Hysteresis Alignment
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: \(D_\mu = \partial_\mu - i g_{\mathrm{YM}}\,\mathrm{ad}_{A_\mu}\); \(\Vert\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\Vert_{C^1(\mathcal{M})} o 0 \implies [F_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{YM}}, \hat{\chi}] o 0\); \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2} o 1\), \(\hat{\chi} \equiv \chi_E\hat{u}\) (Branch II); \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g( au) \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}( au)) o 0\).
  • Homological Mapping: Agents that communicate must read one another's signals in their own frames of reference, and populations of communicating agents converge on shared names and conventions. Carrying a frame of reference from agent to agent corresponds to gauge transport, and the decay of mismatches between frames to the decay of the covariant derivative \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu\); it never corresponds to the anisotropy index \(\chi_E\), which concerns the shape of deformation only. The alignment \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) o 0\) corresponds to the convergence of current exchanges with accumulated common ground.

docs.title: \(O_\Omega\) — Topological Asymptote, Branch II: Bounded Non-Equilibrium Steady State
docs.text:
• Spine Equations: Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)): \( heta \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{C^2(\mathcal{M})} 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^{\infty}\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\) and \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\); \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty\) and \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\); \(\left.\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}(\mathbf{x})\Psi[g_{\mu u}, \mathcal{H}] ight\vert_{\mathcal{H}=\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g]} = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q) rac{\delta\Psi}{\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})} \xrightarrow[ au o\infty]{} 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff rac{\partial\mathcal{H}}{\partial au} o 0\) (with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly as \( au o \infty\)).
  • Homological Mapping: A symbiotic association persists through continuing exchange: never static equilibrium, which for an association is its dissolution, and never a strict periodic return, although cycles of exchange recur. That state corresponds to the Branch II limit: bounded extent, sustained throughput (\(\langle\Theta_E angle o \Theta_\infty > 0\)), decaying shear and coupling transients, and a record whose growth stops when exchanges no longer bring surprise (\(J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0\)). The correspondence makes no claim about any association, agent, or collective, and no test exercises this aperture in this epoch.

docs.title: Macro-Symbiotic Tensor (\(O_0 \to O_\Omega\)): Design Rationale & Notation Companion
docs.text: Companion to: foundational-manifold-2026-10-20-r7.json (companion revision r10). The r7 JSON generalizes r6 under Design Decision 6; every r6 equation is recovered as the Branch I default, and §5.1–§5.12 below verify that case. §5.1–§5.12 are unchanged from r9 except one correction: the reference-prior normalization of §5.4 (and the overlap density of §5.8) is now stated in the \(\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\)-weighted form, which repairs the prior that §5.10 and §5.11 inherit from §5.4, where \(Q\) is non-uniform and r9's unweighted condition did not normalize \(P\).

docs.title: 1. Purpose of This Document
docs.text: This companion document records the modeling decisions, physical intuition, and standardized mathematical notation underlying the nine-coordinate specification in foundational-manifold-2026-10-20-r7.json (and its r6 special case). It connects the systems-theoretic intent of the framework to the differential-geometric equations.

docs.title: 2. Core Modeling Decisions & Design Rationale
Decision 1: Homothetic (Conformally Stationary) Closure at the Asymptote (\(O_\Omega \to O_0\))
docs.text:
• Conceptual Intent: The system is permanently open to environmental flux (\(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} > 0\)) and continuously expands its capacity, yet at the asymptotic horizon (\(O_\Omega\)) it achieves a stable, stationary form that closes the loop back to \(O_0\).
  • Mathematical Implementation: A metric cannot be strictly static (\(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} = 0\)) while its volume is still growing (\( heta = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu > 0\), Branch I). Therefore, \(O_\Omega\) is modeled as a homothetic (self-similar) state: as \( au o \infty\), the expansion scalar approaches a positive constant (\( heta o n H_0 > 0\)) while internal shear decays to zero (\(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} o 0\)). The physical volume grows without bound (\(V_{\mathcal{M}}( au) \sim e^{n H_0 au} o \infty\); precisely, \(e^{-2H_0 au}g_{\mu u} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} G_{\infty,\mu u} \succ 0\) by \(O_5\) Eq. 4), sustaining positive boundary work (\(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} > 0\)), while the conformally rescaled metric \( ilde{g}_{\mu u} = \Omega^{-2}g_{\mu u} o \hat{g}_\infty\) becomes time-independent (\(\partial_ au ilde{g}_{\mu u} o 0\)).
  • Mixed-Index Limit: Because the lower-index metric components \(g_{\mu u}\) grow as \(e^{2H_0 au}\) (with \(e^{-2H_0 au}g_{\mu u} o G_{\infty,\mu u}\), so the Christoffel symbols stay bounded in \(C^1\)), asymptotic convergence in \(O_\Omega\) is written in mixed \((1,1)\) form (\( rac{1}{2}g^{\mu\alpha}\partial_ au g_{\alpha u} o H_0 \delta^\mu_ u\)), which is scale-invariant.

docs.title: Decision 2: Separating Extrinsic Expansion (\(\theta, K_{\mu\nu}\)) from Environmental Stiffness (\(\Pi_{\mu\nu}\)) (\(O_0, O_2, O_3\))
docs.text:
• Conceptual Intent: Navigating a rigid external environment (\(O_2\)) should guide trajectories without crushing internal growth (\(O_3\)).
  • Mathematical Implementation:
  • Synchronous Normal Gauge (\(N = 1, eta^\mu = 0\)): All volumetric growth is carried once by the normal extrinsic expansion scalar \( heta \equiv -N K = rac{1}{2}g^{\mu u}\partial_ au g_{\mu u} = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\) (\(> 0\) in Branch I; r6 wrote \( abla_\mu J_E^\mu\), and Decision 6 separates the currents), avoiding any double-counting between coordinate velocity and metric growth.
  • Unimodular Conformal-Weyl Factorization: The spatial metric is factored non-perturbatively as \(g_{\mu u} = \Omega^2 \hat{g}_{\mu\alpha}(\exp \hat{h})^\alpha_{\; u}\) with \(\det \hat{g} = 1\) and \(\mathrm{Tr}(\hat{h}) = 0\). Because \(\det(\exp \hat{h}) = 1\) at all finite shear amplitudes, the volume element \(\sqrt{\vert g\vert} = \Omega^n\) depends only on the conformal factor \(\Omega\) (a scalar density of weight \(1/n\) in the fixed reference chart), isolating the volume element from anisotropic shear (\(\hat{h}\)). The factorization is a change of variables, so it does not decouple \( heta\) from environmental stiffness: since \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha \xi^\alpha\) with \(\xi_\alpha = \hat{\Pi}_{\alpha\lambda}\eta^\lambda\), the trace of the \( au\)-compatibility law gives the elliptic equation \( rac{2(n-1)}{n} abla^2 heta + rac{2R}{n} heta = -\kappa_G\,\partial_ au( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha) + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\), which ties expansion to precision.

docs.title: Decision 3: Local Subsystem Metrics (\(g^{(i)}\)) vs. the Glued Macroscopic Metric (\(g \equiv g^{\mathrm{macro}}\)) (\(O_3 \to O_5\))
docs.text:
• Conceptual Intent: Individual subsystems (\(O_4\)) bring distinct internal geometries (\(g^{(i)}\)) into shared overlap zones (\(O_5\)), blending them into a coherent macroscopic whole (\(O_7\)).
  • Mathematical Implementation:
  • Fixed Open Cover (\(\mathcal{M} = igcup_i \mathcal{U}_i\)): The coordinate domains \(\mathcal{U}_i\) and their intersections \(\mathcal{U}_{ij} = \mathcal{U}_i \cap \mathcal{U}_j\) are fixed in coordinate space, while their physical Riemannian volumes (\(\int \sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert}\,d^n x\)) dilate over time. This allows the Reynolds transport theorem in \(O_4\) to hold cleanly without moving-coordinate-boundary terms.
  • Riemannian Geometric Mean (\(g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)}\)): On each overlap \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\), the two subsystem metrics are interpolated via their positive-definite geometric mean \(g_{\mu u}^{(ij)} = (g^{(i)} \# g^{(j)})_{\mu u}\) and glued over all geometric overlaps \(\mathcal{K}_0 = \{\langle i,j angle : \mathcal{U}_i \cap \mathcal{U}_j eq \emptyset\}\) via a smooth, time-independent partition of unity (\(\psi_i, \psi_{ij} \ge 0\)) into the single global metric \(g_{\mu u} \equiv g_{\mu u}^{\mathrm{macro}}\). Percolation is measured separately on the actively coupled subgraph \(\mathcal{K} = \{\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}_0 : \eta_{[i o j]} ot\equiv 0\}\) through the fraction \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}(\mathcal{K}) = \vert\mathcal{K}\vert/\vert\mathcal{K}_0\vert > \phi_c\).
  • Avoiding Overdetermination: The exact differential evolution laws (\(O_2\)–\(O_4\)) are imposed on the glued global metric \(g_{\mu u}\), while individual subsystem metrics \(g_{\mu u}^{(i)}\) carry, as standing hypotheses, the asymptotic homothety conditions with a common expansion rate \(H_0\) (\(e^{-2H_0 au}g^{(i)}_{\mu u} o G^{(i)}_{\infty,\mu u} \succ 0\) and \( rac{1}{2}(g^{(i)})^{\mu\alpha}\partial_ au g^{(i)}_{\alpha u} o H_0\delta^\mu_ u\), both in \(C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)\)). The glued metric inherits them, \(e^{-2H_0 au}g_{\mu u} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} G_{\infty,\mu u} \succ 0\) (\(O_5\) Eq. 4); \(O_6\) uses this for the volume shares \(c_{ij} \in (0,1]\) and \(O_\Omega\) uses it to bound the Christoffel symbols. The tilde is reserved for the unit-determinant rescaling \( ilde{g}_{\mu u} = \Omega^{-2}g_{\mu u} o \hat{g}_{\infty,\mu u}\); the \(e^{-2H_0 au}\)-rescaled limits are written \(G_\infty\).

docs.title: Decision 4: Pairwise Joint Density (\(Q_{ij}\)), Overlap Divergence (\(Q_i^{\vert ij}\)), and Asymmetric Lead-Follow Coupling (\(\eta_{[i\to j]}\)) (\(O_6\))
docs.text:
• Conceptual Intent: Coupled partners should sustain positive mutual information flow (\( rac{d}{d au}\mathcal{I} > 0\)) through an asymmetric coupling (\(\eta_{[i o j]} ot\equiv 0\)), even as their local states align (\(D_{\mathrm{KL}} o 0\)). Only the magnitude of the asymmetry enters the dynamics; the equations cannot tell which partner leads.
  • Mathematical Implementation:
  • Joint vs. Overlap-Conditional Distributions: Each pair of coupled subsystems carries a joint distribution \(Q_{ij}\) on \(\mathcal{U}_i imes \mathcal{U}_j\) with marginals \(Q_i\) and \(Q_j\), defining mutual information \(\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j) = D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_{ij} \parallel Q_i \otimes Q_j)\). Meanwhile, distributional alignment is measured on their shared overlap \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) via normalized conditional densities \(Q_i^{\vert ij}\), allowing \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_i^{\vert ij} \parallel Q_j^{\vert ij}) o 0\) while \(\mathcal{I}(Q_i; Q_j)\) continues to grow.
  • Quadratic Asymmetric Coupling in \(M_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\): To ensure the antisymmetric phase-lead \(\eta_{[i o j]}^\lambda = rac{1}{2}(\eta_{i o j}^\lambda - \eta_{j o i}^\lambda)\) drives the stretching-and-folding operator \(M_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\) even when two partners have identical precision stiffness (\(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)} = \hat{\Pi}^{(j)}\)), \(M_{\mu u}^{(ij)}\) includes a trace-free quadratic term in the precision-symmetrized phase-lead 1-form \(J_{[i o j]} = -J_{[j o i]}\). This 1-form is odd under \(i \leftrightarrow j\) (its sign records the leader), but it enters \(M^{(ij)}\) only through its even outer product, so \(M^{(ij)}\), \(S^{(ij)}\), and \(d\mathcal{I}/d au\) are leader-follower symmetric. It generally differs from \( rac{1}{2}(J_{i o j} - J_{j o i})\), with equality when \(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)} = \hat{\Pi}^{(j)}\). Because the quadratic term can still cancel against the conformal-Killing term, \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0 \; orall \mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\) and \(d\mathcal{I}/d au > 0\) are stated as explicit hypotheses. Since \(\mathrm{Tr}\,M^{(ij)} = 0\), the mixed eigenvalues have both signs and sum to zero (\(m_+ > 0 > m_-\)); they need not be equal in magnitude.

docs.title: Decision 5: Smooth Anisotropy Index (\(\chi\)) and Type-\((1,1)\) Density Endomorphisms (\(\hat{\rho}_g, \hat{\rho}_{\mathcal{H}}\)) (\(O_7\))
docs.text:
• Conceptual Intent: The macroscopic network relaxes its deformation toward isotropy (\(\chi o 1\)), tracked covariantly by a gauge field, and aligns its active geometry (\(g_{\mu u}\)) with its accumulated structural memory (\(\mathcal{H}\)). (Local stretching and folding belong to the relational edge, \(M^{(ij)}\) in \(O_6\); \(\chi\) measures the anisotropy of the global deformation \(\mathcal{D}\).)
  • Mathematical Implementation:
  • \(C^2\), Kink-Free Anisotropy Scalar: Instead of a ratio of maximum-to-minimum eigenvalues (which creates non-differentiable kinks where eigenvalues cross), anisotropy is measured by the kink-free invariant \(\chi \equiv rac{n\,\mathrm{Tr}(\mathcal{D}^2)}{(\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathcal{D})^2} = 1 + rac{n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}}{ heta^2} \ge 1\), which is \(C^2\) (it inherits the regularity of \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} \in C^2\)) and converges to \(1\) as shear decays (Branch I, where \( heta o nH_0 > 0\); in Branch II the index is \(\chi_E\), Decision 6).
  • Type-\((1,1)\) Endomorphisms for Relative Entropy: Because matrix logarithms and traces are only coordinate-invariant for \((1,1)\) mixed tensors, \(g_{\alpha u}\) and \( abla_\alpha abla_ u \mathcal{H}\) have their first index raised by the asymptotic inverse reference metric \(\hat{g}_\infty^{\mu\alpha}\) (the density weights cancel in the normalized ratio) to form unit-trace density operators \((\hat{ ho}_g)^\mu_{\; u}\) and \((\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}})^\mu_{\; u}\).

docs.title: Decision 6: Throughput Separated from Expansion; Declared Drive, Transport, and Sink; Two Asymptotic Branches (r7, r10)
docs.text:
Motivation. In r6, one current \(J_E^\mu\) both expands the metric volume (\( heta = abla_\mu J_E^\mu > 0\)) and carries the free-energy throughput (\(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} < 0\)), the free-energy balance law has isotropic constant diffusivity and no interior sink, test trajectories are force-free, and the asymptote requires unbounded homothetic expansion (\(H_0 > 0\)). These are the laws of a homogeneous, sink-free, perpetually inflating medium. Bounded open systems with interior consumption, anisotropic transport, or driven trajectories cannot satisfy them literally. r7 generalizes exactly these points and nothing else.

What changes (r7). Eighteen equation blocks are edited; all other blocks are unchanged. 1. Expansion versus throughput (\(O_0\) Eq. [1], [3], [4]; \(O_1\) Eq. [0], [1]; \(O_2\) Eq. [2]; \(O_3\) Eq. [1]; \(O_4\) Eq. [3]; \(O_6\) Eq. [4]; \(O_7\) Eq. [3]). Every r6 identity of the form \( heta = abla_\mu J_E^\mu\) now reads \( heta = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\), including \(\partial_ au\ln\Omega = heta/n\) (\(O_2\) Eq. [2]) and the \(u_{\mathrm{exp}}\) flux identity (\(O_7\) Eq. [3]); statements of \( heta > 0\) carry the qualifier "\(> 0\) in Branch I". Three currents are distinguished: * \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\), the expansion current: \( heta = abla_\mu J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu \ge 0\) and \(dV_{\mathcal{M}}/d au = \oint J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\,d\Sigma_\mu\). * \(J_W^\alpha = -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), the free-energy transport current of \(O_4\). * \(J_E^\mu\), the throughput current entering \(O_0\) Eq. [2] (hysteresis) and \(O_1\): in Branch I, \(J_E^\mu \equiv J_{\mathrm{geom}}^\mu\) (the r6 identification); in Branch II, \(J_E^\mu \equiv J_W^\mu/p_0\) is fixed (no alternative is admitted, so a declared throughput current cannot be used to satisfy \(O_0\) Eq. [2], \(O_1\), or the \(O_\Omega\) generator condition by construction), for which \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} = -p_0^{-1} abla\mathcal{F}\cdot\mathfrak{K}\cdot abla\mathcal{F} < 0\) holds identically wherever \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\).

Non-equilibrium openness is carried in both branches by \(\Theta_E \equiv \dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}/s_0\) (a rate, since \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}\) is an entropy production density and \(s_0\) an entropy density). \(O_0\) Eq. [1] only defines \(\Theta_E\), \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}}\), and \( au_\Theta\); their positivity and monotonicity are stated in \(O_0\) only as consequences of the \(O_1\) Eq. [1] sign condition, so under the defaults \(O_0\) imposes nothing beyond r6's \(O_0\). Events are ordered by \( au_\Theta( au) = \int_{ au_0}^ au\langle\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au'\) with \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} = \sqrt{ heta^2 + \Theta_E^2} > 0\). \( au_\Theta\) is dimensionless (when \( heta = 0\), it is the count of entropy production per \(s_0\)); \( au\) remains the proper time of normal observers, and \( au_\Theta\) is a strictly monotone reparametrization of it. In Branch I both \( heta\) and \(\Theta_E\) drive \( au_\Theta\) (r6 stated no such clock), and in Branch II \(\Theta_E\) alone does. Power splits into expansion work \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = p_0\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} \ge 0\) (unchanged symbol and formula, \(> 0\) in Branch I) and dissipative power \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} = \int(-J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F})\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^nx > 0\), with \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} > 0\). Keeping \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}}\) as pure expansion work, rather than redefining it as the sum, is what keeps r6's \(O_1\) Eq. [0] intact as the Branch I case. 2. Declared drive (\(O_2\) Eq. [3]; \(a_{\mathrm{d}}\) jointly continuous and locally Lipschitz in \((\mathbf{x}, v)\) locally uniformly in \( au\), with \(\Gamma\) and \(g^{-1}\partial_ au g\) locally Lipschitz in \(\mathbf{x}\) locally uniformly in \( au\), e.g. \(\partial_{\mathbf{x}}\Gamma\) and \(\partial_{\mathbf{x}}\partial_ au g\) jointly continuous, so the whole right side is locally Lipschitz and solutions are unique; joint continuity alone gives existence, not uniqueness). The trajectory equation carries \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2) ig(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - (a_{\mathrm{d}}\cdot v)v^\mu ig)\) on its right side, with \(u^2 = g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u\) and a declared drive acceleration \(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}}\) (zero by default). This projected form is required: an unrestricted drive can push trajectories through \(u^2 = 1\), since along solutions \(du^2/d au = -(1-u^2)\,\partial_ au g_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + 2\,g_{\mu u}v^\mu f^ u\). With the projected form, \(g_{\mu u}v^\mu f^ u = (1-u^2)^2(a_{\mathrm{d}}\cdot v)\), so \(du^2/d au\) carries a factor \((1-u^2)\), \(u^2 = 1\) is invariant, and the timelike condition \(u^2 < 1\) is preserved. 3. Declared transport and sink (\(O_4\) Eq. [1]). \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} + \mathcal{F} heta = - abla_\alpha J_W^\alpha - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\) with \(J_W^\alpha = -\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\), \(\mathfrak{K} \succ 0\) symmetric, and \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\). The defaults \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = D_{\mathcal{F}}g^{\alpha eta}\) and \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = 0\) recover r6. 4. Anisotropy index (\(O_7\) Eq. [5]). \(\chi = n\,\mathrm{Tr}(\mathcal{D}^2)/(\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathcal{D})^2\) is unchanged and remains the Branch I index; its identity with \(1 + n\sigma\sigma/ heta^2\) follows from \(\mathcal{D} = rac{ heta}{n}\delta + \sigma\) and must not be altered. A separate index \(\chi_E \equiv 1 + n\,\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu}/( heta^2 + \langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}}^2)\) is defined in both branches; it is not \(n\,\mathrm{Tr}(\mathcal{D}^2)/(\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathcal{D})^2\), satisfies \(1 \le \chi_E \le \chi\) wherever \( heta > 0\), and tends to \(1\) whenever \(\sigma o 0\) and \(\liminf\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} > 0\). In Branch II the adjoint section is \(\hat{\chi} = \chi_E\hat{u}\). 5. Two asymptotic branches (\(O_5\) Eq. [0] and [4]; \(O_\Omega\) Eq. [0]–[2]). * Branch I (\(H_0 > 0\)) is the r6 homothetic horizon, unchanged. * Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\)) is a bounded non-equilibrium steady state: \( heta o 0\) with \(\int_{ au_0}^\infty\langle heta angle\,d au < \infty\), so \(V_{\mathcal{M}} o V_\infty < \infty\) and \(\mathcal{I} o s_0V_\infty\) (finite capacity); \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\); \(\sigma o 0\); \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} o 0\). * The homothety hypotheses of \(O_5\) Eq. [4] and the derived limits of \(O_6\) Eq. [4] and \(O_\Omega\) Eq. [1] hold for \(H_0 \ge 0\). At \(H_0 = 0\): \(g^{(i)} o G^{(i)}_\infty\) in \(C^2\) and \( rac{1}{2}(g^{(i)})^{-1}\partial_ au g^{(i)} o 0\) are the hypotheses; smoothness and homogeneity of \(\#\) carry both to the glued metric; the volume shares converge, giving \(c_{ij}\); and \(C^2\) convergence of \(g\) bounds the Christoffel symbols and curvature, giving the \(O_\Omega\) Eq. [1] limits. The Branch II premise \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au < \infty\) is implied by \(g o G_\infty\) and is retained for explicitness. * In Branch II, \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty < \infty\) while \(d\mathcal{I}/d au > 0\) (hypothesis), so the \(O_6\) coupling-tensor boundary flux must be integrable on \([ au_0, \infty)\). The \(O_6\) Eq. [3] hypothesis \(M^{(ij)} eq 0\) at every finite \( au\) remains compatible with this, since the flux need only be integrable; it tends to \(0\) under the additional hypothesis that it is uniformly continuous in \( au\) (Barbalat's lemma). r7 states this in the \(O_6\) and \(O_\Omega\) branch-scope fields. * The \(O_\Omega\) generator equivalence divides by \(nH_0\) and therefore holds in Branch I only, where (as in r6 and §5.10) it holds at every \( au\). In Branch II the first term of \(\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}\) vanishes at every \( au\), so imposing \(\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}\Psi = 0\) at every \( au\) would forbid all surprisal transduction. r7 therefore states the Branch II condition asymptotically: with \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) bounded and bounded away from \(0\), uniformly as \( au o \infty\) (the lower bound gives the forward implication, the upper bound the reverse), \(\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}\Psi\vert_{\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}} o 0 \iff J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q o 0 \iff \partial_ au\mathcal{H} o 0\) as \( au o \infty\). The Branch II fixed point is asymptotically stationary hysteresis, and surprisal transduction at finite \( au\) is permitted. * Statements that hold in Branch I only: \(O_5\) Eq. [0]'s strict growth \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} > 0\) (now \(\ge 0\), with \(> 0\) in Branch I), \(O_0\) Eq. [4] (\(V_{\mathrm{field}} = \infty\)), the \(O_1\) "integrates" edge (unbounded boundary flux), the \(\chi o 1\) implication of \(O_7\) Eq. [5] (whose premise is \( heta o nH_0 > 0\)), the deformation-spectrum hypothesis \(\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal{D}) > 0\) of \(O_6\) Eq. [4] (a standing hypothesis in Branch I, as in r6; not asserted in Branch II, where \(\mathcal{D} o 0\)), the definition of \(\chi\) itself (undefined where \( heta = 0\)), and the \(nH_0\) form of the \(O_\Omega\) generator equivalence. Each coordinate of r7 carries an r7_branch_scope field stating this. Several relational edges were updated to state r7 formulas or carry branch labels; all other retained r6 prose and edges, including r6 clauses retained alongside r7 formulas within an edge, describe Branch I with the default constitutive terms, as each r7_branch_scope field states.

Constitutive closure (Amendment A; binding text in r7 \(O_4\), field r7_constitutive_closure). The new terms make the spine more general, so they must not make it unfalsifiable. Any departure from the defaults (\(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} = D_{\mathcal{F}}g^{\alpha eta}\), \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = 0\); the Branch II \(J_E^\mu = J_W^\mu/p_0\) is fixed and admits no departure) must satisfy four conditions: (i) its functional form is a named constitutive law fixed before the test (for example a potential gradient or drag law for \(f_{\mathrm{drive}}\), a measured conductivity or permeability tensor for \(\mathfrak{K}\), first- or zeroth-order kinetics for \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\)); (ii) it has a finite number of parameters declared in advance (tabulated or non-parametric fields are not admissible), estimated from data independent of the test and not merely disjoint in time: a different measurement modality from the one used to test the coordinate, or a declared perturbation or non-stationary regime distinct from the test window (temporal disjointness alone is not independence in a stationary Branch II state, where a later window re-measures an earlier one); (iii) every acceptance tolerance and comparison criterion is fixed before the test; (iv) the default model is fitted to the same test-window data and its residual reported alongside, and if the default fits at least as well under the pre-declared criterion, the departure is rejected and the coordinate is evaluated under the default. The test-window fit of the default is used only for the comparison of (iv): whenever a coordinate is evaluated under the default, its parameters are estimated per (ii), from data independent of the test. A term fitted to the data it closes does not count as satisfying any coordinate in which the term appears. In Branch II, with the fixed \(J_E^\mu\), the \(O_1\) sign condition holds identically; the empirical content of \(O_1\) is then that the declared parametric \(\mathfrak{K}\), with parameters estimated per (ii), predicts the flux: the independently measured free-energy flux \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}}\) (measured directly, within the test window, across a declared surface, by a method that does not use the declared \(\mathfrak{K}\)) agrees with \(-\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} abla_ eta\mathcal{F}\) within the pre-declared tolerance. The gradient \( abla\mathcal{F}\) in this comparison must be obtained within the test window by a method that uses neither \(J_W^{\mathrm{meas}}\) nor the declared \(\mathfrak{K}\) or \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\); otherwise the agreement is automatic. The compared quantity is pre-declared: the total flux through the declared surface \(S\), or the normal flux density pointwise on \(S\). Every evaluation, under the defaults or a declared departure, also requires condition (v): the branch is declared before the test, with a pre-declared estimator and acceptance criterion for the asymptotic regime (an estimate of \(H_0 > 0\) for Branch I; the trend of \(\langle heta angle\), a bound on \(\int\langle heta angle\,d au\), and an estimate of \(\lim\langle\Theta_E angle > 0\) for Branch II), supported by evidence independent of the \(O_1\) test, and a configuration declared in one branch may not be re-evaluated in the other on the same data. Clause (v) matters because the branch switches \(J_E\), and with it the content of \(O_1\) (a sign test in Branch I, a flux-prediction test in Branch II) and the anisotropy index of \(O_7\).

Scope of verification. §5.1–§5.12 verify the Branch I default and are unchanged except for the normalization correction noted in the header. §5.13 constructs and verifies one Branch II witness. Nothing in r10 claims that the generalized system is jointly satisfiable beyond what those sections verify.

docs.title: 3. Standing Hypotheses (r3, extended in r4–r6)
docs.text:
Regularity: \(g_{\mu u}, g^{(i)}_{\mu u} \in C^3\), \(\partial_ au g_{\mu u} \in C^2\), \(\Phi, \Phi^{(j)} \in C^4\), \(\eta, \eta_{i o j} \in C^2\), \(\psi \in C^\infty\), \(\hat{u} \in C^2\), \(A_\mu \in C^1\); Lipschitz boundaries \(\partial\mathcal{U}_i, \partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}\); outward unit normal \(\hat{n}_\mu\); \(\sup_ au \Vert J_E^\mu\Vert_{C^1} < \infty\) in coordinate components (compatible with divergent boundary flux, since \(\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\) grows like \(e^{nH_0 au}\) (Branch I)). Timelike test trajectories satisfy \(g_{\mu u}v^\mu v^ u < 1\).

Added in r4: * Topology and cover: \(\mathcal{M}\) connected; \(N_{\mathrm{nodes}} \ge 2\); overlap pairs \(\langle i,j angle\) have \(i eq j\) (so \(\mathcal{K}_0 eq \emptyset\) and \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}}\) is defined). * Regularity: \(\mathcal{F} \in C^2(\mathcal{M})\); \(\hat{g}_{\mu u} \in C^3(\mathcal{M})\), so that \(\hat{h} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} \hat{h}_\infty\) (\(O_3\) Eq. 3); \(\Phi^{(j)} \in C^4(\mathcal{M})\) and \(\eta^\lambda_{i o j} \in C^2(\mathcal{M})\) on all of \(\mathcal{M}\), so \(S^{(ij)}_{\mu u}\) is defined on \(\partial\mathcal{U}_{ij}\); \(\mathbf{J}^{\mathrm{harm}}_{\mathcal{M}} \in \Omega^1(\mathcal{M}) \cap C^2( ar{\mathcal{M}})\). * Operators: \( ho_{\mathrm{total}}( au)\) is a positive trace-class operator on \(L^2(\mathcal{M}, d\mathrm{vol}_g)\). * Asymptotics: For every \(i\), \(e^{-2H_0 au}g^{(i)}_{\mu u} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} G^{(i)}_{\infty,\mu u} \succ 0\) and \( rac{1}{2}(g^{(i)})^{\mu\alpha}\partial_ au g^{(i)}_{\alpha u} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{U}_i)} H_0\delta^\mu_ u\), with common \(H_0 > 0\) (Branch I; Decision 6 extends this to \(H_0 \ge 0\), with \(H_0 = 0\) in Branch II). Derived: \(e^{-2H_0 au}g_{\mu u} \xrightarrow{C^2(\mathcal{M})} G_{\infty,\mu u} \succ 0\). * Coupling: \(M^{(ij)}(\mathbf{x}) eq 0\) for all \(\mathbf{x} \in ar{\mathcal{U}}_{ij}\); \(\eta^\lambda_{[i o j]} ot\equiv 0\) on \(\mathcal{U}_{ij}\) for \(\langle i,j angle \in \mathcal{K}\). * Notation: The directed boundary element is \(d\Sigma_\mu \equiv \hat{n}_\mu\,dA\) (formerly \(dA_\mu\)), so that it is not confused with the gauge connection \(A_\mu\).

Clarified in r6: * Conformal factor: \(\Omega( au,\mathbf{x}) > 0\) is stated explicitly (\(O_2\)). * Harmonic current: \(\mathbf{J}^{\mathrm{harm}}_{\mathcal{M}}( au)\) is defined slice-wise on \(\Sigma_ au\) with the Hodge operators of \(g_{\mu u}( au)\) (\(O_5\)). * Functional derivatives: \(\delta\Psi/\delta g_{\mu u}(\mathbf{x})\) and \(\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}(\mathbf{x})\) are taken with respect to the coordinate measure \(d^n x\), so both are weight-1 densities (\(O_\Omega\)). * Macroscopic free energy: \(\hat{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{macro}} = \sum_i \hat{\mathcal{F}}_i\) sums the single-node weights \(\psi_i\) only; the overlap weights \(\psi_{ij}\) carry no free-energy section (\(O_7\)).

Clarified in r5: * Subsystem densities: \(Q_i\) is an independent object on \(\mathcal{U}_i\) that need not coincide with the restriction of the global \(Q\); nothing forbids equality (the §5 model has \(\mathcal{U}_1 = \mathcal{M}\) and \(Q_1 = Q\)).

Added in r7/r10 (Decision 6): * Branches: every configuration is in Branch I (\(H_0 > 0\), the r6 hypotheses) or Branch II (\(H_0 = 0\), \(\int_{ au_0}^\infty\langle heta angle_{\mathcal{M}}\,d au < \infty\), \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} o \Theta_\infty > 0\)). The homothety hypotheses of \(O_5\) Eq. [4] are stated for common \(H_0 \ge 0\). * Throughput: \(\Theta_E = \dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}}/s_0 > 0\) everywhere on \(\mathcal{M}\) at every \( au\), in both branches. * Branch declaration: every evaluation declares its branch before the test (closure condition (v)). * Constitutive closure: \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}}\), \(\mathfrak{K}^{\alpha eta} \succ 0\), and \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} \ge 0\) take their defaults unless declared a priori from named constitutive laws with independently measured parameters.
