docs.title: 5. Joint Satisfiability: Explicit Two-Subsystem Model on a Flat Annular Domain
docs.text: This section exhibits one configuration with \(n = 3\) and \(N_{\mathrm{nodes}} = 2\) that satisfies every equation and hypothesis of foundational-manifold-2026-10-20-r6.json simultaneously, so the hypothesis set is not contradictory. Everything is written in the fixed chart \(\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3\), with \(\varrho = \sqrt{(x^1)^2 + (x^2)^2}\), azimuth \(\varphi\), and \(\vert\mathbf{x}\vert\) the Euclidean norm.

docs.title: 5.1 Domain and cover
docs.text:
• Domain. \(\mathcal{M}\) is the hollow cylinder \(\{R_1 \le \varrho \le R_2, \; 0 \le x^3 \le L\}\) (\(0 < R_1 < R_2\)), with its four circular rim edges rounded axisymmetrically so that \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) is smooth, as \(O_0\) requires; the unrounded cylinder has corners.
  • Topology. \(\mathcal{M}\) is compact and connected with \(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(\mathcal{M}) \cong \mathbb{R}\). It avoids the \(x^3\)-axis, so \(\vert\mathbf{x}\vert \ge R_1 > 0\) and \(\varphi\) is smooth on \(\bar{\mathcal{M}}\).
  • Cover. \(\mathcal{U}_1 = \mathcal{M}\). \(\mathcal{U}_2 = E\) is an open oblate ellipsoid with semi-axes \(b_1 < b_2 = b_3\), its short axis along \(x^1\), contained in the interior of \(\mathcal{M}\) (for example centred at \(((R_1+R_2)/2, 0, L/2)\) with \(b_1, b_2\) small). Then \(\mathcal{U}_{12} = E\) is geodesically convex with smooth boundary.
  • Graph. \(\mathcal{K}_0 = \mathcal{K} = \{\langle 1,2 \rangle\}\), so \(\phi_{\mathrm{perc}} = 1 > \phi_c\).
  • Partition of unity. \(\psi_{12} \in C^\infty_c(E)\) with \(0 \le \psi_{12} \le 1\), \(\psi_2 = 0\), and \(\psi_1 = 1 - \psi_{12}\).

docs.title: 5.2 Metric and kinematics
docs.text:
• Metrics. \(g^{(1)}_{\mu u} = g^{(2)}_{\mu u} = e^{2H_0 au}\delta_{\mu u}\). Hence \(g^{(12)} = g^{(1)} \# g^{(2)} = g^{(1)}\), and the glued metric is \(g_{\mu u} = e^{2H_0 au}\delta_{\mu u}\).
  • Weyl split. \(\Omega = e^{H_0 au}\), \(\hat{g} = \delta\), \(\hat{h} = \hat{h}_\infty = 0\), \(\hat{g}_\infty = ilde{g} = \delta\), and \(G^{(i)}_\infty = G_\infty = \delta\).
  • Expansion and shear. \( heta = 3H_0\) and \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = 0\), so the shear law holds for any \(\gamma_\sigma > 0\). \(\mathcal{D}^\mu_{\; u} = H_0\delta^\mu_ u\), so \(\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal{D}) = H_0 > 0\).
  • Curvature. \(\Gamma^\lambda_{\mu u} = 0\) and the Riemann tensor vanishes.
  • Asymptotics. \(O_5\) Eq. 4 and \(O_\Omega\) Eq. 1 hold exactly, not just in the limit.

docs.title: 5.3 Flux, free energy, potential, stress
docs.text:
• Exogenous flux. \(J_E^\mu = H_0 x^\mu\). Then \( abla_\mu J_E^\mu = 3H_0 = heta\), \(\sup_ au \Vert J_E\Vert_{C^1} < \infty\), and \(\oint_{\partial\mathcal{M}} J_E^\mu \, d\Sigma_\mu = 3H_0 V_{\mathcal{M}} o \infty\).
  • Free energy. \(\mathcal{F} = c_{\mathcal{F}}\,e^{-3H_0 au}/\vert\mathbf{x}\vert\) with \(c_{\mathcal{F}} > 0\), which is \(C^2\) on \(\mathcal{M}\).
  • Balance law: \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} + heta\mathcal{F} = 0 = D_{\mathcal{F}} abla^2\mathcal{F}\), since \(\Delta\vert\mathbf{x}\vert^{-1} = 0\) away from the origin.
  • Gradient condition: \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} = -H_0 c_{\mathcal{F}}\,e^{-3H_0 au}/\vert\mathbf{x}\vert < 0\), so \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\) and \(\dot{s}_{\mathrm{prod}} > 0\).
  • Global potential and stress. \(\Phi = rac{c_\Phi}{2}\vert\mathbf{x}\vert^2\) gives \(\Pi_{\mu u} = c_\Phi\delta_{\mu u}\), so \(\hat{\Pi}_{\mu u} = 0\) and \(\xi_ u = 0\) for any \(C^2\) field \(\eta^\lambda\) (take \(\eta^\lambda = 0\)). Then:
  • \(T^{\mathrm{mat}}_{\mu u} = 0 = G_{\mu u}\), \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha = 0\), and \( abla^\mu T_{\mu u} = 0\).
  • The \( au\)-compatibility law and its elliptic trace hold with both sides zero.

docs.title: 5.4 Global information and the asymptotic generator
docs.text:
• Generative density. \( ho_{\mathrm{total}}( au) = \vert\phi_0 angle\langle\phi_0\vert\), where \(\phi_0 = \mathrm{Vol}_g(\mathcal{M})^{-1/2}\) is the constant Neumann mode. Its eigenvalue is 0, so it passes any gate \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}} \ge 0\). This gives \(Q = e^{-3H_0 au}/\mathrm{Vol}_\delta(\mathcal{M}) > 0\), normalized, with \(q\) spatially constant, so \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu q = 0\).
  • Reference prior. \(P = Q\,(1 + \epsilon( au)u)\), with \(\int_{\mathcal{M}} u\,Q\sqrt{\vert g\vert} \, d^3x = 0\) (here \(Q\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\) is spatially constant, so this is \(\int_{\mathcal{M}} u \, d^3x = 0\); every later reuse of this prior, in §5.10, §5.11 and §5.13, uses the weighted condition, which is what normalization \(\int P\sqrt{\vert g\vert} = 1\) requires; where \(Q\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\) varies in \( au\) the condition must hold at every \( au\). In §5.10 (flat, homothetic), \(Q\sqrt{\vert g\vert} = (1-\varepsilon_q)/ ar{V} + \varepsilon_q ar{\phi}_1^2\) with a fixed \( ar{\phi}_1\), so a \( au\)-independent \(u\) needs the two moment conditions \(\int u = 0\) and \(\int u\, ar{\phi}_1^2 = 0\). In §5.11, \(\sqrt{\vert g\vert} = e^{3H_0 au}z^{\sqrt{2}}\) and the shear changes the shape of the first Neumann mode, so the conditions are \(\int u\,z^{\sqrt{2}}\,d^3x = 0\) and \(\int u\, ar{\phi}_1( au)^2z^{\sqrt{2}}\,d^3x = 0\) for every \( au\); one construction satisfying all of them is an axisymmetric (\(m = 0\)) mode \(\phi_1\), which §5.11 permits, with \(u = b(\varrho, z)\cos\varphi\) and \(\vert b\vert < 1\), since the azimuthal integral of \(\cos\varphi\) vanishes against every axisymmetric weight), \(\vert u \vert < 1\), \(u ot\equiv 0\), and \(\epsilon( au) \in (0,1)\) decreasing to \(0\). Then \(Q \ll P\), \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\) (so \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} > 0\)), and \(V_Q/V_P o 1\).
  • Hysteresis. \(\mathcal{H} = rac{c_{\mathcal{H}}}{2}\vert\mathbf{x}\vert^2\) with \(c_{\mathcal{H}} > 0\).
  • \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = 0 = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\).
  • \( abla_\alpha abla_ eta\mathcal{H} = c_{\mathcal{H}}\delta_{\alpha eta} \succ 0\).
  • \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}} = \hat{ ho}_g = rac{1}{3}\delta^\mu_ u\), so \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) = 0\).
  • Generator (\(O_\Omega\)). \(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}(g,\mathbf{x}) = rac{c_{\mathcal{H}}}{2}\vert\mathbf{x}\vert^2\) is ultralocal with \(\partial\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}/\partial g_{\mu u} = 0\), which equals the right-hand side of \(O_\Omega\) Eq. 2 because \(J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q = 0\). Take \(\Psi[g,\mathcal{H}] = \int_{\mathcal{M}} \mathcal{H} \, d^3x\). Then \(\delta\Psi/\delta g = 0\), \(\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H} = 1 eq 0\), the locus condition holds, and \(\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}\Psi = 0\).

docs.title: 5.5 Relational edge
docs.text:
• Local potentials. \(\Phi^{(1)} = \Phi^{(2)} = rac{1}{2}\left((x^1)^2 - (x^2)^2 ight)\) on all of \(\mathcal{M}\). Then \(\hat{\Pi}^{(j)}_{\mu u} = \mathrm{diag}(1,-1,0)\), which is already \(g\)-trace-free.
  • Coupling fields. \(\eta^\lambda_{1 o 2} = -\eta^\lambda_{2 o 1} = a( au)\,\delta^\lambda_1\) with \(a( au) = a_0 e^{3H_0 au/2}\) and \(a_0 eq 0\). These are spatially constant, hence \(C^2\) on \(\mathcal{M}\).
  • Derived 1-forms. \(\eta_{[1 o 2]} = a\,\partial_1 ot\equiv 0\). \(J_{1 o 2} + J_{2 o 1} = 0\), so the first term of \(M^{(12)}\) vanishes. \(J_{[1 o 2]} = a\,dx^1\), and \(F^{(1 o 2)} = F^{(2 o 1)} = 0\).
  • Coupling tensor. \(S^{(12)}_{\mu u} = M^{(12)}_{\mu u} = \gamma_M a^2\left(\delta_{\mu 1}\delta_{ u 1} - rac{1}{3}\delta_{\mu u} ight)\).
  • It is trace-free and nonzero at every point of \( ar{E}\).
  • Its mixed eigenvalues are \(e^{-2H_0 au}\gamma_M a^2\,( frac{2}{3}, - frac{1}{3}, - frac{1}{3})\), so \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\) with \(m_+ eq -m_-\).
  • Boundary flux. With \(\hat{n}^\mu = e^{-H_0 au} u^\mu\) and \(dA = e^{2H_0 au}dA_\delta\):
  • \(\oint_{\partial E} S^{(12)}_{\mu u}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u \, dA = \gamma_M a( au)^2\,C_E\), where \(C_E \equiv \oint_{\partial E}( u_1^2 - frac{1}{3}) \, dA_\delta\).
  • \(C_E = 0\) when \(E\) is a ball, because a constant trace-free tensor has zero flux through a sphere. That would force \(d\mathcal{I}/d au = 0\), which is why \(\mathcal{U}_{12}\) must not be a ball.
  • For an oblate \(E\) with short axis along \(x^1\), \(C_E > 0\); numerically, \(C_E \approx 3.64\) for semi-axes \((0.2, 1, 1)\).
  • Subsystem densities. \(Q_1 = 1/\mathrm{Vol}_g(\mathcal{M})\) and \(Q_2 = 1/\mathrm{Vol}_g(E)\) (uniform). Then \(Q_1^{\vert 12} = Q_2^{\vert 12}\) (uniform on \(E\)), so \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_1^{\vert 12} \parallel Q_2^{\vert 12}) = 0\) for all \( au\).
  • Required mutual information. \(\mathcal{I}( au) = k_{\mathcal{I}}\gamma_M a_0^2 C_E\,(e^{3H_0 au} - e^{3H_0 au_0})/(3H_0)\), so \(d\mathcal{I}/d au = k_{\mathcal{I}}\gamma_M a_0^2 C_E\,e^{3H_0 au} > 0\).
  • Joint density (sketch). Partition \(\mathcal{M}\) and \(E\) into \(m\) cells each, of equal relative volume. Set \(Q_{12} = (1-w)\,Q_1 \otimes Q_2 + w\,m\,(Q_1 \otimes Q_2)\,\mathbf{1}_{ ext{matched cells}}\).
  • For every \(w \in [0,1]\) this has exact marginals \(Q_1, Q_2\) and satisfies \(Q_{12} \ll Q_1 \otimes Q_2\).
  • Its mutual information increases continuously from \(0\) to \(\ln m\) as \(w\) goes from 0 to 1.
  • Interpolating between nested refinements \(m o km\) in the same way extends the range to \([0, \infty)\), so a choice of \((m, w)\) as a function of \( au\) realizes the prescribed \(\mathcal{I}( au)\). The densities are piecewise constant, which the specification permits (no regularity is imposed on \(Q_{ij}\)).
  • Saturation and volume share. Setting \(s_0 = k_{\mathcal{I}}\gamma_M a_0^2 C_E / (3H_0\,\mathrm{Vol}_\delta(\mathcal{M}))\) gives \(\mathcal{I}/(s_0 V_{\mathcal{M}}) o 1\). Also \(V_{1\cup 2}/V_{\mathcal{M}} = 1 \in (0,1]\).

docs.title: 5.6 Harmonic current and gauge sector
docs.text:
• Harmonic current. \(\mathbf{J}^{\mathrm{harm}}_{\mathcal{M}} = c_{\mathrm{harm}}\,d\varphi\) with \(c_{\mathrm{harm}} \neq 0\).
  • It is smooth on \(\bar{\mathcal{M}}\) and closed.
  • \(d^\dagger\mathbf{J} = 0\) because \(\Delta\varphi = 0\); the conformal factor is spatially constant, so this holds for every \(\tau\).
  • On an axisymmetric boundary \(\hat{n}\) lies in the meridian plane, so \(\iota_n\mathbf{J} = 0\) and \(\iota_n d\mathbf{J} = 0\) (absolute boundary conditions).
  • It represents the generator of \(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(\mathcal{M})\).
  • Gauge sector. \(G_{\mathrm{gauge}} = SU(2)\) on the trivial bundle, with \(A_\mu = 0\), \(g_{\mathrm{YM}} = 1\), and constant unit \(\hat{u}, \hat{e}_i\).
  • \(\chi = 1\) (since \(\sigma = 0\)), so \(\hat{\chi} = \hat{u}\), \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu = 0\), and \([F^{\mathrm{YM}}_{\mu\nu}, \hat{\chi}] = 0\).
  • Take \(u_{\mathrm{exp}} = J_E\). Then \(\mathcal{L}_{\mathbf{J}_E}(\hat{h} - \hat{h}_\infty) = 0\) and \(\mathcal{A}_{\mathcal{M}} = 0\).

docs.title: 5.7 Differences from the transmitted model, and limits
docs.text:
• Rounded edges. Added so that \(\partial\mathcal{M}\) is smooth.
  • Hysteresis term dropped. The term \( rac{c_q}{3H_0}\ln\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\) is omitted from \(\mathcal{H}\) (i.e., \(c_q = 0\)).
  • With \(c_q eq 0\) the model would need \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu q = c_q\), which forces \(Q \propto \vert\mathbf{x}\vert^{-c_q/H_0}\) times a degree-0 angular factor.
  • \(O_4\) requires \(Q = \langle\mathbf{x}\vert ho_{\mathrm{local}}\vert\mathbf{x} angle\) with \( ho_{\mathrm{local}}\) in the range of a finite-rank Neumann low-pass projector. It has not been shown that such a \(Q\) has this form.
  • With \(c_q = 0\), the \(O_\Omega\) generator equivalence holds with both sides zero. It is therefore satisfied but only trivially exercised.
  • \(\hat{\Pi}^{(j)} eq 0\) does not by itself imply \(M^{(12)} eq 0\). Here \(M^{(12)} eq 0\) because \(J_{[1 o 2]} = \hat{\Pi}\,\eta_{[1 o 2]} eq 0\) at every point for the chosen \(\eta\).
  • The overlap is an oblate ellipsoid, not a ball. See the flux discussion in §5.5.
  • Orientation matters, not just non-sphericity. \(C_E\) changes sign with shape: a prolate ellipsoid with its long axis along \(x^1\) (semi-axes \((2,1,1)\)) gives \(C_E \approx -4.19 < 0\), which would violate \(d\mathcal{I}/d au > 0\). The overlap must be flattened along the direction of \(J_{[1 o 2]}\).
  • Data added to complete the model: \(\mathcal{F}\), \( ho_{\mathrm{total}}\), \(Q\), \(P\), the cover and partition of unity, \(\eta_{i o j}\) with growth rate \(a( au)\), \(Q_{12}\), \(s_0\), \(\Psi\), and the gauge data.
  • Scope. The model establishes consistency of the hypothesis set, not genericity. Constructing \(Q_{12}( au)\) smoothly in \( au\) is sketched, not written out.
  • Independent re-check (r5). Every equation and hypothesis of the r5 JSON was re-derived against this model. Numerical checks confirm \(C_E \approx 3.642\) for semi-axes \((0.2,1,1)\) and \(C_E \approx 0\) for a sphere. For the block coupling, the marginals are exact, and the mutual information increases monotonically from \(0\) to \(\ln m\). Under nested refinement it covers \([\ln m, \ln km]\): coarse-graining to the level-\(m\) cells gives exactly \(\ln m\), so data processing bounds it below. The model is deliberately degenerate in places: \(\hat{\Pi} = 0\) globally (so \(T^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\) and \(\kappa_G\) is unexercised), \(\sigma \equiv 0\), \(A_\mu = 0\), \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu q = 0\), and \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_1^{\vert 12} \parallel Q_2^{\vert 12}) \equiv 0\). §5.8 switches most of those sectors on; two remain trivial, for reasons stated there.

docs.title: 5.8 Non-degenerate active-sector extension (r6)
docs.text:
This extension keeps the domain, cover, partition of unity, \(J_E^\mu = H_0 x^\mu\), \( ho_{\mathrm{total}}\), \(Q\), \(P\), and \(\Psi\) of §5.1–5.6, and replaces the rest as listed. It switches on shear, \(\chi > 1\), \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) > 0\), global \(\hat{\Pi}\), \(\eta\), \(\xi\), a non-flat gauge connection with \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_\mu ot\equiv 0\), and a non-zero overlap divergence. All of these decay to their asymptotic values. Every claim below was checked symbolically or numerically for r6.

Constants. \(H_0 > 0\); a shear amplitude \(s_\sigma\) with \(0 < s_\sigma < H_0/2\) (written \(s_0\) in the transmitted model; renamed because \(s_0\) is the information-saturation constant of \(O_\Omega\)); \(\gamma_\sigma > 0\). Write \(a( au) \equiv (2 s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma)(1 - e^{-\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)})\), which increases from \(0\) to \(a_\infty \equiv 2 s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma\).

Metric and shear. * Metric (axisymmetric Bianchi I). \(g^{(1)} = g^{(2)} = g = e^{2H_0 au}\,\mathrm{diag}(e^{a}, e^{a}, e^{-2a})\). Its Weyl split is \(\hat{g} = \delta\), \(\Omega = e^{H_0 au}\), \(\hat{h} = a( au)\,\mathrm{diag}(1,1,-2)\). * Asymptotic metrics. \(\hat{h}_\infty = a_\infty\,\mathrm{diag}(1,1,-2) eq 0\), and \(\hat{g}_\infty = G_\infty = G^{(i)}_\infty = \mathrm{diag}(e^{a_\infty}, e^{a_\infty}, e^{-2a_\infty})\), with \(\det = 1\). * Flat slices. The components are spatially constant, so \(\Gamma = 0\) and the Riemann tensor vanishes on every slice. Hence \(G_{\mu u} = 0\), \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma]_{\mu u} = 0\), and \( abla abla heta = 0\) for all \( au\), even though the shear is non-zero. * Shear. \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = frac{1}{2}\partial_ au\hat{h} = s_\sigma e^{-\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)}\,\mathrm{diag}(1,1,-2) ot\equiv 0\). * It obeys the \(O_3\) damping law exactly. * \( heta = 3H_0\). * \(\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal{D}) = H_0 - 2 s_\sigma e^{-\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)} \ge H_0 - 2s_\sigma > 0\). * \( frac{1}{2}g^{-1}\partial_ au g = H_0 I + \sigma o H_0 I\), as \(O_5\) Eq. 4 and \(O_\Omega\) Eq. 1 require. * Anisotropy. \(\chi( au) = 1 + 2 s_\sigma^2 e^{-2\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)}/H_0^2\), which is \(> 1\) for finite \( au\) and tends to \(1\).

Hysteresis and endomorphisms. * Hysteresis. \(\mathcal{H} = frac{c_{\mathcal{H}}}{2}\,\hat{g}_{\infty,\alpha eta}x^\alpha x^ eta\) (\(c_{\mathcal{H}} > 0\)), so \( abla abla\mathcal{H} = c_{\mathcal{H}}\hat{g}_\infty \succ 0\) and \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}} = frac{1}{3}\delta\). * Metric endomorphism. \(\hat{ ho}_g = \mathrm{diag}(e^{a-a_\infty}, e^{a-a_\infty}, e^{-2(a-a_\infty)})/\mathrm{Tr}(\cdot)\), which differs from \( frac{1}{3}\delta\) at every finite \( au\). * Relative entropy. Therefore \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) > 0\), and it tends to \(0\). * Consistency with \(O_0\). \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = 0 = J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\), since \(q\) is spatially constant.

Free energy (corrected). * The §5.3 choice fails here. \(c_{\mathcal{F}}e^{-3H_0 au}/\vert\mathbf{x}\vert\) is not harmonic for the anisotropic Laplacian \( abla^2 = e^{-2H_0 au}[e^{-a}(\partial_1^2 + \partial_2^2) + e^{2a}\partial_3^2]\). * So does the transmitted variant. \(\vert\mathbf{x}\vert^{-1}_{\hat{g}( au)}\) fails the balance law, because its \( au\)-dependence through \(a( au)\) adds \(\partial_ au\) terms (checked symbolically). * Replacement. Use \(\mathcal{F} = c_{\mathcal{F}}\,e^{-3H_0 au}\ln(\varrho_0/\varrho)\) (\(c_{\mathcal{F}} > 0\), \(\varrho_0 > 0\)). * \(\ln\varrho\) is planar-harmonic and independent of \(x^3\), so \( abla^2\mathcal{F} = 0\) for every \(a\). * The balance law \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} + heta\mathcal{F} = 0 = D_{\mathcal{F}} abla^2\mathcal{F}\) is therefore exact. * \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} = -c_{\mathcal{F}}H_0 e^{-3H_0 au} < 0\). * \(\mathcal{F}\) is \(C^2\) on \(\mathcal{M}\), which avoids the axis.

Global potential, control field, stress. * Potential. \(\Phi = frac{c_\Phi}{6}((x^1)^2 + (x^2)^2 - 2(x^3)^2)\) (\(c_\Phi eq 0\)) gives a diagonal \(\hat{\Pi} ot\equiv 0\) with in-plane entries \(\hat{\Pi}_{11} = \hat{\Pi}_{22} = \pi_\perp( au) \equiv frac{c_\Phi}{9}(1 + 2e^{3a( au)}) eq 0\). * This corrects the transmitted \( frac{2c_\Phi}{9}(1 + e^{3a})\), which gives \(4c_\Phi/9\) instead of the correct \(c_\Phi/3\) at \(a = 0\). * Control field. \(\eta = (\omega_0/\pi_\perp)(-x^2, x^1, 0)\) (\(\omega_0 eq 0\)). Then \(\xi = \omega_0(-x^2\,dx^1 + x^1\,dx^2) ot\equiv 0\), with \(d\xi = 2\omega_0\,dx^1 \wedge dx^2\). * Stress. \(\partial_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)} = 0\) and \( abla\cdot\xi = 0\), so \(T^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0 = G\) for any \(\kappa_G\). The elliptic vector condition holds because \( abla^2\xi = 0\) and the Ricci tensor vanishes. * Caveat. \(\xi^\mu\) is a rotational Killing field of \(g\) (the \(x^1x^2\) block is isotropic). This is the trivial case flagged in the r1 review. \(\hat{\Pi}\), \(\eta\), \(\xi\) are non-zero, but \(T^{\mathrm{mat}} \equiv 0\) and \(\kappa_G\) remains unexercised. On flat slices this cannot be avoided, because \(G = 0\) forces \(T^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\). Exercising \(\kappa_G\) requires a model with curved slices.

Relational edge. * Coupling operator. \(\Phi^{(j)} = frac{1}{2}((x^1)^2 - (x^2)^2)\) still has a \(g\)-trace-free Hessian, since \(g^{11} = g^{22}\). So \(J_{[1 o 2]} = a_\eta\,dx^1\) with \(a_\eta = a_0 e^{3H_0 au/2}\), and \(M^{(12)} = \gamma_M a_\eta^2(\delta_{\mu 1}\delta_{ u 1} - frac{1}{3}g^{11}g_{\mu u}) eq 0\) everywhere. * Flux under shear: a new constraint, not in the transmitted model. The shear stretches the overlap ellipsoid in \(g\)-geometry. The flux is \(\oint_{\partial E} S\,\hat{n}\hat{n}\,dA = \gamma_M a_\eta^2\,e^{-a}\,C_E(b_1 e^{a/2}, b_2 e^{a/2}, b_3 e^{-a})\). * For semi-axes \((0.2, 1, 1)\), \(e^{-a}C_E\) takes the values \(3.64,\ 1.47,\ 0.40,\ -0.10\) at \(a = 0,\ 0.5,\ 1.0,\ 1.5\). It changes sign at \(a^* \approx 1.365\). * Since \(a( au)\) increases to \(a_\infty\), \(d\mathcal{I}/d au > 0\) for all \( au\) requires \(a_\infty = 2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma < a^*\). For example, \(s_\sigma = 0.2H_0\) with \(\gamma_\sigma \ge H_0\) gives \(a_\infty \le 0.4\). * Saturation constant. It becomes \(s_0 = k_{\mathcal{I}}\gamma_M a_0^2\,e^{-a_\infty}C_E^\infty/(3H_0\,\mathrm{Vol}_\delta(\mathcal{M}))\), with \(C_E^\infty \equiv C_E(b_1 e^{a_\infty/2}, b_2 e^{a_\infty/2}, b_3 e^{-a_\infty})\). * Overlap divergence. \(Q_2 = \mathrm{Vol}_g(E)^{-1}(1 + \delta_2 e^{-\gamma_Q( au- au_0)}u_E)\) with \(u_E \in C^\infty_c(E)\), \(\int_E u_E\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^3x = 0\) (the normalization condition; on the flat model this is \(\int_E u_E\,d^3x = 0\)), \(u_E ot\equiv 0\), and \(\vert\delta_2 u_E\vert < 1\). Then \(Q_2^{\vert 12} = Q_2\), and \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q_1^{\vert 12} \parallel Q_2^{\vert 12}) > 0\) for finite \( au\), tending to \(0\). * Joint density (replaces the §5.5 block construction). * Map each \(Q_i\) to the uniform density on \((0,1)^3\) by its Rosenblatt transform. * Couple the three coordinate pairs by a Gaussian copula with common correlation \( ho( au)\). * This gives exact marginals, and \(\mathcal{I} = - frac{3}{2}\ln(1- ho^2)\), because mutual information is invariant under the bijections. Hence \( ho = \sqrt{1 - e^{-2\mathcal{I}/3}}\). * Smoothness fix. \( ho\) is not differentiable where \(\mathcal{I} = 0\), so start from \(\mathcal{I}( au_0) = \mathcal{I}_0 > 0\) rather than \(0\). The offset does not affect the asymptotic saturation. Then \( ho( au) \in (0,1)\) is smooth, and \(Q_{12}\) is \(C^\infty\) in \( au\).

Gauge sector. * Setup. \(SU(2)\) with \(\hat{T}_a = \sigma_a/2\), \(\hat{u} = \hat{T}_3\), so \(\hat{\chi} = \chi( au)\hat{T}_3\). The connection is \(A_1 = b_1 x^2\hat{T}_3\), \(A_2 = e^{-\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)}b_2 x^1\hat{T}_1\), \(A_3 = 0\) (\(b_1, b_2 eq 0\)). * Curvature. \(F^{\mathrm{YM}}_{12} = -b_1\hat{T}_3 + e^{-\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)}(b_2\hat{T}_1 + g_{\mathrm{YM}}b_1 b_2 x^1 x^2\hat{T}_2) ot\equiv 0\), tending to \(-b_1\hat{T}_3\). * Impedance gradient. \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_1 = 0\) and \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_2 = -g_{\mathrm{YM}}\chi\,e^{-\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)}b_2 x^1\hat{T}_2 ot\equiv 0\), which tends to \(0\) in \(C^1\). * Commutator. \([F^{\mathrm{YM}}_{12}, \hat{\chi}] = i\chi\,e^{-\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)}(g_{\mathrm{YM}}b_1 b_2 x^1 x^2\hat{T}_1 - b_2\hat{T}_2) ot\equiv 0\), tending to \(0\). * Checks. The identity \(-ig_{\mathrm{YM}}[F_{12}, \hat{\chi}] = D_1\hat{\mathcal{E}}_2 - D_2\hat{\mathcal{E}}_1\) was verified symbolically. \(A_\mu\) is \(C^1\) and uniformly bounded.

Harmonic current. \(c_{\mathrm{harm}}\,d\varphi\) remains harmonic, and the absolute boundary conditions still hold. * Because \(g^{11} = g^{22}\), the Laplacian on \(x^3\)-independent functions is proportional to the planar one. * The \(g\)-normal on the axisymmetric boundary stays in the meridian plane.

Still trivial in §5.8. * Stress sector. \(T^{\mathrm{mat}} \equiv 0\) and \(\kappa_G\) is unexercised; this needs curved slices. * Surprisal sector. \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu q = 0\), so \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = 0\), \(\mathcal{A}_{\mathcal{M}} = 0\), and the \(O_\Omega\) generator equivalence holds with both sides zero. * What it would take. Switching on the surprisal sector needs a non-constant \(Q\) from a finite-rank Neumann projection, with \(\mathcal{H}\) and \(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}\) rebuilt around it. §5.10 does this. §5.9 activates the stress sector, but only in a model that provably fails \(O_7\).

docs.title: 5.9 Curved slices: cigar \(\times\,\mathbb{R}\) activates \(\kappa_G\) but cannot satisfy \(O_7\) (r7)
docs.text:
Result. The transmitted cigar model, with one correction, satisfies every stress-sector requirement with \(T^{\mathrm{mat}} ot\equiv 0\). However, no hysteresis field on cigar \( imes\,\mathbb{R}\) meets \(O_7\), so this model does not establish joint satisfiability with the stress sector active. All claims below were checked symbolically (exact, sympy) except the obstruction, which is proved by hand.

Metric. \(g = e^{2H_0 au} ar{g}\), with \( ar{g} = w^{-1}((dx^1)^2 + (dx^2)^2) + (dx^3)^2\) and \(w \equiv 1 + k_0^2\varrho^2\). * Curvature (confirmed). \(R_{ab} = 2k_0^2 w^{-2}\delta_{ab}\), \(R = 4k_0^2 e^{-2H_0 au}/w > 0\), \(G_{ab} = 0\), \(G_{33} = -2k_0^2/w\). * Weyl split (confirmed). \(\Omega = e^{H_0 au}w^{-1/3}\), \(\hat{g} = \mathrm{diag}(w^{-1/3}, w^{-1/3}, w^{2/3})\), \(\hat{h} = 0\). * Precision (confirmed). \(\Phi = - frac{3}{4}(x^3)^2\) gives \(\hat{\Pi} = \mathrm{diag}( frac{1}{2w}, frac{1}{2w}, -1)\).

Correction: the control field was a factor of 2 too small. The cigar is a steady gradient soliton with \(R_{\mu u} = ar{ abla}_\mu ar{ abla}_ u \ln w\), not \( frac{1}{2} ar{ abla} ar{ abla}\ln w\). * As transmitted. \(\eta = frac{2k_0^2}{\kappa_G}(x^1, x^2, 0)\) gives \(\xi = frac{1}{2\kappa_G}d\ln w\) and \(\kappa_G abla_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)} = frac{1}{2}R_{\mu u}\), so \(G eq \kappa_G T^{\mathrm{mat}}\). * Corrected. \(\eta = frac{4k_0^2}{\kappa_G}(x^1, x^2, 0)\) gives \(\xi = frac{1}{\kappa_G}d\ln w\). Then, exactly: * \(R_{\mu u} = \kappa_G abla_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)}\) and \(G = \kappa_G T^{\mathrm{mat}}\), with \(T^{\mathrm{mat}} = \mathrm{diag}(0, 0, -2k_0^2/(\kappa_G w)) ot\equiv 0\); * the elliptic vector condition \( abla^2\xi + \mathrm{Ric}\cdot\xi = 0\); * the \( heta\)-equation, via \(-\kappa_G\partial_ au( abla\cdot\xi) = 2H_0 R\).

Other transmitted claims (confirmed). * Flux. \(J_E^a = H_0 x^a\,w\ln w/(k_0^2\varrho^2)\), \(J_E^3 = H_0 x^3\) gives \( abla\cdot J_E = 3H_0\). * Free energy. \(\ln(\varrho_0/\varrho)\) is harmonic for \(g\), so the balance law holds exactly. \(J_E\cdot abla\ln(\varrho_0/\varrho) = -H_0 w\ln w/(k_0^2\varrho^2) < 0\). * Harmonic current. \(c_{\mathrm{harm}}\,d\varphi\) remains harmonic with absolute boundary conditions (the planar block is conformally flat and axisymmetric).

Obstruction to \(O_7\) (proof). Here \(\hat{h} = 0\), so \(\hat{ ho}_g = frac{1}{3}\delta\) for all \( au\). Since \(\hat{g}_\infty = \hat{g}\) is pointwise proportional to \( ar{g}\), the condition \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) o 0\) forces the limiting hysteresis to satisfy \( ar{ abla} ar{ abla}\mathcal{H}_\infty = \lambda ar{g}\) with \(\lambda > 0\). * Step 1 (splitting). On the product, the mixed components give \(\partial_a\partial_3\mathcal{H}_\infty = 0\), so \(\mathcal{H}_\infty = A(x^1, x^2) + B(x^3)\). * Step 2 (\(\lambda\) is constant). \(B'' = \lambda\) and \(\mathrm{Hess}_{\mathrm{cig}}A = \lambda ar{g}_{\mathrm{cig}}\) make \(\lambda\) a function of \(x^3\) alone and of \((x^1, x^2)\) alone, hence constant. * Step 3 (contradiction). Take the divergence of \(\mathrm{Hess}_{\mathrm{cig}}A = \lambda ar{g}\). Since \(\Delta A = 2\lambda\) is constant, this gives \(K\, abla A = 0\). The Gaussian curvature \(K = 2k_0^2/w > 0\), so \( abla A = 0\), which contradicts \(\lambda > 0\).

The argument is local, so it applies on every subdomain and does not depend on how \(\mathcal{H}\) evolves in time. Gemini's note ("Tashiro") pointed at this; the conclusion is that the obstruction is real and cannot be removed by choosing \(\mathcal{H}\) differently.

Also not addressed for the cigar. The relational edge was not recomputed on the curved metric: * \(\hat{\Pi}^{(j)}\) for \(\Phi^{(j)} = frac{1}{2}((x^1)^2 - (x^2)^2)\) picks up Christoffel terms, which changes \(M^{(12)}\) and the flux sign analysis of §5.5 and §5.8. * Geodesic convexity of the coordinate ellipsoid \(E\) is no longer automatic (it holds for \(E\) small enough).

Candidate route (not verified). Use a rotationally symmetric steady gradient soliton: the Bryant soliton, \( ar{g} = dr^2 + w(r)^2 g_{S^2}\). * Why the hysteresis obstruction disappears. Any radial \(f\) with \(f' = w\) satisfies \( ar{ abla} ar{ abla}f = w' ar{g}\), which is \(\succ 0\) because \(w' > 0\). With \(\hat{h} = 0\), this gives \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}} = \hat{ ho}_g\) exactly. * Why the stress sector still works. \(\xi = \kappa_G^{-1} abla h\) from the soliton potential gives \(T^{\mathrm{mat}} ot\equiv 0\). * Remaining construction. Take \(\mathcal{M}\) to be a smooth solid torus away from the tip, so that \(H^1 eq 0\); the harmonic field then exists by Hodge–Morrey–Friedrichs. Choose \(\Phi\) radial with \(\Phi'' eq \Phi' w'/w\) so that \(\hat{\Pi}\) is invertible, and set \(\eta = \hat{\Pi}^{-1}\xi\). * Not closed form. The soliton is an ODE solution. Its needed properties (\(0 < w' < 1\), \(w'' < 0\)) follow from positive sectional curvature, but this route has not been checked in detail.

docs.title: 5.10 Active surprisal sector, \(J_E^\mu\nabla_\mu q \not\equiv 0\) (r7)
docs.text:
Correction to the transmitted version. With constant \(\varepsilon_q\), \(S_q \equiv J_E^\mu abla_\mu q\) is \( au\)-independent, so \(\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{H}_0 + ( au - au_0)S_q\). * The defect. As \( au o \infty\), \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}\) tends to the normalized \(\mathrm{Hess}\,S_q\). On flat slices, \(O_7\) then forces \(\mathrm{Hess}\,S_q = \lambda\delta\) with constant \(\lambda > 0\) (the same divergence argument as in §5.9), i.e., \(S_q\) an exact positive quadratic. * Why it fails. For \(q = -\ln(v_0Q)\) built from Neumann modes, \(S_q\) involves logarithms of trigonometric/Bessel products, which are not quadratic. So \(\mathrm{Hess}\,\mathcal{H}\) eventually loses positive-definiteness and \(O_7\) fails. * Why the finite-interval option doesn't help. Restricting to \( au \le au_{\max}\) is not an option, since the hypotheses are asymptotic.

Repaired construction (flat isotropic model of §5.1–5.6). * State. \( ho_{\mathrm{total}} = (1-\varepsilon_q)\vert\phi_0 angle\langle\phi_0\vert + \varepsilon_q\vert\phi_1 angle\langle\phi_1\vert\) with decaying weight \(\varepsilon_q( au) = \varepsilon_0 e^{-\gamma_q( au- au_0)}\), \(0 < \varepsilon_0 < 1\). * \(\phi_k = e^{-3H_0 au/2} ar{\phi}_k\), where \( ar{\phi}_1\) is a non-constant Neumann mode with \( ar{\lambda}_1 e^{-2H_0 au_0} \le \Lambda_{\mathrm{gate}}^2\). * The gate therefore passes both modes for all \( au \ge au_0\), and \( ho_{\mathrm{local}} = ho_{\mathrm{total}}\). * Density. \(Q = e^{-3H_0 au}((1-\varepsilon_q)/ ar{V} + \varepsilon_q ar{\phi}_1^2) > 0\), normalized. * Surprisal source. \(S_q = J_E\cdot abla q = -H_0\,x\cdot abla\ln((1-\varepsilon_q)/ ar{V} + \varepsilon_q ar{\phi}_1^2) ot\equiv 0\) for \(\varepsilon_q > 0\). It is \(O(\varepsilon_q)\) in \(C^2\). * Hysteresis. Choose the initial value so the limit is quadratic: \(\mathcal{H}( au, \mathbf{x}) = frac{c_{\mathcal{H}}}{2}\vert\mathbf{x}\vert^2 - \int_ au^\infty S_q( au', \mathbf{x})\,d au'\). Then: * \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = S_q\) (\(O_0\)); * \(\mathrm{Hess}\,\mathcal{H} = c_{\mathcal{H}}\delta - O(\varepsilon_0/\gamma_q) \succ 0\) for \(\varepsilon_0/\gamma_q\) small; * \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}} o frac{1}{3}\delta = \hat{ ho}_g\), so \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) > 0\) for finite \( au\), tending to \(0\) (\(O_7\)). * Ultralocal solution (\(O_\Omega\)). On the homothetic flat model, \(\ln\sqrt{\det g} = 3H_0 au\), so \( au(g) \equiv \ln\sqrt{\det g}/(3H_0)\) is an ultralocal function of \(g\). Set \(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}(g, \mathbf{x}) \equiv \mathcal{H}( au(g), \mathbf{x})\). * Then \(\partial\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}/\partial g_{\mu u} = S_q\cdot\partial au/\partial g_{\mu u} = frac{1}{2}(S_q/(3H_0))g^{\mu u}\), which is exactly the \(O_\Omega\) right-hand side, and its trace-free part is \(0\). * This generalizes the transmitted \( frac{S_q}{3H_0}\ln\sqrt{\det g}\) ansatz to \( au\)-dependent \(S_q\). * Functional. \(\Psi = \int_{\mathcal{M}}(\mathcal{H} - \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}[g])\,d^3x\) gives \(\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H} = 1 eq 0\), and the locus condition holds identically. * \(\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}\Psi = -2H_0 g_{\mu u} frac{S_q}{6H_0}g^{\mu u} + S_q = 0\). * Both sides of the generator equivalence are now non-zero at every finite \( au\), so the equivalence is exercised non-trivially. * Remaining data. Take \(P = Q(1 + \epsilon( au)u)\) as in §5.4.

Status after r7. * Surprisal sector (§5.10). Active and jointly satisfiable on the flat model. * Shear, gauge, overlap and \(\hat{\Pi}\) sectors (§5.8). Active, in separate constructions. * Stress sector. Active only on the cigar (§5.9), where \(O_7\) provably fails. * Open problems. 1. Exhibit a curved-slice model satisfying \(O_7\); §5.9 suggests the Bryant-soliton route. 2. Combine all sectors in a single configuration.

docs.title: 5.11 Consolidated model: all sectors active on an exact warped soliton (r8)
docs.text:
This section closes both open problems of §5.10. The construction was transmitted by Gemini Argon 4 and verified symbolically here (exact sympy, both with and without shear), with two corrections.

Domain. \(\mathcal{M}\) is the rounded hollow cylinder \(\{R_1 \le \varrho \le R_2,\ z_1 \le z \le z_2\}\) with \(z \equiv x^3\) and \(z_1 > 0\). It is compact and connected, with \(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}} \cong \mathbb{R}\).

Metric. \(g = e^{2H_0 au}\,\mathrm{diag} ig(z^{\sqrt{2}}e^{a( au)},\ z^{\sqrt{2}}e^{a( au)},\ e^{-2a( au)} ig)\), where: * \(a( au) = (2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma)(1 - e^{-\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)})\) with \(0 < s_\sigma < H_0/2\); * \(a \equiv 0\) recovers the unsheared soliton \( ar{g} = z^{\sqrt{2}}((dx^1)^2 + (dx^2)^2) + dz^2\), a warped product with flat fiber and warping \(w = z^{1/\sqrt{2}}\).

Correction 1: use axisymmetric shear. The transmitted planar shear \(\hat{h} = a\,\mathrm{diag}(1,-1,0)\) preserves the stress sector, but it destroys the harmonicity of \(d\varphi\) (the \(O_5\) harmonic current) and of \(\ln\varrho\); both were checked symbolically. * The axisymmetric shear \(\hat{h} = a\,\mathrm{diag}(1,1,-2)\) keeps every closed-form object. * It is locally isometric to the unsheared soliton by constant rescalings of \(x^{1,2}\) and \(z\).

Weyl split and kinematics. * \(\Omega = e^{H_0 au}z^{\sqrt{2}/3}\), \(\hat{g} = \mathrm{diag}(z^{\sqrt{2}/3}, z^{\sqrt{2}/3}, z^{-2\sqrt{2}/3})\) with \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\hat{h} = a\,\mathrm{diag}(1,1,-2)\). * \( heta = 3H_0\). * \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = s_\sigma e^{-\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)}\,\mathrm{diag}(1,1,-2)\). * \(\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal{D}) \ge H_0 - 2s_\sigma > 0\). * \(\chi = 1 + 2s_\sigma^2 e^{-2\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)}/H_0^2\). * \(G_\infty = \hat{g}_\infty\) up to the conformal factor, and \(\succ 0\).

Curvature (confirmed). * \(R = (2\sqrt{2} - 3)\,e^{-2H_0 au}/z^2 < 0\) (shown for \(a = 0\); \(a e 0\) only rescales by \(e^{\pm a}\) factors). * \(G_{33} = 1/(2z^2)\) and \(G_{ab} = - rac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2z^2} ar{g}_{ab}\), so all three diagonal components are non-zero.

Stress sector, active (confirmed with and without shear). * \(\Phi = frac{3}{4}z^2\) gives \(\hat{\Pi}_{33} = 1 - frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), which is \( au\)-independent even under shear. * \(\eta = (0, 0, -\sqrt{2}/(\kappa_G z))\) gives \(\xi = - rac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\kappa_G z}\,dz\). * Then, exactly: * \(R_{\mu u} = \kappa_G abla_{(\mu}\xi_{ u)}\); * \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T^{\mathrm{mat}}_{\mu u} ot\equiv 0\); * \( abla^2\xi + \mathrm{Ric}\cdot\xi = 0\). * \(\kappa_G\) is genuinely exercised.

Shear coupling, active. * \( heta\) is constant, so the \( au\)-compatibility law reduces to \(\kappa_G\partial_ au T^{\mathrm{mat}} = \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma]\). * It was verified that \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma]_{\mu u} = \partial_ au G_{\mu u}\), with non-zero planar components (\(\propto \dot{a}\)) and \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma]_{33} = 0\). * The elliptic \( heta\)-equation holds.

Flux and free energy. * Correction 2: the flux coefficient. The transmitted \(J_E = ( frac{3-\sqrt{2}}{2}H_0x^1, frac{3-\sqrt{2}}{2}H_0x^2, H_0z)\) gives \( abla\cdot J_E = 4H_0\), not \(3H_0\); the planar terms contribute \((3-\sqrt{2})H_0\), not \((2-\sqrt{2})H_0\). The correct coefficient is \( frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{2}\): \(J_E = ( frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{2}H_0x^1, frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{2}H_0x^2, H_0z)\) has \( abla\cdot J_E = 3H_0\) exactly, at all \(a\). * Free energy. \(\mathcal{F} = c_{\mathcal{F}}e^{-3H_0 au}z^{1-\sqrt{2}}\) is harmonic at all \(a\). Then \(J_E\cdot abla\mathcal{F} = -(\sqrt{2}-1)H_0 c_{\mathcal{F}}e^{-3H_0 au}z^{1-\sqrt{2}} < 0\), unaffected by Correction 2. * Harmonic current. \(c_{\mathrm{harm}}\,d\varphi\) remains harmonic, and the absolute boundary conditions hold (the planar block is isotropic).

Hysteresis and \(O_7\) (no obstruction). * \(\mathcal{H}_0 = rac{c_{\mathcal{H}}}{1+1/\sqrt{2}}z^{1+1/\sqrt{2}}\) satisfies \( abla abla\mathcal{H}_0 \propto g\) with a positive factor at every \( au\) (verified with shear). Therefore \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}_0} = \hat{ ho}_g\) exactly. * The §5.9 obstruction does not apply, because the warped product has \(\mathcal{H}_0' \propto w\) and \(w' > 0\).

Surprisal sector (§5.10 construction, transplanted). * State. \( ho_{\mathrm{total}} = (1-\varepsilon_q)\vert\phi_0 angle\langle\phi_0\vert + \varepsilon_q\vert\phi_1 angle\langle\phi_1\vert\) with \(\varepsilon_q = \varepsilon_0 e^{-\gamma_q( au- au_0)}\), where \(\phi_1\) is a non-constant Neumann mode of \(- abla^2_{g( au)}\). * Hysteresis. \(\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{H}_0 - \int_ au^\infty S_q\,d au'\). * Ultralocal solution. \(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}(g, \mathbf{x}) = \mathcal{H}( au(g, \mathbf{x}), \mathbf{x})\) with \( au(g, \mathbf{x}) = \ln(\sqrt{\det g}/z^{\sqrt{2}})/(3H_0)\). Shear does not change \(\det g\), so \(\partial\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}/\partial g_{\mu u} = frac{1}{2}(S_q/(3H_0))g^{\mu u}\) exactly. * Consequences. The \(O_\Omega\) generator equivalence is exercised non-trivially. \(\mathrm{Hess}\,\mathcal{H} \succ 0\) for \(\varepsilon_0/\gamma_q\) small, and \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) > 0\) for finite \( au\), tending to \(0\).

Relational edge. * Coupling. \(\Phi^{(1)} = \Phi^{(2)} = frac{3}{4}z^2\) and \(\eta_{1 o 2} = -\eta_{2 o 1} = rac{a_0e^{3H_0 au/2}}{1-1/\sqrt{2}}\,\partial_z\) give \(J_{[1 o 2]} = a_0e^{3H_0 au/2}\,dz\), \(F = 0\), and \(M^{(12)} = \gamma_M a_0^2 e^{3H_0 au}(\delta_{\mu 3}\delta_{ u 3} - frac{1}{3}g^{33}g_{\mu u}) eq 0\) everywhere. * Overlap. Take \(\mathcal{U}_2 = E\), a small coordinate ellipsoid flattened along \(z\). * The axisymmetric shear compresses \(z\) physically (\(g_{33} \propto e^{-2a}\), \(a \ge 0\)), so \(E\) only becomes more oblate along the coupling direction. Unlike §5.8, no threshold \(a^*\) arises. * Flux positivity and geodesic convexity are argued for \(E\) small, where curvature corrections are \(O(\mathrm{diam}\,E)\). This is the standard small-domain argument, not Whitehead's theorem, which concerns geodesic balls. It was not computed numerically on the curved metric. * Overlap divergence and gauge sector. Carried over unchanged from §5.8. * The gauge sector depends only on \(\chi( au)\), which is spatially constant here. * Use the Gaussian-copula \(Q_{12}\) with \(\mathcal{I}( au_0) > 0\).

Status after r8. Both open problems of §5.10 are closed. * A curved-slice model with \(G = \kappa_G T^{\mathrm{mat}} ot\equiv 0\) satisfies \(O_7\). * A single configuration has every sector active simultaneously: curved stress, shear with \(\mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma] ot\equiv 0\), \(\chi > 1\), \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) > 0\), gauge curvature with \(\hat{\mathcal{E}} ot\equiv 0\), overlap divergence, and active surprisal.

Not elementary, contrary to the transmission. The metric, stress, flux, free energy, harmonic current and \(\mathcal{H}_0\) are closed-form. The Neumann mode \(\phi_1\) (and hence \(Q\), \(S_q\), \(\mathcal{H}\)), the Rosenblatt maps in \(Q_{12}\), and the small-\(E\) flux bound exist but are not explicit.

Remaining checks. * A numerical flux computation on the curved metric. * A careful written verification of the whole combined configuration in one place: the components were verified sector by sector.

docs.title: 5.12 Numerical flux, convexity, and end-to-end verification of §5.11 (r9)
docs.text:
The two remaining checks of §5.11 are now done. All numbers below come from flux.py and convex.py, and the full configuration is checked by e2e_5_11.py (36/36 checks pass, about 15 s).

Flux integrand. The coupling tensor is \(S^{(12)} = \gamma_M a_\eta^2(\delta_{\mu 3}\delta_{ u 3} - frac{1}{3}g^{33}g_{\mu u})\). Write \( u\) for the Euclidean unit covector normal, \(\hat{n}^\mu = g^{\mu u} u_ u/\vert u\vert_{g^{-1}}\), and \(dA_g = \sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,\vert u\vert_{g^{-1}}\,dA_\delta\). All \( au\)-factors cancel, and $\( rac{\oint_{\partial E}S^{(12)}_{\mu u}\hat{n}^\mu\hat{n}^ u dA}{\gamma_M a_\eta^2} \equiv C(a) = \oint_{\partial E} e^{3a/2}z^{\sqrt{2}/2}\, rac{ frac{2}{3}e^{3a}z^{\sqrt{2}} u_3^2 - frac{1}{3}( u_1^2+ u_2^2)}{\sqrt{ u_1^2+ u_2^2+e^{3a}z^{\sqrt{2}} u_3^2}}\,dA_\delta .\)$ * Validation. This closed form agrees to all printed digits with a brute-force evaluation built from the induced metric and the \(g\)-unit normal. * Correction to the transmitted integrand. The transmitted \(C_E^{\mathrm{warped}}\) places \(z^{\sqrt{2}}\) on the wrong components: it contracts with \(g_{ab}\) where \(g^{ab}\) is required. It differs numerically, for example \(0.517\) versus the correct \(0.654\) at \(a = 0\) for semi-axes \((0.25, 0.25, 0.05)\). Its sign is nonetheless also positive throughout.

Flux is positive. \(C(a) > 0\) for every tested ellipsoid flattened along \(z\), over \(a \in [0, 8]\). Because the shear compresses \(z\), \(C(a)\) increases with \(a\).

semi-axes \(C(0)\) \(C(0.5)\) \(C(1)\) \(C(2)\) \((0.25, 0.25, 0.05)\) \(0.654\) \(3.07\) \(13.9\) \(281\) \((0.2, 0.2, 0.04)\) \(0.419\) \(1.96\) \(8.92\) \(180\)

Convexity is not automatic; this corrects §5.11's "small \(E\)" argument. Strict positivity of the Riemannian second fundamental form of \(\partial E\) in \(g\) was checked directly. The smallest principal curvature is computed from \(\mathrm{Hess}_g F\vert_{T\partial E}/\vert abla F\vert_g\) with \(F = \sum_i((x - c)_i/b_i)^2 - 1\), over a dense surface grid. * Why it can fail. Near its bottom pole, a flat ellipsoid is nearly a level set $z = $ const. In this warped metric those level sets bend away from the bottom face, with a contribution \(-\Gamma^3_{ab}\partial_3 F \propto e^{3a}\). * Criterion. Convexity therefore holds only while \(a < a_c\), with $\(a_c \approx frac{1}{3}\ln\! ig(b_3/(p\,z_0^{\sqrt{2}-1}b_1^2) ig), \qquad p = 1/\sqrt{2},\ z_0 = 2.\)$ The numerical thresholds match this estimate to within \(0.3\%\).

semi-axes numerical \(a_c\) estimate \((0.25, 0.25, 0.05)\) not convex at \(a = 0\) \(-0.055\) \((0.2, 0.2, 0.04)\) \(0.023\) \(0.020\) \((0.1, 0.1, 0.02)\) \(0.252\) \(0.251\) \((0.05, 0.05, 0.01)\) \(0.483\) \(0.482\) \((0.1, 0.1, 0.05)\) \(0.560\) \(0.556\) \((0.05, 0.05, 0.025)\) \(0.789\) \(0.787\) \((0.02, 0.02, 0.01)\) \(1.094\) \(1.093\)
  • Consequence. Both transmitted example ellipsoids fail for essentially any shear: \((0.25, 0.25, 0.05)\) is not convex even at \(a = 0\), and \((0.2, 0.2, 0.04)\) only up to \(a \approx 0.023\). The hypothesis "\(\mathcal{U}_{12}\) geodesically convex for all \( au\)" requires \(a_\infty = 2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma < a_c(E)\). The overlap must therefore be chosen after the shear parameters, and its size must shrink like \(e^{-3a_\infty/2}\) at fixed aspect ratio.

Recommended concrete choice. * Parameters. \(s_\sigma = 0.2H_0\) and \(\gamma_\sigma = H_0\), so \(a_\infty = 0.4\). Take \(E\) centered at \((2, 0, 2)\) with semi-axes \((0.05, 0.05, 0.025)\), inside \(\mathcal{M} = \{1 \le \varrho \le 3,\ 1 \le z \le 3\}\). * Flux. \(C(a)\) increases from \(0.0213\) to \(0.0833\) over \(a \in [0, 0.4]\), and \(C_\infty = C(0.4) = 0.0833\). * Convexity. The minimum principal curvature over \(a \in [0, 0.4]\) is \(1.18 > 0\), and \(a_c = 0.79 > a_\infty\). * Geodesic convexity. \(\mathrm{II} \succ 0\) gives local convexity: minimizing geodesics between points of \( ar{E}\) stay in \( ar{E}\). \(E\) has diameter \(0.1\), far below the curvature scale (\(\vert\mathrm{Riem}\vert \sim 0.1\) near \(z = 2\)), so geodesics are also unique. This last step is a scale argument; no conjugate-point computation was done.

Saturation constant. With \(a_\eta = a_0e^{3H_0 au/2}\), \(d\mathcal{I}/d au = k_{\mathcal{I}}\gamma_M a_0^2 e^{3H_0 au}C(a( au))\) and \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = e^{3H_0 au}\int_{\mathcal{M}}z^{\sqrt{2}}d^3x\). Since \(C(a( au)) o C_\infty\) exponentially, $\(s_0 = rac{k_{\mathcal{I}}\gamma_M a_0^2\,C_\infty}{3H_0\int_{\mathcal{M}}z^{\sqrt{2}}\,d^3x} \quad ext{gives}\quad rac{\mathcal{I}}{s_0V_{\mathcal{M}}} o 1 .\)$ The transmitted alternative \(a_\eta = a_0e^{3H_0 au/2 - a}\) is not needed. With \(C\) defined as the whole integral, the transmitted factor \(e^{2a_\infty}\) does not appear.

End-to-end script (e2e_5_11.py): what it checks. The symbolic checks are exact (sympy) with general \(s_\sigma, \gamma_\sigma, H_0, \kappa_G\) and the explicit shear profile \(a( au)\). * \(O_0\). \( heta\) in all three forms; \( abla\cdot J_E = heta\) with the corrected coefficient. It also records that the transmitted coefficient gives \(4H_0\). * \(O_1\)/\(O_4\). The free-energy balance law, and \(J_E\cdot abla\mathcal{F} < 0\). * \(O_2\). The Weyl split, \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\partial_ au\ln\Omega = heta/3\), \(\xi = \hat{\Pi}\eta\), \(G = \kappa_G T^{\mathrm{mat}}\) with all three diagonal entries non-zero, \(R = \kappa_G abla\cdot\xi\), the full \( au\)-law \(\kappa_G\partial_ au T^{\mathrm{mat}} = \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma] ot\equiv 0\), and the traced \( heta\)-equation. * \(O_3\). \(\sigma\) in closed form, the damping law, tracelessness, and \(\hat{h}_\infty\). * \(O_4\). \(\mathrm{tr}\,T^{\mathrm{mat}}\), and the elliptic condition (hence \( abla\cdot T^{\mathrm{mat}} = 0\)). * \(O_5\). \(e^{-2H_0 au}g o G_\infty \succ 0\), the mixed-rate limit, harmonicity of \(d\varphi\), and the absolute boundary condition on an axisymmetric boundary. * \(O_6\). \(M\) is symmetric and trace-free with mixed spectrum \(\gamma_M\vert J\vert^2( frac{2}{3}, - frac{1}{3}, - frac{1}{3})\); \(\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathcal{D} = heta\); \(\lambda_{\min}(\mathcal{D}) = H_0 - 2s_\sigma e^{-\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)}\); and, numerically, flux positivity and convexity. * \(O_7\). The \(\chi\) formula, \(\hat{ ho}_g o frac{1}{3}\delta\), \(\mathrm{Hess}\,\mathcal{H}_0 = \lambda g\) with \(\lambda > 0\), and the gauge identity with \(\hat{\mathcal{E}}_2 ot\equiv 0 o 0\). * \(O_\Omega\). For a generic surprisal source \(S_q\), \(\partial au(g,\mathbf{x})/\partial g_{\mu u} = g^{\mu u}/(6H_0)\) on a generic symmetric matrix, hence \(\partial\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}/\partial g = frac{1}{2}(S_q/(3H_0))g^{\mu u}\) and \(\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}\Psi = 0\).

What the script does not check. * The Neumann mode. \(\phi_1\) on the rounded, warped, sheared domain is not explicit. Positivity of \(Q\), the bound \(\mathrm{Hess}\,\mathcal{H} \succ 0\) for small \(\varepsilon_0/\gamma_q\), and the magnitude of \(S_q\) rest on the qualitative argument of §5.10. * The copula. The Rosenblatt maps of the Gaussian-copula \(Q_{12}\) are not computed. * The rounded rims. The rim rounding is not modelled. The boundary-condition check uses a general axisymmetric normal, which covers it. * Global uniqueness of geodesics. In \(E\) this rests on the scale argument above.

Status after r9. Joint satisfiability of the full hypothesis set, with every sector active, is established by an explicit configuration. Everything closed-form is verified exactly and the overlap geometry numerically, with the caveats listed above. The correction found here is substantive: the overlap \(E\) must satisfy \(a_\infty < a_c(E)\).

docs.title: 5.13 Branch II witness: a bounded, curved, non-equilibrium steady state with relaxing shear (r10)
docs.text:
This section verifies one configuration of the generalized r7 system with \(H_0 = 0\). Claims marked verified were checked by exact symbolic computation (sympy) in r10_branch2_witness_check.py, which is distributed with this document and prints a PASS/FAIL line for each check (40 checks: 36 for the witness, 4 for a Branch I regression). Claims marked derived follow from verified quantities by a stated one-line argument and have no PASS line of their own.

Domain. The rounded hollow cylinder of §5.11, \(\{R_1 \le \varrho \le R_2,\ z_1 \le z \le z_2\}\) with \(z_1 > 0\); compact, connected, \(H^1_{\mathrm{dR}} \cong \mathbb{R}\).

Metric. \(g = \mathrm{diag} ig(z^{\sqrt{2}}e^{a( au)},\ z^{\sqrt{2}}e^{a( au)},\ e^{-2a( au)} ig)\): the §5.11 metric with \(H_0 = 0\), where \(a( au) = (2s_\sigma/\gamma_\sigma)(1 - e^{-\gamma_\sigma( au- au_0)})\) with \(s_\sigma = 0.2\gamma_\sigma\), \(\gamma_\sigma > 0\), so \(a_\infty = 0.4\). The domain and overlap are those of §5.11: \(\mathcal{M} = \{1 \le \varrho \le 3,\ 1 \le z \le 3\}\), with \(E\) centred at \((2, 0, 2)\) and semi-axes \((0.05, 0.05, 0.025)\), for which §5.12 found convexity for all \(a < a_c = 0.79\) and \(C(a) > 0\) on \(a \in [0, 0.4]\), the range used here (\(a \in [0, 0.4]\) throughout). The script treats \(a( au)\) as an arbitrary function, so every identity below holds for any shear history, except the \(O_3\) Eq. [2] damping law, which is checked for the declared exponential \(a( au)\) only.

Kinematics (verified). \(\det g = z^{2\sqrt{2}}\) is independent of \(a\), so \( heta = 0\) exactly and \(\partial_ au\sqrt{\vert g^{(i)}\vert} = 0\) (verified), which satisfies the r7 form of \(O_5\) Eq. [0] (\(\ge 0\) in Branch II), \(\Omega = z^{\sqrt{2}/3}\) is \( au\)-independent (\(O_2\) Eq. [2] with \(J_{\mathrm{geom}} = 0\)), the \(u_{\mathrm{exp}}\) flux identity of \(O_7\) Eq. [3] holds with \(J_{\mathrm{geom}} = u_{\mathrm{exp}} = 0\) (derived), and the shear \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = rac{\dot{a}}{2}\mathrm{diag}(1,1,-2)\) (verified) is active and decays; \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu} = rac{3}{2}\dot{a}^2\) (verified) \( o 0\) (derived, since \(\dot{a} o 0\)). \(J_{\mathrm{geom}} = 0\), \(\dot{V}_{\mathcal{M}} = 0\), \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0\), and \(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\) for all \( au\). \( rac{1}{2}g^{-1}\partial_ au g\) is proportional to \(\dot{a}\) and tends to \(0\), and \(g o G_\infty\) as \(a o a_\infty\), so \(O_5\) Eq. [4] holds with \(H_0 = 0\).

Curved stress sector (verified, with shear). With \(\Phi = rac{3}{4}z^2\) and \(\eta = (0, 0, -\sqrt{2}/(\kappa_G z))\) as in §5.11: * \(\xi = rac{1-\sqrt{2}}{\kappa_G z}\,dz\), independent of \( au\); * \(G_{\mu u} = \kappa_G T^{\mathrm{mat}}_{\mu u} ot\equiv 0\), \(R = \kappa_G abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha\), and \( abla^2\xi_ u + R_ u^{\;\alpha}\xi_\alpha = 0\); * the \( au\)-compatibility law \(\kappa_G\partial_ au T^{\mathrm{mat}} = \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Ein}}[\sigma]\) (its \( heta\) terms vanish) and the elliptic \( heta\)-equation \(0 = -\kappa_G\partial_ au( abla_\alpha\xi^\alpha) + 2 abla^\alpha abla^ eta\sigma_{\alpha eta} - 2\sigma^{\alpha eta}R_{\alpha eta}\) both hold exactly at every \( au\).

So \(\kappa_G\) is exercised in a bounded configuration with shear, without any expansion.

Free energy with anisotropic transport and an interior sink (verified). * Declared constitutive terms: \(\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} = \mathrm{diag}(k_1, k_1, k_3)\) in coordinate components (\(k_1, k_3 > 0\), \(k_1 eq k_3\) in general; positive definite and anisotropic relative to \(g\)), and a zeroth-order (saturated) sink \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} = r_0 > 0\). * \(\mathcal{F}(z)\) with \(\partial_z\mathcal{F} = ig(r_0z^{1+\sqrt{2}}/(1+\sqrt{2}) - C_{\mathcal{F}} ig)/(k_3z^{\sqrt{2}})\) is static and satisfies the r7 balance law \(0 = abla_\mu(\mathfrak{K}^{\mu u} abla_ u\mathcal{F}) - \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}}\) exactly (with \( heta = 0\), \(\partial_ au\mathcal{F} = 0\)). * For \(C_{\mathcal{F}} > r_0z_2^{1+\sqrt{2}}/(1+\sqrt{2})\), \(\partial_z\mathcal{F} < 0\) on all of \([z_1, z_2]\), so \( abla\mathcal{F} eq 0\): the numerator \(r_0z^{1+\sqrt{2}}/(1+\sqrt{2}) - C_{\mathcal{F}}\) is increasing in \(z\) (verified), so its value at \(z_2\) (verified negative) bounds it. * Here \( abla_\mu J_E^\mu = -r_0/p_0 eq 0\) while \( heta = 0\) (verified): \(J_E\) is not an expansion current in Branch II, which is why every \( heta\) identity uses \(J_{\mathrm{geom}}\).

Throughput (verified). With the Branch II \(J_E^\mu = J_W^\mu/p_0\): * \(J_E^\mu abla_\mu\mathcal{F} = -k_3(\partial_z\mathcal{F})^2/p_0 < 0\); * \(\Theta_E = eta_{\mathrm{th}}k_3(\partial_z\mathcal{F})^2/(p_0s_0)\) (verified), pointwise independent of \( au\) (verified), and \(> 0\) because \(\partial_z\mathcal{F} < 0\) (derived); since \(\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\) is static, \(\langle\Theta_E angle_{\mathcal{M}} = \Theta_\infty > 0\) (derived); * \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{diss}} = (s_0/ eta_{\mathrm{th}})\int\Theta_E\sqrt{\vert g\vert} > 0\) and \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{tot}} > 0\) while \(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{ext}} = 0\) (derived); * \(\Theta_{\mathrm{tot}} = \Theta_E\) because \( heta = 0\), so \( au_\Theta\) increases strictly (derived); * \(\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\sigma^ u_{\;\mu} = rac{3}{2}\dot{a}^2\) (verified), so \(\chi_E = 1 + rac{9}{2}\dot{a}^2/\Theta_\infty^2 o 1\) (derived), while \(\chi\) itself is undefined (\( heta = 0\)), as Decision 6 anticipates.

Hysteresis and \(O_7\) (verified). \(\mathcal{H}_0 = rac{z^{1+1/\sqrt{2}}}{1+1/\sqrt{2}}\) has \( abla abla\mathcal{H}_0 = \lambda g\) with \(\lambda = rac{\sqrt{2}}{2}z^{-1+\sqrt{2}/2}e^{2a} > 0\) at every \( au\) (both verified), so \(\hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}} = \hat{ ho}_g\) and \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}}) = 0\).

Surprisal sector (by construction, trivial; normalization uses the weighted condition \(\int u\,Q\sqrt{\vert g\vert}\,d^3x = 0\)). The gated state is the constant Neumann mode, \( ho_{\mathrm{local}} = \vert\phi_0 angle\langle\phi_0\vert\), so \(Q\) is uniform, \( abla q = 0\), \(\partial_ au\mathcal{H} = J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q = 0\), and \(\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{H}_0\). The reference prior is inherited from §5.4: \(P = Q(1 + \epsilon( au)u)\) with \(\int u\,z^{\sqrt{2}}\,d^3x = 0\) (the weighted condition, since \(Q\) is uniform and \(\sqrt{\vert g\vert} = z^{\sqrt{2}}\)), \(\vert u\vert < 1\), \(u ot\equiv 0\), and \(\epsilon( au) \in (0,1)\) decreasing to \(0\), so \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q \parallel P) > 0\) (\(\dot{W}_{\mathrm{var}} > 0\)) and \(V_Q/V_P o 1\). Declare \(\Psi = \int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathcal{H}\,d^3x\) and the ultralocal \(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}(g, \mathbf{x}) = \mathcal{H}_0(z)\). Then \(\delta\Psi/\delta g_{\mu u} = 0\), \(\partial\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}/\partial g_{\mu u} = 0\), and \(\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H} \equiv 1\), so the \(O_\Omega\) Eq. [2] locus condition holds, \(\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H} eq 0\), and \(\vert\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H}\vert\) is bounded and bounded away from \(0\) uniformly (derived). The Branch II generator condition \(\hat{\mathbb{L}}_{\mathrm{stat}}\Psi = (J_E^\lambda abla_\lambda q)\,\delta\Psi/\delta\mathcal{H} = 0\) therefore holds at every \( au\), and a fortiori asymptotically. An active, decaying surprisal sector (as in §5.10) is not constructed here.

Relational edge (verified). With \(\Phi^{(1)} = \Phi^{(2)} = rac{3}{4}z^2\) and \(\eta_{1 o 2} = -\eta_{2 o 1} = rac{c_J( au)}{1 - 1/\sqrt{2}}\partial_z\), where \(c_J( au) = c_0e^{-\gamma_c( au- au_0)}\) (\(c_0, \gamma_c > 0\)) decays integrably (Branch II requires this; see Decision 6): * \(J_{[1 o 2]} = c_J( au)\,dz\), \(J_{1 o 2} + J_{2 o 1} = 0\), and \(F^{(1 o 2)} = 0\) at every \( au\), so the curvature bracket is inactive; * \((M^{(12)})^\mu_{\; u} = \gamma_Mc_J^2e^{2a}\mathrm{diag}(- rac{1}{3}, - rac{1}{3}, rac{2}{3})\): trace-free and non-zero everywhere at every finite \( au\), with the eigenvalue formula and \(m_+ eq -m_-\) verified and the signs \(m_+ > 0 > m_-\) read off from it, and, since \(e^{2a} \le e^{0.8}\) is bounded, \(\vert M^{(12)}\vert \le \mathrm{const}\cdot c_J^2\) is integrable and tends to \(0\) (derived); * with a constant coupling amplitude, the \(O_6\) flux law would make \(\mathcal{I}\) grow linearly without bound, contradicting \(\mathcal{I} o s_0V_\infty\); the decaying amplitude makes \(\int d\mathcal{I} < \infty\).

Harmonic current. \(d\varphi\) (\(\varphi\) the azimuth) is co-closed for \(g\) at every \( au\) (verified), because the planar block is isotropic; \(c_{\mathrm{harm}}\,d\varphi\) satisfies the absolute boundary conditions of §5.11 (inherited, not checked).

Drive (default in this witness; cone-preservation identity verified for arbitrary \(a_{\mathrm{d}}\)). The witness uses the default \(a_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\), so its trajectories obey the r6 geodesic equation. An arbitrary potential \(\Phi_{\mathrm{d}} \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\) would be a non-parametric field and is not admissible under the closure; closure conditions (ii)–(v) are empirical and are not applicable to a mathematical witness. For the projected form \(f^\mu_{\mathrm{drive}} = (1-u^2)(a^\mu_{\mathrm{d}} - (a_{\mathrm{d}}\cdot v)v^\mu)\) with any \(a_{\mathrm{d}}\), the script verifies, for this metric and arbitrary \((\mathbf{x}, v, a_{\mathrm{d}})\), that along solutions \(du^2/d au = (1-u^2) ig(-\partial_ au g_{ ho\epsilon}v^ ho v^\epsilon + 2(1-u^2)\,a_{\mathrm{d}}\cdot v ig)\), so \(u^2 = 1\) is invariant and \(u^2 < 1\) is preserved. The right side is smooth, so trajectories exist locally and are unique.

Inherited, not recomputed. * Flux positivity and geodesic convexity of the overlap \(E\) (§5.12). With the \(e^{3H_0 au/2}\) factor removed from \(\eta\), \(M_{\mu u}\) is invariant under \(g o cg\); the unit normals contribute \(c^{-1}\) and \(dA\) contributes \(c\), so the boundary flux is unchanged up to the positive factor \(c_J( au)^2/c_0^2\), and the sign of the second fundamental form is preserved under constant rescaling. The tested ellipsoids, the range \(a \in [0, 8]\), and the convexity threshold therefore carry over, but they were not re-run. * The gauge sector and overlap divergence (§5.8), with \(\hat{\chi} = \chi_E\hat{u}\) and \(\chi_E\) spatially constant here. * The Gaussian-copula \(Q_{12}\) of §5.8, with initial information \(\mathcal{I}( au_0)\) and normalization chosen so that the integrated flux, finite because \(c_J\) decays integrably, brings \(\mathcal{I}( au) o s_0V_\infty\).

Branch I regression (verified). The same code, applied to the §5.11 metric with \(H_0 > 0\), confirms \( heta = 3H_0\), \(G = \kappa_G T^{\mathrm{mat}}\), the \( au\)-compatibility law, and the elliptic \( heta\)-equation with shear. This is an independent re-implementation of the §5.11 stress-sector checks, not a re-run of e2e_5_11.py.

Status after r10. * The generalized r7 system has at least one Branch II configuration, with each property verified, derived, or inherited as itemized above, with \( heta = 0\), \(\Theta_E > 0\), curvature \(G eq 0\) with active \(\kappa_G\), relaxing shear, anisotropic \(\mathfrak{K}\), an interior sink \(\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F}} > 0\), and a decaying relational coupling. Each r7 block, edited or not, was reviewed against it (including \(O_0\) Eq. [0], satisfied by the rounded hollow cylinder of §5.11, whose box description above is before rounding, and \(O_2\) Eq. [1], satisfied by the explicit smooth metric); \(O_5\) Eq. [0] required the r7 amendment to \(\ge 0\) noted above. Blocks not otherwise discussed above are, by status: * Verified: \(O_3\) Eq. [2] (the damping law \(\partial_ au\sigma^\mu_{\; u} = -\gamma_\sigma\sigma^\mu_{\; u}\) for the declared \(a( au)\)). * Derived: \(O_3\) Eq. [0] (\(f^{\mathrm{top}} = - abla\Phi\) with the declared \(\Phi\); \(V_{\mathrm{local}}\) constant because \(\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{H}_0\) is static), Eq. [1] and Eq. [3] (\( heta = 0\), the Weyl split with \(\det\hat{g} = 1\), \(\hat{h} o \hat{h}_\infty\)); \(O_7\) Eq. [2] (\(\hat{ ho}_g o rac{1}{3}\delta\) as \(a o a_\infty\), since \(g o G_\infty = \Omega^2\hat{g}_\infty\)); \(O_6\) Eq. [4] (\(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\) for all \( au\), so the volume shares and \(c_{ij}\) are constant); \(O_\Omega\) Eq. [1] (\( heta = 0 = nH_0\), \(\int\langle heta angle = 0\), \(\langle\Theta_E angle = \Theta_\infty > 0\), \(\sigma o 0\), and bounded Christoffel symbols and curvature on the compact domain as \(a o a_\infty\)); \(O_\Omega\) Eq. [2] (with \(\Psi\) and \(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{sol}}\) as declared above). In \(O_7\) Eq. [3], \(u_{\mathrm{exp}} = 0\), \(J_E\) is static and smooth on a compact domain (so \(\sup\Vert J_E\Vert_{C^1} < \infty\)), and \(\mathcal{L}_{\mathbf{J}_E}(\hat{h} - \hat{h}_\infty) = 0\) exactly: \(\hat{h} - \hat{h}_\infty\) is diagonal with spatially constant mixed components, and \(\partial_ u J_E^\mu\) is diagonal (only its \((z,z)\) entry is non-zero), so the Lie derivative reduces to the commutator of two diagonal matrices, which vanishes. * Inherited: \(O_\Omega\) Eq. [0] (\(V_{\mathcal{M}} = V_\infty\) derived; \(\mathcal{I} o s_0V_\infty\) via the inherited copula). * Trivial: \(O_7\) Eq. [0], since \(\mathcal{A}_{\mathcal{M}} = 0\) because \( abla q = 0\). * Inherited from §5.11 with \(\mathcal{U}_1 = \mathcal{M}\), \(\mathcal{U}_2 = E\), and \(g^{(1)} = g^{(2)} = g\): \(O_5\) Eq. [0]–[3] (cover, geometric mean, \(\mathbf{C}_{\mathrm{top}}\), gluing). * Inherited from §5.8: \(O_6\) Eq. [0]–[1] (joint and conditional densities, through the copula) and \(O_7\) Eq. [1]'s overlap-divergence limit. * Inherited, as stated above: \(O_7\) Eq. [4] (gauge sector). * Default: \(O_2\) Eq. [3] (\(a_{\mathrm{d}} = 0\); cone-preservation identity verified for arbitrary \(a_{\mathrm{d}}\)). * Not shown: a witness, in either branch, in which the conformal-Killing term of \(O_6\) Eq. [3] is non-zero (\(J_{i o j} + J_{j o i} = 0\) in every witness) or in which \(\hat{\Pi}^{(i)} eq \hat{\Pi}^{(j)}\) (so the \(O_6\) Eq. [2] distinction is never exercised); a Branch II witness with \( heta > 0\) decaying integrably (\(J_{\mathrm{geom}} eq 0\), \(V_{\mathcal{M}}\) actually converging; here \( heta \equiv 0\), so \(O_0\) Eq. [4] Branch II and the \(O_7\) Eq. [3] flux identity are exercised only trivially), with non-zero \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\hat{ ho}_g \parallel \hat{ ho}_{\mathcal{H}})\) or \(\mathcal{A}_{\mathcal{M}}\) (both \(\equiv 0\) here), with distinct subsystem metrics \(g^{(1)} eq g^{(2)}\) (here equal, so the geometric mean and gluing of \(O_5\) Eq. [1]–[3] are exercised only trivially), with a gradient not aligned with an eigendirection of \(\mathfrak{K}\) (here \( abla\mathcal{F} \parallel dz\), so \(k_1\) never enters; the anisotropy exercised is \(\mathfrak{K} ot\propto g^{-1}\), not \(k_1 eq k_3\)), with an active surprisal sector (permitted by r7, which states the Branch II generator condition asymptotically), a non-zero curvature bracket, a non-trivial \(f_{\mathrm{drive}}\) with verified trajectory properties, or a spatially varying sink. These remain open.
